all_sections.heading: Frequently asked questions
all_sections.content:
Common questions aboutGST Registration Online in India.

What Is GST Registration?

GST Registration is the process by which a business or individual obtains a unique Goods and Services Tax Identification Number (GSTIN) from the Government of India. This registration is mandatory for businesses that meet the prescribed turnover threshold or fall under specific categories as defined under the GST law.

Once registered, the business is legally authorized to collect GST from customers, file GST returns, and claim input tax credit. You can learn more about GST in India and get started with [GST Registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-registration) easily online.

Who Needs GST Registration?

The following businesses and individuals are required to obtain GST Registration:

- Businesses with an annual turnover exceeding Rs. 40 lakhs (Rs. 20 lakhs for service providers)
- Inter-state suppliers of goods and services
- E-commerce operators and sellers on e-commerce platforms
- Casual taxable persons and non-resident taxable persons
- Businesses required to pay tax under reverse charge mechanism
- Input service distributors
- Agents supplying goods or services on behalf of registered taxpayers

To understand more about GST applicability and to complete your [GST Registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-registration), get started today.

Is GST Registration Mandatory?

Yes, GST registration is mandatory for eligible businesses based on turnover, interstate supply, e-commerce activities, or specific taxable categories.

What Is the Threshold Limit for GST Registration?

The threshold limit for GST registration varies based on the type of business and location. Service Providers - Annual turnover exceeding Rs. 20 lakhs (Rs. 10 lakhs for special category states). Goods Suppliers - Annual turnover exceeding Rs. 40 lakhs (Rs. 20 lakhs for special category states). Special Category States such as Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland, and Tripura have a lower threshold of Rs. 10 lakhs. Businesses involved in interstate supply must register regardless of their turnover.

Who Is Eligible for GST Registration?

The following businesses and individuals are eligible for GST registration:

- Businesses with an annual turnover exceeding Rs. 40 lakhs (Rs. 20 lakhs for service providers)
- Businesses in special category states with turnover exceeding Rs. 20 lakhs
- Inter-state suppliers of goods and services
- E-commerce operators and sellers on e-commerce platforms
- Casual taxable persons and non-resident taxable persons
- Businesses required to pay tax under reverse charge mechanism
- Input service distributors

Voluntary GST registration is also available for businesses that do not meet the threshold but wish to avail input tax credit benefits.

What Documents Are Required for GST Registration?

The documents required for GST registration are as follows. Refer to the detailed list at [GST Registration Documents Required](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-registration/document-required):
PAN card of the business or applicant
Aadhaar card of the proprietor, partners, or directors
Proof of business registration or incorporation certificate
Identity and address proof of promoters or directors
Address proof of the principal place of business (electricity bill, rent agreement, or NOC)
Bank account statement or cancelled cheque
Digital signature (for companies and LLPs)
Letter of authorisation or board resolution for authorised signatory

What Is Rule 14A in GST Registration?

Rule 14A in GST registration deals with the authentication of Aadhaar for GST registration. Under this rule:

- Applicants are required to undergo Aadhaar authentication at the time of applying for GST registration
- If Aadhaar authentication is successful, the application is processed within 7 working days
- If the applicant opts out of Aadhaar authentication, physical verification of the business premises is carried out
- In such cases, the registration may take up to 30 working days

For more details, visit [GST Registration Rule 14A](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-registration/rule-14a).

How to Get GST Registration?

You can get GST registration by following these steps:

- Determine your eligibility based on turnover or business type
- Gather all required documents such as PAN, Aadhaar, and address proof
- Visit the GST portal and fill out Form GST REG-01
- Complete Aadhaar authentication
- Submit the application and wait for verification
- Upon approval, a GSTIN (GST Identification Number) and GST registration certificate will be issued

You can also get assistance from IndiaFilings to complete your GST registration quickly and hassle-free.

How to Apply for GST Registration Online?

To apply for GST registration online, follow these steps:

- Visit the official GST portal
- Click on Services and select New Registration
- Fill in Part A of Form GST REG-01 with your PAN, mobile number, and email ID
- Verify via OTP sent to your mobile and email
- Fill in Part B with business details, promoter information, and upload required documents
- Complete Aadhaar authentication
- Submit the application using DSC, e-Sign, or EVC
- Track your application status using the ARN (Application Reference Number)

Upon approval, your GSTIN will be issued.

How Much Does GST Registration Cost?

GST registration on the government portal is free of charge. However, if you choose to use a professional service to assist with the application, service charges may apply. IndiaFilings offers affordable GST registration packages. Check the latest pricing at [GST Registration Pricing](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-registration/pricing).

Is GST Registration Free?

Yes, GST registration through the official government GST portal is completely free. There are no government fees for obtaining a GSTIN. However, if you seek professional assistance from a service provider like IndiaFilings, nominal service charges may apply.

How Many Days Does GST Registration Take?

The time taken for GST registration depends on the authentication method chosen:

- With Aadhaar authentication: Registration is typically completed within 7 working days
- Without Aadhaar authentication (physical verification): Registration may take up to 30 working days
- If additional documents or clarifications are sought by the GST officer, it may take additional time

Ensure all documents are accurate and complete to avoid delays.

How to Check GST Registration Status?

You can check your GST registration status by following these steps:

- Visit the official GST portal
- Click on Services and select Track Application Status
- Enter your ARN (Application Reference Number) received at the time of application
- Click on Search to view the current status of your application

The status will indicate whether your application is pending, approved, or requires clarification.

How to Download GST Registration Certificate?

To download your GST registration certificate, follow these steps:

- Log in to the official GST portal using your GSTIN and password
- Go to Services and click on User Services
- Select View or Download Certificates
- Click on Download to save your GST registration certificate in PDF format

The GST registration certificate contains your GSTIN, business name, principal place of business, and validity details.

What Are the Benefits of GST Registration?

GST registration offers several key benefits:
Legal recognition as a supplier of goods or services
Ability to collect GST from customers and pass on input tax credit
Avail input tax credit on purchases and reduce overall tax liability
Eligibility to participate in inter-state trade without restrictions
Enhanced business credibility and trust with customers and vendors
Access to various government schemes and tenders that require GSTIN
Simplified and unified tax compliance under one system

Is Current Account Mandatory for GST Registration?

No, a current account is not mandatory for GST registration. You can provide a savings account, current account, or any other bank account details at the time of registration. However, it is advisable for businesses to maintain a current account for smoother business transactions and compliance purposes. Businesses such as [proprietorships](https://www.indiafilings.com/proprietorship) or [partnerships](https://www.indiafilings.com/partnership) can use their existing bank accounts.

Is Trade License Mandatory for GST Registration?

No, a trade license is not mandatory for GST registration. The GST portal accepts various documents as proof of business address, such as:

- Electricity bill
- Rent or lease agreement
- NOC from the property owner
- Municipal khata copy

A trade license can be submitted as supporting proof but is not a compulsory requirement for GST registration.

How to Cancel GST Registration?

GST registration can be cancelled by following these steps:

- Log in to the GST portal using your GSTIN and password
- Navigate to Services and select Application for Cancellation of Registration
- Fill in Form GST REG-16 with the reason for cancellation and relevant details
- Submit the application along with required documents

The GST officer will review the application and issue a cancellation order in Form GST REG-19Note: All pending returns and dues must be cleared before applying for cancellation.

How to Surrender GST Registration?

Surrendering GST registration is the same as applying for voluntary cancellation. To surrender your GST registration:
Log in to the GST portal
Go to Services and select Application for Cancellation of Registration
Fill in Form GST REG-16 stating the reason as voluntary surrender or discontinuation of business
Ensure all pending returns are filed and dues are cleared
Submit the application and await the cancellation order
File the final return in Form GSTR-10 after receiving the cancellation order

How to Activate Cancelled GST Registration?

If your GST registration has been cancelled, you can apply for revocation (reactivation) by following these steps:
Log in to the GST portal using your credentials
Go to Services and select Application for Revocation of Cancelled Registration
Fill in Form GST REG-21 with the reason for revocation
Submit the application within 30 days from the date of cancellation order
The GST officer will review the application and if satisfied, restore your GST registration

Note: If the cancellation was done by the tax officer, you must file all pending returns and pay dues before applying for revocation.

# GST Letter of Undertaking(LUT) Filing Online in India

Filing a **Letter of Undertaking (LUT)** under GST is mandatory for exporters who wish to export goods or services without paying **[Integrated Goods and Services Tax](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/igst)(IGST)**. Understanding the **GST LUT filing online** process helps businesses streamline their [GST compliance](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst) and avoid unnecessary tax outflows.

[GST Registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-registration) is the first step before you can file an LUT online in India.

## What is LUT in GST?

A **Letter of Undertaking (LUT)** is a declaration filed by exporters under **GST Form RFD-11**, allowing them to export goods or services without paying IGST. Instead of paying tax and later claiming a [GST refund](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-refund), businesses can use an LUT to conduct **zero-rated supply** transactions seamlessly.

The **LUT under GST** is valid for one financial year and must be renewed annually. It is a critical compliance requirement for all **GST registered exporters** in India.

## Who is Eligible to File LUT Under GST?

Any **GST-registered taxpayer** who intends to supply goods or services without payment of IGST can file an LUT. However, the following conditions must be met:

- The taxpayer must be registered under **GST LUT registration**
- The exporter must not have been prosecuted for [tax](https://www.indiafilings.com/income-tax) evasion exceeding ₹2.5 crore
- The business must be engaged in **zero-rated exports under GST**
- Suppliers making supplies to **Special Economic Zones (SEZs)** are also eligible
- Businesses involved in deemed exports can apply for **GST LUT compliance**

If the taxpayer does not meet these conditions, they must furnish a **LUT bond GST** instead of an LUT.

## What are the Documents Required for GST LUT Filing?

Before initiating the **GST LUT online filing** process, ensure the following documents are ready:

- **GST LUT application** form (RFD-11)
- [GSTIN](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-search)(GST Identification Number)
- [PAN Card](https://www.indiafilings.com/pan-card) of the business
- KYC documents of the authorized signatory
- IEC ( [Import Export Code](https://www.indiafilings.com/import-export-code)) for exporters
- Bank details of the business
- Previous LUT copy (for renewal)
- Letter of Authorization or Board Resolution

Having all the **GST LUT document checklist** ready in advance will help speed up the filing process significantly.

## What is the Step-by-Step Process to File LUT Online?

The **GST LUT filing procedure step by step** is entirely online through the GST portal. Here's how you can complete the process smoothly:

### Step-by-Step Guide: How to File LUT in GST Portal Online

1. **Step 1:** Visit the official GST portal at **www.gst.gov.in**
2. **Step 2:** Log in using your **GSTIN** credentials
3. **Step 3:** Navigate to _Services > User Services > Furnish Letter of Undertaking (LUT)_
4. **Step 4:** Select the relevant **financial year** for which LUT is being filed
5. **Step 5:** Fill in the **GST Form RFD-11** with required details
6. **Step 6:** Upload supporting documents as required
7. **Step 7:** Preview the form and verify all details
8. **Step 8:** Submit using **DSC (Digital Signature Certificate)** or **EVC (Electronic Verification Code)**
9. **Step 9:** Download the acknowledgment receipt

### How to File LUT for Export?

For exporters specifically, **how to file LUT in GST portal online** involves selecting the export category during the application. Exporters must confirm that they are filing for **export without IGST** and provide their **IEC code**. Once submitted, the **LUT certificate download** is available immediately on the GST portal, enabling export transactions without tax payment.

## What is the Validity of LUT Under GST?

The **LUT GST validity** is for one financial year (April 1 to March 31). A new LUT must be filed at the beginning of each financial year. Businesses can file the LUT for the upcoming financial year even before the current year ends to ensure continuity in **export without payment of tax**.

### When to Apply/File an LUT

The **GST LUT filing last date** is ideally before making the first export supply of the financial year. There is no strict deadline, but it is recommended to file it at the start of the financial year or before the first zero-rated transaction to avoid paying IGST on exports.

## What are the Tax & Process Details for GST LUT Forms?

Filing an LUT allows exporters to make **zero-rated supply GST** transactions without upfront tax payment. The key tax implications are:

| Particulars | LUT (Letter of Undertaking) | Bond |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tax Payment Required | No | No |
| Security/Surety | Not Required | Required |
| Eligibility | All GST-registered exporters (non-prosecuted) | Exporters with prosecution history |
| Validity | One Financial Year | As per bond terms |
| Process | Online via GST Portal | Manual/Online |

### Process for GST LUT Forms

The **GST LUT for exporters** process involves filing **Form RFD-11** online. Once approved, businesses can use [GST e-Invoice](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-einvoice) integration to mark their export invoices as LUT-based zero-rated supplies without paying IGST.

## How to Download and Furnish the LUT Certificate on GST Portal?

After successfully filing the LUT, you can **download LUT certificate from GST portal** by following these steps:

1. Log in to the GST portal
2. Go to _Services > User Services > View My Submitted LUTs_
3. Select the relevant financial year
4. Click on **Download** to get the LUT certificate in PDF format

The downloaded **LUT certificate** must be furnished to the customs department or buyer as proof of zero-rated supply eligibility. Use [GST Software](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-software) to maintain digital records of your LUT certificates efficiently.

## Why Should You Renew Your LUT Under GST?

Since the **annual LUT GST** is valid only for one financial year, timely renewal is critical. Failure to renew means the exporter must pay IGST on all export transactions and then claim a [GST refund](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-refund), which can disrupt cash flow significantly.

### How to Renew Letter of Undertaking (LUT): Step-by-Step Process

1. Log in to the GST portal at **www.gst.gov.in**
2. Navigate to _Services > User Services > Furnish Letter of Undertaking (LUT)_
3. Select the **new financial year** for renewal
4. Fill in **Form RFD-11** with updated details
5. Submit using DSC or EVC
6. Download the renewed **LUT certificate**

It is advisable to track your **GST LUT status** regularly using the [GST Return Filing](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-return-filing) dashboard to ensure all compliances are up to date.

## What are the Key Points to Note for GST LUT Registration?

Here are the important compliance points every exporter should be aware of regarding **GST LUT compliance**:

- LUT must be filed before making the first **zero-rated export supply** of the financial year
- The LUT is applicable for both **goods and services exports**
- Supplies to **SEZ units and SEZ developers** are also covered under LUT
- If the exporter violates LUT conditions, the **GST LUT cancellation** may be initiated
- Exporters must file **[GST returns](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-annual-return)** regularly to maintain LUT eligibility
- Non-realization of export proceeds within the stipulated time can lead to LUT withdrawal
- Track **GST notices** using the [GST Notice](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-notice) tracker to avoid compliance issues
- Maintain proper records of all **[export invoices](https://www.indiafilings.com/import-export)** linked to the LUT
- File **[GSTR-1](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/guide-to-gstr-1-filing) and [GSTR-3B](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/gstr-3b)** on time using GST Annual Return compliance tools

## Frequently asked questions

Common questions aboutGST LUT Filing Online for Exporters in India Without IGST Tax.

What is LUT full form?

LUT full form is "Letter of Undertaking." The LUT is a document that allows Indian exporters to export goods and services without paying the Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGST) upfront.

What is LUT in GST?

LUT in GST refers to the "Letter of Undertaking" that exporters file with the GST department. LUT in GST enables exporters to supply goods or services outside India or to Special Economic Zones (SEZs) without paying IGST upfront, provided they comply with specific eligibility criteria. This is what is LUT in GST refers to and the purpose it entails.

What is LUT in export and why is it important?

Most exports are confused with the question of what is LUT in export. LUT in export is a declaration filed by exporters, allowing them to ship goods or provide services internationally without paying IGST at the time of export. LUT in export is crucial because it ensures that the transaction is treated as zero-rated under GST, meaning no tax is payable on export supplies. This is what is LUT in export means and the importance it possesses.

How would I know that the process of furnishing the LUT has been completed?

After successful filing, the system will generate ARN and acknowledgment. You will be informed about successful filing via SMS and Email, and you can also download the acknowledgment as a PDF.

Is it possible to view the LUT application after filing?

Yes, the Taxpayer will be able to see his LUT after filing.

Is it mandatory to file GST LUT?

It is mandatory to furnish the Letter of undertaking (LUT) to export the goods, services, or both without paying the IGST.

What happens when the exporter fails to furnish the LUT?

In case if the exporter fails to provide the LUT then he has to pay the IGST or furnish an export bond.

Who is eligible to furnish LUT under GST?

Any person who is exporting goods or services can furnish the LUT.

Who is not eligible to furnish under GST?

A person who has been prosecuted for evading tax of Rs. 2.5 crore or above under the act cannot furnish the LUT.

What are the documents required for LUT under GST?

LUT cover letter- duly signed by an authorized person
Copy of the GST registration
PAN of the entity.

What if the LUT is not furnished on time?

If the LUT is not filed on time the exporter is required to pay the tax while carrying out exports and then claim a refund to avail the benefit of the zero-rated exports.

What is Form RFD 11?

Furnishing of the bond or letter of the undertaking for export of goods or services in Form RFD 11.

What should be filed in the letter of undertaking?

GSTIN and Name (Legal Name) of the Taxpayer will be prefilled based on login. The Taxpayer needs to select the financial year for which LUT is being filed, enter the name, address, and occupation details of two independent and reliable witnesses.

Is it mandatory to record them manually approved LUT in online records?

It is not mandatory, but if the Taxpayer wants to record the manually approved LUT to be available in online records, he can furnish it with the online application.

Who has to sign the LUT application?

Primary authorized signatory/Any other Authorized Signatory needs to sign and file the verification with DSC/EVC. The authorized signatory can be the working partner, the managing director, or the proprietor or by a person duly authorized by such operating partner or Board of Directors of such company or proprietor to execute the form.

all_sections.heading: What is LUT in GST?
all_sections.content:
A **Letter of Undertaking (LUT)** is a declaration filed by exporters under **GST Form RFD-11**, allowing them to export goods or services without paying IGST. Instead of paying tax and later claiming a [GST refund](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-refund), businesses can use an LUT to conduct **zero-rated supply** transactions seamlessly.

The **LUT under GST** is valid for one financial year and must be renewed annually. It is a critical compliance requirement for all **GST registered exporters** in India.

all_sections.heading: Who is Eligible to File LUT Under GST?
all_sections.content:
Any **GST-registered taxpayer** who intends to supply goods or services without payment of IGST can file an LUT. However, the following conditions must be met:

- The taxpayer must be registered under **GST LUT registration**
- The exporter must not have been prosecuted for [tax](https://www.indiafilings.com/income-tax) evasion exceeding ₹2.5 crore
- The business must be engaged in **zero-rated exports under GST**
- Suppliers making supplies to **Special Economic Zones (SEZs)** are also eligible
- Businesses involved in deemed exports can apply for **GST LUT compliance**

If the taxpayer does not meet these conditions, they must furnish a **LUT bond GST** instead of an LUT.

all_sections.heading: Frequently asked questions
all_sections.content:
Common questions aboutGST LUT Filing Online for Exporters in India Without IGST Tax.

What is LUT full form?

LUT full form is "Letter of Undertaking." The LUT is a document that allows Indian exporters to export goods and services without paying the Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGST) upfront.

What is LUT in GST?

LUT in GST refers to the "Letter of Undertaking" that exporters file with the GST department. LUT in GST enables exporters to supply goods or services outside India or to Special Economic Zones (SEZs) without paying IGST upfront, provided they comply with specific eligibility criteria. This is what is LUT in GST refers to and the purpose it entails.

What is LUT in export and why is it important?

Most exports are confused with the question of what is LUT in export. LUT in export is a declaration filed by exporters, allowing them to ship goods or provide services internationally without paying IGST at the time of export. LUT in export is crucial because it ensures that the transaction is treated as zero-rated under GST, meaning no tax is payable on export supplies. This is what is LUT in export means and the importance it possesses.

How would I know that the process of furnishing the LUT has been completed?

After successful filing, the system will generate ARN and acknowledgment. You will be informed about successful filing via SMS and Email, and you can also download the acknowledgment as a PDF.

Is it possible to view the LUT application after filing?

Yes, the Taxpayer will be able to see his LUT after filing.

Is it mandatory to file GST LUT?

It is mandatory to furnish the Letter of undertaking (LUT) to export the goods, services, or both without paying the IGST.

What happens when the exporter fails to furnish the LUT?

In case if the exporter fails to provide the LUT then he has to pay the IGST or furnish an export bond.

Who is eligible to furnish LUT under GST?

Any person who is exporting goods or services can furnish the LUT.

Who is not eligible to furnish under GST?

A person who has been prosecuted for evading tax of Rs. 2.5 crore or above under the act cannot furnish the LUT.

What are the documents required for LUT under GST?

LUT cover letter- duly signed by an authorized person
Copy of the GST registration
PAN of the entity.

What if the LUT is not furnished on time?

If the LUT is not filed on time the exporter is required to pay the tax while carrying out exports and then claim a refund to avail the benefit of the zero-rated exports.

What is Form RFD 11?

Furnishing of the bond or letter of the undertaking for export of goods or services in Form RFD 11.

What should be filed in the letter of undertaking?

GSTIN and Name (Legal Name) of the Taxpayer will be prefilled based on login. The Taxpayer needs to select the financial year for which LUT is being filed, enter the name, address, and occupation details of two independent and reliable witnesses.

Is it mandatory to record them manually approved LUT in online records?

It is not mandatory, but if the Taxpayer wants to record the manually approved LUT to be available in online records, he can furnish it with the online application.

Who has to sign the LUT application?

Primary authorized signatory/Any other Authorized Signatory needs to sign and file the verification with DSC/EVC. The authorized signatory can be the working partner, the managing director, or the proprietor or by a person duly authorized by such operating partner or Board of Directors of such company or proprietor to execute the form.

# GST Refund Online in India for Registered Taxpayers

**GST refund online in India** is a formal mechanism that allows registered taxpayers to recover excess tax paid to the government. Whether you are an exporter, a business dealing with an [inverted duty structure refund](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-refund/gst-inverted-duty-refund), or a business with accumulated input tax credit, filing a GST refund claim ensures your working capital is not unnecessarily blocked. With the GST portal enabling end-to-end online filing, businesses can now submit and track refund applications with complete transparency.

## Understanding GST Refund Filing in India

GST refund filing is the structured process through which a registered taxpayer applies to recover excess GST paid or accumulated input tax credit that cannot be utilised. Under the GST framework, refunds are governed by Section 54 of the CGST Act, 2017, and are filed using **Form RFD-01** on the GST portal.

A **GST refund application** can arise in various scenarios such as export of goods or services, excess payment due to errors, tax paid on deemed exports, or refund of pre-deposit. Understanding the filing mechanism is the first step for any business looking to recover funds.

- Refunds are processed electronically through the **GST portal**
- Form RFD-01 is the primary application form for all refund types
- Refunds are credited directly to the taxpayer's registered bank account
- The process is governed under Section 54 to Section 58 of the CGST Act

## GST Refund Rules and Who Qualifies in India

The **GST refund rules India** are clearly defined under the CGST Act and corresponding rules. Not every taxpayer can file a refund — specific conditions and situations trigger eligibility. Knowing these rules helps businesses avoid rejections and delays in processing.

Key rules that govern **GST refund procedure** include the two-year limitation period, the doctrine of unjust enrichment, and mandatory documentation requirements. Businesses must ensure that the refund amount has not been passed on to consumers before filing a claim.

- Refund must be filed within **two years** from the relevant date
- Doctrine of unjust enrichment applies to most refund categories
- Refunds below ₹1,000 are not processed under GST rules
- Proper reconciliation of GSTR-1, GSTR-3B is mandatory before claiming

## GST Refund Eligibility Criteria for Taxpayers in India

Understanding who qualifies for a **GST refund claim process** is essential before initiating an application. The GST law specifies distinct categories of taxpayers and situations that make a business eligible for refund claims in India.

### Who Can Claim a GST Refund?

- **Exporters of goods or services** — IGST paid on exports or accumulated ITC
- **SEZ units and SEZ developers** — receiving zero-rated supplies
- Businesses with **inverted duty structure** — where input tax rate exceeds output tax rate
- Taxpayers who made **excess GST payment** due to clerical errors
- Suppliers of **deemed exports** as notified by the government
- Businesses receiving **refund of pre-deposit** during appeals
- UN bodies, embassies and other [GST registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-registration) exempt entities

Every category has specific documentation and procedural requirements that must be fulfilled to successfully process the **online GST refund India** application.

## Key Categories of GST Refunds Under Indian Tax Law

Indian GST law recognises multiple types of refunds depending on the nature of the taxpayer's business and the reason for excess tax payment. Each category follows a distinct process and timeline under the **GST refund claim** framework.

### Types of GST Refunds Available

| Refund Type | Applicable To | Form Used |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Export of Goods with Payment of Tax | Exporters paying IGST | RFD-01 |
| Export of Goods without Payment of Tax | Exporters using LUT/Bond | RFD-01 |
| Inverted Duty Structure | Manufacturers, traders | RFD-01 |
| Excess Cash Ledger Balance | All registered taxpayers | RFD-01 |
| Refund on Deemed Exports | Suppliers to EOU/AA holders | RFD-01 |
| IGST Paid on Imports | Importers of goods/services | RFD-01 |
| SEZ Supplies | SEZ units and developers | RFD-01 |

Identifying the correct refund category is critical for accurate filing of your **GST refund application process** and avoiding rejection by the tax authorities.

## How Does the GST Refund Claim Process Work Online in India?

The **GST refund for export of goods** and other categories follows a structured online process through the GST portal. Filing a refund application online ensures transparency, faster processing, and real-time tracking of your claim status.

1. **Login** to the GST portal at gstin.gov.in using your credentials
2. Navigate to **Services > Refunds > Application for Refund**
3. Select the appropriate **refund category** from the dropdown menu
4. Fill in **Form RFD-01** with relevant tax period and refund amount details
5. Upload all **supporting documents** as per the refund category
6. Submit the application using **DSC or EVC** for verification
7. Receive the **ARN (Application Reference Number)** for tracking
8. Tax officer issues **acknowledgement in Form RFD-02** within 15 days
9. Refund sanctioned via **Form RFD-06** and credited to bank account

You can track your **GST refund status check** at any time using the ARN on the GST portal. For a detailed walkthrough, refer to our [step-by-step guide to claim your GST refund](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-refund/stepbystep-guide-to-claim-your-gst-refund).

## What Documents Do You Need for GST Refund Filing in India?

Accurate documentation plays a vital role in the successful processing of your **GST refund documents required** application. Incomplete or incorrect documents are among the leading causes of refund rejections in India.

- Declaration regarding **unjust enrichment** (where applicable)

- GSTR-2A reconciliation statement for **input tax credit refund**

- For inverted duty structure — relevant date is the end of the financial year in which the claim arises

Filing within the **GST refund processing time** window ensures your claim remains valid and is processed without complications.

## How is the GST Rate Calculated for Refund Claims in India?

Understanding how the **GST refund inverted duty** calculation works is essential for businesses filing under the inverted duty structure category. The formula determines the maximum refund amount a taxpayer can claim in any given tax period.

## Frequently asked questions

Common questions aboutGST Refund Online Claim Process in India for Businesses.

What is a GST refund?

A GST refund is the process through which taxpayers can claim back excess GST paid to the government, arising due to exports, input tax accumulation, mistaken tax payments, or other eligible scenarios.

Who is eligible to claim a GST refund?

Exporters, SEZ units/developers, businesses with excess Input Tax Credit (ITC), UN agencies, embassies, unregistered persons in specific cases, and taxpayers who overpaid GST can claim a refund.

What are zero-rated supplies in the context of GST?

Zero-rated supplies refer to the export of goods and services and supplies to SEZ units/developers, where the tax rate is 0%, but input tax credit can be claimed.

What is the time limit to file a GST refund claim?

GST refund claims must be filed within 2 years from the relevant date of the transaction triggering the refund.

What is Form GST RFD-01?

Form RFD-01 is the official form used to file a GST refund claim on the GST portal. It must be submitted along with supporting documentation.

How long does it take to receive a GST refund?

Typically, GST refunds are processed within 30 to 45 days of application. In case of delays beyond 60 days, the applicant is entitled to interest on the refund.

Can a refund be claimed for input tax credit under the inverted duty structure?

Yes, if the tax rate on inputs is higher than on outputs, resulting in an accumulation of ITC, a refund can be claimed for the unutilized credit.

Can unregistered persons claim GST refunds?

Yes, under specific circumstances such as cancellation or termination of contracts, unregistered persons can claim refunds by submitting the required documents under Notification 26/2022.

What documents are needed to file a GST refund?

Key documents include export invoices, BRC/FIRC, GSTR-1, GSTR-3B, supporting contracts, cancellation letters, and in some cases, a Chartered Accountant’s certificate.

How can I track the status of my GST refund application?

Refund status can be tracked on the GST portal through post-login or pre-login options using the Application Reference Number (ARN).

Is it possible to file a single refund claim for multiple tax periods?

Yes, a single refund application for multiple tax periods within the same financial year can be submitted in Form RFD-01.

What happens if there’s a mismatch between GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B?

Any mismatch may delay the refund process. It’s important that GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B are correctly and consistently filled before claiming a refund.

Will interest be paid on delayed GST refunds?

Yes, if the refund is not processed within 60 days, interest is payable by the government to the taxpayer.

IndiaFilings provides end-to-end assistance — from checking eligibility, documentation, and form filing to department follow-ups and tracking — ensuring a hassle-free refund experience.

- Refund must be filed within **two years** from the relevant date
- Doctrine of unjust enrichment applies to most refund categories
- Refunds below ₹1,000 are not processed under GST rules
- Proper reconciliation of GSTR-1, GSTR-3B is mandatory before claiming

all_sections.heading: GST Refund Eligibility Criteria for Taxpayers in India
all_sections.content: Understanding who qualifies for a **GST refund claim process** is essential before initiating an application. The GST law specifies distinct categories of taxpayers and situations that make a business eligible for refund claims in India.

all_sections.heading: Who Can Claim a GST Refund?
all_sections.content:
- **Exporters of goods or services** — IGST paid on exports or accumulated ITC
- **SEZ units and SEZ developers** — receiving zero-rated supplies
- Businesses with **inverted duty structure** — where input tax rate exceeds output tax rate
- Taxpayers who made **excess GST payment** due to clerical errors
- Suppliers of **deemed exports** as notified by the government
- Businesses receiving **refund of pre-deposit** during appeals
- UN bodies, embassies and other [GST registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-registration) exempt entities

Every category has specific documentation and procedural requirements that must be fulfilled to successfully process the **online GST refund India** application.

all_sections.heading: Key Categories of GST Refunds Under Indian Tax Law
all_sections.content: Indian GST law recognises multiple types of refunds depending on the nature of the taxpayer's business and the reason for excess tax payment. Each category follows a distinct process and timeline under the **GST refund claim** framework.

all_sections.heading: Types of GST Refunds Available
all_sections.content:
| Refund Type | Applicable To | Form Used |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Export of Goods with Payment of Tax | Exporters paying IGST | RFD-01 |
| Export of Goods without Payment of Tax | Exporters using LUT/Bond | RFD-01 |
| Inverted Duty Structure | Manufacturers, traders | RFD-01 |
| Excess Cash Ledger Balance | All registered taxpayers | RFD-01 |
| Refund on Deemed Exports | Suppliers to EOU/AA holders | RFD-01 |
| IGST Paid on Imports | Importers of goods/services | RFD-01 |
| SEZ Supplies | SEZ units and developers | RFD-01 |

Identifying the correct refund category is critical for accurate filing of your **GST refund application process** and avoiding rejection by the tax authorities.

all_sections.heading: How Does the GST Refund Claim Process Work Online in India?
all_sections.content: The **GST refund for export of goods** and other categories follows a structured online process through the GST portal. Filing a refund application online ensures transparency, faster processing, and real-time tracking of your claim status.

all_sections.heading: Step-by-Step GST Refund Filing Process
all_sections.content:
1. **Login** to the GST portal at gstin.gov.in using your credentials
2. Navigate to **Services > Refunds > Application for Refund**
3. Select the appropriate **refund category** from the dropdown menu
4. Fill in **Form RFD-01** with relevant tax period and refund amount details
5. Upload all **supporting documents** as per the refund category
6. Submit the application using **DSC or EVC** for verification
7. Receive the **ARN (Application Reference Number)** for tracking
8. Tax officer issues **acknowledgement in Form RFD-02** within 15 days
9. Refund sanctioned via **Form RFD-06** and credited to bank account

You can track your **GST refund status check** at any time using the ARN on the GST portal. For a detailed walkthrough, refer to our [step-by-step guide to claim your GST refund](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-refund/stepbystep-guide-to-claim-your-gst-refund).

all_sections.heading: What Documents Do You Need for GST Refund Filing in India?
all_sections.content: Accurate documentation plays a vital role in the successful processing of your **GST refund documents required** application. Incomplete or incorrect documents are among the leading causes of refund rejections in India.

all_sections.heading: Common Documents Required
all_sections.content:
- Copy of **GST registration certificate**
- Statement of invoices — **Statement 3 or Statement 5B** as applicable
- Bank realisation certificates (BRC/FIRC) for **export of services**
- Shipping bills and export invoices for **GST refund for exporters**
- Copy of **LUT or Bond** for exports without payment of tax
- Declaration regarding **unjust enrichment** (where applicable)
- Undertaking in **Form RFD-01A** if applicable
- Bank account details with cancelled cheque
- GSTR-2A reconciliation statement for **input tax credit refund**

Ensuring all documents are in order before filing prevents delays and queries from the [GST notice](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-notice) authorities during scrutiny.

all_sections.heading: Can You File GST Refund Claims Manually in India?
all_sections.content: With the complete digitisation of GST processes, manual filing of refund applications has been largely discontinued. The GST Council has mandated that all **GST refund RFD-01 filing** must be done online through the official GST portal.

all_sections.heading: Manual vs Online GST Refund Filing
all_sections.content:
| Parameter | Manual Filing | Online Filing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mode | Physical submission | GST Portal (gstin.gov.in) |
| Processing Time | Longer, paper-dependent | Faster, real-time tracking |
| Availability | Largely discontinued | Fully available |
| Document Submission | Physical copies | Digital uploads |
| Status Tracking | Not available | Real-time ARN tracking |
| Error Correction | Difficult | Easy through portal |

Online filing through the GST portal is now the standard and mandatory mode for all **GST refund claim process** submissions across India. Refer to our [GST return filing](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-return-filing) page to understand how returns and refunds are interlinked.

all_sections.heading: What is the Time Limit for Claiming a GST Refund in India?
all_sections.content:
The **GST refund time limit** is a critical compliance factor that every registered taxpayer must be aware of. Missing the prescribed deadline results in forfeiture of the refund claim and cannot be revived under normal circumstances.

- The standard time limit is **2 years from the relevant date**
- For export of goods — relevant date is the date of shipment
- For export of services — relevant date is the date of receipt of payment in foreign currency
- For excess payment — relevant date is the date of payment of tax
- For inverted duty structure — relevant date is the end of the financial year in which the claim arises

Filing within the **GST refund processing time** window ensures your claim remains valid and is processed without complications.

all_sections.heading: When is the Right Time to Claim a GST Refund in India?
all_sections.content: Knowing **when can the GST refund be claimed** is as important as knowing how to file. Businesses should not wait until the deadline approaches — proactive filing ensures faster refunds and better cash flow management.

all_sections.heading: Ideal Scenarios to Initiate GST Refund Claims
all_sections.content:
- Immediately after completing **export shipments** with IGST payment
- At the end of each quarter if you have **accumulated excess ITC**
- After receiving the **appeal order** for pre-deposit refunds
- Upon identifying **excess cash balance** in the electronic cash ledger
- After filing **GSTR-3B and GSTR-1** for the relevant tax period

Timely filing using the **GST refund tracking India** system ensures you can monitor the progress and respond to any queries raised by the tax officer promptly. Check your compliance status through [GST annual return](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-annual-return) filings before initiating your refund claim.

all_sections.heading: What Are the Common Errors in GST Refund Filing in India?
all_sections.content: Even experienced businesses make mistakes during **GST refund application** filing, which leads to rejection or delay. Being aware of these pitfalls helps ensure a smooth and successful refund process.

all_sections.heading: Frequent Mistakes to Avoid
all_sections.content:
- Selecting the **wrong refund category** in Form RFD-01
- Mismatch between **GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B** figures for export invoices
- Missing or incorrect **bank account details** in the application
- Not attaching the **unjust enrichment declaration** where required
- Claiming refund on **blocked input tax credit** under Section 17(5)
- Filing refund without completing the **GSTR-3B reconciliation**
- Exceeding the **two-year time limit** without applying in time

Using [GST software](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-software) helps automate reconciliation and reduces errors in refund applications significantly.

all_sections.heading: How is the GST Rate Calculated for Refund Claims in India?
all_sections.content: Understanding how the **GST refund inverted duty** calculation works is essential for businesses filing under the inverted duty structure category. The formula determines the maximum refund amount a taxpayer can claim in any given tax period.

all_sections.heading: GST Refund Calculation Formula
all_sections.content:
| Parameter | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Maximum Refund Amount | \[(Turnover of Inverted Rated Supply of Goods/Services) × Net ITC ÷ Adjusted Total Turnover\] − Tax Payable on Inverted Rated Supply |
| Net ITC | ITC availed on inputs during the tax period (excluding capital goods and input services) |
| Adjusted Total Turnover | Total turnover in the state during the tax period excluding exempted supplies |

The **GST refund for excess input tax credit India** is calculated based on the above formula as per Rule 89(5) of the CGST Rules. Accurate calculation ensures you claim the correct refund amount and avoid future discrepancies. Learn more about your overall [GST](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst) obligations and how refunds fit into your compliance framework.

Frequently asked questions
all_sections.content:
Common questions aboutGST Refund Online Claim Process in India for Businesses.

What is a GST refund?

A GST refund is the process through which taxpayers can claim back excess GST paid to the government, arising due to exports, input tax accumulation, mistaken tax payments, or other eligible scenarios.

Who is eligible to claim a GST refund?

Exporters, SEZ units/developers, businesses with excess Input Tax Credit (ITC), UN agencies, embassies, unregistered persons in specific cases, and taxpayers who overpaid GST can claim a refund.

What are zero-rated supplies in the context of GST?

Zero-rated supplies refer to the export of goods and services and supplies to SEZ units/developers, where the tax rate is 0%, but input tax credit can be claimed.

What is the time limit to file a GST refund claim?

GST refund claims must be filed within 2 years from the relevant date of the transaction triggering the refund.

What is Form GST RFD-01?

Form RFD-01 is the official form used to file a GST refund claim on the GST portal. It must be submitted along with supporting documentation.

How long does it take to receive a GST refund?

Typically, GST refunds are processed within 30 to 45 days of application. In case of delays beyond 60 days, the applicant is entitled to interest on the refund.

Can a refund be claimed for input tax credit under the inverted duty structure?

Yes, if the tax rate on inputs is higher than on outputs, resulting in an accumulation of ITC, a refund can be claimed for the unutilized credit.

Can unregistered persons claim GST refunds?

Yes, under specific circumstances such as cancellation or termination of contracts, unregistered persons can claim refunds by submitting the required documents under Notification 26/2022.

What documents are needed to file a GST refund?

Key documents include export invoices, BRC/FIRC, GSTR-1, GSTR-3B, supporting contracts, cancellation letters, and in some cases, a Chartered Accountant’s certificate.

How can I track the status of my GST refund application?

Refund status can be tracked on the GST portal through post-login or pre-login options using the Application Reference Number (ARN).

Is it possible to file a single refund claim for multiple tax periods?

Yes, a single refund application for multiple tax periods within the same financial year can be submitted in Form RFD-01.

What happens if there’s a mismatch between GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B?

Any mismatch may delay the refund process. It’s important that GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B are correctly and consistently filled before claiming a refund.

Will interest be paid on delayed GST refunds?

Yes, if the refund is not processed within 60 days, interest is payable by the government to the taxpayer.

IndiaFilings provides end-to-end assistance — from checking eligibility, documentation, and form filing to department follow-ups and tracking — ensuring a hassle-free refund experience.

## GST Revocation in India

GST Revocation allows taxpayers to restore a cancelled GST number. If your GST was cancelled due to non-filing, errors, or notices, apply for revocation online and restart your business legally.

## Apply for GST Revocation Online

Get your cancelled GST registration restored with our expert GST revocation service. We prepare and file your GST Revocation Application (FORM GST REG-21) and ensure quick compliance.

- Review of Cancellation Order
- Drafting Revocation Application
- Filing on GST Portal
- Follow-up & Approval Support

# GST Registration Revocation Online in India

**GST registration revocation in India** allows businesses whose GST registration has been cancelled to restore it. Whether cancelled voluntarily or by a tax officer, the revocation process helps taxpayers resume their business operations legally under the **GST portal revocation** mechanism governed by Section 30 of the CGST Act.

If your GST registration has been cancelled, you can apply for [GST Registration revocation online](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/revocation-of-gst-registration-cancellation) through the official GST portal to restore your GSTIN and continue your business activities without interruption.

## What is GST Registration Revocation?

**Revocation of GST registration** is the process of withdrawing or reversing a GST cancellation order. When a taxpayer's GST registration is cancelled — either by the officer or voluntarily — revocation allows the taxpayer to apply for reinstatement of their GSTIN. This is governed under **Section 30 of the CGST Act, 2017**.

The **GST cancellation revocation** process is initiated by filing an application on the [GST](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst) portal within the prescribed time limit. Once approved by the tax officer, the registration is restored, and the taxpayer can resume filing returns and conducting business transactions legally. Learn more about the complete revocation of GST registration cancellation process in detail.

## What are the Key Aspects of GST Revocation?

Understanding the key aspects of **GST registration reactivation** is essential before filing an application. Here are the critical highlights:

- **Legal Provision:** Section 30 of the CGST Act, 2017 governs the **revocation of GST registration** process.
- **Applicable Cases:** Revocation applies only when the cancellation is initiated by a tax officer ( **suo moto GST cancellation revocation**). Voluntary cancellations cannot be revoked.
- **Form Required:** Application must be filed in **Form GST REG-21** on the GST portal.
- **Pending Returns:** All pending GST returns must be filed before applying for revocation.
- **Officer Review:** The tax officer reviews the application and may issue a notice in **Form GST REG-23** if clarification is needed.
- **Approval or Rejection:** The officer issues an order in **Form GST REG-22** (approval) or **Form GST REG-05** (rejection).
- **Time Limit:** The application must be submitted within 90 days (extendable) from the date of the cancellation order.
- **Expert Assistance:** Consult our [GST revocation experts](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-revocation/experts) to ensure your application is filed accurately and without delays.

## Why is GST Registration Cancelled?

A [cancellation of GST registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst/cancellation-of-gst-registration) order can be issued for various reasons. Understanding why a registration gets cancelled helps businesses take preventive measures and act quickly for **GST cancellation revocation**.

| Reason for Cancellation | Type | Revocation Possible? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Business discontinued | Voluntary | No |
| Non-filing of GST returns | Suo Moto (Officer) | Yes |
| Fraud or misrepresentation | Officer-initiated | Yes (with justification) |
| Violation of GST provisions | Officer-initiated | Yes |
| Turnover below threshold | Voluntary | No |
| Business transferred or merged | Voluntary | No |

## Who Can Apply for Revocation of GST Registration Cancellation?

Not every taxpayer is eligible for **GST number reactivation India**. The following eligibility criteria must be met to apply for **GST registration cancellation reversal**:

- The [GST registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-registration) must have been cancelled by a **tax officer** (suo moto cancellation) and not voluntarily by the taxpayer.
- The taxpayer must not have an existing valid GST registration for the same business.
- All pending [GST return filing](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-return-filing) obligations must be completed along with payment of applicable taxes, interest, and penalties.
- The application must be filed within the prescribed **GST revocation time limit** from the date of the cancellation order.
- Taxpayers whose registration was cancelled for fraud or willful misstatement must provide adequate justification.

## What are the Documents Required for GST Revocation?

Before filing the **GST revocation application**, ensure you have the following documents ready. Proper documentation ensures faster approval of your **revocation of cancelled GST** application:

- Copy of the GST Cancellation Order
- Reason for revocation (written explanation/justification letter)
- Proof of filing all pending [GST annual returns](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-annual-return) and regular returns
- Proof of payment of pending taxes, interest, and late fees
- Business registration proof (if applicable)
- [PAN card](https://www.indiafilings.com/pan-card) of the business/proprietor
- [Aadhaar card](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/eaadhaar-download) of the authorized signatory
- Bank account details and cancelled cheque
- Any additional documents requested by the GST officer via **[Form GST REG-23](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/revocation-of-gst-registration-cancellation)**

## What is the Time Limit for GST Revocation Application?

The **GST revocation time limit** is a critical factor in determining your eligibility to file the revocation application. Under the CGST Act and subsequent amendments and amnesty schemes, the time limits are as follows:

### GST Revocation After 180 Days

As per the original provision under **Section 30 of the CGST Act**, a taxpayer applying for **GST registration revocation after 180 days** must obtain approval from an Additional or Joint Commissioner. The standard 90-day limit can be extended by the officer up to 180 days if sufficient cause is shown. During this period, all pending returns and dues must be cleared. For a simplified walkthrough, refer to the [GST revocation online simplified guide](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-revocation/gst-revocation-online-simplified-guide).

### GST Revocation After 270 Days

For **GST revocation after 270 days**, the application requires approval from a Commissioner-level officer. The taxpayer must provide a valid justification for the delay. This extended period for **how to revoke cancelled GST registration after 270 days** was introduced to give taxpayers additional time under special circumstances. Filing all pending [GST LUT](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-lut) and regular returns along with clearing all dues is mandatory before the application is accepted.

### GST Revocation After 2 Years

The GST amnesty scheme for revocation of cancelled registrations was a one-time relief introduced to help taxpayers restore registrations cancelled on or before 31st December 2022. It allowed filing of pending returns and payment of dues to obtain revocation, with applications permitted only up to the 2023 deadline. As of 2026, this scheme is no longer in force and cannot be used for revocation. Taxpayers must now follow Section 30 of the CGST Act where applicable, or seek relief through GST Appellate Tribunal, High Court, or apply for fresh registration.

## How to Apply for Revocation of GST Registration – Step by Step?

Here is the complete **GST registration revocation process step by step** to help you **reinstate GST registration** online through the GST portal:

1. **Step 1 – Login to GST Portal:** Visit www.gst.gov.in and log in using your GSTIN credentials.
2. **Step 2 – Navigate to Services:** Go to _Services > Registration > Application for Revocation of Cancelled Registration_.
3. **Step 3 – Fill Form GST REG-21:** Fill in the **GST revocation form REG-21** with all required details including the reason for revocation.
4. **Step 4 – File Pending Returns:** Ensure all pending **GST cancellation and revocation** related return obligations are completed before submitting the application.
5. **Step 5 – Upload Documents:** Attach all required supporting documents including the cancellation order, proof of return filing, and tax payment receipts.
6. **Step 6 – Submit Application:** Submit the application using DSC (Digital Signature Certificate) or EVC (Electronic Verification Code).
7. **Step 7 – ARN Generation:** Upon successful submission, an **Application Reference Number (ARN)** is generated for tracking the **GST revocation application status**.
8. **Step 8 – Officer Review:** The GST officer reviews the application. If clarification is needed, a notice is issued via **Form GST REG-23**. Respond within 7 working days.
9. **Step 9 – Approval/Rejection:** The officer issues an order within 30 days. If approved, the **GSTIN reactivation** is confirmed via **Form GST REG-22**. If rejected, the order is issued in **Form GST REG-05**.

## What Happens After GST Revocation is Approved or Rejected?

Once your **GST revocation online process** is completed, here is what you can expect:

### If GST Revocation is Approved:

- Your GSTIN is reactivated and restored to active status on the [GST search](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-search) portal.
- You can resume issuing [GST e-invoices](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-einvoice) and collecting GST from customers.
- You must file all pending returns from the date of cancellation to the date of revocation.
- [Input Tax Credit](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/input-tax-credit) (ITC) restoration may be applicable subject to conditions.
- You can also apply for a [GST refund](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-refund) for any excess tax paid during the cancellation period, if applicable.
- Read our customer [GST revocation reviews](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-revocation/reviews) to understand how businesses successfully restored their GSTIN with IndiaFilings.

### If GST Revocation is Rejected:

- You will receive a rejection order in **Form GST REG-05**.
- You can file an appeal with the Appellate Authority under **Section 107 of the CGST Act** against the [GST notice](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-notice) or rejection order.
- If the appeal is also rejected, you may approach the GST Tribunal or High Court.
- Alternatively, you may apply for a fresh [GST registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-registration-for-foreigners) or domestic businesses if eligible.

## Why Choose IndiaFilings for GST Registration Revocation in India?

IndiaFilings simplifies the **GST registration revocation in India** process for businesses across the country. With expert guidance, end-to-end application support, and thorough knowledge of [GST amendments](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-amendment) and compliance requirements.

IndiaFilings ensures your **revocation of GST registration** is handled accurately and efficiently, helping you restore your GSTIN without unnecessary delays or errors.

## Frequently asked questions

Common questions aboutGST Registration Revocation.

What is GST revocation?

GST revocation refers to the process of canceling or revoking the registration of a taxpayer under the Goods and Services Tax regime.

Why would my GST registration be revoked?

Your GST registration can be revoked if you violate any provisions of the GST Act, fail to file returns for a specific period, or engage in fraudulent activities

How can I request the revocation of my GST registration?

You can submit an application for revocation of GST registration through the GST portal.

What documents are required for GST revocation?

The specific documents required may vary based on your circumstances, but generally, you would need to provide a revocation application, along with supporting documents such as financial statements, bank statements, and compliance-related documents

Is there a time limit for applying for GST revocation?

Yes, you must apply for GST revocation within thirty days from the date of GST Registration cancellation

Can I voluntarily apply for GST revocation?

Yes, you can voluntarily apply for GST revocation if you believe you no longer meet the requirements for GST registration or wish to cease your business activities.

How long does the GST revocation process take?

The time taken for GST revocation can vary, but generally, it takes around 15-30 days from the date of application submission

Will I be liable for any penalties if my GST registration is revoked?

If your GST registration is revoked, you may be liable for penalties for any non-compliance or violations committed during the period of your registration.

Can I reapply for GST registration after revocation?

Yes, you can reapply for GST registration after the revocation of your previous registration.

Can GST revocation be done on a retrospective basis?

No, GST revocation is not allowed retrospectively. It can only be applied for from the date of cancellation or a future date.

What happens to my Input Tax Credit (ITC) if my GST registration is revoked?

If your GST registration is revoked, you may lose the unutilized Input Tax Credit available in your account

Will I have to pay any tax dues before applying for GST revocation?

Yes, you must clear all outstanding tax dues and file any pending returns before applying for GST revocation

Can I appeal against the revocation of my GST registration?

Yes, you can file an appeal against the revocation of your GST registration within the prescribed time limit.

What is the effect of GST revocation on my business operations?

Once your GST registration is revoked, you cannot collect GST from customers or claim ITC. It may affect your ability to conduct certain business transactions.

How do I restore my cancelled GST registration after 1 year?

IF your GST registration has been canceled for more than one year, you cannot restore the canceled registration. In such cases, you would need to apply for a new GST registration by following the regular registration process.

What is the Time Limit for Revocation of Cancelled GST Registration?

The time limit for revocation of cancelled GST registration in India depends on who initiated the cancellation. If taxpayers voluntarily cancel their registration, they have 30 days from the cancellation event to apply for revocation. For cancellations initiated by the tax authorities, they have 30 days to issue a revocation order after starting proceedings.

Frequently asked questions
all_sections.content:
Common questions aboutGST Registration Revocation.

What is GST revocation?

GST revocation refers to the process of canceling or revoking the registration of a taxpayer under the Goods and Services Tax regime.

Why would my GST registration be revoked?

Your GST registration can be revoked if you violate any provisions of the GST Act, fail to file returns for a specific period, or engage in fraudulent activities

How can I request the revocation of my GST registration?

You can submit an application for revocation of GST registration through the GST portal.

What documents are required for GST revocation?

The specific documents required may vary based on your circumstances, but generally, you would need to provide a revocation application, along with supporting documents such as financial statements, bank statements, and compliance-related documents

Is there a time limit for applying for GST revocation?

Yes, you must apply for GST revocation within thirty days from the date of GST Registration cancellation

Can I voluntarily apply for GST revocation?

Yes, you can voluntarily apply for GST revocation if you believe you no longer meet the requirements for GST registration or wish to cease your business activities.

How long does the GST revocation process take?

The time taken for GST revocation can vary, but generally, it takes around 15-30 days from the date of application submission

Will I be liable for any penalties if my GST registration is revoked?

If your GST registration is revoked, you may be liable for penalties for any non-compliance or violations committed during the period of your registration.

Can I reapply for GST registration after revocation?

Yes, you can reapply for GST registration after the revocation of your previous registration.

Can GST revocation be done on a retrospective basis?

No, GST revocation is not allowed retrospectively. It can only be applied for from the date of cancellation or a future date.

What happens to my Input Tax Credit (ITC) if my GST registration is revoked?

If your GST registration is revoked, you may lose the unutilized Input Tax Credit available in your account

Will I have to pay any tax dues before applying for GST revocation?

Yes, you must clear all outstanding tax dues and file any pending returns before applying for GST revocation

Can I appeal against the revocation of my GST registration?

Yes, you can file an appeal against the revocation of your GST registration within the prescribed time limit.

What is the effect of GST revocation on my business operations?

Once your GST registration is revoked, you cannot collect GST from customers or claim ITC. It may affect your ability to conduct certain business transactions.

How do I restore my cancelled GST registration after 1 year?

IF your GST registration has been canceled for more than one year, you cannot restore the canceled registration. In such cases, you would need to apply for a new GST registration by following the regular registration process.

What is the Time Limit for Revocation of Cancelled GST Registration?

The time limit for revocation of cancelled GST registration in India depends on who initiated the cancellation. If taxpayers voluntarily cancel their registration, they have 30 days from the cancellation event to apply for revocation. For cancellations initiated by the tax authorities, they have 30 days to issue a revocation order after starting proceedings.

# GSTR-10 Final Return Online Filing in India

**GSTR-10 Final Return online in India** is a mandatory return that must be filed by every taxpayer whose GST registration has been cancelled or surrendered. Also known as the **GST final return**, it is a one-time filing obligation under the GST law that ensures all pending tax liabilities and input tax credits are settled before the registration is officially closed.

If your GST registration has been cancelled, you must file [GSTR-10](https://www.indiafilings.com/gstr-10) within the prescribed due date on the official GST portal to avoid heavy late fees and penalties.

## What is GSTR-10 Final Return?

**GSTR-10** is the **final return under GST** that a registered taxpayer must file after their GST registration is cancelled or surrendered. It is a statement of stocks held on the date immediately preceding the date from which cancellation is effective. The purpose of **GSTR-10 filing online** is to ensure that the taxpayer reverses any Input Tax Credit (ITC) availed on the closing stock and settles all outstanding [tax](https://www.indiafilings.com/income-tax) liabilities before their **GST registration cancellation return** is completed.

Unlike regular returns, GSTR-10 is a **one-time filing** triggered by the cancellation or surrender of GST registration. It is filed on the [GST registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-registration) portal under the returns section.

## What are the Key Aspects of GSTR-10?

Understanding the key aspects of **GSTR-10 final return** is essential before filing. Here are the critical highlights every taxpayer must know:

- **Legal Provision:** GSTR-10 is governed under **Section 45 of the CGST Act, 2017** and Rule 81 of the CGST Rules.
- **One-Time Filing:** It is a one-time return, not a periodic filing obligation. It is triggered only when GST registration is cancelled or surrendered.
- **Closing Stock Details:** The taxpayer must declare **GSTR-10 closing stock** held on the effective date of cancellation.
- **ITC Reversal:** **GSTR-10 ITC reversal** is mandatory for inputs held in stock, semi-finished goods, finished goods, and capital goods.
- **Tax Payment:** The taxpayer must pay the higher of the ITC reversed or the tax on the market value of the closing stock.
- **Due Date:** GSTR-10 must be filed within **3 months** from the date of cancellation order or date of cancellation, whichever is later.
- **Late Fee:** A late fee of **₹200 per day** (₹100 CGST + ₹100 SGST) is applicable for delayed filing.
- **Form Used:** The return is filed in **GSTR-10 form** on the official GST portal.

## Who is Required to File GSTR-10 Final Return?

Not all GST taxpayers are required to file **GSTR-10 return filing India**. Here is a clear breakdown of who must file and who is exempt:

| Category | Required to File GSTR-10? |
| --- | --- |
| Regular taxpayers whose registration is cancelled by officer | ✅ Yes |
| Taxpayers who voluntarily surrender GST registration | ✅ Yes |
| Input Service Distributors (ISD) | ❌ No |
| Non-resident taxable persons | ❌ No |
| Composition scheme taxpayers | ❌ No |
| Persons liable to deduct TDS under Section 51 | ❌ No |
| Persons liable to collect TCS under Section 52 | ❌ No |

## What is the Due Date for Filing GSTR-10?

The **GSTR-10 due date** is a critical compliance deadline. As per the CGST Act, the **GSTR-10 filing last date** is within **3 months** from the date of the cancellation order or the date of cancellation, whichever is later. Taxpayers must file the return within this period to avoid accumulation of **GSTR-10 late fees**.

Under the **GSTR-10 amnesty scheme** announced by the government, taxpayers who missed the original due date were given a special window to file their pending GSTR-10 returns with a **GSTR-10 waiver of late fee**, capping the fee at ₹1,000 (₹500 CGST + ₹500 SGST). Taxpayers must use [GST software](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-software) to track their due dates and ensure timely compliance.

## What are the Documents Required for GSTR-10 Filing?

Before initiating the **GSTR-10 filing procedure**, ensure you have the following documents ready for a smooth and accurate submission:

- GST Registration Cancellation Order copy
- Details of **GSTR-10 stock details** — closing stock as on the effective date of cancellation
- Details of inputs held in stock, semi-finished goods, finished goods, and capital goods
- ITC availed on closing stock details for **GSTR-10 ITC reversal**
- Previous GST returns filed — [GST annual return](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-annual-return) and regular returns
- Tax payment challans for any pending tax dues
- Bank account details linked to the GST registration
- [PAN card](https://www.indiafilings.com/pan-card) and [Aadhaar card](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/eaadhaar-download) of the authorized signatory
- [Digital Signature Certificate](https://www.indiafilings.com/digital-signature) (DSC) or [EVC](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/what-is-evc-in-income-tax-return) credentials for submission

## How to File GSTR-10 Final Return Online – Step-by-Step?

What is the deadline for getting registered under GST?

An entity liable to be registered under GST should apply for registration within 30 days of meeting the criteria. Casual taxable persons and non-resident taxable persons are required to be registered under GST prior to commencing business.

Who is the primary authorized signatory?

The primary authorized signatory is the person who is primarily responsible to undertake tasks on the GST portal on behalf of the taxpayer. It could be the promotion of the business or any other trustworthy person nominated by the promoters of the business.

Is PAN mandatory for obtaining GST registration?

Yes. PAN is mandatory for obtaining GST registration. In the case of proprietorship, the PAN of the proprietor can be used. In the case of LLP or Company or Trust or other types of a legal entity, PAN must first be obtained for the entity. However, PAN is not mandatory for the GST registration of foreigners and foreign companies. For non-resident taxable persons, GSTIN with a fixed expiry date will be provided based on the other documents provided to prove existence.

What is the validity of GST registration?

GST registration does not have an expiry date. Hence, it will be valid until it’s cancelled, surrendered or suspended.Only GST registration for non-resident taxable persons and casual taxable persons have a validity period that is fixed by the authorities while issuing the GST registration certificate.

Can a person with no GST registration collect GST?

No, only persons registered under GST are allowed to collect GST from the customers. A person not registered under GST cannot even claim the input tax credit on the GST paid.

What is GSTR-10?

GSTR-10 is a final return required to be filed by taxpayers who have opted for cancellation or whose registration has been cancelled, surrendered or has lapsed.

How does GSTR-10 work?

GSTR-10 works by allowing taxpayers to declare their total tax liability during the period of registration and submit their returns accordingly.

Who needs to file GSTR-10?

Taxpayers who have opted for cancellation or whose registration has been cancelled, surrendered or has lapsed need to file GSTR-10.

When is the due date for GSTR-10?

The due date for GSTR-10 is 30 days from the date of cancellation/surrender of registration.

What information is required to file GSTR-10?

The information required to file GSTR-10 includes details such as the taxpayer’s GSTIN, date of cancellation/surrender of registration and total tax liability during the period of registration.

Is GSTR-10 available online?

Yes, GSTR-10 is available online through the Goods and Services Tax Network (GSTN) portal. IndiaFilings can help you file GSTR-10 quickly and easily,

How can I file GSTR-10?

GSTR-10 can be filed online through the GSTN portal.

Can I make corrections to GSTR-10 after filing?

Yes, corrections can be made to GSTR-10 after filing.

Is there a penalty for late filing of GSTR-10?

Yes, there is a penalty for late filing of GSTR-10. You will be charged Rs. 100 CGST and Rs. 100 SGST per day.

Does the GSTR-10 return need to be filed every year?

Only those whose GST registration has been cancelled or surrendered are needed to file GSTR 10 and it is a one-time process.

How do I check the status of my GSTR-10 filing?

You can check the status of your GSTR-10 filing by logging into your GST portal account and navigating to the Returns tab. Select View Returns/Payments and search for GSTR-10. You can view the status of your filing from the search results.

Are there any exemptions from filing GSTR-10?

Yes, certain businesses are exempt from filing GSTR-10. For example, businesses registered under the Composition Scheme, Input Service Distributors and Non-resident taxable persons are exempt from filing GSTR-10.

What documents should I keep for GSTR-10 filing?

The documents you should keep for GSTR-10 filing include GST Invoices, GST returns, GST challans, GST credit ledger and GST debit ledger.

How do I access the GSTR-10 portal?

You can access the GSTR-10 portal by logging into your GST portal account. The GSTR-10 portal can be found under the Returns tab.

What is the difference between GSTR-10 and GSTR-9?

GSTR-10 is a Final Return which needs to be filed by a registered person to report the details of GST taxes paid, input tax credit availed, and other details. GSTR-9 is an Annual Return which needs to be filed by a registered person to report the details of GST taxes paid and input tax credit availed during the financial year.

What is GSTR 10?

GSTR 10 return is mandated by the Goods and Services Tax (GST) in India. It's a final return filed by registered taxable persons whose GST registration gets cancelled or surrendered. It essentially acts as a statement of the taxpayer's stock holdings on the day before the cancellation becomes effective.
