# Company Annual Filing India- MCA Compliance

[IndiaFilings](https://www.indiafilings.com/) provides expert assistance for **Company Annual Filing** in India, ensuring every registered company meets its statutory obligations under the **Companies Act, 2013**. Every company registered in India must complete annual compliance filings with the **Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA)** to maintain active status and avoid heavy penalties.

## What is Company Annual Filing?

**Company Annual Filing** is the process of submitting mandatory statutory documents and financial statements to the **Registrar of Companies (ROC)** through the **MCA21 portal** every financial year. It is a critical **ROC compliance** requirement under the **Companies Act, 2013** for all registered companies in India, including [Private Limited Companies](https://www.indiafilings.com/company-registration), [Public Limited Companies](https://www.indiafilings.com/public-limited-company), [One Person Companies](https://www.indiafilings.com/one-person-company) (OPC), [Section 8 Companies](https://www.indiafilings.com/section-8-company-registration), and [Indian Subsidiaries](https://www.indiafilings.com/indian-subsidiary).

The **annual ROC filing** process involves filing key forms such as **AOC-4** (financial statements), **MGT-7/MGT-7A** (annual return), **ADT-1** (auditor appointment), and **DIR-3 KYC** (director KYC). Every company must complete these filings within the prescribed due dates to avoid late filing penalties, legal consequences, and risk of company strike-off.

Explore our comprehensive guide on [importance of company compliance for annual filing](https://www.indiafilings.com/company-annual-filing/importance-of-company-compliance-for-annual-filing) to understand why timely **annual company compliance** is critical for every business in India.

## Who is Required to File Company Annual Returns in India?

All companies registered under the **Companies Act, 2013** are mandatorily required to complete their **company annual filing** every financial year, regardless of whether they have commenced business operations or generated revenue. Here is a complete overview of entities required to file **annual ROC filing India**:

| Company Type | Annual Filing Required | Key Forms |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Private Limited Company** | ✅ Mandatory | AOC-4, MGT-7, ADT-1, DIR-3 KYC |
| **Public Limited Company** | ✅ Mandatory | AOC-4, MGT-7, ADT-1, DIR-3 KYC |
| **One Person Company (OPC)** | ✅ Mandatory | AOC-4, MGT-7A, ADT-1, DIR-3 KYC |
| **Section 8 Company** | ✅ Mandatory | AOC-4, MGT-7, ADT-1, DIR-3 KYC |
| **Indian Subsidiary** | ✅ Mandatory | AOC-4, MGT-7, ADT-1, DIR-3 KYC |
| **Nidhi Company** | ✅ Mandatory | AOC-4, MGT-7, NDH-3, DIR-3 KYC |
| **Dormant Company** | ✅ Mandatory | MSC-3 (Annual Return for Dormant Company) |

- Companies that have **not commenced business** but are registered must still file annual returns
- Companies with **zero turnover or NIL transactions** must file annual compliance forms
- Companies under **strike-off proceedings** must clear all pending filings before applying for closure
- **Foreign companies** operating in India must also comply with annual filing requirements
- Companies that have received **deposits from public** must additionally file **DPT-3**

Read our detailed [company compliance guideline for success](https://www.indiafilings.com/company-annual-filing/company-compliance-guideline-for-success) to understand which forms are applicable to your company type.

## What are the Different Types of Company Annual Filing Forms?

The **MCA annual filing** process involves multiple statutory forms, each serving a specific compliance purpose. Here is a detailed overview of all major **annual compliance for pvt ltd company** and other entity types:

### AOC-4 (Financial Statements Filing)

**AOC-4** is the form used for filing a company's **annual financial statements** with the ROC. It includes the Balance Sheet, Profit & Loss Account, Directors' Report, Auditor's Report, and other financial documents. **AOC-4 filing** must be completed within **30 days** from the conclusion of the Annual General Meeting (AGM). For OPCs, the deadline is **180 days** from the close of the financial year. This is one of the most critical **statutory compliance India** requirements for all registered companies.

### MGT-7 / MGT-7A (Annual Return Filing)

**MGT-7** is the annual return form for Private Limited and Public Limited Companies, while **MGT-7A** is a simplified version applicable for **OPC annual filing** and small companies. The **MGT-7 annual return** contains details of shareholders, directors, registered office, share capital, debentures, and other key company information. It must be filed within **60 days** from the conclusion of the AGM. The **company annual return** is a comprehensive document reflecting the company's overall standing during the financial year.

### DIR-3 KYC & ADT-1

**DIR-3 KYC** is the annual KYC form that every director who has been allotted a **Director Identification Number (DIN)** must file every year to keep their DIN active. Failure to file DIR-3 KYC results in DIN deactivation and a penalty of **₹5,000** for reactivation. **ADT-1** is the form for intimating the ROC about the appointment of the company's statutory auditor. It must be filed within **15 days** of the AGM. Additionally, companies that have accepted deposits must file **DPT-3 filing** to report outstanding deposits and loans.

## What are the Key MCA Annual Filing Deadlines for 2026 in India?

Staying updated with **MCA compliance calendar** deadlines is critical for every company to avoid late filing fees and penalties. Here are the key **company annual filing due date** milestones for the financial year 2025-26:

| Form | Purpose | Deadline 2026 | Applicable For |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **ADT-1** | Auditor Appointment | 15 days from AGM (October 15, 2026) | All Companies |
| **AOC-4** | Financial Statements Filing | 30 days from AGM (October 30, 2026) | All Companies (except OPC) |
| **AOC-4 (OPC)** | Financial Statements – OPC | 180 days from FY end (September 27, 2026) | One Person Company |
| **MGT-7** | Annual Return | 60 days from AGM (November 29, 2026) | Private & Public Limited Companies |
| **MGT-7A** | Annual Return – OPC & Small Companies | 60 days from AGM (November 29, 2026) | OPC & Small Companies |
| **DIR-3 KYC** | Director KYC | September 30, 2026 | All Directors with DIN |
| **DPT-3** | Deposits & Loans Return | June 30, 2026 | Companies with outstanding deposits/loans |
| **MSME Form I** | Outstanding dues to MSME suppliers | April 30 & October 31, 2026 | Companies with MSME dues |

Stay updated with the latest compliance requirements through our guide on [CCFS 2026](https://www.indiafilings.com/company-annual-filing/ccfs-2026) and [CCFS 2026 Scheme](https://www.indiafilings.com/company-annual-filing/ccfs-2026-scheme) for special condonation of delay schemes announced by MCA.

## What are the Due Dates for Company Annual Filing in India?

The **company annual filing due date** is calculated based on the date of the Annual General Meeting (AGM). For most companies, the AGM must be held within **6 months** from the end of the financial year (i.e., by September 30, 2026 for FY 2025-26). Here is the complete **annual filing MCA portal** due date summary:

| Company Type | AGM Deadline | AOC-4 Due Date | MGT-7/7A Due Date |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Private Limited Company** | September 30, 2026 | October 30, 2026 | November 29, 2026 |
| **Public Limited Company** | September 30, 2026 | October 30, 2026 | November 29, 2026 |
| **One Person Company (OPC)** | No AGM Required | September 27, 2026 | November 29, 2026 |
| **Section 8 Company** | September 30, 2026 | October 30, 2026 | November 29, 2026 |
| **Small Company** | September 30, 2026 | October 30, 2026 | November 29, 2026 (MGT-7A) |

✅ **Important Note:** The AGM can be held on or before September 30, 2026 for FY 2025-26. All due dates for **AOC-4 filing** and **MGT-7 annual return** are calculated from the date of AGM. Stay compliant with expert help from [MCA Services](https://www.indiafilings.com/mca-services) offered by IndiaFilings.

## What are the Documents Required for Company Annual Filing?

Having the right **company annual filing documents** ready ensures a smooth and error-free submission on the MCA portal. Here is the complete document checklist for **annual compliance for pvt ltd company** and other entity types:

| Document | Purpose | Applicable Form |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Audited Financial Statements** | Balance Sheet, P&L, Cash Flow Statement | AOC-4 |
| **Directors' Report** | Annual report by Board of Directors | AOC-4 |
| **Auditor's Report** | Statutory auditor's opinion on financial statements | AOC-4 |
| **Board Resolution** | Approving financial statements and annual return | AOC-4, MGT-7 |
| **List of Shareholders** | Details of all shareholders as on the date of AGM | MGT-7/MGT-7A |
| **List of Directors** | Details of all directors including DIN, designation | MGT-7/MGT-7A |
| **AGM Notice & Minutes** | Proof of Annual General Meeting conducted | MGT-7, AOC-4 |
| **Auditor Appointment Letter** | Consent letter from appointed auditor | ADT-1 |
| **DIR-3 KYC Documents** | PAN, Aadhaar, mobile, email of directors | DIR-3 KYC |
| **DSC of Directors** | Digital Signature Certificate for form submission | All Forms |

## What is the Procedure for Company Annual Filing?

The **company annual filing process step by step** involves a series of well-defined actions to be completed in sequence. Here is the complete **annual filing MCA portal** procedure for FY 2025-26:

01. **Step 1 – Conduct Board Meeting** – Hold a Board Meeting to approve the draft financial statements, Directors' Report, and fix the date, time, and venue of the Annual General Meeting (AGM).
02. **Step 2 – Get Accounts Audited** – Appoint a statutory auditor (if not already appointed) and get the annual accounts audited. The **auditor report filing** is mandatory for **AOC-4 filing**.
03. **Step 3 – Hold Annual General Meeting (AGM)** – Conduct the AGM within 6 months from the close of FY (by September 30, 2026). At the AGM, approve financial statements, declare dividends (if any), and appoint/reappoint auditors and directors.
04. **Step 4 – File ADT-1 (Auditor Appointment)** – File Form ADT-1 within **15 days** of AGM to intimate the ROC about the auditor appointment for the current financial year.
05. **Step 5 – File AOC-4 (Financial Statements)** – Submit Form AOC-4 with audited financial statements, Directors' Report, and Auditor's Report within **30 days** of AGM on the MCA portal.
06. **Step 6 – File MGT-7/MGT-7A (Annual Return)** – File the annual return in Form MGT-7 (or MGT-7A for OPC/small companies) within **60 days** of AGM with complete details of shareholders, directors, and company structure.
07. **Step 7 – File DIR-3 KYC (Director KYC)** – All directors must file DIR-3 KYC by **September 30, 2026** to keep their DIN active and comply with **statutory compliance India** requirements.
08. **Step 8 – File DPT-3 (if applicable)** – Companies with outstanding deposits or loans must file **DPT-3 filing** by June 30, 2026.
09. **Step 9 – File MSME Form I (if applicable)** – Companies with outstanding dues to MSME suppliers must file MSME Form I by April 30 and October 31, 2026.
10. **Step 10 – Verify Filing Status** – Track all filing statuses on the **MCA21 annual filing** portal and ensure all forms are approved by the ROC without any defects or resubmission notices.

Get expert guidance on [how to ensure company compliance for your business](https://www.indiafilings.com/company-annual-filing/how-to-ensure-company-compliance-for-your-business) with IndiaFilings end-to-end annual filing assistance. Also, stay informed about the latest regulatory updates through our guide on [proposal for amendment in rules](https://www.indiafilings.com/company-annual-filing/proposal-for-ammendement-in-rules) impacting company annual compliance in India.

## What are the Penalties for Non-Compliance in Company Annual Filing?

Failure to complete **ROC annual return** filings within the prescribed due dates attracts significant penalties under the Companies Act, 2013. Here is the complete **company annual filing fees** and penalty structure for late or non-filing:

| Form | Normal Filing Fee | Late Filing Additional Fee | Consequence of Non-Filing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **AOC-4** | ₹200 per day | ₹100 per day after due date | Company strike-off, prosecution of directors |
| **MGT-7/MGT-7A** | ₹200 per day | ₹100 per day after due date | Company strike-off, prosecution of directors |
| **ADT-1** | ₹300 per day | ₹300 per day after due date | Penalty up to ₹5,00,000 |
| **DIR-3 KYC** | NIL (if filed on time) | ₹5,000 one-time fee for reactivation | DIN deactivation |
| **DPT-3** | As applicable | ₹500 per day of default | Penalty up to ₹1,00,00,000 |
| **MSME Form I** | As applicable | ₹200 per day of default | Penalty on company and officers |

✅ **Important Note:** Continued non-filing can lead to the **[company strike-off India](https://www.indiafilings.com/winding-up-of-a-company)** by the ROC under Section 248 of the Companies Act, 2013. Directors of struck-off companies may be disqualified under Section 164(2) from being appointed as director in any other company for 5 years. Stay compliant with company annual filing services from IndiaFilings to avoid these severe consequences.

## What are the Advantages of Company Compliance?

Maintaining timely **annual company compliance** through regular **MCA annual filing** offers numerous strategic and financial benefits for every registered company in India. Here are the key advantages of staying compliant with **company law compliance India** requirements:

- **Avoid Company Strike-Off** – Timely **ROC compliance** prevents the ROC from initiating strike-off proceedings under Section 248 of the Companies Act, 2013.
- **Director DIN Remains Active** – Regular **DIR-3 KYC filing** ensures all directors' DINs remain active, preventing disqualification and legal complications.

## Frequently asked questions

Common questions aboutCompany Annual Filing.

What are the filings for the company?

Company filing refers to submitting various legal forms and documents to the Registrar of Companies (ROC) as required by the Companies Act 2013. Some of the common types of company filings that need to be filed with the MCA are as follows:

- Incorporation Documents
- Annual Returns
- Financial Statements
- Changes in Directors or Shareholders
- Registered Office Change
- Director Identification Number
- Company Filings for Approval
- Charge Management

.

Can I run a small business without registering?

In India, small businesses can be run without formal company registration, though registering a business is generally recommended to access certain benefits and ensure legal compliance. Some common unregistered business structures used by small enterprises are Sole Proprietorship, Partnership Firm, and Hindu Undivided Family (HUF).

How do I legally file a Business?

Starting a business in India requires compliance with various legal requirements, including registering the business, obtaining necessary licenses and permits, and complying with labor and tax laws. Some of the essential legal requirements for starting a business in India include choosing a business structure, registering your business name, obtaining a Director Identification Number (DIN), incorporating the business, obtaining PAN and TAN, securing other required licenses and permits, ensuring labor law compliance, meeting tax compliance requirements, obtaining insurance, and opening a business bank account.

Does the appointment of the statutory auditor fall under annual compliance?

A company can appoint a statutory auditor either for five consecutive years or till the conclusion of the next Annual general meeting. Therefore, an appointment of the statutory auditor cannot be considered as a part of annual compliance.

What are the compliances of a Private Limited Company?

A company is required to maintain the compliances once the company is incorporated. The auditor is to be appointed within 30 days. Additionally, there is income tax filing and annual return filing that is to be done every year.

Is it necessary to conduct AGM?

The annual general meeting (AGM) is held for the management and the shareholders to interact with each other. The Companies Act,2013 makes it compulsory to hold meetings to discuss the yearly results and appoint auditors.

Is it mandatory to get a Private Limited Company audited?

The statutory audit as the name suggests is a mandatory audit for all companies. All the entities that are unregistered under the Companies Act as Private or Public Limited Companies need to get the books of accounts audited every year.

How to file the annual returns of the Company?

The companies incorporated under the Companies Act,1956 are required to file the following documents with the ROC

The balance sheet in form 23AC which is to be filed by all the companies
Profit and loss account in form 23ACA which is to be file by all the companies.

Is audit report mandatory for all the private limited companies?

The Private Limited Companies are required to file the annual accounts and the returns that disclose the details of the shareholder and the directors to the ROC.

When is annual return to be filed after the AGM?

After the AGM all the private limited companies are required to file the annual return within 60 days of holding the annual general meeting.

What is ROC Compliance?

ROC is the officer governed by the MCA that deals with the functioning, the ROC has to ensure that the Private Limited Companies and the LLPs comply with the statutory requirement of the ACT. The registrar of the companies functions as the regulator for the companies registered with them.

Which Form is to be filed for the appointment of the statutory auditor?

Form ADT-1 is filed for appointing or replacing the Statutory Auditor.

Which form is to be attached to the Companies Director Report?

MGT-9 is attached to the company's director report, which is an extract of MGT -7

Are audited Financial statements mandatory while annual filing of the Private Limited Companies?

Audited financial statements are necessary for every company from its incorporation. The company must file the audited statements only.

What is the annual Compliance of the company?

Annual Compliance means a specific set of Compliance that a company has to fulfill post-incorporation to commence and continue its operations. Under the Companies Act 2013, various compliances must be completed every Year.

What is the main purpose of Compliance?

The main purpose of company compliance is to adhere to internal policies and procedures and governmental laws. Implementing compliance procedures protects the company's reputational risk, improves the company's vision and value, and prevents and detects violations of rules.

Learn more about the [main purpose of Compliance](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/what-is-the-main-purpose-of-compliance/)

What are the different types of Compliance?

There are two main types of Compliance; External and Internal. Both types of Compliance involve a framework of regulations, practices, and rules.

Refer to [our article](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/what-are-different-types-of-compliance/) to know more about the different types of Compliance.

process_sections.heading: What is Company Annual Filing?
process_sections.content:
**Company Annual Filing** is the process of submitting mandatory statutory documents and financial statements to the **Registrar of Companies (ROC)** through the **MCA21 portal** every financial year. It is a critical **ROC compliance** requirement under the **Companies Act, 2013** for all registered companies in India, including [Private Limited Companies](https://www.indiafilings.com/company-registration), [Public Limited Companies](https://www.indiafilings.com/public-limited-company), [One Person Companies](https://www.indiafilings.com/one-person-company) (OPC), [Section 8 Companies](https://www.indiafilings.com/section-8-company-registration), and [Indian Subsidiaries](https://www.indiafilings.com/indian-subsidiary).

The **annual ROC filing** process involves filing key forms such as **AOC-4** (financial statements), **MGT-7/MGT-7A** (annual return), **ADT-1** (auditor appointment), and **DIR-3 KYC** (director KYC). Every company must complete these filings within the prescribed due dates to avoid late filing penalties, legal consequences, and risk of company strike-off.

Explore our comprehensive guide on [importance of company compliance for annual filing](https://www.indiafilings.com/company-annual-filing/importance-of-company-compliance-for-annual-filing) to understand why timely **annual company compliance** is critical for every business in India.

process_sections.heading: Who is Required to File Company Annual Returns in India?
process_sections.content:
All companies registered under the **Companies Act, 2013** are mandatorily required to complete their **company annual filing** every financial year, regardless of whether they have commenced business operations or generated revenue. Here is a complete overview of entities required to file **annual ROC filing India**:

| Company Type | Annual Filing Required | Key Forms |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Private Limited Company** | ✅ Mandatory | AOC-4, MGT-7, ADT-1, DIR-3 KYC |
| **Public Limited Company** | ✅ Mandatory | AOC-4, MGT-7, ADT-1, DIR-3 KYC |
| **One Person Company (OPC)** | ✅ Mandatory | AOC-4, MGT-7A, ADT-1, DIR-3 KYC |
| **Section 8 Company** | ✅ Mandatory | AOC-4, MGT-7, ADT-1, DIR-3 KYC |
| **Indian Subsidiary** | ✅ Mandatory | AOC-4, MGT-7, ADT-1, DIR-3 KYC |
| **Nidhi Company** | ✅ Mandatory | AOC-4, MGT-7, NDH-3, DIR-3 KYC |
| **Dormant Company** | ✅ Mandatory | MSC-3 (Annual Return for Dormant Company) |

- Companies that have **not commenced business** but are registered must still file annual returns
- Companies with **zero turnover or NIL transactions** must file annual compliance forms
- Companies under **strike-off proceedings** must clear all pending filings before applying for closure
- **Foreign companies** operating in India must also comply with annual filing requirements
- Companies that have received **deposits from public** must additionally file **DPT-3**

Read our detailed [company compliance guideline for success](https://www.indiafilings.com/company-annual-filing/company-compliance-guideline-for-success) to understand which forms are applicable to your company type.

process_sections.heading: What are the Different Types of Company Annual Filing Forms?
process_sections.content: The **MCA annual filing** process involves multiple statutory forms, each serving a specific compliance purpose. Here is a detailed overview of all major **annual compliance for pvt ltd company** and other entity types:

process_sections.heading: AOC-4 (Financial Statements Filing)
process_sections.content: **AOC-4** is the form used for filing a company's **annual financial statements** with the ROC. It includes the Balance Sheet, Profit & Loss Account, Directors' Report, Auditor's Report, and other financial documents. **AOC-4 filing** must be completed within **30 days** from the conclusion of the Annual General Meeting (AGM). For OPCs, the deadline is **180 days** from the close of the financial year. This is one of the most critical **statutory compliance India** requirements for all registered companies.

process_sections.heading: MGT-7 / MGT-7A (Annual Return Filing)
process_sections.content: **MGT-7** is the annual return form for Private Limited and Public Limited Companies, while **MGT-7A** is a simplified version applicable for **OPC annual filing** and small companies. The **MGT-7 annual return** contains details of shareholders, directors, registered office, share capital, debentures, and other key company information. It must be filed within **60 days** from the conclusion of the AGM. The **company annual return** is a comprehensive document reflecting the company's overall standing during the financial year.

| **AOC-4 (OPC)** | Financial Statements – OPC | 180 days from FY end (September 27, 2026) | One Person Company |
| **MGT-7** | Annual Return | 60 days from AGM (November 29, 2026) | Private & Public Limited Companies |
| **MGT-7A** | Annual Return – OPC & Small Companies | 60 days from AGM (November 29, 2026) | OPC & Small Companies |
| **DIR-3 KYC** | Director KYC | September 30, 2026 | All Directors with DIN |
| **DPT-3** | Deposits & Loans Return | June 30, 2026 | Companies with outstanding deposits/loans |

process_sections.heading: What is the Procedure for Company Annual Filing?
process_sections.content:
The **company annual filing process step by step** involves a series of well-defined actions to be completed in sequence. Here is the complete **annual filing MCA portal** procedure for FY 2025-26:

01. **Step 1 – Conduct Board Meeting** – Hold a Board Meeting to approve the draft financial statements, Directors' Report, and fix the date, time, and venue of the Annual General Meeting (AGM).
02. **Step 2 – Get Accounts Audited** – Appoint a statutory auditor (if not already appointed) and get the annual accounts audited. The **auditor report filing** is mandatory for **AOC-4 filing**.
03. **Step 3 – Hold Annual General Meeting (AGM)** – Conduct the AGM within 6 months from the close of FY (by September 30, 2026). At the AGM, approve financial statements, declare dividends (if any), and appoint/reappoint auditors and directors.
04. **Step 4 – File ADT-1 (Auditor Appointment)** – File Form ADT-1 within **15 days** of AGM to intimate the ROC about the auditor appointment for the current financial year.
05. **Step 5 – File AOC-4 (Financial Statements)** – Submit Form AOC-4 with audited financial statements, Directors' Report, and Auditor's Report within **30 days** of AGM on the MCA portal.
06. **Step 6 – File MGT-7/MGT-7A (Annual Return)** – File the annual return in Form MGT-7 (or MGT-7A for OPC/small companies) within **60 days** of AGM with complete details of shareholders, directors, and company structure.
07. **Step 7 – File DIR-3 KYC (Director KYC)** – All directors must file DIR-3 KYC by **September 30, 2026** to keep their DIN active and comply with **statutory compliance India** requirements.
08. **Step 8 – File DPT-3 (if applicable)** – Companies with outstanding deposits or loans must file **DPT-3 filing** by June 30, 2026.
09. **Step 9 – File MSME Form I (if applicable)** – Companies with outstanding dues to MSME suppliers must file MSME Form I by April 30 and October 31, 2026.
10. **Step 10 – Verify Filing Status** – Track all filing statuses on the **MCA21 annual filing** portal and ensure all forms are approved by the ROC without any defects or resubmission notices.

process_sections.heading: What are the Penalties for Non-Compliance in Company Annual Filing?
process_sections.content:
Failure to complete **ROC annual return** filings within the prescribed due dates attracts significant penalties under the Companies Act, 2013. Here is the complete **company annual filing fees** and penalty structure for late or non-filing:

| Form | Normal Filing Fee | Late Filing Additional Fee | Consequence of Non-Filing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **AOC-4** | ₹200 per day | ₹100 per day after due date | Company strike-off, prosecution of directors |
| **MGT-7/MGT-7A** | ₹200 per day | ₹100 per day after due date | Company strike-off, prosecution of directors |
| **ADT-1** | ₹300 per day | ₹300 per day after due date | Penalty up to ₹5,00,000 |
| **DIR-3 KYC** | NIL (if filed on time) | ₹5,000 one-time fee for reactivation | DIN deactivation |
| **DPT-3** | As applicable | ₹500 per day of default | Penalty up to ₹1,00,00,000 |
| **MSME Form I** | As applicable | ₹200 per day of default | Penalty on company and officers |

✅ **Important Note:** Continued non-filing can lead to the **[company strike-off India](https://www.indiafilings.com/winding-up-of-a-company)** by the ROC under Section 248 of the Companies Act, 2013. Directors of struck-off companies may be disqualified under Section 164(2) from being appointed as director in any other company for 5 years. compliance_and_timing_sections.heading: What is the Procedure for Company Annual Filing?
compliance_and_timing_sections.content:
The **company annual filing process step by step** involves a series of well-defined actions to be completed in sequence. Here is the complete **annual filing MCA portal** procedure for FY 2025-26:

01. **Step 1 – Conduct Board Meeting** – Hold a Board Meeting to approve the draft financial statements, Directors' Report, and fix the date, time, and venue of the Annual General Meeting (AGM).
02. **Step 2 – Get Accounts Audited** – Appoint a statutory auditor (if not already appointed) and get the annual accounts audited. The **auditor report filing** is mandatory for **AOC-4 filing**.
03. **Step 3 – Hold Annual General Meeting (AGM)** – Conduct the AGM within 6 months from the close of FY (by September 30, 2026). At the AGM, approve financial statements, declare dividends (if any), and appoint/reappoint auditors and directors.
04. **Step 4 – File ADT-1 (Auditor Appointment)** – File Form ADT-1 within **15 days** of AGM to intimate the ROC about the auditor appointment for the current financial year.
05. **Step 5 – File AOC-4 (Financial Statements)** – Submit Form AOC-4 with audited financial statements, Directors' Report, and Auditor's Report within **30 days** of AGM on the MCA portal.
06. **Step 6 – File MGT-7/MGT-7A (Annual Return)** – File the annual return in Form MGT-7 (or MGT-7A for OPC/small companies) within **60 days** of AGM with complete details of shareholders, directors, and company structure.
07. **Step 7 – File DIR-3 KYC (Director KYC)** – All directors must file DIR-3 KYC by **September 30, 2026** to keep their DIN active and comply with **statutory compliance India** requirements.
08. **Step 8 – File DPT-3 (if applicable)** – Companies with outstanding deposits or loans must file **DPT-3 filing** by June 30, 2026.
09. **Step 9 – File MSME Form I (if applicable)** – Companies with outstanding dues to MSME suppliers must file MSME Form I by April 30 and October 31, 2026.
10. **Step 10 – Verify Filing Status** – Track all filing statuses on the **MCA21 annual filing** portal and ensure all forms are approved by the ROC without any defects or resubmission notices.

compliance_and_timing_sections.content:
Failure to complete **ROC annual return** filings within the prescribed due dates attracts significant penalties under the Companies Act, 2013. Here is the complete **company annual filing fees** and penalty structure for late or non-filing:

| Form | Normal Filing Fee | Late Filing Additional Fee | Consequence of Non-Filing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **AOC-4** | ₹200 per day | ₹100 per day after due date | Company strike-off, prosecution of directors |
| **MGT-7/MGT-7A** | ₹200 per day | ₹100 per day after due date | Company strike-off, prosecution of directors |
| **ADT-1** | ₹300 per day | ₹300 per day after due date | Penalty up to ₹5,00,000 |
| **DIR-3 KYC** | NIL (if filed on time) | ₹5,000 one-time fee for reactivation | DIN deactivation |
| **DPT-3** | As applicable | ₹500 per day of default | Penalty up to ₹1,00,00,000 |
| **MSME Form I** | As applicable | ₹200 per day of default | Penalty on company and officers |

✅ **Important Note:** Continued non-filing can lead to the **[company strike-off India](https://www.indiafilings.com/winding-up-of-a-company)** by the ROC under Section 248 of the Companies Act, 2013. Directors of struck-off companies may be disqualified under Section 164(2) from being appointed as director in any other company for 5 years. compliance_and_timing_sections.heading: What are the Advantages of Company Compliance?
compliance_and_timing_sections.content:
Maintaining timely **annual company compliance** through regular **MCA annual filing** offers numerous strategic and financial benefits for every registered company in India. Here are the key advantages of staying compliant with **company law compliance India** requirements:

- **Avoid Company Strike-Off** – Timely **ROC compliance** prevents the ROC from initiating strike-off proceedings under Section 248 of the Companies Act, 2013.

- **Business Credibility** – A company with consistent **annual ROC filing** record commands greater trust and credibility in the market.
- **Smooth Exit Process** – Companies with all pending compliances cleared can opt for a smooth voluntary winding up or strike-off process without legal complications.
- **Avoid Compounding of Offences** – Timely filing avoids the need for compounding of offences before the ROC or NCLT, saving significant time and legal costs.

| **DIR-3 KYC** | Director KYC | September 30, 2026 | All Directors with DIN |
| **DPT-3** | Deposits & Loans Return | June 30, 2026 | Companies with outstanding deposits/loans |

all_sections.heading: What are the Due Dates for Company Annual Filing in India?
all_sections.content:
The **company annual filing due date** is calculated based on the date of the Annual General Meeting (AGM). For most companies, the AGM must be held within **6 months** from the end of the financial year (i.e., by September 30, 2026 for FY 2025-26). Here is the complete **annual filing MCA portal** due date summary:

| Company Type | AGM Deadline | AOC-4 Due Date | MGT-7/7A Due Date |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Private Limited Company** | September 30, 2026 | October 30, 2026 | November 29, 2026 |
| **Public Limited Company** | September 30, 2026 | October 30, 2026 | November 29, 2026 |
| **One Person Company (OPC)** | No AGM Required | September 27, 2026 | November 29, 2026 |
| **Section 8 Company** | September 30, 2026 | October 30, 2026 | November 29, 2026 |
| **Small Company** | September 30, 2026 | October 30, 2026 | November 29, 2026 (MGT-7A) |

✅ **Important Note:** The AGM can be held on or before September 30, 2026 for FY 2025-26. All due dates for **AOC-4 filing** and **MGT-7 annual return** are calculated from the date of AGM. all_sections.heading: What is the Procedure for Company Annual Filing?
all_sections.content:
The **company annual filing process step by step** involves a series of well-defined actions to be completed in sequence. Here is the complete **annual filing MCA portal** procedure for FY 2025-26:

01. **Step 1 – Conduct Board Meeting** – Hold a Board Meeting to approve the draft financial statements, Directors' Report, and fix the date, time, and venue of the Annual General Meeting (AGM).
02. **Step 2 – Get Accounts Audited** – Appoint a statutory auditor (if not already appointed) and get the annual accounts audited. The **auditor report filing** is mandatory for **AOC-4 filing**.
03. **Step 3 – Hold Annual General Meeting (AGM)** – Conduct the AGM within 6 months from the close of FY (by September 30, 2026). At the AGM, approve financial statements, declare dividends (if any), and appoint/reappoint auditors and directors.
04. **Step 4 – File ADT-1 (Auditor Appointment)** – File Form ADT-1 within **15 days** of AGM to intimate the ROC about the auditor appointment for the current financial year.
05. **Step 5 – File AOC-4 (Financial Statements)** – Submit Form AOC-4 with audited financial statements, Directors' Report, and Auditor's Report within **30 days** of AGM on the MCA portal.
06. **Step 6 – File MGT-7/MGT-7A (Annual Return)** – File the annual return in Form MGT-7 (or MGT-7A for OPC/small companies) within **60 days** of AGM with complete details of shareholders, directors, and company structure.
07. **Step 7 – File DIR-3 KYC (Director KYC)** – All directors must file DIR-3 KYC by **September 30, 2026** to keep their DIN active and comply with **statutory compliance India** requirements.
08. **Step 8 – File DPT-3 (if applicable)** – Companies with outstanding deposits or loans must file **DPT-3 filing** by June 30, 2026.
09. **Step 9 – File MSME Form I (if applicable)** – Companies with outstanding dues to MSME suppliers must file MSME Form I by April 30 and October 31, 2026.
10. **Step 10 – Verify Filing Status** – Track all filing statuses on the **MCA21 annual filing** portal and ensure all forms are approved by the ROC without any defects or resubmission notices.

all_sections.heading: What are the Penalties for Non-Compliance in Company Annual Filing?
all_sections.content:
Failure to complete **ROC annual return** filings within the prescribed due dates attracts significant penalties under the Companies Act, 2013. Here is the complete **company annual filing fees** and penalty structure for late or non-filing:

| Form | Normal Filing Fee | Late Filing Additional Fee | Consequence of Non-Filing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **AOC-4** | ₹200 per day | ₹100 per day after due date | Company strike-off, prosecution of directors |
| **MGT-7/MGT-7A** | ₹200 per day | ₹100 per day after due date | Company strike-off, prosecution of directors |
| **ADT-1** | ₹300 per day | ₹300 per day after due date | Penalty up to ₹5,00,000 |
| **DIR-3 KYC** | NIL (if filed on time) | ₹5,000 one-time fee for reactivation | DIN deactivation |
| **DPT-3** | As applicable | ₹500 per day of default | Penalty up to ₹1,00,00,000 |
| **MSME Form I** | As applicable | ₹200 per day of default | Penalty on company and officers |

✅ **Important Note:** Continued non-filing can lead to the **[company strike-off India](https://www.indiafilings.com/winding-up-of-a-company)** by the ROC under Section 248 of the Companies Act, 2013. Directors of struck-off companies may be disqualified under Section 164(2) from being appointed as director in any other company for 5 years. Stay compliant with company annual filing services from IndiaFilings to avoid these severe consequences.

all_sections.heading: Frequently asked questions
all_sections.content:
Common questions aboutCompany Annual Filing.

What are the filings for the company?

Company filing refers to submitting various legal forms and documents to the Registrar of Companies (ROC) as required by the Companies Act 2013. Some of the common types of company filings that need to be filed with the MCA are as follows:

- Incorporation Documents
- Annual Returns
- Financial Statements
- Changes in Directors or Shareholders
- Registered Office Change
- Director Identification Number
- Company Filings for Approval
- Charge Management

.

Can I run a small business without registering?

In India, small businesses can be run without formal company registration, though registering a business is generally recommended to access certain benefits and ensure legal compliance. Some common unregistered business structures used by small enterprises are Sole Proprietorship, Partnership Firm, and Hindu Undivided Family (HUF).

How do I legally file a Business?

Starting a business in India requires compliance with various legal requirements, including registering the business, obtaining necessary licenses and permits, and complying with labor and tax laws. Some of the essential legal requirements for starting a business in India include choosing a business structure, registering your business name, obtaining a Director Identification Number (DIN), incorporating the business, obtaining PAN and TAN, securing other required licenses and permits, ensuring labor law compliance, meeting tax compliance requirements, obtaining insurance, and opening a business bank account.

Does the appointment of the statutory auditor fall under annual compliance?

A company can appoint a statutory auditor either for five consecutive years or till the conclusion of the next Annual general meeting. Therefore, an appointment of the statutory auditor cannot be considered as a part of annual compliance.

What are the compliances of a Private Limited Company?

A company is required to maintain the compliances once the company is incorporated. The auditor is to be appointed within 30 days. Additionally, there is income tax filing and annual return filing that is to be done every year.

Is it necessary to conduct AGM?

The annual general meeting (AGM) is held for the management and the shareholders to interact with each other. The Companies Act,2013 makes it compulsory to hold meetings to discuss the yearly results and appoint auditors.

Is it mandatory to get a Private Limited Company audited?

The statutory audit as the name suggests is a mandatory audit for all companies. All the entities that are unregistered under the Companies Act as Private or Public Limited Companies need to get the books of accounts audited every year.

How to file the annual returns of the Company?

The companies incorporated under the Companies Act,1956 are required to file the following documents with the ROC

The balance sheet in form 23AC which is to be filed by all the companies
Profit and loss account in form 23ACA which is to be file by all the companies.

Is audit report mandatory for all the private limited companies?

The Private Limited Companies are required to file the annual accounts and the returns that disclose the details of the shareholder and the directors to the ROC.

When is annual return to be filed after the AGM?

After the AGM all the private limited companies are required to file the annual return within 60 days of holding the annual general meeting.

What is ROC Compliance?

ROC is the officer governed by the MCA that deals with the functioning, the ROC has to ensure that the Private Limited Companies and the LLPs comply with the statutory requirement of the ACT. The registrar of the companies functions as the regulator for the companies registered with them.

Which Form is to be filed for the appointment of the statutory auditor?

Form ADT-1 is filed for appointing or replacing the Statutory Auditor.

Which form is to be attached to the Companies Director Report?

MGT-9 is attached to the company's director report, which is an extract of MGT -7

Are audited Financial statements mandatory while annual filing of the Private Limited Companies?

Audited financial statements are necessary for every company from its incorporation. The company must file the audited statements only.

What is the annual Compliance of the company?

Annual Compliance means a specific set of Compliance that a company has to fulfill post-incorporation to commence and continue its operations. Under the Companies Act 2013, various compliances must be completed every Year.

What is the main purpose of Compliance?

The main purpose of company compliance is to adhere to internal policies and procedures and governmental laws. Implementing compliance procedures protects the company's reputational risk, improves the company's vision and value, and prevents and detects violations of rules.

Learn more about the [main purpose of Compliance](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/what-is-the-main-purpose-of-compliance/)

What are the different types of Compliance?

There are two main types of Compliance; External and Internal. Both types of Compliance involve a framework of regulations, practices, and rules.

Refer to [our article](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/what-are-different-types-of-compliance/) to know more about the different types of Compliance.

# OPC Compliance Online in India

**OPC compliance online in India** is a critical legal obligation for every One Person Company registered under the Companies Act, 2013. A One Person Company, despite having a single shareholder and director, must adhere to a defined set of annual and periodic compliance requirements mandated by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA). Staying compliant not only keeps the company in good legal standing but also protects the sole director from penalties and legal liabilities.

From filing annual returns to maintaining statutory registers, **one person company compliance** encompasses a range of activities that must be completed within prescribed deadlines. Understanding the [**OPC compliance requirements**](https://www.indiafilings.com/opc-compliance/understanding-opc-compliance-comprehensive-guide) in detail ensures your company remains active, credible, and penalty-free throughout the financial year.

## What is OPC Compliance for One Person Companies in India?

OPC compliance refers to the set of statutory obligations that a One Person Company must fulfil on an annual and ongoing basis as prescribed under the Companies Act, 2013. These obligations cover financial reporting, ROC filings, board meetings, director KYC, and income tax returns. Failure to meet these requirements can lead to heavy penalties and even strike-off of the company from the MCA register.

The **OPC annual compliance** framework is structured to ensure that even single-owner businesses maintain transparency, accountability, and financial discipline. Unlike private limited companies, OPCs enjoy certain relaxations, but the core compliance requirements remain equally important and mandatory.

- **Annual ROC Filings:** Submission of Form MGT-7A and Form AOC-4 to the Registrar of Companies every year.
- **Financial Statements:** Preparation and filing of audited balance sheets and profit & loss accounts.
- **Director Report:** Filing of the annual director's report as part of the compliance package.
- **[Income Tax Return](https://www.indiafilings.com/income-tax-filing):** Filing of ITR for the OPC with the Income Tax Department.
- **DIN KYC:** Annual Director Identification Number KYC update via [Form DIR-3 KYC](https://www.indiafilings.com/dir-3-kyc).

Refer to the [**OPC annual filing**](https://www.indiafilings.com/opc-compliance/opc-annual-filing-guide) details to get a comprehensive overview of all forms, timelines, and procedures involved in maintaining your OPC compliance status.

### Types of OPC Compliance in India

- Annual ROC Compliance (Form MGT-7A and AOC-4)
- Statutory Audit Compliance
- Income Tax Filing Compliance
- Director KYC Compliance
- Board Meeting Compliance
- Registered Office Compliance

## Who Needs to Complete OPC Compliance in India?

Every One Person Company incorporated in India under the Companies Act, 2013 is mandatorily required to complete its annual and periodic compliance obligations, regardless of whether the company has conducted any business activity during the financial year. Even dormant or newly incorporated OPCs must comply with the statutory requirements.

The **OPC statutory compliance** obligations apply to:

- All active One Person Companies registered with MCA
- OPCs that have not commenced business operations
- OPCs undergoing conversion to private limited company
- OPCs with ongoing or pending ROC filings from previous years

It is important to note that non-filing of compliance forms even for a dormant OPC attracts late fees and penalties. Entrepreneurs planning to register an OPC must factor in the ongoing **OPC compliance checklist** requirements from the very first financial year of incorporation. Learn more about the [**one person company annual filing requirements**](https://www.indiafilings.com/one-person-company/understanding-opc-annual-filing-requirements) before starting your compliance journey.

### Key Applicability Criteria

- Company must be registered as an OPC under Companies Act, 2013
- Applicable irrespective of turnover or business activity
- Mandatory from the first financial year of incorporation
- Continues until the company is officially wound up or converted

## What are the Annual OPC Compliance Requirements in India?

The annual compliance calendar for a One Person Company includes multiple filings and statutory obligations spread across the financial year. Each requirement has a specific due date, and missing any of these deadlines can result in additional late fees, penalties, and regulatory scrutiny from the MCA.

| Compliance Requirement | Form/Filing | Due Date |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Annual Return Filing | Form MGT-7A | Within 60 days of AGM (or 31st December) |
| Financial Statements Filing | Form AOC-4 | Within 180 days from end of financial year |
| Director KYC Update | Form DIR-3 KYC | 30th September every year |
| Income Tax Return | ITR-6 | 31st October every year |
| Statutory Audit | Auditor's Report | Before filing AOC-4 |
| Board Meeting | Minutes of Meeting | At least once in every 6 months |

Maintaining a structured compliance calendar and engaging professionals for **OPC MCA annual return** filing ensures that no deadline is missed. Explore the [**OPC ROC filing**](https://www.indiafilings.com/company-annual-filing/mgt-7-and-aoc-4) procedures for Form MGT-7A and AOC-4 in detail to understand what information needs to be submitted.

## What Documents Are Required for OPC Compliance Filing in India?

Accurate and complete documentation is essential for smooth and timely OPC compliance filing. The required documents vary depending on the specific compliance form being filed, but a standard set of records must be maintained and ready throughout the financial year to avoid last-minute delays.

### Documents Required for OPC Annual Compliance

- Certificate of Incorporation of the OPC
- PAN Card of the company and director
- DSC (Digital Signature Certificate) of the director
- DIN (Director Identification Number) details
- Audited Financial Statements (Balance Sheet & P&L Account)
- Director's Report for the financial year
- Statutory Auditor's Report
- Memorandum and Articles of Association
- Details of registered office address
- Bank account statements of the OPC
- Details of nominee director

Having all these documents in order well before the compliance due dates significantly reduces the risk of errors and filing rejections. Professional assistance for **OPC compliance documents** preparation and submission ensures your filings are accurate and complete. The [**company compliance requirements**](https://www.indiafilings.com/mca-services/understanding-company-compliance-key-insights) for OPCs are well-defined and must be strictly followed to avoid regulatory action.

## How Does the OPC Compliance Process Work Online in India?

The **OPC compliance process** in India is entirely online and is conducted through the MCA21 portal of the Ministry of Corporate Affairs. The process involves preparation of financial statements, statutory audit, drafting of the director's report, and submission of the relevant ROC forms within the prescribed deadlines.

### Steps to Complete OPC Compliance Online

1. **Conduct Statutory Audit:** Appoint a qualified chartered accountant to audit the OPC's financial statements for the financial year.
2. **Prepare Financial Statements:** Prepare the audited balance sheet, profit and loss account, and cash flow statement in the prescribed format.
3. **Draft Director's Report:** Prepare the annual director's report covering key business highlights, compliance declarations, and financial summaries.
4. **Hold Board Meeting:** Conduct at least one board meeting in every six months and maintain proper minutes as part of **OPC board meeting compliance**.
5. **File Form AOC-4:** Submit the audited financial statements to the ROC through Form AOC-4 within 180 days from the close of the financial year.
6. **File Form MGT-7A:** Submit the annual return through Form MGT-7A within 60 days of the due date of the Annual General Meeting.
7. **Complete Director KYC:** Update the director's KYC details annually via Form DIR-3 KYC on the MCA portal before 30th September.
8. **File Income Tax Return:** Submit the OPC's income tax return before 31st October of the assessment year.

Following this structured process ensures complete and timely **OPC annual compliance India** without any defaults. You can also refer to the [**OPC compliance steps**](https://www.indiafilings.com/opc-compliance/opc-compliance-steps-one-person-company-requirements) for a step-by-step breakdown tailored specifically for One Person Companies.

## What is the Penalty for Non-Compliance of OPC Annual Return in India?

The MCA imposes significant financial penalties on One Person Companies that fail to meet their annual compliance obligations within the prescribed deadlines. The **OPC compliance penalty** structure is designed to discourage non-compliance and ensure that all registered companies maintain their statutory obligations diligently.

- **Late Filing Fee for AOC-4 and MGT-7A:** ₹100 per day per form for every day of delay beyond the due date.
- **Penalty for Non-Filing:** The company and its director can face penalties up to ₹50,000 under the Companies Act, 2013.
- **DIN Deactivation:** Failure to complete DIR-3 KYC results in deactivation of the Director's DIN, preventing any further filings.
- **Company Strike-Off:** Persistent non-compliance can lead to the company being struck off from the MCA register.

Understanding the **OPC filing due date** and penalty structure helps sole directors plan their compliance activities proactively. The [**ROC late fees on annual return**](https://www.indiafilings.com/company-annual-filing/roc-late-fees-on-annual-return) can accumulate significantly if left unaddressed, making timely compliance an absolute priority.

### Consequences of OPC Non-Compliance

- Daily late fees of ₹100 per form per day of delay
- Director DIN deactivation due to KYC non-compliance
- Personal liability on the sole director for defaults
- Company strike-off from MCA register
- Difficulty in obtaining loans, tenders, or business contracts
- Reputational damage affecting future business prospects

## What is the Cost of OPC Compliance in India?

The **OPC annual filing fees** depend on the authorised share capital of the company, the number of forms to be filed, and whether professional assistance is engaged. While the government filing fees are nominal, the overall cost of OPC compliance includes charges for statutory audit, professional fees, and documentation.

| Compliance Component | Approximate Cost (INR) |
| --- | --- |
| Statutory Audit Fees | ₹3,000 – ₹8,000 |
| Form AOC-4 Filing Fee | ₹200 – ₹500 (Government Fee) |
| Form MGT-7A Filing Fee | ₹200 – ₹500 (Government Fee) |
| DIR-3 KYC Filing Fee | ₹500 (Government Fee) |
| Income Tax Return Filing | ₹1,500 – ₹3,000 |
| Professional Assistance Fees | ₹5,000 – ₹15,000 |

The total cost of **OPC compliance fees** in India typically ranges between ₹8,000 and ₹25,000 per financial year depending on the complexity and scale of business operations. Engaging a professional compliance service ensures accuracy and timely submissions without the risk of penalties. Explore the [**company annual filing**](https://www.indiafilings.com/company-annual-filing/company-annual-filing-guide) cost structure to compare OPC compliance costs with other business entity types.

## How is OPC Compliance Different from Private Limited Company Compliance in India?

While both OPCs and private limited companies are governed by the Companies Act, 2013, there are notable differences in their compliance requirements. Understanding these differences helps sole entrepreneurs appreciate the relative simplicity of **OPC MCA filing** requirements compared to multi-shareholder companies.

- **Annual General Meeting:** OPCs are exempt from conducting a formal Annual General Meeting (AGM), unlike private limited companies.
- **Annual Return Form:** OPCs file Form MGT-7A (simplified), while private limited companies file the more detailed Form MGT-7.
- **Cash Flow Statement:** OPCs with turnover below ₹2 crore are exempt from preparing a cash flow statement.
- **Board Meetings:** OPCs need to hold only one board meeting per half-year, compared to four per year for private limited companies.

Despite these relaxations, the **OPC statutory audit** and ROC filing obligations remain mandatory and must be completed within the prescribed timelines. Entrepreneurs considering an OPC structure can explore the [**one person company registration process**](https://www.indiafilings.com/one-person-company/opc-registration-process-guide) to understand the full lifecycle of forming and managing an OPC in India.

## Frequently asked questions

Common questions aboutOPC Compliance Online for One Person Company in India.

What is a One Person Company (OPC)?

An OPC is a company structure introduced under the Companies Act, 2013, allowing a single individual to incorporate a private limited company with the benefits of limited liability and separate legal status.

Is annual compliance mandatory for an OPC?

Yes. OPCs must fulfill statutory and regulatory compliance requirements annually, regardless of their turnover or business activity.

Which forms are filed annually with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA)?

The key forms include Form AOC-4 (for filing audited financials) and Form MGT-7A (for annual return), along with DIR-3 KYC and ADT-1 (auditor appointment, if applicable).

Do OPCs need to file income tax returns?

Yes. An OPC must file its income tax return in Form ITR-6, even if there is no income.

Is statutory audit mandatory for an OPC?

Yes. OPCs are required to get their financial statements audited annually by a Chartered Accountant.

What is the due date for filing AOC-4 for an OPC?

AOC-4 must be filed within 180 days from the end of the financial year, usually by 27th September if the financial year ends on 31st March.

What is the due date for filing MGT-7A?

MGT-7A must be filed within 60 days from the date of signing the financial statements.

Do OPCs need to hold Annual General Meetings (AGMs)?

No. OPCs are exempt from holding AGMs under Section 96 of the Companies Act, 2013.

What is DIR-3 KYC?

DIR-3 KYC is a mandatory annual form to update the KYC details of the director in the MCA records. It must be filed every year.

Are there penalties for non-filing of annual forms?

Yes. Delayed filings attract penalties such as ₹100 per day per form, and repeated non-compliance can lead to disqualification of directors and strike-off of the company.

Do OPCs need to register under GST?

Only if the aggregate turnover exceeds the threshold limit (₹20/₹40 lakh), or if the OPC deals in interstate supply or e-commerce.

Is GST return filing required for OPCs?

Yes, if the OPC is registered under GST, it must file GSTR-1, GSTR-3B, and GSTR-9 (if applicable), based on turnover and filing category.

What is Form ADT-1?

Form ADT-1 is filed with the RoC to intimate the appointment of a statutory auditor within 15 days of the board meeting in which the appointment is made.

What is Form DPT-3?

DPT-3 is filed annually to report the details of loans or borrowings (secured or unsecured) by the company, even if they are not deposits.

When should Form INC-20A be filed?

Form INC-20A is a declaration of commencement of business and must be filed within 180 days of incorporation, if the OPC was registered with share capital.

Do OPCs need to maintain statutory registers?

Yes. Despite being exempt from many provisions, OPCs are required to maintain statutory registers and records like Register of Members and Minutes Book.

Can an OPC be converted into a private limited company?

Yes. OPCs can voluntarily convert into private limited companies after completing two years or upon exceeding ₹2 crore paid-up capital or ₹2 crore turnover.

What are the key exemptions available to OPCs?

OPCs are exempt from holding AGMs, rotation of auditors, applicability of CARO, and certain board meeting requirements.

What documents are required for OPC annual compliance?

- Bank statements
- Sales and purchase invoices
- TDS and GST returns
- Financial statements
- Director’s report
- Details of shareholder and director(s)

all_sections.heading: What is OPC Compliance for One Person Companies in India?
all_sections.content:
OPC compliance refers to the set of statutory obligations that a One Person Company must fulfil on an annual and ongoing basis as prescribed under the Companies Act, 2013. These obligations cover financial reporting, ROC filings, board meetings, director KYC, and income tax returns. Failure to meet these requirements can lead to heavy penalties and even strike-off of the company from the MCA register.

The **OPC annual compliance** framework is structured to ensure that even single-owner businesses maintain transparency, accountability, and financial discipline. Unlike private limited companies, OPCs enjoy certain relaxations, but the core compliance requirements remain equally important and mandatory.

- **Annual ROC Filings:** Submission of Form MGT-7A and Form AOC-4 to the Registrar of Companies every year.
- **Financial Statements:** Preparation and filing of audited balance sheets and profit & loss accounts.
- **Director Report:** Filing of the annual director's report as part of the compliance package.
- **[Income Tax Return](https://www.indiafilings.com/income-tax-filing):** Filing of ITR for the OPC with the Income Tax Department.
- **DIN KYC:** Annual Director Identification Number KYC update via [Form DIR-3 KYC](https://www.indiafilings.com/dir-3-kyc).

Refer to the [**OPC annual filing**](https://www.indiafilings.com/opc-compliance/opc-annual-filing-guide) details to get a comprehensive overview of all forms, timelines, and procedures involved in maintaining your OPC compliance status.

all_sections.heading: What are the Annual OPC Compliance Requirements in India?
all_sections.content:
The annual compliance calendar for a One Person Company includes multiple filings and statutory obligations spread across the financial year. Each requirement has a specific due date, and missing any of these deadlines can result in additional late fees, penalties, and regulatory scrutiny from the MCA.

| Compliance Requirement | Form/Filing | Due Date |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Annual Return Filing | Form MGT-7A | Within 60 days of AGM (or 31st December) |
| Financial Statements Filing | Form AOC-4 | Within 180 days from end of financial year |
| Director KYC Update | Form DIR-3 KYC | 30th September every year |
| Income Tax Return | ITR-6 | 31st October every year |

Maintaining a structured compliance calendar and engaging professionals for **OPC MCA annual return** filing ensures that no deadline is missed. all_sections.heading: Steps to Complete OPC Compliance Online
all_sections.content:
1. **Conduct Statutory Audit:** Appoint a qualified chartered accountant to audit the OPC's financial statements for the financial year.
2. **Prepare Financial Statements:** Prepare the audited balance sheet, profit and loss account, and cash flow statement in the prescribed format.
3. **Draft Director's Report:** Prepare the annual director's report covering key business highlights, compliance declarations, and financial summaries.
4. **Hold Board Meeting:** Conduct at least one board meeting in every six months and maintain proper minutes as part of **OPC board meeting compliance**.
5. **File Form AOC-4:** Submit the audited financial statements to the ROC through Form AOC-4 within 180 days from the close of the financial year.
6. **File Form MGT-7A:** Submit the annual return through Form MGT-7A within 60 days of the due date of the Annual General Meeting.
7. **Complete Director KYC:** Update the director's KYC details annually via Form DIR-3 KYC on the MCA portal before 30th September.
8. **File Income Tax Return:** Submit the OPC's income tax return before 31st October of the assessment year.

Following this structured process ensures complete and timely **OPC annual compliance India** without any defaults. You can also refer to the [**OPC compliance steps**](https://www.indiafilings.com/opc-compliance/opc-compliance-steps-one-person-company-requirements) for a step-by-step breakdown tailored specifically for One Person Companies.

all_sections.heading: What is the Penalty for Non-Compliance of OPC Annual Return in India?
all_sections.content:
The MCA imposes significant financial penalties on One Person Companies that fail to meet their annual compliance obligations within the prescribed deadlines. The **OPC compliance penalty** structure is designed to discourage non-compliance and ensure that all registered companies maintain their statutory obligations diligently.

- **Late Filing Fee for AOC-4 and MGT-7A:** ₹100 per day per form for every day of delay beyond the due date.
- **Penalty for Non-Filing:** The company and its director can face penalties up to ₹50,000 under the Companies Act, 2013.
- **DIN Deactivation:** Failure to complete DIR-3 KYC results in deactivation of the Director's DIN, preventing any further filings.
- **Company Strike-Off:** Persistent non-compliance can lead to the company being struck off from the MCA register.

Understanding the **OPC filing due date** and penalty structure helps sole directors plan their compliance activities proactively. The [**ROC late fees on annual return**](https://www.indiafilings.com/company-annual-filing/roc-late-fees-on-annual-return) can accumulate significantly if left unaddressed, making timely compliance an absolute priority.

- Personal liability on the sole director for defaults
- Company strike-off from MCA register
- Difficulty in obtaining loans, tenders, or business contracts

all_sections.content:
Common questions aboutOPC Compliance Online for One Person Company in India.

What is a One Person Company (OPC)?

An OPC is a company structure introduced under the Companies Act, 2013, allowing a single individual to incorporate a private limited company with the benefits of limited liability and separate legal status.

Is annual compliance mandatory for an OPC?

Yes. OPCs must fulfill statutory and regulatory compliance requirements annually, regardless of their turnover or business activity.

Which forms are filed annually with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA)?

The key forms include Form AOC-4 (for filing audited financials) and Form MGT-7A (for annual return), along with DIR-3 KYC and ADT-1 (auditor appointment, if applicable).

Do OPCs need to file income tax returns?

Yes. An OPC must file its income tax return in Form ITR-6, even if there is no income.

Is statutory audit mandatory for an OPC?

Yes. OPCs are required to get their financial statements audited annually by a Chartered Accountant.

What is the due date for filing AOC-4 for an OPC?

AOC-4 must be filed within 180 days from the end of the financial year, usually by 27th September if the financial year ends on 31st March.

What is the due date for filing MGT-7A?

MGT-7A must be filed within 60 days from the date of signing the financial statements.

Do OPCs need to hold Annual General Meetings (AGMs)?

No. OPCs are exempt from holding AGMs under Section 96 of the Companies Act, 2013.

What is DIR-3 KYC?

DIR-3 KYC is a mandatory annual form to update the KYC details of the director in the MCA records. It must be filed every year.

Are there penalties for non-filing of annual forms?

Yes. Delayed filings attract penalties such as ₹100 per day per form, and repeated non-compliance can lead to disqualification of directors and strike-off of the company.

Do OPCs need to register under GST?

Only if the aggregate turnover exceeds the threshold limit (₹20/₹40 lakh), or if the OPC deals in interstate supply or e-commerce.

Is GST return filing required for OPCs?

Yes, if the OPC is registered under GST, it must file GSTR-1, GSTR-3B, and GSTR-9 (if applicable), based on turnover and filing category.

What is Form ADT-1?

Form ADT-1 is filed with the RoC to intimate the appointment of a statutory auditor within 15 days of the board meeting in which the appointment is made.

What is Form DPT-3?

DPT-3 is filed annually to report the details of loans or borrowings (secured or unsecured) by the company, even if they are not deposits.

When should Form INC-20A be filed?

Form INC-20A is a declaration of commencement of business and must be filed within 180 days of incorporation, if the OPC was registered with share capital.

Do OPCs need to maintain statutory registers?

Yes. Despite being exempt from many provisions, OPCs are required to maintain statutory registers and records like Register of Members and Minutes Book.

Can an OPC be converted into a private limited company?

Yes. OPCs can voluntarily convert into private limited companies after completing two years or upon exceeding ₹2 crore paid-up capital or ₹2 crore turnover.

What are the key exemptions available to OPCs?

OPCs are exempt from holding AGMs, rotation of auditors, applicability of CARO, and certain board meeting requirements.

What documents are required for OPC annual compliance?

- Bank statements
- Sales and purchase invoices
- TDS and GST returns
- Financial statements
- Director’s report
- Details of shareholder and director(s)

# Change Company Registered Office Address Online in India

Change company registered office address is a formal legal process governed under the Companies Act, 2013. Every company registered in India must maintain an official registered office address, and any change to this address requires proper documentation, board or shareholder approval, and timely MCA filings. Whether relocating within the same city, shifting to a new ROC jurisdiction, or moving to another state, understanding the complete process helps ensure full legal compliance without penalties or delays.

Companies planning a [change of company registered office](https://www.indiafilings.com/registered-office/change-company-registered-office-easy) must follow the correct procedure under the Companies Act, 2013 to avoid compliance issues and ensure the MCA records are updated accurately.

## What Is a Registered Office Address and Why Does It Matter in India?

A registered office address is the official address of a company as recorded with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA). All legal notices, government communications, and statutory documents are sent to this address. Maintaining an accurate and updated registered office is a legal obligation for every company operating in India.

- The **registered office address** serves as the company's official point of contact with government authorities.
- All statutory registers, books of accounts, and compliance documents must be maintained at this address.
- Failure to update the address after relocation can attract penalties under the Companies Act, 2013.
- A **company registered address update** must be completed within 30 days of the change.
- The address is publicly available on the MCA portal and visible to clients, investors, and regulators.

### Types of Registered Office Address Change

The process and legal requirements for a **registered office change procedure** vary based on the nature and extent of the relocation. Understanding the type of change helps determine the correct forms and approvals required.

- **Within the same city or town:** Requires only a board resolution and Form INC-22 filing.
- **Within the same state but different ROC:** Requires a special resolution and Regional Director approval.
- **From one state to another:** Requires special resolution, creditor approval, and Central Government approval.
- **Within the same ROC jurisdiction:** Simplest process with minimal regulatory requirements.

## How Does the Process to Change Company Registered Office Work in India?

The **company address change MCA** process follows a structured legal pathway depending on the type of relocation involved. Each step must be completed in the correct sequence to ensure MCA acceptance and avoid rejection of filings. Here is how the process works from start to finish.

### Step-by-Step Process for Registered Office Change Within Same City

1. **Hold a Board Meeting** — Pass a **board resolution for office address change** approving the new registered office address.
2. **Update the new address** — Obtain proof of the new premises such as a rent agreement or ownership document.
3. **File Form INC-22** — Submit **Form INC-22 filing** on the MCA portal within 30 days of the board resolution.
4. **Attach supporting documents** — Include utility bill, NOC from owner, and board resolution as attachments.
5. **MCA approval** — Once verified, MCA updates the company's registered office address in its records.

### Process for Registered Office Change to a Different ROC Within Same State

1. Hold an Extraordinary General Meeting (EGM) and pass a **special resolution registered office change**.
2. File **Form [MGT-14](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/mgt-14)** within 30 days of passing the special resolution.
3. Apply to the Regional Director using Form INC-23 for confirmation of the address change.
4. Publish a notice in a local newspaper at the new location about the intended change.
5. File Form INC-28 after receiving Regional Director's order of confirmation.
6. File Form INC-22 to update the registered office address on MCA records.

Companies planning to [shift their registered office to a new ROC within the same state](https://www.indiafilings.com/registered-office/shifting-company-office-same-state-new-roc) must complete this multi-step process within the prescribed timelines to avoid regulatory complications.

## What Documents Are Required to Change Registered Office Address in India?

Accurate and complete **registered office change documents India** are essential for a successful MCA filing. Missing or incorrect documents are the most common reason for rejection of address change applications. Here is a detailed list of documents required for the process.

### Documents Required for Registered Office Change

- Board Resolution or Special Resolution approving the change of registered office
- Proof of new registered office address — rent agreement or sale deed
- Latest utility bill (electricity, water, or gas) not older than 2 months
- No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the owner of the premises
- Copy of the altered Memorandum of Association (if state is changing)
- List of creditors and their consent (for inter-state change)
- Newspaper advertisement copy (for change involving different ROC)
- Director's identity proof — Aadhaar, [PAN](https://www.indiafilings.com/pan-card), and DIN details
