all_sections.heading: Tax Residency Certificate Online in India
all_sections.content: A **tax residency certificate** is an essential document issued by the Income Tax Department of India that establishes your tax residency status for claiming benefits under Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements (DTAA). This certificate enables Indian tax residents to avoid paying double taxes on foreign income and claim treaty benefits in other countries. The certificate serves as official proof of your Indian tax residency and is crucial for international tax planning and compliance. Understanding the [**income tax regulations**](https://www.indiafilings.com/income-tax) in India is fundamental before applying for this important document.

all_sections.heading: What is a Tax Residency Certificate in India?
all_sections.content:
A Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) is an official document issued by the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) under the Income Tax Department of India. This certificate confirms that an individual, company, or entity is a tax resident of India for a specific assessment year. The primary purpose of this certificate is to enable the holder to claim benefits under various Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements that India has signed with different countries worldwide.

The certificate contains crucial information including the applicant's name, address, Permanent Account Number (PAN), assessment year, and an official declaration confirming Indian tax residency status. This document is internationally recognized and accepted by foreign tax authorities as valid proof of Indian tax residency. Having a proper [**PAN card registration**](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/download-epan-card) is mandatory before applying for a tax residency certificate.

The TRC plays a vital role in international taxation scenarios, particularly for individuals and businesses with cross-border income. It helps establish eligibility for reduced withholding tax rates and treaty benefits as per the applicable DTAA provisions between India and other countries.

all_sections.heading: Types of Tax Residency Certificate
all_sections.content:
Tax Residency Certificates issued by the Income Tax Department are categorized based on both the nature of the applicant and their residential status under Indian tax laws. Understanding these different types is crucial for determining eligibility and claiming appropriate DTAA benefits.

**Based on Entity Type:**

**Individual Tax Residency Certificate:** This type is issued to individuals who are tax residents of India and need to claim DTAA benefits on their foreign income. It covers resident individuals, Hindu Undivided Families (HUFs), and other individual entities who meet the tax residency criteria under Indian tax laws.

**Corporate Tax Residency Certificate:** This category covers companies, firms, associations of persons, body of individuals, and other corporate entities that are tax residents of India. These entities typically require TRC for claiming treaty benefits on their overseas business income, dividends, royalties, and other forms of international revenue.

**Based on Residential Status:**

**Resident and Ordinarily Resident (ROR):** This TRC is issued to individuals who qualify as both resident and ordinarily resident of India. ROR individuals are taxed on their global income in India and can claim TRC to avoid double taxation on foreign income. They must satisfy both the basic residency test and the ordinary residence conditions under Section 6 of the Income Tax Act.

**Resident but Not Ordinarily Resident (RNOR):** This certificate is for individuals who are residents of India but do not meet the ordinary residence criteria. RNOR individuals are taxed only on income that is received, deemed to be received, or accrues in India, plus foreign income from business or profession controlled from India. This status is particularly beneficial for returning Indians and new residents.

**TRC for Non-Residents:** In specific circumstances, even non-residents can obtain a tax residency certificate if they have significant ties with India or if required under specific DTAA provisions. This is typically applicable for individuals who may be considered residents under the tie-breaker rules of DTAAs or for specific treaty benefits where residency status needs clarification.

| TRC Type | Residential Status | Taxation Scope | Common Applicants |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Individual TRC | ROR | Global income | Long-term residents |
| Individual TRC | RNOR | India-sourced income + controlled foreign income | Returning Indians, new residents |
| Corporate TRC | Resident Entity | Global income | Indian companies |
| Special TRC | Non-Resident | As per DTAA provisions | Treaty-specific cases |

The type of TRC you require depends on your residential status as determined under Indian tax laws, which is based on the number of days you stay in India during the relevant financial year and your stay pattern in previous years. Each category has different implications for tax liability and the scope of DTAA benefits available.

all_sections.heading: How Does a Tax Residency Certificate Help in Avoiding Double Taxation?
all_sections.content:
Double taxation occurs when the same income is taxed in two different countries, creating an unfair tax burden on taxpayers. A Tax Residency Certificate serves as the key mechanism to avoid this scenario by establishing your tax residency status in India and enabling you to claim relief under Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements.

When you present a TRC to foreign tax authorities or financial institutions, they recognize your Indian tax residency status and apply the beneficial tax rates specified in the relevant DTAA. This typically results in reduced withholding tax rates on various types of income including dividends, interest, royalties, and capital gains. For comprehensive understanding of these benefits, refer to [**detailed TRC guidelines**](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/tax-residency-certificate).

- Reduced withholding tax on dividend income from foreign sources
- Lower tax rates on interest earned from overseas investments
- Beneficial treatment of royalty and technical service fees
- Capital gains tax relief under specific DTAA provisions
- Exemption from double taxation on business profits
- Credit for foreign taxes paid in India

The certificate also enables you to claim foreign tax credit in India for taxes paid abroad, ensuring that your total tax liability doesn't exceed what would be payable under Indian tax laws alone. This mechanism promotes international business and investment activities while ensuring fair taxation.

all_sections.heading: How Tax Residency Certificate Helps NRIs
all_sections.content:
Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) who maintain tax residency in India while living abroad face unique taxation challenges that a Tax Residency Certificate can effectively address. Many NRIs continue to have significant income sources in India while also earning income in their country of residence, creating potential double taxation scenarios.

For NRIs who qualify as Indian tax residents based on the residential status criteria, a TRC becomes instrumental in claiming DTAA benefits in their country of residence. This is particularly beneficial for NRIs working in countries like the UAE, Singapore, UK, USA, and Canada, where India has comprehensive DTAAs in place.

The certificate helps NRIs in several ways: reducing tax burden on Indian income when filing returns abroad, claiming treaty benefits on investment income, avoiding double taxation on pension and retirement benefits, and optimizing tax planning for cross-border investments. NRIs should also understand [**Form 10FA requirements**](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/form-10fa) for claiming tax treaty benefits.

all_sections.heading: Who Should Apply for a Tax Residency Certificate in India?
all_sections.content:
Several categories of taxpayers should consider applying for a Tax Residency Certificate based on their income patterns, residential status, and international tax obligations. The primary applicants include Indian tax residents who earn income from foreign sources and need to claim DTAA benefits to avoid double taxation.

Individuals who have moved abroad for employment, business, or other purposes but continue to maintain Indian tax residency status should apply for TRC. This includes professionals working overseas, business owners with international operations, and investors with foreign income sources.

Companies and corporate entities with overseas subsidiaries, foreign income, or international business operations also require TRC to establish their Indian tax residency status. This helps them claim treaty benefits and optimize their global tax structure while remaining compliant with international tax regulations.

all_sections.heading: Who Needs a Tax Residency Certificate?
all_sections.content:
The need for a Tax Residency Certificate extends to various categories of taxpayers based on their specific circumstances and international tax exposure. Understanding who needs this certificate is crucial for proper tax planning and compliance.

**Individuals with Foreign Income:** Anyone earning salary, business income, investment returns, or other forms of income from foreign sources needs a TRC to claim DTAA benefits. This includes employees of multinational companies, freelancers working for overseas clients, and investors with foreign portfolios.

**NRIs with Indian Tax Residency:** Non-residents who qualify as Indian tax residents based on their stay in India or other criteria need TRC to avoid double taxation in their country of residence.

**Corporate Entities:** Companies with overseas operations, foreign subsidiaries, export businesses earning foreign exchange, and entities receiving royalties or technical fees from abroad require TRC for treaty benefit claims.

**Investors and Traders:** Individuals and entities investing in foreign securities, real estate, or other assets need TRC to claim beneficial tax treatment on their investment returns and capital gains.

all_sections.heading: How to Apply for a Tax Residency Certificate in India?
all_sections.content:
The application process for a Tax Residency Certificate has been digitized and can be completed entirely online through the Income Tax Department's e-filing portal. The process is straightforward and designed to minimize paperwork while ensuring proper verification of applicant credentials.

To begin the application, taxpayers must have a valid PAN card and should have filed their income tax returns for the relevant assessment year. The online portal provides a user-friendly interface for completing the application and uploading required documents.

all_sections.heading: Step-by-Step Process to Obtain TRC in India
all_sections.content:
1. **Access the e-Filing Portal:** Visit the official Income Tax Department website and log in using your PAN and password
2. **Navigate to TRC Section:** Go to the 'e-File' menu and select 'Miscellaneous' followed by 'Tax Residency Certificate'
3. **Fill Application Form:** Complete all required fields including personal details, assessment year, and country for which certificate is needed
4. **Upload Documents:** Submit all required documents in PDF format as per the specified guidelines
5. **Payment of Fees:** Pay the prescribed fee through online payment modes available on the portal
6. **Submit Application:** Review all details carefully and submit the application to receive acknowledgment number
7. **Track Status:** Use the acknowledgment number to track application status and receive updates via email
8. **Certificate Download:** Once approved, download the digital certificate from the portal

The entire process typically takes 15-20 working days from submission to certificate issuance, depending on the completeness of documentation and verification requirements.

all_sections.heading: What Documents Are Required for a Tax Residency Certificate in India?
all_sections.content:
The documentation requirements for Tax Residency Certificate applications are specific and must be submitted in the prescribed format to ensure smooth processing. Proper documentation is crucial as incomplete or incorrect documents are the primary reasons for application delays or rejections.

All documents must be self-attested and uploaded in clear, readable PDF format. The file size should not exceed the specified limits, and all documents should be in English or accompanied by certified translations if in regional languages.

all_sections.heading: Documents Required for TRC Application
all_sections.content:

| Bank Statement | Statement showing Indian bank account details | Mandatory |

| Passport Copy | For individuals with foreign travel history | If applicable |

For corporate applicants, additional documents include certificate of incorporation, memorandum and articles of association, board resolution authorizing the TRC application, and audited financial statements for the relevant financial year.

all_sections.heading: What is the Validity Period of a Tax Residency Certificate in India?
all_sections.content:
Understanding the validity period of a Tax Residency Certificate is crucial for proper tax planning and ensuring continuous compliance with international tax obligations. The validity is tied to specific assessment years and cannot be extended beyond the prescribed period.

A Tax Residency Certificate issued by the Income Tax Department is valid for one assessment year only. This means that the certificate covers the specific financial year for which tax residency status is established and verified. For example, a TRC issued for Assessment Year 2025-26 (Financial Year 2024-25) is valid only for that particular year.

all_sections.heading: Key Points on TRC Validity
all_sections.content:
- **Annual Requirement:** A fresh TRC application must be submitted for each assessment year where treaty benefits are required
- **Effective Period:** The certificate is effective from April 1st to March 31st of the relevant financial year
- **No Automatic Renewal:** There is no facility for automatic renewal; each application must be processed separately
- **Income Period Coverage:** The certificate must cover the period during which foreign income was earned or received
- **Treaty Claim Timing:** The certificate should be available before claiming treaty benefits in foreign jurisdictions

This annual requirement ensures that the Income Tax Department can verify the current tax residency status of applicants based on their latest circumstances, income patterns, and compliance with Indian tax laws.

all_sections.heading: What are the Common Mistakes to Avoid During Tax Residency Certificate Application?
all_sections.content:
Many TRC applications face delays or rejections due to common mistakes that can be easily avoided with proper preparation and attention to detail. Understanding these common pitfalls helps ensure smooth processing and timely certificate issuance.

The most frequent mistakes include incomplete documentation, incorrect assessment year selection, mismatched information across documents, and failure to meet eligibility criteria. Applicants often overlook the importance of having filed their income tax returns before applying for TRC.

all_sections.heading: Common Mistakes in TRC Application
all_sections.content:
- **Incomplete ITR Filing:** Applying without filing income tax return for the relevant assessment year
- **Document Mismatch:** Inconsistent information across different documents and application form
- **Wrong Assessment Year:** Selecting incorrect assessment year for which certificate is required
- **Poor Quality Uploads:** Submitting unclear or illegible document scans
- **Missing Signatures:** Forgetting to self-attest uploaded documents
- **Incorrect Address:** Using different addresses in various documents without proper explanation
- **Fee Payment Issues:** Payment failures or using incorrect payment methods
- **Late Application:** Submitting application too close to the deadline for claiming treaty benefits

To avoid these mistakes, applicants should carefully review all requirements, ensure consistency across documents, and double-check all information before submission. It's also advisable to apply well in advance of when the certificate is needed.

all_sections.heading: What are the Reasons for Rejection of a TRC Application in India?
all_sections.content:
Tax Residency Certificate applications can be rejected for various reasons, primarily related to eligibility criteria, documentation issues, or non-compliance with tax obligations. Understanding these rejection reasons helps applicants prepare better applications and avoid common pitfalls.

The Income Tax Department has strict criteria for issuing TRC, and applications that don't meet these standards are systematically rejected. The most common rejection reasons relate to failure to establish tax residency status in India or incomplete compliance with tax filing obligations.

all_sections.heading: Key Reasons for TRC Application Rejection
all_sections.content:
- **Non-Resident Status:** Applicant doesn't qualify as Indian tax resident for the relevant assessment year
- **ITR Non-Filing:** Failure to file income tax return for the assessment year in question
- **Incomplete Documentation:** Missing mandatory documents or poor-quality document uploads
- **Tax Compliance Issues:** Outstanding tax demands, penalties, or non-compliance with tax obligations
- **Incorrect Information:** False or misleading information provided in the application
- **Duplicate Applications:** Multiple applications for the same assessment year
- **Jurisdiction Issues:** Applying for countries where India doesn't have DTAA
- **Processing Delays:** Application submitted after prescribed deadlines

When an application is rejected, the Income Tax Department provides specific reasons for rejection. Applicants can address these issues and reapply with corrected documentation and information. However, the fee paid for rejected applications is typically non-refundable.

Ensure complete compliance for your Partnership Firm with expert assistance. We handle income tax filing, GST returns, accounting, and statutory requirements so your business stays compliant and penalty-free.

- Income Tax Return Filing (ITR-5)
- Bookkeeping & Financial Statement Preparation

- Annual Compliance & Partner Reporting

# Partnership Tax Return Filing

Operating a [Partnership Firm](https://www.indiafilings.com/partnership) in India involves a range of crucial financial and legal responsibilities. It is imperative to adhere to various tax and regulatory requirements to ensure the smooth functioning and growth of your business. These obligations encompass filing Income [Tax Returns](https://www.indiafilings.com/business-itr-filing), [TDS Returns](https://www.indiafilings.com/tds-return-filing), [GST Returns](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-return-filing), [EPF Returns](https://www.indiafilings.com/pf-return-filing), and occasionally undergoing a Tax Audit if the partnership firm audit limit exceeds. Partnership firms must understand the income tax rate for partnership firm and ensure to file the returns on or before the specified deadline.

The submission of tax returns as per partnership firm tax rate is a fundamental responsibility for Partnership Firms in India. At IndiaFilings, we recognize the importance of complying with Indian taxation of partnership firm and the potential advantages associated with it. Our comprehensive services are meticulously crafted to aid business proprietors in navigating the intricate landscape of compliance. To simplify these compliance duties, IndiaFilings offers expert guidance, streamlining the process and eliminating hassles for business owners.

By partnering with us, you can ensure compliance with income tax on partnership firms and explore opportunities to optimize your tax benefits as per income tax rate for partnership firm, enabling your business to thrive while adhering to tax regulations.

## Partnership Firm

A partnership firm is a business entity formed by two or more individuals working together under a single enterprise. There are two main categories of partnership firms:

- **Registered Partnership Firm:** A registered partnership firm is one that has undergone formal registration with the RoC and has received a registration certificate as evidence of its legal existence.
- **Unregistered Partnership Firm:** Any partnership that lacks a registration certificate from the Registrar of Firms is referred to as an unregistered partnership.

Partnership, in essence, is an agreement entered into by two or more persons who have mutually consented to share the profits or losses arising from a jointly conducted business. The individuals involved in a partnership arrangement are individually known as partners and collectively referred to as a firm. Partners need to be aware of the partnership firm tax rate and how it affects the distribution of profits. Partners are responsible for maximizing firm advantage, fair dealings, and maintaining accurate records with full transparency for all partners' benefit.

## Income Tax Return filing for Partnership Firm

Every partnership firm in India is obligated to file income tax returns annually as per partnership tax rate, regardless of whether the firm has generated income or incurred losses during the financial year. Understanding the partnership firm tax rate (30%) is crucial for making informed financial decisions within the business. Even if there was no business activity and the partnership firm's income is zero (NIL), filing an NIL income tax return within the stipulated income tax return for partnership firm due date is still mandatory.

### Partnership Firm Income Tax slabs / LLP for AY 2023-24

Under the provisions of the Income Tax Act 1961, a partnership firm in India is subject to the following partnership firm income tax slab percentages:

- **Partnership firm tax rate:** Partnership firms are liable to pay income tax at a partnership firm tax rate of 30% on their taxable income.
- **Surcharge on Partnership firm:** If the taxable income of the partnership firm exceeds one crore rupees, a surcharge on partnership firm is 12% is applicable in addition to the income tax.
- **Interest on Capital:** Partnership firms can claim a deduction of up to 12% on the interest paid on capital.
- **Health and Education Cess:** A 4% Health and Education Cess is levied on the total tax amount, including surcharges.
- **Marginal Relief :** In case Net Income exceeds 1 crore, the amount payable as income tax and Surcharge shall not exceed the total amount payable as income tax on Total Income of Rs.1 crore by more than the amount of income that exceeds Rs.1 crore.

### Minimum Alternate Tax for Partnership Firms

Similar to income tax applicable for a company, partnership firms are subject to minimum alternate Tax under the taxation of partnership firm. A minimum alternate tax of 18.5% of adjusted total income is applicable. Hence, income tax payable by a partnership firm's profits cannot be less than 18.5 percent (increased by income tax surcharge, education cess, and secondary and higher education cess).

### Deductions Allowed

When computing the liability of income tax on partnership firm as usual based on partnership tax rate, deductions are permitted for the following:

- Remunerations or interest paid to partners that do not conform to the terms of the partnership agreement.
- Salaries, bonuses, remunerations, and commissions are paid to non-working partners of the firm.
- If remuneration paid to partners complies with the partnership deed but relates to transactions that pre-date the partnership deed.

### ITR Forms for a Partnership Firm

Partnership Firms can file their ITR for income tax on partnership firms through Form ITR-4 or ITR-5.

#### ITR-4

ITR-4 is to be filed by those partnership firms which are a Total Income of up to 50 lakh and have income from Business and Profession, which is computed under presumptive basis.

#### ITR-5

ITR-5 is to be filed by those partnership firms who are required to get their account audited.

### Income Tax Return for Partnership Firm Due Date

The deadline for filing ITR for a partnership firm depends on whether an audit is required:

- If the firm is not subject to an audit, returns must be filed by 31st July.
- If an audit is necessary, the firm must file its returns by 31st October.

## Filing of GST Returns

Every GST-registered person is required to file GST Returns, and every partnership firm is required to be under GST if its aggregate annual turnover exceeds Rs. 20 lacs. Usually, the GST-registered partnership firms have to file GSTR-1, GSTR-3B, and GSTR-9 returns. If the firm has opted for a composition scheme, then GSTR-4 is to be filed.

## TDS Return

The TDS Return is to be filed where the partnership firm has a valid TAN, and the type of return to be filed depends upon the purpose of deduction. The types of TDS Return are:

- Form 24Q – TDS on Salary
- Form 27Q – TDS where the deductee is a non-resident, foreign company
- Form 26QB – TDS on payment for transfer of immovable property
- Form 26Q – TDS in any other case

## EPF Return filing

The partnership firm is required to get EPF registration if it employs more than ten persons, and accordingly, filing of EPF return becomes mandatory.

## Accounting and bookkeeping

Books of account are required to be maintained if the partnership firm's sale/turnover/gross receipts from the business is more than Rs. 25,00,000 or the income from the business is more than Rs. 2,50,000 in any of the three preceding years.

## Tax Audit

A partnership firm is required to have a tax audit carried out if the sales, turnover, or gross receipts of business exceed the partnership firm audit limit of Rs. 1 crore in the financial year. However, it may be required to get its account audited in certain other circumstances.

What is a partnership firm?

What are the types of partnership firms?

What are the responsibilities of partners in a firm?

Partners are responsible for operating the firm effectively, dealing fairly in all transactions, and maintaining accurate and transparent records for the benefit of all partners.

Is it mandatory for a partnership firm to file income tax returns?

You must meet the compliance requirements of income tax on partnership firms to avoid penalties and legal issues.

What are the partnership firm tax slabs?

According to the Partnership firm tax slab structure, one needs to pay 30% income tax on taxable income, with possible surcharges for incomes over one crore rupees and a 4% Health and Education Cess on the total tax amount.

What is Minimum Alternate Tax (MAT) for partnership firms?

Partnership firms are subject to MAT at 18.5% of adjusted total income, ensuring that tax payable is not less than 18.5% of profits.

What deductions are allowed for partnership firms?

Deductions include interest paid on capital up to 12%, and certain remunerations to partners, provided they conform to the partnership agreement.

What ITR forms should partnership firms use?

Partnership firms can file using ITR-4 (for presumptive income under 50 lakh) or ITR-5 (if audit is required).

What is the deadline for partnership firms to file ITR?

Are partnership firms required to file GST returns?

When is a partnership firm required to file TDS returns?

Is EPF registration necessary for partnership firms?

all_sections.content:
A partnership firm is a business entity formed by two or more individuals working together under a single enterprise. There are two main categories of partnership firms:

- **Registered Partnership Firm:** A registered partnership firm is one that has undergone formal registration with the RoC and has received a registration certificate as evidence of its legal existence.
- **Unregistered Partnership Firm:** Any partnership that lacks a registration certificate from the Registrar of Firms is referred to as an unregistered partnership.

Partnership, in essence, is an agreement entered into by two or more persons who have mutually consented to share the profits or losses arising from a jointly conducted business. The individuals involved in a partnership arrangement are individually known as partners and collectively referred to as a firm. Partners need to be aware of the partnership firm tax rate and how it affects the distribution of profits. Partners are responsible for maximizing firm advantage, fair dealings, and maintaining accurate records with full transparency for all partners' benefit.

all_sections.heading: Partnership Firm Income Tax slabs / LLP for AY 2023-24
all_sections.content:
Under the provisions of the Income Tax Act 1961, a partnership firm in India is subject to the following partnership firm income tax slab percentages:

- **Partnership firm tax rate:** Partnership firms are liable to pay income tax at a partnership firm tax rate of 30% on their taxable income.
- **Surcharge on Partnership firm:** If the taxable income of the partnership firm exceeds one crore rupees, a surcharge on partnership firm is 12% is applicable in addition to the income tax.
- **Interest on Capital:** Partnership firms can claim a deduction of up to 12% on the interest paid on capital.
- **Health and Education Cess:** A 4% Health and Education Cess is levied on the total tax amount, including surcharges.
- **Marginal Relief :** In case Net Income exceeds 1 crore, the amount payable as income tax and Surcharge shall not exceed the total amount payable as income tax on Total Income of Rs.1 crore by more than the amount of income that exceeds Rs.1 crore.

all_sections.heading: Minimum Alternate Tax for Partnership Firms
all_sections.content: Similar to income tax applicable for a company, partnership firms are subject to minimum alternate Tax under the taxation of partnership firm. A minimum alternate tax of 18.5% of adjusted total income is applicable. Hence, income tax payable by a partnership firm's profits cannot be less than 18.5 percent (increased by income tax surcharge, education cess, and secondary and higher education cess).

all_sections.heading: Deductions Allowed
all_sections.content:
When computing the liability of income tax on partnership firm as usual based on partnership tax rate, deductions are permitted for the following:

- Remunerations or interest paid to partners that do not conform to the terms of the partnership agreement.
- Salaries, bonuses, remunerations, and commissions are paid to non-working partners of the firm.
- If remuneration paid to partners complies with the partnership deed but relates to transactions that pre-date the partnership deed.

all_sections.content: Partnership Firms can file their ITR for income tax on partnership firms through Form ITR-4 or ITR-5.

all_sections.heading: ITR-4
all_sections.content: ITR-4 is to be filed by those partnership firms which are a Total Income of up to 50 lakh and have income from Business and Profession, which is computed under presumptive basis.

all_sections.heading: ITR-5
all_sections.content: ITR-5 is to be filed by those partnership firms who are required to get their account audited.

all_sections.heading: Income Tax Return for Partnership Firm Due Date
all_sections.content:
The deadline for filing ITR for a partnership firm depends on whether an audit is required:

- If the firm is not subject to an audit, returns must be filed by 31st July.
- If an audit is necessary, the firm must file its returns by 31st October.

all_sections.heading: Filing of GST Returns
all_sections.content: Every GST-registered person is required to file GST Returns, and every partnership firm is required to be under GST if its aggregate annual turnover exceeds Rs. 20 lacs. Usually, the GST-registered partnership firms have to file GSTR-1, GSTR-3B, and GSTR-9 returns. If the firm has opted for a composition scheme, then GSTR-4 is to be filed.

all_sections.heading: TDS Return
all_sections.content:
The TDS Return is to be filed where the partnership firm has a valid TAN, and the type of return to be filed depends upon the purpose of deduction. The types of TDS Return are:

- Form 24Q – TDS on Salary
- Form 27Q – TDS where the deductee is a non-resident, foreign company
- Form 26QB – TDS on payment for transfer of immovable property
- Form 26Q – TDS in any other case

all_sections.content: Books of account are required to be maintained if the partnership firm's sale/turnover/gross receipts from the business is more than Rs. 25,00,000 or the income from the business is more than Rs. 2,50,000 in any of the three preceding years.

all_sections.heading: Tax Audit
all_sections.content: A partnership firm is required to have a tax audit carried out if the sales, turnover, or gross receipts of business exceed the partnership firm audit limit of Rs. 1 crore in the financial year. However, it may be required to get its account audited in certain other circumstances.

[TDS return filing](https://www.indiafilings.com/tds-return-filing/tds-return-filing-guidelines-essential-steps) is a mandatory compliance requirement for every deductor in India. Whether you are an employer deducting tax on salaries or a business deducting TDS on rent and professional fees, timely and accurate filing ensures you remain compliant with the Income Tax Act, 1961. Understanding the complete process helps you avoid penalties and manage your tax obligations efficiently.

## What is Tax Deducted at Source and How Does It Work in India?

Tax Deducted at Source is a mechanism under the Indian taxation system where the payer deducts a certain percentage of tax at the time of payment and deposits it with the government on behalf of the recipient. This system ensures continuous tax collection throughout the financial year rather than a lump sum at year end.

### Types of TDS Deductions in India

- **TDS on salary** – Deducted by employers under Section 192 based on estimated annual income
- **TDS on rent** – Applicable under Section 194I when annual rent exceeds the threshold limit
- **TDS on professional fees** – Covered under Section 194J for payments to professionals and technical service providers
- **TDS on property purchase** – Applicable under Section 194IA when property value exceeds Rs. 50 lakhs
- **TDS for non-residents** – Governed under Section 195 for payments made to non-resident individuals or foreign companies

### Key TDS Rates in India

| Nature of Payment | Section | TDS Rate | Threshold Limit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Salary | 192 | As per slab | Basic exemption limit |
| Rent | 194I | 10% | Rs. 2,40,000 per year |
| Professional Fees | 194J | 10% | Rs. 30,000 per year |
| Property Purchase | 194IA | 1% | Rs. 50,00,000 |
| Non-Resident Payments | 195 | As applicable | Nil |

## How Does the TDS Return Filing Process Work in India?

Filing a **TDS return online** involves submitting quarterly statements that capture all TDS deductions made during that quarter. The process is carried out through the TRACES and Income Tax e-filing portal, and each return must be filed within the specified due dates to avoid interest and penalties.

### Steps to File TDS Return Online in India

1. Register as a deductor on the Income Tax e-filing portal using your TAN
2. Collect all TDS deduction details including PAN of deductees, payment amounts, and TDS amounts
3. Pay the TDS amount using the **TDS challan** through the bank or NSDL portal
4. Download and install the RPU (Return Preparation Utility) from the TRACES website
5. Prepare the TDS return in the correct form — Form 24Q for salary, Form 26Q for others
6. Validate the return using File Validation Utility (FVU)
7. Upload the validated return file on the income tax e-filing portal
8. Download the acknowledgement receipt after successful submission

### TDS Return Forms and Their Applicability

| Form | Nature of Payment | Who Should File |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Form 24Q | TDS on salary | Employers |
| Form 26Q | TDS on non-salary payments | All deductors except salary |
| Form 27Q | TDS on payments to non-residents | Deductors making payments abroad |
| Form 27EQ | Tax collected at source | Collectors under TCS provisions |

## Why Should Businesses in India Comply with TDS Filing Obligations?

**TDS compliance India** is not just a legal obligation — it is a financial safeguard for both deductors and deductees. Non-compliance attracts heavy penalties, interest on late payments, and disallowance of business expenses. - Avoids interest under Section 201(1A) at 1.5% per month on late deposits
- Prevents penalties under Section 271H for late or incorrect filing
- Ensures smooth issuance of **TDS certificate Form 16** to employees
- Maintains deductee credit in Form 26AS for income tax return filing
- Reduces risk of tax notices and scrutiny from the Income Tax Department

## What Are the TDS Return Filing Due Dates in India?

Every deductor must adhere to the quarterly **TDS filing due date** schedule prescribed by the Income Tax Department. Missing these deadlines results in a late filing fee of Rs. 200 per day under Section 234E, which accumulates until the return is filed.

### Quarterly TDS Filing Due Date Calendar

| Quarter | Period | Due Date |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Q1 | April to June | 31st July |
| Q2 | July to September | 31st October |
| Q3 | October to December | 31st January |
| Q4 | January to March | 31st May |

Deductors must also ensure the **TDS payment challan** is deposited by the 7th of the following month for all months except March, where the due date is 30th April.

Before initiating the **TDS filing process India**, it is essential to gather all relevant documents to ensure a smooth and error-free submission. Missing or incorrect details can lead to return rejection or mismatch in deductee records.

## Frequently asked questions

Common questions aboutTax Deducted at Source Filing Online in India Process.

What is TDS Return Filing?

TDS return filing is the process of submitting a quarterly statement to the Income Tax Department that contains details of TDS deducted and deposited by the deductor.

Who needs to file a TDS return?

Any individual or entity that deducts TDS under the Income Tax Act—such as employers, companies, and contractors—is required to file TDS returns quarterly.

What is TAN and why is it necessary?

TAN (Tax Deduction and Collection Account Number) is a 10-digit alphanumeric number mandatory for filing TDS returns and depositing TDS.

What are the different forms used for TDS returns?

- Form 24Q: TDS on salary
- Form 26Q: TDS on non-salary (for residents)
- Form 27Q: TDS on payments to non-residents
- Form 27EQ: Tax Collected at Source (TCS)

When is the TDS return due?

| Quarter | Period | Due Date |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Q1 | Apr–Jun | 31st July |
| Q2 | Jul–Sep | 31st October |
| Q3 | Oct–Dec | 31st January |
| Q4 | Jan–Mar | 31st May |

What happens if I miss the TDS return deadline?

A late fee of ₹200 per day under Section 234E is levied until the return is filed, subject to the TDS amount. Additional penalties may also apply.

Can I revise a TDS return after filing?

Yes, you can revise a TDS return if there are errors like incorrect PAN, challan details, or deduction amount, provided the original return is accepted.

Is TDS return filing mandatory even if no tax was deducted?

No, if there is no TDS deduction in a quarter, then filing a NIL TDS return is not mandatory. However, voluntary NIL filing is advisable for compliance.

What details are needed to file a TDS return?

- TAN and PAN of deductor
- PAN of deductees
- Challan details
- TDS payment amount
- Nature of payment
- Deduction dates

How do I file TDS returns online?

Use the Income Tax e-Filing portal or TRACES. Prepare your return using the RPU (Return Preparation Utility), validate it with FVU (File Validation Utility), and upload it on the portal.

What is Form 16/16A?

These are TDS certificates:

Form 16: Issued for TDS on salary

Form 16A: Issued for TDS on non-salary payments

How can a deductee claim TDS credit?

By filing their income tax return and quoting the correct TDS details reflected in Form 26AS.

What is TRACES in TDS return filing?

TRACES (TDS Reconciliation Analysis and Correction Enabling System) is an official portal for downloading TDS certificates, checking TDS status, and requesting consolidated files.

What is the penalty for non-deduction of TDS?

Interest of 1% per month for late deduction and 1.5% per month for late payment of deducted TDS. Additionally, penalties up to the amount of tax may apply.

Is a digital signature (DSC) mandatory for filing TDS returns?

Yes, for companies and individuals/firms who are required to get their accounts audited under the Income Tax Act.

How is TDS deposited?

TDS is deposited online using Challan ITNS-281 through the NSDL portal. Offline payment via banks is also allowed in some cases.

What is a consolidated TDS file?

It is a file containing all the TDS details filed for a quarter, required for filing a revised TDS return. It is downloadable from TRACES.

What is the role of Form 26AS?

Form 26AS is a tax credit statement that shows the amount of TDS deducted and deposited against a PAN, and is useful for verifying deductions.

What payments attract TDS deduction?

TDS is applicable on salary, interest, rent, contractor payments, professional fees, commission, dividends, etc.

Why should I choose IndiaFilings for TDS filing?

IndiaFilings offers expert support in document preparation, error-free filing, on-time submissions, and legal compliance, ensuring peace of mind and avoiding penalties.

all_sections.heading: What is Tax Deducted at Source and How Does It Work in India?
all_sections.content: Tax Deducted at Source is a mechanism under the Indian taxation system where the payer deducts a certain percentage of tax at the time of payment and deposits it with the government on behalf of the recipient. This system ensures continuous tax collection throughout the financial year rather than a lump sum at year end.

all_sections.heading: Types of TDS Deductions in India
all_sections.content:
- **TDS on salary** – Deducted by employers under Section 192 based on estimated annual income
- **TDS on rent** – Applicable under Section 194I when annual rent exceeds the threshold limit
- **TDS on professional fees** – Covered under Section 194J for payments to professionals and technical service providers
- **TDS on property purchase** – Applicable under Section 194IA when property value exceeds Rs. 50 lakhs
- **TDS for non-residents** – Governed under Section 195 for payments made to non-resident individuals or foreign companies

all_sections.heading: Key TDS Rates in India
all_sections.content:
| Nature of Payment | Section | TDS Rate | Threshold Limit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Salary | 192 | As per slab | Basic exemption limit |
| Rent | 194I | 10% | Rs. 2,40,000 per year |
| Professional Fees | 194J | 10% | Rs. 30,000 per year |
| Property Purchase | 194IA | 1% | Rs. 50,00,000 |
| Non-Resident Payments | 195 | As applicable | Nil |

all_sections.heading: How Does the TDS Return Filing Process Work in India?
all_sections.content: Filing a **TDS return online** involves submitting quarterly statements that capture all TDS deductions made during that quarter. The process is carried out through the TRACES and Income Tax e-filing portal, and each return must be filed within the specified due dates to avoid interest and penalties.

all_sections.heading: Steps to File TDS Return Online in India
all_sections.content:
1. Register as a deductor on the Income Tax e-filing portal using your TAN
2. Collect all TDS deduction details including PAN of deductees, payment amounts, and TDS amounts
3. Pay the TDS amount using the **TDS challan** through the bank or NSDL portal
4. Download and install the RPU (Return Preparation Utility) from the TRACES website
5. Prepare the TDS return in the correct form — Form 24Q for salary, Form 26Q for others
6. Validate the return using File Validation Utility (FVU)
7. Upload the validated return file on the income tax e-filing portal
8. Download the acknowledgement receipt after successful submission

all_sections.content:

| Form 26Q | TDS on non-salary payments | All deductors except salary |
| Form 27Q | TDS on payments to non-residents | Deductors making payments abroad |
| Form 27EQ | Tax collected at source | Collectors under TCS provisions |

all_sections.heading: Why Should Businesses in India Comply with TDS Filing Obligations?
all_sections.content: **TDS compliance India** is not just a legal obligation — it is a financial safeguard for both deductors and deductees. Non-compliance attracts heavy penalties, interest on late payments, and disallowance of business expenses. Businesses that file their [TDS returns](https://www.indiafilings.com/tds-return-filing/tds-return-filing) on time avoid unnecessary litigation and maintain a clean tax record.

all_sections.heading: Benefits of Timely TDS Return Filing

- Prevents penalties under Section 271H for late or incorrect filing
- Ensures smooth issuance of **TDS certificate Form 16** to employees
- Maintains deductee credit in Form 26AS for income tax return filing
- Reduces risk of tax notices and scrutiny from the Income Tax Department

all_sections.heading: What Are the TDS Return Filing Due Dates in India?
all_sections.content: Every deductor must adhere to the quarterly **TDS filing due date** schedule prescribed by the Income Tax Department. Missing these deadlines results in a late filing fee of Rs. 200 per day under Section 234E, which accumulates until the return is filed.

all_sections.heading: Quarterly TDS Filing Due Date Calendar

| Q1 | April to June | 31st July |
| Q2 | July to September | 31st October |

Deductors must also ensure the **TDS payment challan** is deposited by the 7th of the following month for all months except March, where the due date is 30th April.

all_sections.heading: How Much Does TDS Return Filing Cost in India?
all_sections.content: The cost of filing a **TDS return online India** depends on the number of deductee entries, complexity of transactions, and whether you opt for professional assistance. Here is a general overview of the cost structure:

all_sections.heading: TDS Return Filing Cost Overview

all_sections.content: Before initiating the **TDS filing process India**, it is essential to gather all relevant documents to ensure a smooth and error-free submission. Missing or incorrect details can lead to return rejection or mismatch in deductee records.

Common questions aboutTax Deducted at Source Filing Online in India Process.

What is TDS Return Filing?

TDS return filing is the process of submitting a quarterly statement to the Income Tax Department that contains details of TDS deducted and deposited by the deductor.

Who needs to file a TDS return?

Any individual or entity that deducts TDS under the Income Tax Act—such as employers, companies, and contractors—is required to file TDS returns quarterly.

What is TAN and why is it necessary?

TAN (Tax Deduction and Collection Account Number) is a 10-digit alphanumeric number mandatory for filing TDS returns and depositing TDS.

What are the different forms used for TDS returns?

- Form 24Q: TDS on salary
- Form 26Q: TDS on non-salary (for residents)
- Form 27Q: TDS on payments to non-residents
- Form 27EQ: Tax Collected at Source (TCS)

When is the TDS return due?

| Quarter | Period | Due Date |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Q1 | Apr–Jun | 31st July |
| Q2 | Jul–Sep | 31st October |
| Q3 | Oct–Dec | 31st January |
| Q4 | Jan–Mar | 31st May |

What happens if I miss the TDS return deadline?

A late fee of ₹200 per day under Section 234E is levied until the return is filed, subject to the TDS amount. Additional penalties may also apply.

Can I revise a TDS return after filing?

Yes, you can revise a TDS return if there are errors like incorrect PAN, challan details, or deduction amount, provided the original return is accepted.

Is TDS return filing mandatory even if no tax was deducted?

No, if there is no TDS deduction in a quarter, then filing a NIL TDS return is not mandatory. However, voluntary NIL filing is advisable for compliance.

What details are needed to file a TDS return?

- TAN and PAN of deductor
- PAN of deductees
- Challan details
- TDS payment amount
- Nature of payment
- Deduction dates

How do I file TDS returns online?

Use the Income Tax e-Filing portal or TRACES. Prepare your return using the RPU (Return Preparation Utility), validate it with FVU (File Validation Utility), and upload it on the portal.

What is Form 16/16A?

These are TDS certificates:

Form 16: Issued for TDS on salary

Form 16A: Issued for TDS on non-salary payments

How can a deductee claim TDS credit?

By filing their income tax return and quoting the correct TDS details reflected in Form 26AS.

What is TRACES in TDS return filing?

TRACES (TDS Reconciliation Analysis and Correction Enabling System) is an official portal for downloading TDS certificates, checking TDS status, and requesting consolidated files.

What is the penalty for non-deduction of TDS?

Interest of 1% per month for late deduction and 1.5% per month for late payment of deducted TDS. Additionally, penalties up to the amount of tax may apply.

Is a digital signature (DSC) mandatory for filing TDS returns?

Yes, for companies and individuals/firms who are required to get their accounts audited under the Income Tax Act.

How is TDS deposited?

TDS is deposited online using Challan ITNS-281 through the NSDL portal. Offline payment via banks is also allowed in some cases.

What is a consolidated TDS file?

It is a file containing all the TDS details filed for a quarter, required for filing a revised TDS return. It is downloadable from TRACES.

What is the role of Form 26AS?

Form 26AS is a tax credit statement that shows the amount of TDS deducted and deposited against a PAN, and is useful for verifying deductions.

What payments attract TDS deduction?

TDS is applicable on salary, interest, rent, contractor payments, professional fees, commission, dividends, etc.

Why should I choose IndiaFilings for TDS filing?

IndiaFilings offers expert support in document preparation, error-free filing, on-time submissions, and legal compliance, ensuring peace of mind and avoiding penalties.

# TDS Return Filing Online in India

**TDS Return Filing** is a mandatory quarterly compliance requirement for all entities deducting **Tax Deducted at Source (TDS)** in India. Every deductor must file accurate TDS returns on the **income tax e-filing portal** to ensure proper **TDS credit** in the payee's Form 26AS and maintain complete **TDS compliance India**.

For complete end-to-end support, explore [income tax filing](https://www.indiafilings.com/income-tax-filing) services offered by IndiaFilings.

## What is TDS Return Filing?

**TDS Return Filing** is the process of submitting a quarterly statement to the Income Tax Department that contains details of all **TDS deductions** made during that quarter. The return includes details of the **deductor, deductee, PAN, TDS amount deducted, and TDS deposited** in the government account. It is governed under **Section 200(3) of the Income Tax Act, 1961** and is a critical part of [income tax compliance India](https://www.indiafilings.com/income-tax) for all businesses and individuals acting as deductors.

### Why is TDS Return Filing Mandatory in India?

TDS return filing is mandatory because it:

- Enables the **Income Tax Department** to track all tax deductions at source
- Ensures proper **TDS credit in Form 26AS** of the payee or deductee
- Allows the payee to **claim TDS credit** while filing their income tax return
- Establishes proof of **TDS deduction and deposit** by the deductor
- Avoids penalties under **Section 234E** and **Section 271H** of the Income Tax Act
- Ensures compliance with **quarterly TDS return deadlines** for all deductors

### Difference Between TDS and TCS

| Feature | TDS (Tax Deducted at Source) | TCS (Tax Collected at Source) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Who Deducts or Collects | Payer deducts tax before making payment | Seller collects tax from the buyer |
| Applicable On | Salary, rent, interest, professional fees | Sale of goods, scrap, minerals, alcohol |
| Return Form | Form 24Q, 26Q, 27Q | Form 27EQ |
| Governing Section | Chapter XVII-B of Income Tax Act | Section 206C of Income Tax Act |
| Certificate Issued | Form 16 / Form 16A | Form 27D |

## What are the Key Details of TDS Return Filing?

The following overview table covers all essential details about **TDS return filing online in India** that every deductor must know before initiating the quarterly filing process.

| Category | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Governing Section | Section 200(3) of the Income Tax Act, 1961 |
| Filing Frequency | Quarterly – 4 times a year |
| Applicable Forms | Form 24Q, 26Q, 27Q, 27EQ |
| Filing Portal | TRACES Portal (tdscpc.gov.in) and Income Tax e-Filing Portal |
| Verification Mode | Digital Signature Certificate (DSC) or EVC |
| Late Filing Fee | Rs. 200 per day under Section 234E |
| Penalty for Non-Filing | Rs. 10,000 to Rs. 1 lakh under Section 271H |
| TDS Certificate | Form 16 (Salary) / Form 16A (Non-Salary) |
| TAN Requirement | Mandatory for all TDS deductors |

## What are the Types of TDS Returns?

There are **four types of TDS return forms** prescribed by the Income Tax Department. Each form covers a specific category of payment and deductee. Understanding the correct form to use is essential for accurate **quarterly TDS return filing India**.

### Form 24Q – TDS on Salary

[**Form 24Q**](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/tds-form-24q) is filed for reporting **TDS deducted on salary payments** made to employees under Section 192 of the Income Tax Act. It is filed quarterly by all employers and forms the basis for generating **Form 16** for employees. Every employer making salary payments must file Form 24Q every quarter regardless of the number of employees.

### Form 26Q – TDS on Non-Salary Payments

[**Form 26Q**](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/form-26q) is filed for reporting **TDS deducted on non-salary payments** made to residents of India. It covers TDS deducted on rent, interest, professional fees, contractor payments, commission, and all other payments to resident individuals and entities under various TDS sections.

### Form 27Q – TDS on Payments to Non-Residents

[**Form 27Q**](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/form-27q-nri-tds-returns) is filed for reporting **TDS deducted on payments made to non-residents and foreign companies** under Section 195 and other applicable sections. Entities making foreign payments must also ensure compliance with [15CA 15CB filing](https://www.indiafilings.com/15ca-15cb-filing) requirements alongside Form 27Q for complete foreign remittance compliance.

### Form 27EQ – TCS Return

[**Form 27EQ**](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/form-27eq-tcs-return) is filed for reporting **Tax Collected at Source (TCS)** by sellers on specified transactions such as sale of scrap, alcohol, tendu leaves, minerals, and e-commerce transactions under Section 206C of the Income Tax Act.

### TDS Return Forms Comparison Table

| Form | Applicable For | Governing Section | Certificate Generated |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Form 24Q | TDS on Salary | Section 192 | Form 16 |
| Form 26Q | TDS on Non-Salary (Residents) | Sections 193 to 196D | Form 16A |
| Form 27Q | TDS on Payments to Non-Residents | Sections 195, 196A, 196B, 196C, 196D | Form 16A |
| Form 27EQ | TCS on Specified Transactions | Section 206C | Form 27D |

## Who Should File a TDS Return in India?

Under the Income Tax Act, every person or entity responsible for **deducting tax at source** must file quarterly TDS returns. A valid [TAN registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/tan-registration) is mandatory before any TDS return can be filed on the income tax portal. Without an active TAN, the deductor cannot access the TDS filing system or generate TDS certificates for deductees.

### Entities Liable to File TDS Returns

- **Companies** – [Private limited](https://www.indiafilings.com/company-registration), [public limited](https://www.indiafilings.com/public-limited-company), and government companies deducting TDS on salary, rent, and vendor payments
- **[Partnership firms](https://www.indiafilings.com/partnership) and [LLPs](https://www.indiafilings.com/llp-registration)** – For TDS on salary and professional fee payments
- **Individuals and HUFs** – Subject to tax audit under Section 44AB who make applicable payments
- **Government departments** – Central and state government offices making salary and vendor payments
- **[Trusts](https://www.indiafilings.com/trust-registration), societies, and [NGOs](https://www.indiafilings.com/producer-company-registration)** – For TDS on contractor and vendor payments
- **Banks and financial institutions** – For TDS on fixed deposit interest payments
- **E-commerce operators** – For TCS on amounts paid to sellers under Section 206C(1H)

### Who is Exempt from TDS Return Filing?

- Individuals buying immovable property using **Form 26QB** (one-time TDS payment without quarterly return)
- Individuals paying rent using **Form 26QC** under Section 194IB
- Persons not required to deduct TDS under any provision of the Income Tax Act
- Deductors with **nil TDS deduction** for the entire quarter (nil return may still be required)

## What are the Benefits of TDS Return Filing?

Filing **TDS returns accurately and on time** brings significant legal, financial, and operational advantages to businesses and individuals. Entities that maintain consistent TDS compliance also simplify their annual [business tax return filing](https://www.indiafilings.com/business-itr-filing) process by ensuring all TDS credits are correctly reflected in Form 26AS throughout the year.

### Key Benefits of Filing TDS Returns

- **Avoidance of Penalties** – Prevents late filing fee of Rs. 200 per day under Section 234E
- **Correct TDS Credit** – Ensures payees receive accurate TDS credit in Form 26AS and AIS
- **Smooth Income Tax Refunds** – Enables deductees to claim TDS refunds while filing their ITR
- **Legal Compliance** – Fulfils mandatory quarterly obligation under Section 200(3) of the Income Tax Act
- **Issuance of TDS Certificates** – Enables deductors to generate and issue Form 16 and Form 16A to payees
- **Reduced Scrutiny Risk** – Timely filing reduces chances of income tax notices and departmental scrutiny
- **Clean Financial Records** – Maintains accurate books of accounts and reconciliation with GST returns
- **Ease of Annual Filing** – Simplifies income tax return preparation for both deductor and deductee

## What are the TDS Deduction Rates in India?

The **TDS deduction rates in India** vary based on the nature of payment, residency status of the payee, and applicable provisions of the Income Tax Act. Individuals and HUFs with business income who are also subject to TDS deduction must file their annual returns using [ITR 3 Form](https://www.indiafilings.com/itr-3-form) to claim accurate TDS credits and compute net tax liability.

### TDS Rates for Common Payments

| Nature of Payment | Section | TDS Rate (Resident) | Threshold Limit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Salary | Section 192 | As per income tax slab | Above basic exemption limit |
| Interest on Securities | Section 193 | 10% | Rs. 10,000 |
| Interest (other than securities) | Section 194A | 10% | Rs. 40,000 (Rs. 50,000 for senior citizens) |
| Dividend | Section 194 | 10% | Rs. 5,000 |
| Contractor Payments | Section 194C | 1% (Individual/HUF) / 2% (Others) | Rs. 30,000 per payment / Rs. 1 lakh annual |
| Professional and Technical Fees | Section 194J | 10% (Professional) / 2% (Technical) | Rs. 30,000 |
| Rent (Land and Building) | Section 194I | 10% | Rs. 2,40,000 per year |
| Commission and Brokerage | Section 194H | 5% | Rs. 15,000 |
| Purchase of Immovable Property | Section 194IA | 1% | Rs. 50 lakh |
| Payment to Non-Residents | Section 195 | As per DTAA or applicable rate | No threshold – all payments |
| E-Commerce Transactions | Section 194O | 1% | Rs. 5 lakh (for individual/HUF) |

## What are the TDS Return Filing Due Dates for AY 2026-27?

Every deductor must strictly adhere to the **quarterly TDS return due dates** to avoid late filing fees and penalties under the Income Tax Act. The due dates are fixed for all four quarters of the financial year 2025-26.

### Quarterly TDS Return Due Dates AY 2026-27

| Quarter | Period | Due Date for TDS Return Filing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Q1 | April to June 2025 | 31st July 2025 |
| Q2 | July to September 2025 | 31st October 2025 |
| Q3 | October to December 2025 | 31st January 2026 |
| Q4 | January to March 2026 | 31st May 2026 |

### TDS Payment Due Dates

| Category | TDS Payment Due Date |
| --- | --- |
| Government Deductors (without challan) | Same day as deduction |
| Government Deductors (with challan) | 7th of the following month |
| Non-Government Deductors (April to February) | 7th of the following month |
| Non-Government Deductors (March) | 30th April |
| TDS on Property Purchase (Section 194IA) | 30 days from end of month of deduction |

## What Documents are Required for TDS Return Filing?

Having all the required documents ready ensures accurate and error-free **TDS return filing online India**. All deductors must maintain proper records for at least 7 years as per the provisions of the Income Tax Act.

### Documents Required for TDS Return Filing

| Document | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| TAN of the Deductor | Mandatory for all TDS return filings |
| PAN of the Deductor | Required for identity verification on portal |
| PAN of all Deductees | Mandatory for TDS credit in Form 26AS |
| TDS Payment Challans (Form 281) | Proof of TDS deposited in government account |
| Challan Identification Number (CIN) | Required for linking challan to return |
| BSR Code and Date of Deposit | Required for challan verification |
| Salary Details (for Form 24Q) | Employee-wise salary and TDS deduction details |
| Payment Details (for Form 26Q and 27Q) | Nature of payment, amount, and TDS deducted |
| TRACES Login Credentials | Required for accessing TRACES portal for filing |
| Digital Signature Certificate (DSC) | Mandatory for companies and government deductors |

## What is the TDS Return Filing Process?

The **TDS return filing process** involves multiple steps starting from preparation of deductee details to generation of the FVU file and final submission on the TRACES portal. Companies filing their annual corporate tax returns must also ensure their [ITR 6 Form](https://www.indiafilings.com/itr-6-form) is aligned with all quarterly TDS returns filed during the year for seamless reconciliation.

### Overview of TDS Return Filing Process

1. Collect all **deductee PAN details** and payment information for the quarter
2. Verify all **TDS payment challans** and Challan Identification Numbers (CIN)
3. Prepare the TDS return data using **NSDL RPU (Return Preparation Utility)**
4. Validate the prepared data using the **File Validation Utility (FVU)**
5. Generate the **.fvu file** after successful validation
6. Upload the FVU file on the **TRACES portal or income tax e-filing portal**
7. Verify and submit using **Digital Signature Certificate (DSC) or EVC**
8. Download the **acknowledgement receipt (Token Number)** for records

## How to File TDS Return on the Income Tax Portal?

The **income tax e-filing portal** provides a direct interface for filing TDS returns online. Deductors can use this portal to upload the FVU file and complete the submission process seamlessly.

### Step-by-Step Guide to File TDS Return Online

1. Log in to **incometax.gov.in** using your **TAN and password**
2. Navigate to **e-File, then Income Tax Forms, then File Income Tax Forms**
3. Select **Form 24Q, 26Q, 27Q, or 27EQ** as applicable for the quarter
4. Select the **financial year and quarter** for which the return is being filed
5. Upload the **validated FVU file** generated from the NSDL RPU utility
6. Review the **challan and deductee details** on the portal
7. Verify the return using **DSC (mandatory for companies) or EVC**
8. Submit the return and download the **acknowledgement with Token Number**
9. Track the processing status on the **TRACES portal** using the Token Number

### How to File TDS Return Using Offline Utility?

1. Download the **Return Preparation Utility (RPU)** from the NSDL Protean portal

## What is the Penalty for Late TDS Return Filing?

Missing the **TDS return due date** can attract significant penalties and interest under the Income Tax Act. Non-compliance with TDS return obligations can also trigger an [income tax notice](https://www.indiafilings.com/income-tax-notice) from the department, requiring the deductor to respond with complete documentation and payment of outstanding dues.

### Late Filing Fee Under Section 234E

Under **Section 234E**, a **late filing fee of Rs. 200 per day** is levied for every day of delay in filing the TDS return after the due date. The total late filing fee cannot exceed the **total TDS amount** for that quarter. This fee is mandatory and must be paid before filing the belated return.

### Penalty Under Section 271H

In addition to the late filing fee under Section 234E, the Assessing Officer may levy a **penalty ranging from Rs. 10,000 to Rs. 1 lakh** under Section 271H in cases of:

- Failure to file TDS return within **1 year from the due date**
- Furnishing **incorrect information** in the TDS return
- Providing **incorrect PAN details** of deductees
- Quoting **wrong challan details** in the TDS return

### Interest on Late TDS Payment Under Section 201(1A)

| Type of Default | Interest Rate | Period |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Non-deduction of TDS | 1% per month | From date of deductibility to date of actual deduction |
| Deducted but not deposited | 1.5% per month | From date of deduction to date of actual deposit |

## What are the Common Mistakes in TDS Return Filing?

Errors in TDS return filing can result in **mismatches in Form 26AS**, denial of TDS credit to deductees, and penalties from the Income Tax Department. Deductors who have filed incorrect TDS returns can file a [revised return](https://www.indiafilings.com/revised-return) by submitting a **correction statement on the TRACES portal** to rectify all errors before they cause compliance issues.

### Common Errors in TDS Deduction and Filing

- Quoting **incorrect PAN** of deductees leading to TDS credit mismatch
- Entering wrong **Challan Identification Number (CIN)** or BSR code
- Incorrect **nature of payment code** in the TDS return
- Mismatch between **TDS amount deducted and deposited**
- Filing return under **wrong form type**
- Not mentioning **lower deduction certificate details** when applicable
- Omitting transactions where **PAN of deductee is not available**
- Not updating **address and contact details** of the deductor on TRACES

### How to Correct Errors in TDS Returns?

1. Log in to the **TRACES portal** at tdscpc.gov.in using TAN credentials
2. Navigate to **Defaults, then Request for Correction**
3. Select the **financial year, quarter, and form type** to be corrected
4. Choose the **type of correction** – challan, deductee, or salary detail correction

8. Verify using **DSC or EVC** and submit the correction statement

## Frequently asked questions

Common questions aboutTDS Return Online India.

What is TDS?

Tax deduction at source (TDS) means deduction of tax on specified payments by the payer while crediting/paying to the payee and depositing the same to the government on behalf of payee. This mechanism was introduced to reduce tax evasion by the payee.

What is TAN? Which Form in IT Portal provides details of TDS?

TAN stands for Tax Deduction Account Number and it is a 10-digit alphanumeric number alloted to Tax Deductor by IT department. TDS details in respect of deductee are available in Form 26AS.

What is TDS Return?

A TDS return is a quarterly statement submitted by the deductor to the Income Tax Department, summarizing all TDS-related transactions during the quarter. It includes details such as TDS paid, challan details, and PAN of both the deductor and deductee. This statement filled with TDS related details refers to what is TDS return means.

What are the important TDS Returns to be filed by an Assessee?

There are different forms prescribed for different payments:

- **Form 24Q:** For TDS on salaries
- **Form 26Q:** For TDS on all payments other than salaries
- **Form 27Q:** For TDS on payments made to non-residents

What is the Time Limit for remittance of TDS?

- (i) For Tax deducted in April to February, due date for remittance is 7th of succeeding month.
- (ii) For Tax deducted in March, due date for remittance is 30th April.

What are the last TDS return filing dates for various quarters?

TDS returns must be filed quarterly. The last TDS return filing date as follows:

- April to June (Q1): 31st July
- July to September (Q2): 31st October
- October to December (Q3): 31st January
- January to March (Q4): 31st May

What is the late fee payable for delay in filing TDS Return?

As per Section 234E, a Fee at Rs 200 per day shall be levied for the period of delay in filing TDS Return but shall not exceed the amount of tax deductible.

What is the interest payable for delay in deduction of Tax?

If TDS is not deducted on time, interest at 1% per month or part of the month is levied from the date the tax was deductible until the actual date of deduction.

What is the interest payable for delay in remittance of TDS?

If TDS is deducted but not deposited on time, interest at 1.5% per month or part of the month is levied from the date of deduction to the actual date of deposit.

What is the penalty payable for delay in filing/incorrect filing of TDS Return?

As per Section 271H, a penalty ranging from Rs 10,000 to Rs 1,00,000 can be levied for incorrect or non-filing of TDS returns. This penalty is in addition to the interest payable. However, if the return was furnished within one year from the last TDS return date after payment of tax, interest and fees, no penalty shall be levied for the reason of failure to file return within the last TDS return date

What are the provisions related to Prosecution for non-payment of TDS?

Under Section 276B, failure to pay the TDS to the credit of the government within the prescribed time may result in rigorous imprisonment for a term ranging from 3 months to 7 years along with a fine.

What are the provisions related to disallowance of expenses consequent to failure to deduct or deposit Tax on expenses?

**Under Section 40(a)(i)/(ia), if TDS is not deducted or deposited, the expense will be disallowed for computing taxable income:**

- For Domestic Payments: **30%** of the amount of expenses on which TDS was required but not deducted will be disallowed.
- For Payments to Non-Residents: The **entire** amount of expenses will be disallowed.

When TDS is applicable on Salaries? What is the TDS rate?

TDS on Salaries is applicable under Section 192 if ‘Income under the head Salaries’ exceed basic exemption limit. TDS needs to be done at normal slab rate.

When TDS is applicable on Rent? What is the TDS rate?

TDS is applicable under Section 194I if rent exceeds Rs 2,40,000 in a financial year. The TDS rate is 2% in case of Plant & Machinery and 10% in case of Building & other assets.

When TDS is applicable on Payments to Contractors? What is the TDS rate?

TDS is applicable on amount credited or paid to Contractors under Section 194C if amount of single invoice exceeds Rs 30,000 or if aggregate amount of multiple invoices exceed Rs 1,00,000 in financial year. The applicable TDS Rate is 1% if payee is Individual and 2% in case of others.

When TDS is applicable on Professional and Consultancy charges? What is the TDS rate?

TDS is applicable under Section 194J if amount credited or paid exceeds Rs 30,000 in a financial year. The TDS rate is 10% in case of Professional Services and 2% in case of Technical Services.

When TDS is applicable on Commission or Brokerage? What is the TDS rate?

TDS is applicable under Section 194H if amount credited or paid exceeds Rs 15,000 in a financial year. The TDS rate is 2% from 1.10.2024. Prior to 1.10.2024, the TDS rate was 5%.

At what rate TDS needs to be done if payee does not have PAN?

If payee does not have PAN, TDS is applicable at specified rate or 20%, whichever is higher.

What is the procedure of TDS Apply Online?

To TDS apply online, you need to file your TDS return through the Income Tax Department's e-filing portal. Ensure you have a valid TAN, DSC, and the necessary data in the prescribed format. This process involves uploading the TDS return forms (e.g., Form 24Q, 26Q) and verifying them online.

How to Fill TDS Online?

The procedure of how to fill TDS online is followed by: Log in to the Income Tax e-filing portal, download the appropriate TDS return form (e.g., Form 24Q, 26Q), fill it with accurate details of TDS deductions, validate the form, and upload it using a digital signature. Ensure all details match the Form 26AS for reconciliation.

Is TDS applicable on Invoice value including GST or excluding GST?

TDS is applicable on Invoice amount excluding GST.

process_sections.heading: What is TDS Return Filing?
process_sections.content: **TDS Return Filing** is the process of submitting a quarterly statement to the Income Tax Department that contains details of all **TDS deductions** made during that quarter. The return includes details of the **deductor, deductee, PAN, TDS amount deducted, and TDS deposited** in the government account. It is governed under **Section 200(3) of the Income Tax Act, 1961** and is a critical part of [income tax compliance India](https://www.indiafilings.com/income-tax) for all businesses and individuals acting as deductors.

process_sections.heading: Why is TDS Return Filing Mandatory in India?
process_sections.content:
TDS return filing is mandatory because it:

- Enables the **Income Tax Department** to track all tax deductions at source
- Ensures proper **TDS credit in Form 26AS** of the payee or deductee
- Allows the payee to **claim TDS credit** while filing their income tax return
- Establishes proof of **TDS deduction and deposit** by the deductor
- Avoids penalties under **Section 234E** and **Section 271H** of the Income Tax Act
- Ensures compliance with **quarterly TDS return deadlines** for all deductors

process_sections.content: Under the Income Tax Act, every person or entity responsible for **deducting tax at source** must file quarterly TDS returns. Without an active TAN, the deductor cannot access the TDS filing system or generate TDS certificates for deductees.

- **[Partnership firms](https://www.indiafilings.com/partnership) and [LLPs](https://www.indiafilings.com/llp-registration)** – For TDS on salary and professional fee payments

compliance_and_timing_sections.heading: What is TDS Return Filing?
compliance_and_timing_sections.content: **TDS Return Filing** is the process of submitting a quarterly statement to the Income Tax Department that contains details of all **TDS deductions** made during that quarter. The return includes details of the **deductor, deductee, PAN, TDS amount deducted, and TDS deposited** in the government account. It is governed under **Section 200(3) of the Income Tax Act, 1961** and is a critical part of [income tax compliance India](https://www.indiafilings.com/income-tax) for all businesses and individuals acting as deductors.

compliance_and_timing_sections.heading: Why is TDS Return Filing Mandatory in India?
compliance_and_timing_sections.content:
TDS return filing is mandatory because it:

- Enables the **Income Tax Department** to track all tax deductions at source
- Ensures proper **TDS credit in Form 26AS** of the payee or deductee
- Allows the payee to **claim TDS credit** while filing their income tax return
- Establishes proof of **TDS deduction and deposit** by the deductor
- Avoids penalties under **Section 234E** and **Section 271H** of the Income Tax Act
- Ensures compliance with **quarterly TDS return deadlines** for all deductors

| Filing Portal | TRACES Portal (tdscpc.gov.in) and Income Tax e-Filing Portal |

compliance_and_timing_sections.heading: Who Should File a TDS Return in India?
compliance_and_timing_sections.content: Under the Income Tax Act, every person or entity responsible for **deducting tax at source** must file quarterly TDS returns. A valid [TAN registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/tan-registration) is mandatory before any TDS return can be filed on the income tax portal. Without an active TAN, the deductor cannot access the TDS filing system or generate TDS certificates for deductees.

compliance_and_timing_sections.heading: Entities Liable to File TDS Returns
compliance_and_timing_sections.content:
- **Companies** – [Private limited](https://www.indiafilings.com/company-registration), [public limited](https://www.indiafilings.com/public-limited-company), and government companies deducting TDS on salary, rent, and vendor payments
- **[Partnership firms](https://www.indiafilings.com/partnership) and [LLPs](https://www.indiafilings.com/llp-registration)** – For TDS on salary and professional fee payments
- **Individuals and HUFs** – Subject to tax audit under Section 44AB who make applicable payments
- **Government departments** – Central and state government offices making salary and vendor payments
- **[Trusts](https://www.indiafilings.com/trust-registration), societies, and [NGOs](https://www.indiafilings.com/producer-company-registration)** – For TDS on contractor and vendor payments
- **Banks and financial institutions** – For TDS on fixed deposit interest payments
- **E-commerce operators** – For TCS on amounts paid to sellers under Section 206C(1H)

compliance_and_timing_sections.content:
- Individuals buying immovable property using **Form 26QB** (one-time TDS payment without quarterly return)
- Individuals paying rent using **Form 26QC** under Section 194IB
- Persons not required to deduct TDS under any provision of the Income Tax Act
- Deductors with **nil TDS deduction** for the entire quarter (nil return may still be required)
