content_sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
content_sections.content:
Common questions aboutForm 49B TAN Application.

What is Form 49B?

Form 49B is an application form for obtaining a Tax Deduction and Collection Account Number (TAN) or TAN registration. It is required under Section 203A of the Income Tax Act, 1961, for all persons who are responsible for deducting Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) on various transactions.

Who needs to apply for TAN registration using Form 49B?

Any individual, Hindu Undivided Family (HUF), firm, company, trust, association of persons, body of individuals, local authority, or artificial juridical person required to deduct TDS from payments made to others needs to apply for a TAN using Form 49B.

What is the purpose of obtaining a TAN?

The primary purpose of obtaining a TAN is to facilitate the deduction and deposit of TDS by the deductor. It serves as a unique identifier for the deductor and helps the Income Tax Department track and reconcile TDS payments made by various deductors.

How can I obtain Form 49B?

Form 49B can be downloaded from the official website of the Income Tax Department or various other websites that provide tax-related services. It is a PDF form that can be filled out electronically or printed and filled manually.

What information is required to be filled in Form 49B?

Form 49B requires details such as the applicant's name, address, Permanent Account Number (PAN), status (individual, company, firm, etc.), and information about the authorized representative, if applicable. It also requires details of the principal place of business or profession.

Is it mandatory to provide a PAN while applying for TAN?

Yes, providing a valid PAN is mandatory while applying for TAN using Form 49B. If the applicant does not have a PAN, they must apply for one before applying for TAN.

What are the documents required to be submitted along with Form 49B?

The documents required to be submitted along with Form 49B may vary depending on the applicant's status (individual, company, firm, etc.). Generally, proof of identity, proof of address, and proof of business or profession are required.

How long is the TAN valid?

The TAN is a permanent number and does not have an expiry date. However, if there is a change in the name, address, or constitution of the deductor, it needs to be intimated to the Income Tax Department.

Can I apply for TAN online?

Yes, it is possible to apply for TAN online through the Income Tax Department's website or other authorized service providers. The process involves filling out the application form electronically and uploading the required documents.

What are the consequences of not obtaining a TAN when required?

Failure to obtain a TAN when required can lead to penalties and interest charges under the Income Tax Act. It is considered a non-compliance issue, and the deductor may be liable to pay the amount of TDS deducted, along with applicable interest and penalties.

content_sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
content_sections.content:
Common questions aboutFSSAI License Renewal After Expiry.

What is the new policy for renewing the FSSAI License/Registration after the expiry date?

The new policy announced by FSSAI allows Food Business Operators (FBOs) to renew their FSSAI License/Registration even after the expiry date by paying penalties. For the 1st to 90th day after expiry, FBOs need to pay three times the existing annual license/registration fee. From the 91st to 180th day, they need to pay five times the existing annual fee.

Why was this new policy introduced?

Due to the prevailing Covid-19 pandemic, many FBOs failed to renew their License/Registration within the provided time. Previously, they were required to obtain a new License/Registration to continue their food business. This new policy was introduced to facilitate food businesses to continue with the same license number even after the expiry date.

What is the validity period for this new policy?

The policy shall be valid till the date of implementation/operationalization of the FSS (Licensing and Registration of Food Businesses) Amendment Regulations, 2021.

Can FBOs conduct food business during the period between the original expiry date and the issuance of the renewed license?

No, FBOs shall not be permitted to conduct any food business during this period. Any food business conducted during this period will be subject to penalties and punishment as per Section 63 of the FSS Act, 2006.

What happens after the renewed License/Registration is granted?

A fresh validity date will be generated on the grant of the renewed License/Registration.

Is there any condition for FBOs to avail of this new policy?

Yes, this provision of filing a renewal application after the expiry date shall be subjected to online submission of due Annual Returns through FoSCoS by the licensed food manufacturer or importer.

How long after the original expiry date can FBOs avail of this new policy?

FBOs whose license/registration has expired within the last 180 days from the date of issuance of this order can avail of the policy and apply for Renewal of License/Registration through the Food Safety Compliance System, FoSCoS.

What is the prescribed date for FSSAI Renewal?

According to the Food Safety Standard (Licensing and Registration of Food Businesses) Regulations, 2011, FBOs must apply for the Renewal of a license as early as 30 days before the expiry date mentioned in the permit.

What is the late fee for non-renewal of the FSSAI License?

If the Renewal of a license is not filed 30 days before the expiry date, a late fee of Rs. 100 per day is to be paid by FBO, along with the renewal fee. However, this late fee is not applicable in the case of Registration.

What are the steps to apply for FSSAI License Renewal through FoSCoS?

Access the official webpage of the Food Safety Compliance System (FoSCoS), login, navigate to "Renewal" and select "Apply for Renewal of license/registration". Fill in the required details, upload mandatory documents, select the year for which the license is required, choose a payment method, and complete the payment. A receipt with a 17-digit reference number will be generated, which can be used for future reference.

content_sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
content_sections.content:
Common questions aboutDigital Signature Certificate in India: Secure Your Transactions.

What is a Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)?

A Digital Signature Certificate (DSC) is a cryptographically secure key issued by certifying authorities to validate and verify the identity of the person holding the certificate. It is predominantly used for digitally signing documents online, securely authenticating the signature, and validating the signed copy.

What is the difference between a digital signature and a digital signature certificate?

A digital signature is a method of confirming the authenticity of a transaction, document, or message, ensuring that the sender generated it and it was not modified by an external party. On the other hand, a digital signature certificate functions like an identification card issued by recognized authorities, providing details about the certifying authority, the subscriber's name and information, their public key, and the certificate's validity period.

What are the benefits of using a Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)?

Some benefits of using a DSC include authentication (providing legal evidence of authenticity), high security (reducing fraud and document alteration risks), cost-effectiveness (no need for physical presence), time-effectiveness (instant digital signing), and easy verification for government agencies.

What are the different formats of Digital Signature Certificates?

The two common formats of Digital Signature Certificates are PFX File (a file format that can be circulated via email) and USB Token (a pen drive-like device attached to the computer for added security).

What are the different types of Digital Signature Certificates based on their purpose?

The three main types of Digital Signature Certificates based on their purpose are Sign DSC (for signing documents), Encrypt DSC (for encrypting documents), and Sign & Encrypt DSC (for both signing and encrypting documents).

What are the different classes of Digital Signature Certificates?

The three classes of Digital Signature Certificates are Class 1 (for verifying an email address association, no legal validity), Class 2 (for verifying a person's identity against a pre-verified database, used for various filings), and Class 3 (the most secure form used for e-commerce, e-tendering, and various registrations).

What are the key components of a Digital Signature Certificate?

The key components of a Digital Signature Certificate include the public key, the name and email address of the holder, the name of the company, the serial number of the digital ID, and the digital signature of the certifying authority.

How long is a Digital Signature Certificate valid?

Digital Signature Certificates are generally valid for one or two years, but they are renewable. It is recommended to submit the renewal request at least 45 days before the expiry of the current certificate's validity period.

Who are the prescribed authorities to issue Digital Signature Certificates in India?

The Office of the Controller of Certification Agencies under the Information Technology Act, 2000, has appointed eight Certifying Authorities to issue Digital Signature Certificates in India. These include NIC, IDRBT, SafeScrypt CA Services, SIFY Communications Ltd, (n) Code Solutions CA, E-MUDHRA, CDAC, and NSDL, among others.

How can one obtain a Digital Signature Certificate?

To obtain a Digital Signature Certificate, an applicant needs to apply to one of the authorized Certifying Authorities by submitting a signed DSC application along with the required gazette copies of documents. Platforms like IndiaFilings.com offer convenient online services to purchase and obtain Class 3 Digital Signature Certificates with ePass Tokens.

The Digital Signature Certificate will issue in the E-pass token; you can use the DSC to sign the documents digitally:

- Step 1: Attach the USB E-Pass token to the USB Portal
- Step 2: A popup will appear asking for a password; enter the password, Click on approves, and uses the DSC.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Common questions aboutDigital Signature Certificate in India: Secure Your Transactions.

What is a Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)?

A Digital Signature Certificate (DSC) is a cryptographically secure key issued by certifying authorities to validate and verify the identity of the person holding the certificate. It is predominantly used for digitally signing documents online, securely authenticating the signature, and validating the signed copy.

What is the difference between a digital signature and a digital signature certificate?

A digital signature is a method of confirming the authenticity of a transaction, document, or message, ensuring that the sender generated it and it was not modified by an external party. On the other hand, a digital signature certificate functions like an identification card issued by recognized authorities, providing details about the certifying authority, the subscriber's name and information, their public key, and the certificate's validity period.

What are the benefits of using a Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)?

Some benefits of using a DSC include authentication (providing legal evidence of authenticity), high security (reducing fraud and document alteration risks), cost-effectiveness (no need for physical presence), time-effectiveness (instant digital signing), and easy verification for government agencies.

What are the different formats of Digital Signature Certificates?

The two common formats of Digital Signature Certificates are PFX File (a file format that can be circulated via email) and USB Token (a pen drive-like device attached to the computer for added security).

What are the different types of Digital Signature Certificates based on their purpose?

The three main types of Digital Signature Certificates based on their purpose are Sign DSC (for signing documents), Encrypt DSC (for encrypting documents), and Sign & Encrypt DSC (for both signing and encrypting documents).

What are the different classes of Digital Signature Certificates?

The three classes of Digital Signature Certificates are Class 1 (for verifying an email address association, no legal validity), Class 2 (for verifying a person's identity against a pre-verified database, used for various filings), and Class 3 (the most secure form used for e-commerce, e-tendering, and various registrations).

What are the key components of a Digital Signature Certificate?

The key components of a Digital Signature Certificate include the public key, the name and email address of the holder, the name of the company, the serial number of the digital ID, and the digital signature of the certifying authority.

How long is a Digital Signature Certificate valid?

Digital Signature Certificates are generally valid for one or two years, but they are renewable. It is recommended to submit the renewal request at least 45 days before the expiry of the current certificate's validity period.

Who are the prescribed authorities to issue Digital Signature Certificates in India?

The Office of the Controller of Certification Agencies under the Information Technology Act, 2000, has appointed eight Certifying Authorities to issue Digital Signature Certificates in India. These include NIC, IDRBT, SafeScrypt CA Services, SIFY Communications Ltd, (n) Code Solutions CA, E-MUDHRA, CDAC, and NSDL, among others.

How can one obtain a Digital Signature Certificate?

To obtain a Digital Signature Certificate, an applicant needs to apply to one of the authorized Certifying Authorities by submitting a signed DSC application along with the required gazette copies of documents. Platforms like IndiaFilings.com offer convenient online services to purchase and obtain Class 3 Digital Signature Certificates with ePass Tokens.

content_sections.heading: Documents Required for Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)
content_sections.content: A [Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/basics-digital-signature) is a secure digital key that is issued by the certifying authorities to validate and certify the identity of the person holding this certificate. Now, DSC is a statutory requirement for submitting various forms to the Government of India.To obtain a digital signature certificate, the applicant must submit the required documents to the certifying authorities. The types of documents required for DSC differ based on the applicant type. In this article, we provide a comprehensive list of Documents Required for a Digital Signature Certificate (DSC) in India.

content_sections.heading: Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)
content_sections.content: A [Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)](https://www.indiafilings.com/digital-signature) is the equivalent of a physical signature in an electronic format, as it establishes the identity of the sender of an electronic document on the Internet. It’s mandatory for [Company Registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/company-registration), [GST Registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-registration),[Trademark Registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/trademark-filing), [Income Tax Filings](https://www.indiafilings.com/income-tax-filing), and Many other Government Forms like Tenders.

content_sections.heading: Documents Required for Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)
content_sections.content:
The Documents Required for DSC are mainly classified into four categories, which are as follows:

- Documents Required for Indian Nationals
- Documents Required for an Indian Organization
- Documents Required for Foreign Nationals
- Documents Required for Foreign Organization

content_sections.heading: Documents Required for Indian Nationals
content_sections.content: The following documents are required to get Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)

content_sections.heading: Identity Proof
content_sections.content:
The applicant can submit any one of the following documents as Identity Proof:

- [Aadhar Card](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/procedure-to-update-aadhaar-card) (eKYC Service)
- Passport
- [PAN Card](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/epan) of the Applicant
- Driving Licence
- Post Office ID Card
- Bank Account Passbook containing the photograph and signed by an individual with attestation by the concerned Bank official
- Any Government-issued photo ID card bearing the signatures of the individual
- Photo ID card issued by the Ministry of Home Affairs of Centre (MHA) or State Governments

content_sections.heading: Address Proof
content_sections.content:
- Aadhar Card (eKYC Service)
- Telephone Bill
- Voter ID Card
- Driving Licence (DL)/Registration Certificate (RC)
- Water Bill - Not older than 2 months
- Electricity Bill -  Not older than 2 months
- Latest Bank Statements signed by the bank - Not older than 2 Months
- GST  registration certificate
- Property Tax or Corporation or Municipal Corporation Receipt
- Any Government issued photo ID having a Name and address

content_sections.heading: Documents Required for Indian Organization
content_sections.content: Documents Required for Indian Organization are listed as follows:

content_sections.heading: Company
content_sections.content:
- Copy of Organizational PAN Card, If GST number is not provided
- Copy of Recent Bank Statement / Bank Certificate, If GST number is not provided
- Copy of Incorporation, If GST number is not provided
- Proof of Authorized Signatory - List of Directors / Board Resolution / Resolution
- Authorized Signatory ID Proof - Organizational ID Card / PAN Card / etc
- Copy of Applicant PAN Card

content_sections.heading: Partnership Firm
content_sections.content:
- Copy of Organizational PAN Card, If GST number is not provided
- Copy of Recent Bank Statement / Bank Certificate, If GST number is not provided
- Copy of Partnership deed containing a list of Partners / Authorization Letter
- Authorized Signatory ID Proof - Organizational ID Card / PAN Card / etc
- Copy of Applicant PAN Card

content_sections.heading: Proprietorship
content_sections.content:
- Copy of Recent Bank Statement / Bank Certificate, If GST Number is not provided
- Copy of Business Registration Certificate -  Shop and Establishment (S&E) /etc
- Authorized Signatory ID Proof  - Organizational ID Card or PAN Card
- Copy of Applicant PAN Card

content_sections.heading: AOP / BOI - An association of persons or a body of individuals
content_sections.content:
- Copy of Organizational PAN Card, If GST number is not provided

- Copy of Recent Bank Statement / Bank Certificate, If GST number is not provided
- Copy of Incorporation, If GST number is not provided
- Proof of Authorized Signatory - List of Directors / Board Resolution / Resolution
- Authorized Signatory ID Proof - Organizational ID Card / PAN Card / etc
- Copy of Applicant PAN Card

content_sections.heading: Limited Liability Partnership (LLP)
content_sections.content:
- Copy of Organizational PAN Card, If GST number is not provided
- Copy of Recent Bank Statement / Bank Certificate, If GST number is not provided
- Copy of Incorporation, If GST number is not provided
- Proof of Authorized Signatory - List of Directors / Board Resolution / Resolution
- Authorized Signatory ID Proof - Organizational ID Card / PAN Card / etc
- Copy of Applicant PAN Card

content_sections.heading: Non-governmental organization/Trust
content_sections.content:
- Copy of Organizational PAN Card, if GST number not provided
- Copy of Recent Bank Statement / Bank Certificate, If GST No. not provided
- Copy of Incorporation, if GST number not provided
- Proof of Authorized Signatory - List of Directors or Board Resolution or Resolution
- Authorized Signatory ID Proof - Organizational ID Card / PAN Card / etc
- Copy of Applicant PAN Card

content_sections.heading: Documents Required for Foreign Nationals
content_sections.content: The Foreign National needs to submit the following documents:

content_sections.heading: Identity Proof
content_sections.content:
The following documents are mandatory for getting the DSC.

- Attested copy of Applicant Passport
- If the applicant is out of a foreign country- Attested copy of VISA
- If the applicant is in India - Attested copy of Resident Permit certificate

content_sections.heading: Address Proof
content_sections.content:
The following documents are mandatory for getting the DSC

- Attested copy of Applicant Passport
- Attested copy of any other Government issued Address Proof

content_sections.heading: Documents Required for Foreign Organization
content_sections.content:
| | | | --- | --- | | **Identity Proof (All are mandatory)** | **Address Proof (All are mandatory)** | | - Attested copy of Applicant Passport
- Attested copy of VISA (If the applicant is out of the native country).
- Attested copy of Resident Permit certificate (If the applicant is in India) | - Attested copy of Applicant Passport
- Attested copy of any other Government issued Address Proof |

content_sections.heading: Foreign Attestation
content_sections.content:
The identity and address proof of foreign nationals must be attested by the following authorities:

- Embassy of Native Country (If the applicant is not a citizen of India)
- Apostilized by Native Country, after Public Notary (if the country is in Hague Convention)
- Consularized by Native Country, after Public Notary (if the country is not in Hague Convention)

content_sections.heading: General Instructions
content_sections.content:
Follow the general instructions listed below while furnishing the digital signature application form:

- The signature of the applicant should be in Blue Ink only
- The signature of the applicant should be as it is in Identity Proof
- A photo of the applicant in the application form should be signed by the applicant
- All supporting documents should be attested by either of Gazetted Officer / Bank Manager / Post Master
- For proof of attesting officer, either one of the below is mandatory –
- Contact Details of Attesting Officer including the name, designation, office address, and contact number. This should be part of the attestation. If provided separately, it should be attested either by the Applicant or Attesting Officer; or
- Self-Attested copy of Organizational Identity card of Attesting Officer
- Organizational Documents can also be attested by Authorized Signatory. However, if the taxpayer fails to get the Organizational Documents attested by the authorized signatory, in such cases an attested copy of the organizational ID card of the authorized signatory is mandatory.

content_sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
content_sections.content:
Common questions aboutDocuments Required for Digital Signature Certificate India.

What is a Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)?

A Digital Signature Certificate (DSC) is a secure digital key issued by certifying authorities to validate and certify the identity of the person holding the certificate. It serves as an electronic equivalent of a physical signature and is mandatory for various online transactions and submissions with the Government of India.

Why is a DSC required?

A DSC is a statutory requirement for submitting various forms to the Government of India, such as Company Registration, GST Registration, Trademark Registration, Income Tax Filings, and many other government forms like tenders. It ensures secure and authentic electronic transactions and communications.

What documents are required for an Indian national to obtain a DSC?

For an Indian national, the primary documents required for a DSC include an identity proof (Aadhaar Card, Passport, PAN Card, Driving License, etc.), and an address proof (Aadhaar Card, utility bills, bank statements, etc.).

What documents are needed for an Indian organization to obtain a DSC?

Indian organizations must provide their organizational PAN card, GST registration certificate (if applicable), bank statements, proof of incorporation, proof of authorized signatory, and the authorized signatory's ID proof.

Can foreign nationals and organizations obtain a DSC in India?

Yes, foreign nationals and organizations can obtain a DSC in India. They must submit attested copies of their passport, visa/resident permit certificate, and other government-issued identity and address proof documents.

What is the process for attesting documents for foreign nationals and organizations?

The identity and address proof documents of foreign nationals and organizations must be attested by the embassy of their native country, apostilled or consularized, and attested by a public notary, depending on whether their country is part of the Hague Convention or not.

Are there any specific instructions for signing the DSC application form?

Yes, there are specific instructions for signing the DSC application form. The applicant's signature should be in blue ink, matching their identity proof, and their photograph in the application form should be signed by the applicant.

Who can attest the supporting documents for a DSC application?

Supporting documents can be attested by a Gazetted Officer, Bank Manager, Post Master, or the authorized signatory of the organization. If attested by an authorized signatory, an attested copy of their organizational ID card is required.

How recent should the address proof documents be?

For address proof, documents like utility bills (water, electricity) should not be older than 2 months, and bank statements should not be older than 2 months from the date of application.

Can an applicant use the same documents for identity and address proof?

Yes, if the identity proof document (like an Aadhaar Card or Driving License) also contains the applicant's address, it can be used as both identity and address proof.

Indian organizations must provide their organizational PAN card, GST registration certificate (if applicable), bank statements, proof of incorporation, proof of authorized signatory, and the authorized signatory's ID proof. Can foreign nationals and organizations obtain a DSC in India? Yes, foreign nationals and organizations can obtain a DSC in India. They must submit attested copies of their passport, visa/resident permit certificate, and other government-issued identity and address proof documents. What is the process for attesting documents for foreign nationals and organizations? The identity and address proof documents of foreign nationals and organizations must be attested by the embassy of their native country, apostilled or consularized, and attested by a public notary, depending on whether their country is part of the Hague Convention or not. Are there any specific instructions for signing the DSC application form? Yes, there are specific instructions for signing the DSC application form. The applicant's signature should be in blue ink, matching their identity proof, and their photograph in the application form should be signed by the applicant. Who can attest the supporting documents for a DSC application? Supporting documents can be attested by a Gazetted Officer, Bank Manager, Post Master, or the authorized signatory of the organization. If attested by an authorized signatory, an attested copy of their organizational ID card is required. How recent should the address proof documents be? For address proof, documents like utility bills (water, electricity) should not be older than 2 months, and bank statements should not be older than 2 months from the date of application. Can an applicant use the same documents for identity and address proof? Common questions aboutDSC Software Download.

What is a Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)?

A Digital Signature Certificate (DSC) is a cryptographically secure key issued by certifying authorities to validate and verify the identity of the person who holds this certificate. It is primarily used for digitally signing documents online, securely authenticating the signature, and validating the signed copy.

Why is a DSC stored on a hardware device like a USB token?

For security reasons, the Digital Signature Certificate is stored on a hardware device called a Cryptographic USB Token, also known as ePass. The USB token can only hold the DSC, ensuring that the certificate is securely protected and cannot be accessed or tampered with easily.

What is the purpose of installing DSC Software?

DSC Software needs to be installed to use the DSC token. This software enables users to access and utilize the Digital Signature Certificate stored on the USB token for various purposes, such as e-signing documents, filing MCA forms, income tax returns, and GST Returns.

How can I obtain a Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)?

To obtain a Digital Signature Certificate, you need to submit a signed DSC application along with gazette copies of required documents to a Certifying Authority. Alternatively, you can purchase a Class 3 Digital Signature with an ePass Token from a trusted provider like IndiaFilings.com.

What is the validity period of a Class 3 Digital Signature from IndiaFilings.com?

IndiaFilings.com offers Class 3 Digital Signatures with a validity of 2 years, along with a secure USB token (ePass) to protect the Signature until the end of its validity period.

How do I download and install the e-pass 2003 token driver?

To download and install the e-pass 2003 token driver, follow these steps: 1) Download and install the driver before plugging in the USB token. 2) After installation, plug the USB token into your computer's USB port and enter the password. 3) You can change the password by selecting the "CHANGE USER PIN" option.

What should I avoid doing with the e-pass 2003 token driver?

Never click the initialize/delete button in the e-pass 2003 driver menu, as it will delete the Digital Certificate and make the Token unusable. Also, never lose the password for your USB token or inadvertently enter the wrong password multiple times, as there is no way to retrieve or use the Digital Signature in such cases.

How do I use a Class 3 Digital Signature with an ePass Token?

To use a Class 3 Digital Signature with an ePass Token, follow these steps: 1) Attach the USB e-Pass token to the USB port. 2) A popup will appear asking for a password; enter the password and click "Approve" to use the DSC.

What are the common applications of a Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)?

A Digital Signature Certificate (DSC) is commonly used for e-signing documents, filing MCA forms, income tax returns, GST Returns, and various other online transactions that require secure authentication and validation of the signer's identity.

What precautions should I take with my Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)?

When using a Digital Signature Certificate (DSC), it is essential to follow these precautions: 1) Never lose the password for your USB token. 2) Avoid entering the wrong password multiple times, as it may lock the token. 3) Unplug the USB token from your computer after use and store it in a safe place. 4) Never click the initialize/delete button in the token driver menu.

content_sections.heading: Food Business Annual Return
content_sections.content: The [Food Business](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/starting-food-manufacturing-business) Annual Return is crucial for food businesses to comply with regulatory standards. This article explores the importance of the annual return, its purpose, and the key information it entails. By understanding the significance of this document, food businesses can ensure compliance, maintain food safety, and contribute to consumer trust. Additionally, we will discuss the filing process of the FOSCOS annual return, FSSAI annual return fees and the consequences of non-compliance. Stay informed about the FSSAI Annual Return Filing along with FSSAI annual return due date to meet regulatory obligations and operate with integrity in the food industry.

content_sections.heading: Online Food Business Annual Return Filing
content_sections.content: The [Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI)](https://www.indiafilings.com/fssai), on December 18, 2020, issued a Notification regarding the Revised Guidelines for FSSAI Annual Return Filing. With this notification, FSSAI mandates online submission of Annual Return by Food Businesses involved in the manufacturing and importing food products with effect from F.Y. 2020-2021. The revised format of the Annual Return has already been incorporated into Food Safety Compliance System (FOSCOS), and the window for return filing for F.Y. 2022-2023 is opened.

content_sections.heading: Food Business Annual Return
content_sections.content: Following the regulations set by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), every food business holding an FSSAI license must file a separate annual return. This obligation applies to each license held, regardless of whether the same Food Business Operator possesses multiple licenses.

content_sections.heading: Purpose of the Food Business Annual Return
content_sections.content:

content_sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
content_sections.content:
Common questions aboutFood Business Annual Return.

What is a Food Business Annual Return?

A Food Business Annual Return is a crucial document that food businesses holding an FSSAI license must file annually to comply with regulatory standards set by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI). It provides vital information to the FSSAI regarding the business's activities, including the production, handling, storage, and distribution of food products.

Why is filing the Food Business Annual Return important?

Filing the Food Business Annual Return is essential for food businesses to maintain transparency in their operations and ensure compliance with FSSAI regulations. Failure to comply with this requirement may result in penalties or even the suspension of the FSSAI license, jeopardizing the business's operations.

What is the due date for filing the Food Business Annual Return?

According to FSSAI regulations, all licensed Manufacturers and Importers must submit their FSSAI Annual Return by May 31 of every year for the activities conducted during the preceding Financial Year. It is crucial to file the returns before the FSSAI annual return due date to avoid penalties.

What are the key details required for filing the Food Business Annual Return?

The Food Business Operator (FBO) needs to provide details such as the name of the food products manufactured or imported, their quantity, selling price, value, imported quantity, and the list of countries or ports where the food products are imported.

What types of food businesses are eligible for filing the Food Business Annual Return?

Food manufacturers, labellers, importers, packers, and every FBO, including those dealing in milk and milk products, need to file the FSSAI Annual Return online in Form D1 to the Food Licensing Authority.

Are there any exemptions from filing the Food Business Annual Return?

Yes, according to FSSAI regulations, fast food joints, restaurants, grocery stores, and canteens are exempted from filing the FSSAI Annual Return.

What is the penalty for late or non-submission of the Food Business Annual Return?

Any delay in filing the Food Business Annual Return beyond May 31 each year shall attract a penalty of Rs.100 per day for the delay until the date of filing the return. The maximum penalty levied shall not exceed five times the annual license fees.

What is the revised format of the Food Business Annual Return?

FSSAI has introduced a revised format for the Annual Return, which has been incorporated into the Food Safety Compliance System (FOSCOS). The revised format aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the business's activities and compliance with food safety regulations.

Can a single Food Business Operator file one Annual Return for multiple licenses?

No, a food business must file a separate Food License Annual Return for every FSSAI license issued under the FSSAI regulations, irrespective of whether the same Food Business Operator holds more than one license.

What are the benefits of the revised format for the Food Business Annual Return?

The revised format for the Annual Return offers benefits such as eliminating the need for physical records, saving businesses from inadvertent penalties, enabling digital reminders for submission, facilitating country/state-wise data analysis, and providing updated data on business activities.

ICEGATE (Indian Customs Electronic Gateway) is the national portal established by the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) in India. What is the purpose of ICEGATE simplified registration?

The ICEGATE simplified registration process is designed to help importers and exporters quickly access the portal's services without the need for a Digital Signature Certificate (DSC). Who can register for ICEGATE?

What are the benefits of ICEGATE registration?

It streamlines the import and export processes, enhancing efficiency and transparency.

content_sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
content_sections.content:
Common questions aboutDirectorate General of Foreign Trade India.

What is DGFT and what are its primary functions?

DGFT or the Directorate General of Foreign Trade is India's official administrating body for imports and exports. Its primary functions include formulating and implementing various trade policies, particularly the Foreign Trade Policy, conducting research and analysis on policies, licensing of imports and exports, regulating and controlling exports and imports, and playing an advisory role to the Government on policy measures related to national and international economic scenarios.

What is an IEC code and why is it important?

An IEC (Importer Exporter Code) code is a unique identification number that must be obtained by all exporters and importers engaged in the import or export of commodities in India. It is important because it is mandatory for any individual or entity involved in import or export activities, and processing IEC code applications is one of the major tasks undertaken by the DGFT.

What is the SCOMET list and how does DGFT regulate it?

The SCOMET (Special, Chemicals, Organisms, Materials, Equipment and Technologies) list comprises eight categories of sensitive items, including toxic chemical agents, micro-organisms, toxins, aerospace systems, information technology, nuclear materials, and related equipment and technologies. These items can be utilized for both civilian and military purposes. Exports of items under this list are stringently regulated by DGFT.

How does DGFT administer the Foreign Trade Policy?

DGFT is responsible for the complete administration and management of the Foreign Trade Policy. Through this policy, the Government primarily focuses on promoting traditional and sunrise sectors of exports, including services, and simplifying the process of doing business.

Where are the zonal offices of DGFT located?

DGFT has zonal offices located in Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, and Chennai, in addition to several other regional offices across various cities in India, such as Jaipur, Ludhiana, Kanpur, Varanasi, Amritsar, Chandigarh, Panipat, Jammu, Dehradun, Srinagar, Ahmedabad, Pune, Vadodara, Indore, Panaji, Rajkot, Surat, Chhattisgarh, Nagpur, Cuttack, Guwahati, Patna, Shillong, Bangalore, Kochi, Trivandrum, Hyderabad, Coimbatore, Madurai, Puducherry, and Vishakhapatnam.

What role does DGFT play in promoting exports and infrastructure development?

DGFT plays a crucial role in promoting exports and infrastructure development by assisting states in developing their infrastructure for exports, identifying towns with export potential and providing them with amenities for growth, funding export promotion councils, industry and trade associations, and agencies of state governments on various export-related endeavors, and providing financial aid for the development of marketing and meeting expenses related to trade.

How does DGFT facilitate the establishment of Export Oriented Units and Special Economic Zones?

DGFT facilitates the development of Export Oriented Units, Special Economic Zones, Technology and Bio-Tech parks by allowing them to import capital goods and services at a discounted rate of customs duty, thereby promoting the growth of these specialized zones and units.

What are the main categories of items regulated by DGFT?

DGFT regulates the import and export of various categories of items, including traditional export sectors, sunrise sectors (emerging industries), services, and sensitive items listed under the SCOMET (Special, Chemicals, Organisms, Materials, Equipment and Technologies) list.

How can exporters and importers obtain an IEC code from DGFT?

Exporters and importers can obtain an IEC (Importer Exporter Code) from DGFT by submitting an application, either online or through one of the DGFT's regional offices. The IEC code is valid for the entire lifetime of the individual or entity and does not need to be renewed.

What is the purpose of DGFT's zonal and regional offices across India?

DGFT's zonal and regional offices across various cities in India serve the purpose of facilitating trade activities, processing applications for IEC codes and licenses, providing assistance and guidance to exporters and importers, and implementing the Foreign Trade Policy and other trade-related regulations at the local level.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Common questions aboutDirectorate General of Foreign Trade India.

What is DGFT and what are its primary functions?

DGFT or the Directorate General of Foreign Trade is India's official administrating body for imports and exports. Its primary functions include formulating and implementing various trade policies, particularly the Foreign Trade Policy, conducting research and analysis on policies, licensing of imports and exports, regulating and controlling exports and imports, and playing an advisory role to the Government on policy measures related to national and international economic scenarios.

What is an IEC code and why is it important?

An IEC (Importer Exporter Code) code is a unique identification number that must be obtained by all exporters and importers engaged in the import or export of commodities in India. It is important because it is mandatory for any individual or entity involved in import or export activities, and processing IEC code applications is one of the major tasks undertaken by the DGFT.

What is the SCOMET list and how does DGFT regulate it?

The SCOMET (Special, Chemicals, Organisms, Materials, Equipment and Technologies) list comprises eight categories of sensitive items, including toxic chemical agents, micro-organisms, toxins, aerospace systems, information technology, nuclear materials, and related equipment and technologies. These items can be utilized for both civilian and military purposes. Exports of items under this list are stringently regulated by DGFT.

How does DGFT administer the Foreign Trade Policy?

DGFT is responsible for the complete administration and management of the Foreign Trade Policy. Through this policy, the Government primarily focuses on promoting traditional and sunrise sectors of exports, including services, and simplifying the process of doing business.

Where are the zonal offices of DGFT located?

DGFT has zonal offices located in Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, and Chennai, in addition to several other regional offices across various cities in India, such as Jaipur, Ludhiana, Kanpur, Varanasi, Amritsar, Chandigarh, Panipat, Jammu, Dehradun, Srinagar, Ahmedabad, Pune, Vadodara, Indore, Panaji, Rajkot, Surat, Chhattisgarh, Nagpur, Cuttack, Guwahati, Patna, Shillong, Bangalore, Kochi, Trivandrum, Hyderabad, Coimbatore, Madurai, Puducherry, and Vishakhapatnam.

What role does DGFT play in promoting exports and infrastructure development?

DGFT plays a crucial role in promoting exports and infrastructure development by assisting states in developing their infrastructure for exports, identifying towns with export potential and providing them with amenities for growth, funding export promotion councils, industry and trade associations, and agencies of state governments on various export-related endeavors, and providing financial aid for the development of marketing and meeting expenses related to trade.

How does DGFT facilitate the establishment of Export Oriented Units and Special Economic Zones?

DGFT facilitates the development of Export Oriented Units, Special Economic Zones, Technology and Bio-Tech parks by allowing them to import capital goods and services at a discounted rate of customs duty, thereby promoting the growth of these specialized zones and units.

What are the main categories of items regulated by DGFT?

DGFT regulates the import and export of various categories of items, including traditional export sectors, sunrise sectors (emerging industries), services, and sensitive items listed under the SCOMET (Special, Chemicals, Organisms, Materials, Equipment and Technologies) list.

How can exporters and importers obtain an IEC code from DGFT?

Exporters and importers can obtain an IEC (Importer Exporter Code) from DGFT by submitting an application, either online or through one of the DGFT's regional offices. The IEC code is valid for the entire lifetime of the individual or entity and does not need to be renewed.

What is the purpose of DGFT's zonal and regional offices across India?

DGFT's zonal and regional offices across various cities in India serve the purpose of facilitating trade activities, processing applications for IEC codes and licenses, providing assistance and guidance to exporters and importers, and implementing the Foreign Trade Policy and other trade-related regulations at the local level.

content_sections.heading: Import Export Code (IE Code)
content_sections.content:
Import & Export Code is to be obtained by the business entity for import into or export from India. Import & Export Code is popularly known as the IEC number. Import & Export Code is a ten-digit unique number issued by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT).IEC registration certificate is mandatory for a business involved in import and export. Hence, before initiating an import of goods into India, an importer must ensure that the importing entity has [GST registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-registration) and IE code – both of which are required to clear customs.If an importer does not have both IE code and GST Registration, the goods will be stuck at the port and start incurring demurrage charges or could be destroyed.

[Know more about GST on import](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/igst-on-imports)

content_sections.heading: Importance of Import Export Cod e
content_sections.content:
Businesses have a great option to enter the international market with the export and [import](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/dgft-online-module-for-import-authorization) of the products and the services they are involved in. The IE code is an essential requirement while entering the global market as it supports the growth and development of the business to a certain extent. There are various advantages of getting an Import Export Code.

![IEC_72](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2018/04/IEC_72.png)Here we have listed a few of them:

- **International market unlocks:** As the IE Code is a requirement for the import and export business, they allow the products to reach the global market. IE code makes the entry of the international Indian company smoother and opens doors for growth and expansion.
- **Online registration**: The process to find the IE Code is entirely [online](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/registration-of-iecs-in-the-new-dgft-platform) and hassle-free with short document submission.
- **Less document requirement:** It is not required to submit many documents to obtain an IEC.
- **Lifetime Validity:** IE Code is a lifetime registration valid as long as the business exists. Hence, there are no issues with updating, filing, and renewing Import Export Code registration. The IE registration is valid until the company exists or the registration is not revoked or surrendered.
- **Reduces illegal goods transportation**: The most basic requirement for the [Import-Export code](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/procedure-for-obtaining-import-export-code) is that you need to provide authentic information. Without giving proper information, IE code cannot be obtained. This criterion makes the transportation of illegal goods impossible.
- Availing Several Benefits **:** IE code has enormous benefits for importers and exporters. The registered business entities can get help through subsidies from the Customs, Export Promotion Council or other authorities. With LUT filing under GST, the exporters can make exports without paying taxes. If the exports are made with tax payment, the exporter can claim the refunds of the paid tax amount.
- **Compliances:** Unlike other tax registration, the person carrying import or export does not require to fulfill any specific compliance requirements such as the annual filing or the return filings.

content_sections.heading: Validity of IE Code
content_sections.content: As mentioned above, IE Code registration is permanent and valid for a lifetime. Hence, there will be no hassles with updating, filing, and renewing the IEC registration. It is valid till the business exists or the registration is not revoked or surrendered. Further, unlike tax registrations like GST registration or [PF registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/pf-registration), the importer or exporter does not require to file any filings or follow any other compliance requirements like annual filing.As IE code registration is one-time and requires no additional compliance, it is recommended for all exporters & importers to obtain IE code after incorporation.

content_sections.heading: Nature of the Firm obtaining an IEC
content_sections.content:
The nature of the Firm obtaining an IEC may be any of the follows:

- Proprietorship Firm
- Partnership Firm
- Limited Liability Partnership
- Limited Company
- Trust
- Hindu Undivided Family (HUF)

content_sections.heading: Pre-Requisites for Applying for IEC
content_sections.content:
- Valid Login Credentials to DGFT Portal (After Registering on DGFT Portal)
- IEC may be applied on behalf of a firm which may be a Proprietorship, Partnership, LLP, Limited Company, Trust, HUF, and Society.
- The Firm must have an active Firm's Permanent Account Number (PAN) and details like Name as per Pan, Date of Birth, or Incorporation.
- The Firm must also have a bank account in the Name of the Firm and a valid address before applying.

Note: These details will be validated with the Income Tax Department site.

content_sections.heading: Documents required for IEC Code registration
content_sections.content:
The list of scanned documents required for IEC Registration is listed as follows:

- Proof of establishment/incorporation/registration: The following type of Firm needs to submit the establishment/incorporation/registration certificate:

  - Partnership
  - Registered Society
  - Trust
  - HUF
  - Other

- Proof of Address: Proof of Address can be any one of the following documents:

  - Sale Deed
  - Rent agreement
  - Lease deed
  - Electricity bill
  - Telephone landline bill
  - Mobile, post-paid bill
  - MoU
  - Partnership deed
  - Other acceptable documents (for proprietorship only):

    - Aadhar card
    - Passport
    - Voter id

Note: In case the address proof is not in the Name of the applicant firm, a no objection certificate (NOC) by the firm premises owner in favor of the Firm, along with the address proof, is to be submitted as a single PDF document.

- Proof of Firm's Bank Account

  - Canceled Cheque
  - Bank Certificate

- User should have an active DSC or Aadhaar of the Firm's member for submission.
- Active Firm's Bank accounts for entering its details in the Application and making online payment of the application fee.

content_sections.heading: Application Fee for IEC
content_sections.content: The User must pay Rs.500 as the Application fee to get the IEC certificate.

content_sections.heading: Procedure to submit IE Code Application
content_sections.content:
The procedure to get the Importer Exporter Code Certificate is explained in detail below:Visit the official DGFT website. Click on the 'Services' tab on the homepage and Select the 'IEC Profile Management' option from the drop-down list.

![Importer-Exporter-Code-IEC-DGFT-Homepage](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2018/04/Importer-Exporter-Code-IEC-DGFT-Homepage.jpg)

A new page will open. Click on the 'Apply for IEC' option on the Page.

content_sections.heading: DGFT User Registration
content_sections.content:
- Click on the 'Register' option. Enter the required details and click on the 'Sent OTP' button.
- Enter the OTP and click on the 'Register' button.

![Importer-Exporter-Code-IEC-DGFT-Registration](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2018/04/Importer-Exporter-Code-IEC-DGFT-Registration.jpg)

Importer Exporter Code (IEC) - DGFT Registration

- Upon successfully validating the OTP, the User will receive a notification containing the temporary password, which can change after logging into the DGFT website.
- After registering on the DGFT website, log in to the website by entering the user name and password.

![Importer-Exporter-Code-IEC-DGFT-Login](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2018/04/Importer-Exporter-Code-IEC-DGFT-Login.jpg)

Importer Exporter Code (IEC) - DGFT Login

content_sections.heading: Apply for IEC
content_sections.content:
- Post login, click on "Apply for IEC" on the Dashboard. Click on the "Start Fresh Application" button or the "Proceed with Existing Application" button if the User has already saved a draft application.
- Fill out the application form (ANF 2A format), and Enter the details in the General Information Section:

  - Select nature of Concern/Firm
  - Enter Firm Name
  - PAN Details
  - Select Preferred Activities
  - Enter corporate entity number (CIN)
  - Enter GSTIN Number of Concern/Firm
  - Enter Firm Mobile Number
  - Firm Mail ID
  - Enter firm address
  - Attach address proof of the Firm
  - Enter the details in the "Details of Proprietor/Partner/Director/Karta/Managing Trustee" Section
  - Enter the details in the "Bank Account Details" Section
  - Enter the details in the "Other Details (Exports Sectors preferred)" Section

- Under the declaration, accept the terms and conditions by clicking on the check box.
- Check the Application Summary and click on the Sign button to sign the Application using a [digital signature certificate](https://www.indiafilings.com/digital-signature) or Aadhaar.

Note: These details will be verified in real-time from the CBDT database

content_sections.heading: Make Payment
content_sections.content:
- Confirm and proceed to make the payment against the Application.
- After Successful Payment, the Page shall be redirected to the DGFT Website, and the receipt shall be displayed; the User can also download the ticket.

content_sections.content:
The User shall receive the IEC Certificate in the email (used while applying for IEC). If required, the User can download the IEC Certificate after login into the DGFT Website and using the "Print Certificate" feature in "Manage IEC."The IEC shall be transmitted to CBIC, and the transmission status can be seen by Navigating to "My IEC" and checking the IEC Status bar with "CBIC Transmission Status."The Import Export Code is a primary document that is necessary for commencing Import-export activities. For exporting or importing any goods or services the IE code is to be obtained.IEC has numerous benefits for the growth of the business. Certainly, you cannot ignore the necessity of IE code registration as it is mandatory.

content_sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
content_sections.content:
Common questions aboutImport Export Code Benefits, Validity, and Application in India.

What is an Import Export Code (IEC) and why is it important?

An Import Export Code (IEC) is a 10-digit unique code issued by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) in India. It is mandatory for any business entity to obtain an IEC before engaging in import or export activities, unless specifically exempted. The IEC serves as an identification number and is crucial for entering the international market and availing benefits related to imports and exports.

Who needs to obtain an IEC?

Any business entity, including proprietorship, partnership, limited liability partnership (LLP), company, trust, Hindu undivided family (HUF), or society, needs to obtain an IEC if they plan to import or export goods or services from or to India. Exceptions are made only for service providers who do not intend to avail benefits under the Foreign Trade Policy.

What are the benefits of having an IEC?

Some key benefits of obtaining an IEC include access to international markets, smoother entry for Indian companies into global trade, online and hassle-free registration process, lifetime validity, reduced chances of illegal goods transportation, eligibility for subsidies and export incentives, and the ability to claim tax refunds on exports.

What is the validity period of an IEC?

The IEC registration is valid for a lifetime, i.e., until the business entity exists or the registration is revoked or surrendered. Unlike other registrations like GST or PF, IEC holders do not need to file annual returns or comply with any periodic compliance requirements.

What documents are required for IEC registration?

The main documents required for IEC registration include proof of establishment/incorporation/registration (for non-proprietorship firms), proof of address, proof of the firm's bank account (cancelled cheque or bank certificate), and a digital signature certificate (DSC) or Aadhaar of the firm's member.

How can I apply for an IEC?

The IEC application process is entirely online and can be completed through the DGFT website. After registering on the portal and logging in, you need to fill out the application form (ANF 2A format), provide the required details, attach the necessary documents, and make the application fee payment of Rs. 500.

Can an entity have multiple IEC codes?

No, an entity can have only one IEC code. Multiple IEC codes for the same entity are not permitted.

Can I transfer my IEC to another person or entity?

No, an IEC is a non-transferable code issued to a specific entity. If the ownership or nature of the entity changes, the new entity must apply for a fresh IEC.

What should I do if I lose or misplace my IEC certificate?

If you lose or misplace your IEC certificate, you can log in to the DGFT website and download a new copy of the certificate using the "Print Certificate" feature under the "Manage IEC" section.

Can I surrender or cancel my IEC if I no longer need it?

Yes, you can surrender or cancel your IEC if you no longer require it for import or export activities. The process for surrendering an IEC can be initiated through the DGFT website.

- **Less document requirement:** It is not required to submit many documents to obtain an IEC.
- **Lifetime Validity:** IE Code is a lifetime registration valid as long as the business exists. Hence, there are no issues with updating, filing, and renewing Import Export Code registration. The IE registration is valid until the company exists or the registration is not revoked or surrendered.
- **Reduces illegal goods transportation**: The most basic requirement for the [Import-Export code](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/procedure-for-obtaining-import-export-code) is that you need to provide authentic information. Without giving proper information, IE code cannot be obtained. This criterion makes the transportation of illegal goods impossible.
- Availing Several Benefits **:** IE code has enormous benefits for importers and exporters. The registered business entities can get help through subsidies from the Customs, Export Promotion Council or other authorities. With LUT filing under GST, the exporters can make exports without paying taxes. If the exports are made with tax payment, the exporter can claim the refunds of the paid tax amount.
- **Compliances:** Unlike other tax registration, the person carrying import or export does not require to fulfill any specific compliance requirements such as the annual filing or the return filings.

## Validity of IE Code

As mentioned above, IE Code registration is permanent and valid for a lifetime. Hence, there will be no hassles with updating, filing, and renewing the IEC registration. It is valid till the business exists or the registration is not revoked or surrendered. Further, unlike tax registrations like GST registration or [PF registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/pf-registration), the importer or exporter does not require to file any filings or follow any other compliance requirements like annual filing.As IE code registration is one-time and requires no additional compliance, it is recommended for all exporters & importers to obtain IE code after incorporation.

## Nature of the Firm obtaining an IEC

The nature of the Firm obtaining an IEC may be any of the follows:

- Proprietorship Firm
- Partnership Firm
- Limited Liability Partnership
- Limited Company
- Trust
- Hindu Undivided Family (HUF)
- Society

## Pre-Requisites for Applying for IEC

- Valid Login Credentials to DGFT Portal (After Registering on DGFT Portal)
- IEC may be applied on behalf of a firm which may be a Proprietorship, Partnership, LLP, Limited Company, Trust, HUF, and Society.
- The Firm must have an active Firm's Permanent Account Number (PAN) and details like Name as per Pan, Date of Birth, or Incorporation.
- The Firm must also have a bank account in the Name of the Firm and a valid address before applying.

Note: These details will be validated with the Income Tax Department site.

## Documents required for IEC Code registration

The list of scanned documents required for IEC Registration is listed as follows:

- Proof of establishment/incorporation/registration: The following type of Firm needs to submit the establishment/incorporation/registration certificate:

  - Partnership
  - Registered Society
  - Trust
  - HUF
  - Other

- Proof of Address: Proof of Address can be any one of the following documents:

  - Sale Deed
  - Rent agreement
  - Lease deed
  - Electricity bill
  - Telephone landline bill
  - Mobile, post-paid bill
  - MoU
  - Partnership deed
  - Other acceptable documents (for proprietorship only):

    - Aadhar card
    - Passport
    - Voter id

Note: In case the address proof is not in the Name of the applicant firm, a no objection certificate (NOC) by the firm premises owner in favor of the Firm, along with the address proof, is to be submitted as a single PDF document.

- Proof of Firm's Bank Account

  - Canceled Cheque
  - Bank Certificate

- User should have an active DSC or Aadhaar of the Firm's member for submission.
- Active Firm's Bank accounts for entering its details in the Application and making online payment of the application fee.

## Application Fee for IEC

The User must pay Rs.500 as the Application fee to get the IEC certificate.

## Procedure to submit IE Code Application

The procedure to get the Importer Exporter Code Certificate is explained in detail below:Visit the official DGFT website. Click on the 'Services' tab on the homepage and Select the 'IEC Profile Management' option from the drop-down list.

A new page will open. Click on the 'Apply for IEC' option on the Page.

### DGFT User Registration

- Enter the OTP and click on the 'Register' button.

![Importer-Exporter-Code-IEC-DGFT-Registration](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2018/04/Importer-Exporter-Code-IEC-DGFT-Registration.jpg)

- After registering on the DGFT website, log in to the website by entering the user name and password.

## Apply for IEC

- Post login, click on "Apply for IEC" on the Dashboard. Click on the "Start Fresh Application" button or the "Proceed with Existing Application" button if the User has already saved a draft application.
- Fill out the application form (ANF 2A format), and Enter the details in the General Information Section:

  - Select nature of Concern/Firm
  - Enter Firm Name
  - PAN Details

- Check the Application Summary and click on the Sign button to sign the Application using a [digital signature certificate](https://www.indiafilings.com/digital-signature) or Aadhaar.

Note: These details will be verified in real-time from the CBDT database

## Make Payment

- Confirm and proceed to make the payment against the Application.
- After Successful Payment, the Page shall be redirected to the DGFT Website, and the receipt shall be displayed; the User can also download the ticket.

## Get Importer Exporter Code Certificate

The User shall receive the IEC Certificate in the email (used while applying for IEC). If required, the User can download the IEC Certificate after login into the DGFT Website and using the "Print Certificate" feature in "Manage IEC."The IEC shall be transmitted to CBIC, and the transmission status can be seen by Navigating to "My IEC" and checking the IEC Status bar with "CBIC Transmission Status."The Import Export Code is a primary document that is necessary for commencing Import-export activities. For exporting or importing any goods or services the IE code is to be obtained.IEC has numerous benefits for the growth of the business. Certainly, you cannot ignore the necessity of IE code registration as it is mandatory.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Common questions aboutImport Export Code Benefits, Validity, and Application in India.

What is an Import Export Code (IEC) and why is it important?

An Import Export Code (IEC) is a 10-digit unique code issued by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) in India. It is mandatory for any business entity to obtain an IEC before engaging in import or export activities, unless specifically exempted. The IEC serves as an identification number and is crucial for entering the international market and availing benefits related to imports and exports.

Who needs to obtain an IEC?

Any business entity, including proprietorship, partnership, limited liability partnership (LLP), company, trust, Hindu undivided family (HUF), or society, needs to obtain an IEC if they plan to import or export goods or services from or to India. Exceptions are made only for service providers who do not intend to avail benefits under the Foreign Trade Policy.

What are the benefits of having an IEC?

Some key benefits of obtaining an IEC include access to international markets, smoother entry for Indian companies into global trade, online and hassle-free registration process, lifetime validity, reduced chances of illegal goods transportation, eligibility for subsidies and export incentives, and the ability to claim tax refunds on exports.

What is the validity period of an IEC?

The IEC registration is valid for a lifetime, i.e., until the business entity exists or the registration is revoked or surrendered. Unlike other registrations like GST or PF, IEC holders do not need to file annual returns or comply with any periodic compliance requirements.

What documents are required for IEC registration?

The main documents required for IEC registration include proof of establishment/incorporation/registration (for non-proprietorship firms), proof of address, proof of the firm's bank account (cancelled cheque or bank certificate), and a digital signature certificate (DSC) or Aadhaar of the firm's member.

How can I apply for an IEC?

The IEC application process is entirely online and can be completed through the DGFT website. After registering on the portal and logging in, you need to fill out the application form (ANF 2A format), provide the required details, attach the necessary documents, and make the application fee payment of Rs. 500.

Can an entity have multiple IEC codes?

No, an entity can have only one IEC code. Multiple IEC codes for the same entity are not permitted.

Can I transfer my IEC to another person or entity?

No, an IEC is a non-transferable code issued to a specific entity. If the ownership or nature of the entity changes, the new entity must apply for a fresh IEC.

What should I do if I lose or misplace my IEC certificate?

If you lose or misplace your IEC certificate, you can log in to the DGFT website and download a new copy of the certificate using the "Print Certificate" feature under the "Manage IEC" section.

Can I surrender or cancel my IEC if I no longer need it?

Yes, you can surrender or cancel your IEC if you no longer require it for import or export activities. The process for surrendering an IEC can be initiated through the DGFT website.

In simple words it is a transfer of property by the owner to another for the benefit of a third person along with or without himself or a declaration by the owner, to hold the property not for himself and another." content_sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
content_sections.content:
Common questions aboutTrust Registration in India: Process & Requirements.

What is a Trust in the context of India?

A Trust is an obligation annexed to the ownership of property, where the owner (known as the Settlor) transfers the property to another person (known as the Trustee) for the benefit of a third person (known as the Beneficiary) or for a specific purpose. The Trust Act, 1882 defines and governs the creation and operation of Trusts in India.

What are the common purposes for which Public Charitable Trusts are established in India?

Public Charitable Trusts in India are often established for purposes such as social service, education, healthcare, providing recreational facilities, and any other objectives aimed at general public welfare.

Who can create a Trust in India?

Any person in India who is competent to contract and has transferable property in their ownership can create a Trust.

What is a Trust Deed, and what information does it typically contain?

A Trust Deed is a document that establishes the registration of a Trust. It typically contains details like the name of the Trust, its place of office, objects, number of Trustees, their terms and management, appointment or resignation process, powers and duties of Trustees, application of Trust property, and other important matters.

How is a Trust Deed registered in India?

The Trust Deed must be executed on a stamp paper of suitable value and signed by the Settlor and two witnesses. It can then be registered with the local Registrar, who will retain a photocopy and return the original registered Trust Deed.

What is Form 10A in the context of Trust Registration in India?

Form 10A is an online application introduced by the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) for registration of charitable or religious Trusts or institutions under section 12A of the Income Tax Act.

What documents are required for filing Form 10A for Trust Registration?

Some of the key documents required for filing Form 10A include a self-certified copy of the instrument creating the Trust, registration documents with relevant authorities, copies of annual accounts, a note on the Trust's activities, existing registration orders (if any), and rejection orders (if any).

Can a Trust be created without a written instrument in India?

Yes, a Trust can be created in India without a written instrument. In such cases, self-certified copies of documents evidencing the creation of the Trust must be submitted during registration.

Who is a Settlor in the context of a Trust?

A Settlor is the person who creates the Trust by transferring their property to another person (the Trustee) for the benefit of a third person (the Beneficiary) or for a specific purpose.

Can a Trust be created for the benefit of the Settlor themselves?

Yes, a Trust can be created where the Settlor themselves is one of the Beneficiaries, along with others or for their own benefit.

# Trust Registration in India

Trust Registration is done in India by the Trust Act, 1882. The Trust Act, 1882 defines a Trust as "an obligation annexed to the ownership of property and arising out of a confidence reposed in and accepted by the owner, or declared and accepted by him, for the benefit of another or of another and the owner. In simple words it is a transfer of property by the owner to another for the benefit of a third person along with or without himself or a declaration by the owner, to hold the property not for himself and another." In India, majority of the Trusts are registered as public charitable trust a form of not-for-profit entity. Public Charitable Trusts can be established for a number of purposes, including the social service, education, healthcare, provision of facilities for recreation, and any other object of general public welfare. In this article, we look at the process for Trust Registration in India:

## Trust Registration

A Trust can be created by any person in India who is competent to contract, having in his/her power any property with is transferable. The person creating the Trust is called the Settlor and the person to whom the property is transferred on trust is called a Trustee. The person for whose benefit the property is transferred is called the beneficiary.

If the property to be transferred to the Trust is immovable, then the Trust must created by the execution of a Trust Deed that is duly registered. In case the Trust is created by the transfer of a movable property, then the Trust can be created by the property owner himself orally or in writing declaring that he would hold the property, not as owner, but as a Trustee for the benefit of some other person(s).

Usually the Trust Deed is the document that establishes the registration of the Trust and usually details items such as:

- Name of the Trust
- Place of office of the Trust
- Objects of the Trust
- Number of Trustees
- Term of the Trustees
- Trust Management
- Appointment or Resignation or Termination of Trustees
- Power, Function and Duties of the Trustees
- Application of Trust Property
- Other important matters

## Trust Deed Registration

The Trust Deed must be executed on Stamp Paper of suitable value and singed by the settlor and two witnesses. Once the Trust Deed is executed, it can be registered with the Local Registrar. The Registrar would then register the Trust, retain photocopy of the Trust deed and return the original registered Trust Deed back to the settlor.

## Online Trust Registration - Form 10A

The Central Board of Direct Taxes has issued a notification no. 10/2018-Income Tax dated 19.02.2018. Through the said notification, CBDT has substituted entire rule 17A which deals with application for registration of charitable or religious trusts, etc. Under this article we would look at the applicable procedure of trust after implication of notification no. 10/2018-Income Tax.

As per notification no. 10/2018-Income Tax, an application, under section 12A, for registration of charitable or religious trust or institution shall be made online by filing application in form 10A. The CBDT vide the said notification has made the procedure for
obtaining registration of trust online.

## Document Required for Trust Registration

Following documents are required for filing online form 10A –

1. If the trust is created, or the institution is established, under an instrument, than in such case, self-certified copy of the instrument creating the trust or establishment of the institution is to be submitted;
2. If the trust is created, or the institution is established, otherwise than under an instrument, than in such case, self-certified copy of the documents evidencing the creation of the trust or establishment of the institution is to be submitted;
3. Self-certified copy of registration with the Registrar of Companies or Registrar of Firms and Societies or Registrar of Public Trusts, as the case may be;
4. Self-certified copy of the documents evidencing adoption or modification of the objects, if any;
5. Where the trust or institution has been in existence during any year or years prior to the financial year in which the application for registration is made, than in such case self-certified copies of the annual accounts of the trust or institution relating to such prior year or years is to be submitted;
6. A note on the activities of the trust or institution needs to be submitted;
7. Self-certified copy of existing order granting registration under section 12A or section 12AA; and
8. Self-certified copy of order of rejection of application for grant of registration under section 12A or section 12AA, if any.

[Know more about Form 10A.](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/form-10a)
