# FSSAI Food Testing Procedure

To ensure the quality and safety of any food products, food sampling or food analysis can be ordered and carried out by an FSSAI Office. As per the Food and Safety Standards Act, testing of food articles is to be conducted once in six months through NABL accredited or FSSAI-notified lab. For a food analysis, a sample food product would be drawn, packed, sealed, and sent to an authorized lab to analyze the quality and safety of the food product. This article looks at the procedures followed during an FSSAI food testing procedure.In case you require an [FSSAI registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/fssai) for your business, get in touch with an IndiaFilings Advisor at [sales@indiafilings.com](mailto:sales@indiafilings.com)

## Importance of Laboratory testing Under FSSAI

Food testing and analysis are essential for the safekeeping of the food ecosystem. Food laboratory tests ensure that the food is safe for consumption.

- Food testing ensures that the products comply with the Food and Safety Standards Act:
- Lab testing Protect the brand equity and loyalty of consumers by delivering healthy food;
- Protects consumers from contaminated, modified, and healthy food;
- Ensures proper storage, packing, and distribution of food commodities; and
- Laboratory testing under FSSAI provides services in all areas of food testing, including-
  - Food adulterant testing
  - Chemical Contaminant testing
  - Microbial Testing
  - Drug Residue Testing

## Procedure Involved in FSSAI Testing

If an FSSAI officer draws a food sample, the following procedures must be followed during the sample collection process:

### Signature of Witnesses

The Food Safety officer should call for one or more witnesses while taking the sample piece and obtain a signature on all related forms and documents.

### Notice to the Business Operator

If the product has been obtained from the manufacturer or supplier, a notice in Form V-A shall be issued to them. When a product is drawn from an open container, the person drawing the sample should draw another sample from a container in its original condition bearing the same declaration and intimate the same to the Food Analyst.

### Payment for the Sample

The Food Safety Officer should pay the cost of the sample to the person from whom the sample drew it. The price should be calculated at the rate at which the product is sold to the public.

### Packing of Sample

The sample food for the analysis should be taken in clean, dry bottles or jars or in a container that should be adequately sealed to prevent leakage, and evaporation and to avoid the entrance of moisture. When selecting an already packed product as a sample, no further sealing is required.

### Labeling the Package

The package should be properly labeled and should bear the following requirements:

- Code of the sample
- Name of the sender with his official designation
- Date and place of collection
- Nature of the product that has been sent for analysis
- Nature and quantity of preservative added to the sample

### Sealing of package

The sample should be divided into four parts, and each piece should be sealed and wrapped using strong paper. The ends of the form should be folded and affixed. Further, a paper slip that covers the bottom to the top of the container, bearing the signature of the designated officer, should be pasted on the wrapper.The signature or thumb impression of the person from whom the sample has been taken should be affixed so that the paper slip and the wrapper bear part of the signature or the thumb impression. The paper cover should be further protected by means of a strong thread above and across the jar. The knots of the thread should be covered by wax bearing the impression of the sender's seal.

### Dispatch of the Package

The containers of the samples shall be dispatched in the following manner:

- The sealed container of one part of the sample, along with the memorandum in Form VI should be sent to the **_Food Analyst_**.
- The second and third parts of the sample along with two copies of the memorandum in Form VI should be sent to the **_Designated Officer_**.
- The fourth part of the sample along with a copy of the memorandum in Form VI should be sent to an **_accredited laboratory_** along with the prescribed fee.

How often should food products be tested as per FSSAI guidelines?

What types of tests are conducted by FSSAI-authorized laboratories?

FSSAI-authorized laboratories provide services in various areas of food testing, including food adulterant testing, chemical contaminant testing, microbial testing, and drug residue testing.

content_sections.content:
A

[NGO](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/registration-charitable-trust) can avail income tax exemption by getting itself registered and complying with certain other formalities, but such registration does not provide any benefit to the persons making donations. The Income Tax Act has certain provisions, which offer tax benefits to the "donors". All NGO's should avail the advantage of these provisions to attract potential donors. Section 80G is one of such sections. When an NGO secures registration under section 80G, it creates an incentive for potential donors. Individuals or organizations that donate to the registered NGO can claim a 50% deduction from their taxable income. This article provides a comprehensive guide on obtaining [80G registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/80g-registration?), making the process more accessible for potential donors and non-profit organizations.

[Register Now!](https://www.indiafilings.com/80g-registration)

content_sections.heading: What is Section 80G?
content_sections.content:
Section 80G of the Income Tax Act, 1961 is a provision that allows individuals and organizations to claim tax deductions on donations made to eligible charitable organizations.

When an organization obtains an

[80G certificate,](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/guide-to-80g-certificate) it means that it has been registered and recognized by the Income Tax Department as eligible to receive donations exempt from income tax. Donors who contribute to such organizations can claim deductions on their taxable income, up to a specified limit, based on the amount donated.

content_sections.heading: Understanding 80G Registration
content_sections.content:
Under the Income Tax Act of 1961, the

[80G registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/80g-registration?) provides a pathway for donors to avail tax deductions on their contributions to qualified charitable entities. This registration bestows donors with tax relief and benefits the receiving organizations. Organizations holding an 80G certification can attract more contributions due to the associated tax deductions. At the same time, donors can enjoy financial relief by deducting the donated amounts during income tax submissions.

content_sections.heading: Benefits of 80G Registration
content_sections.content:
- **Tax Deductions:** The primary advantage of obtaining 80G registration is eligibility for tax deductions. Donors can claim deductions of up to 50% or 100% of the donated amount. This depends on the category of the charitable institution. The exact percentage of deductions depends on the organisation's classification as defined by the income tax department.
- **Wider Reach:** Being registered under Section 80G enhances the credibility and transparency of charitable organisations, making them more appealing to potential donors. This registration provides access to a larger pool of donors and enables non-profits to raise funds more effectively. Individuals and corporations are more likely to contribute to organisations with 80G registration, as it assures them that their donations will be used for genuine charitable purposes.

content_sections.heading: Eligibility Criteria for 80G Registration
content_sections.content:
To be eligible for 80G registration, charitable organisations must fulfill specific criteria:

- **Legal Structure:** The organisation should be registered under the appropriate legal structure recognised by the Indian government, such as a trust, society, or non-profit company.
- **Non-profit Nature:** The organisation's primary objective must be promoting charitable activities rather than generating profits.
- **Proper Documentation: The** organisation should maintain proper accounting records and have its accounts audited annually. It must maintain compliance with income tax regulations.
- **Registration under Section 12A:** Prior registration under Section 12A is a prerequisite for obtaining 80G registration. Section 12A provides tax exemptions to charitable institutions; therefore, registration under it is necessary before applying for 80G.
- **Non-Exempt Income from Business Activities: The** organisation must not have any non-exempt income derived from business activities. If any business income exists, separate accounting records must be maintained. Donations received should not be used for purposes unrelated to charitable activities.
- **Non-Focus on Specific Communities: The** organisation must not exclusively focus on benefiting a specific religious community or caste.
- **Registration Number from Darpan Portal:** For registration or re-validation, a registration number from the Darpan portal of Niti Aayog is mandatory when receiving or planning to receive grants or assistance from the Central Government or State Government.

content_sections.heading: Documents required for 80G registration
content_sections.content:
To apply for 80G registration, the following documents are mandatory along with Form 10A/10AB:

- Self-certified copy of the organisation's incorporation document.
- Self-certified copy of the registration certificate issued by the relevant authority.
- Self-certified copy of the registration under the Foreign Contribution Regulation Act (FCRA), if applicable.
- Self-certified copy of the existing order granting approval under clause (23C) of section 10.
- Copies of annual accounts for up to three years preceding the application for existing entities.
- If business income is included in the organisation's income, copies of annual accounts and audit reports as per Section 44AB for the three years prior to the application.
- Details of the organisation's operations since its inception or the last three years, whichever is shorter.

content_sections.heading: 80G Certificate
content_sections.content: The 80G Certificate, issued by the Income Tax Department, is a recognition given to non-governmental entities like charitable trusts or Section 8 Companies. Its primary purpose is to incentivize donors to contribute funds to these non-profit organizations. By donating to an institution with an 80G Certificate, donors can benefit from a 50% tax relief on the donated amount, which they can then deduct from their Gross Total Income. To claim this exemption, it's essential for donors to furnish a stamped receipt of their contribution. This receipt should clearly detail the donor’s name, donation date, and the PAN of the recipient organization.

content_sections.heading: Changes in 80G Registration Norms
content_sections.content: While previously, 80G registration was typically a one-time process unless specific restrictions were outlined in the registration certificate, the Finance Act 2020 introduced noteworthy modifications to this framework.

content_sections.heading: Registration Process for New Entrants
content_sections.content:
Organizations seeking an initial registration under section 80G must apply to the Principal Commissioner or Commissioner. Successful applications will result in a provisional registration valid for three years. Importantly, this registration's validity starts from the Assessment Year for which it was sought. As for renewing this registration, organizations must:

- Apply a minimum of six months before the end of the validity period, or
- Submit the renewal application within six months from the beginning of their activities, depending on which of these two deadlines comes first.

content_sections.heading: 80G Registration Validity and Renewal
content_sections.content: The provisional registration is set for three years initially. Once this period concludes, a renewal is essential. However, post-renewal, the registration's validity is capped at five years. At the end of every five-year cycle, a subsequent renewal is necessary to maintain the benefits.

content_sections.heading: 80G Registration Process
content_sections.content:
The procedure for 80G registration can be summarized in the following key steps:

- **Initiation of the Application:** Organizations must direct their 80G certificate application to the Commissioner of Income Tax (Exemption) situated within the jurisdiction of the applying institution.
- **Submission and Inspection:** After submitting the necessary forms and accompanying documents, a physical inspection of the premises is undertaken by the Income Tax department.
- **Provision of Additional Documents:** During the inspection, the Income Tax officials might request supplementary documents or evidence. It's crucial for the institution to promptly provide these additional details.
- **Certification:** Following a thorough review and satisfactory validation of both the documents and the NGO's premises, the Commissioner bestows the institution with the coveted 80G certificate.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Common questions about80G Registration Guide.

What is Section 80G of the Income Tax Act?

Section 80G of the Income Tax Act, 1961 allows individuals and organizations to claim tax deductions on donations made to eligible charitable organizations registered under this section. When an organization obtains an 80G certificate, it becomes eligible to receive tax-exempt donations, making it more appealing for potential donors.

What are the benefits of 80G registration for NGOs?

The primary benefit of obtaining 80G registration is that it allows donors to claim tax deductions of up to 50% or 100% (depending on the category) of the donated amount. Additionally, it enhances the credibility and transparency of the NGO, making it more appealing to potential donors and enabling it to raise funds more effectively.

What are the eligibility criteria for an NGO to obtain 80G registration?

To be eligible for 80G registration, an NGO must be legally registered as a trust, society, or non-profit company, have a non-profit motive, maintain proper accounting records and audits, be registered under Section 12A, not have non-exempt income from business activities, and not focus exclusively on benefiting a specific religious community or caste.

What documents are required for 80G registration?

The mandatory documents required for 80G registration include self-certified copies of the organization's incorporation document, registration certificate, FCRA registration (if applicable), existing approval under Section 10(23C), annual accounts for up to three years, details of operations, and Form 10A/10AB.

What is the validity period of 80G registration for new entrants?

As per the Finance Act 2020, new organizations seeking 80G registration will initially receive a provisional registration valid for three years from the assessment year for which it was sought.

How can an NGO renew its 80G registration?

To renew the 80G registration, NGOs must apply a minimum of six months before the end of the validity period or within six months from the beginning of their activities, whichever comes first. After renewal, the registration is valid for five years before requiring another renewal.

What is the process for obtaining 80G registration?

The process for obtaining 80G registration involves initiating the application with the Commissioner of Income Tax (Exemption), submitting forms and documents, undergoing a physical inspection, providing additional documents if requested, and finally receiving the 80G certificate upon satisfactory review.

Can donors claim tax deductions on donations made to an NGO without 80G registration?

No, donors can only claim tax deductions on donations made to NGOs or charitable organizations that have obtained 80G registration from the Income Tax Department.

IndiaFilings provides a streamlined and hassle-free pathway for NGOs to secure 80G registration, leveraging their expertise to simplify the often complex process. Their team ensures a smooth registration experience, enabling NGOs to quickly obtain the 80G certificate and encourage more donations.

Is it mandatory for an NGO to have a registration number from the Darpan portal for 80G registration?

Yes, as per the eligibility criteria mentioned in the article, having a registration number from the Darpan portal of Niti Aayog is mandatory for registration or re-validation under 80G if the NGO receives or plans to receive grants or assistance from the Central or State Government.

What is an 80G certificate?

An 80G certificate is a document issued by eligible charitable organizations or trusts that allows donors to claim tax exemptions on their donations under Section 80G of the Income Tax Act.

Who can avail tax exemption under 80G?

What is the maximum allowable deduction under 80G?

Can donations made to the Clean Ganga Fund qualify for 80G exemption?

Yes, donations made by a resident assessee to the Clean Ganga Fund set up by the Central Government are eligible for 100% deduction under Section 80G without a qualifying limit.

When was the 80G certificate introduced?

The 80G certificate made its way into the law book during the financial year 1967-68 and continues to be an important tax-saving certificate.

[agricultural income](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/agricultural-income-income-tax-act)

content_sections.heading: Receipts from Hindu Undivided Family

content_sections.heading: Share from a Partnership Firm or LLP

content_sections.heading: NRI Tax Free Incomes
content_sections.content: Certain types of incomes or receipts earned by NRIs are exempt from income tax. Income earned by way of interest on the bonds notified by the Central Government is exempt from income tax. Also, any premium which is applicable to the redemption of the specified bonds is exempt from tax.

content_sections.heading: Income Earned by Foreigners
content_sections.content: Certain types of incomes and receipts of foreigners are exempt from income tax. Remuneration received by a foreigner who is an official of an embassy is exempt from income tax. Also, any money received by a foreigner from his employer for himself, his spouse, or children, in connection with his proceeding on home leave out of India or after retirement or termination of service, is fully exempt from income tax. Also, allowances and perquisites paid by the Government of India to a citizen of India, while rendering services outside of India, are exempt from the scope of Income Tax.

content_sections.heading: Gratuities
content_sections.content: Any amount of gratuity received by a government employee due to death or retirement is exempt from income tax. The gratuity received by private-sector employees on retirement or on becoming incapacitated or on termination is exempt subject to a maximum ceiling limit of ten lakh rupees. The exemption is subject to further limits which are specified by the Income Tax Act. The specified limits are half a month's salary for each year of completed service, calculated on the basis of the average salary for the ten months immediately preceding the year in which the gratuity is paid, or actual gratuity paid.

content_sections.heading: Commutation of Pension
content_sections.content:
The amount received in commutation of pension by a Government servant or any payment in commutation of pension from LIC or any other insurer from their pension funds is exempt from income tax. For private sector employee, only the following amount of commuted pension is exempt:

- Where the employee has received any gratuity, the commuted value of one-third of the pension which he is normally entitled to receive
- In any other case, the commuted value of half of the amount of pension.

The monthly pension receivable by a pensioner is liable to income tax like any other item of salary or income, and no standard deduction is available in respect of pension received by a taxpayer.

content_sections.heading: Leave Salary
content_sections.content:
The maximum amount receivable by an employee of the Central Government as a cash equivalent, up to ten months of leave at the time of their retirement, whether on superannuation or otherwise, is exempt from income tax.

For private-sector employees, the exempt amount would be least of:

- Ten months average salary calculated on the basis of the salary during ten months preceding the employees’ retirement on superannuation or voluntary retirement
- Earned leave standing to the credit of the employee limited to 30 days for every year of actual service rendered for the employer from whose service he has retired
- The amount of leave encashment actually received
- A standard amount of three lakh rupees

content_sections.heading: Voluntary Retirement or Separation Payment
content_sections.content: Any amount received by an employee of a public sector company, of a local authority, of a statutory authority, of a cooperative society or university at the time of voluntary retirement or voluntary separation is completely exempt from tax. The maximum amount of exemption available for the income received at the voluntary retirement has been capped at five lakh rupees.

content_sections.heading: Money Received from Insurance
content_sections.content: Any amount received under a Life Insurance Policy (LIP) or under a Keyman Insurance Policy (KIP) or under an insurance policy for which the premium payable for any of the years during the term of the policy exceeds 10% of the actual capital sum assured, is fully exempt from tax. Also, all proceeds received on the death of an insured person is fully exempt from income tax. Hence, money received from life insurance policies, whether from the LIC or any other private insurance company is exempt from income tax.

content_sections.heading: Money Received from Provident Fund
content_sections.content: Any amount received from a government-recognised provident fund (PF), approved superannuation fund or PPF is fully exempt from income tax.

content_sections.heading: Special Allowances and Benefits
content_sections.content: Any special allowance or benefits received by an employee which is not in the nature of a perquisite is not covered within the scope of income tax. However, the allowance should have been specifically granted to meet the expenses incurred in the performance of duties connected with employment.

01. Income by way of interest, the premium obtained on redemption or other payment on securities, bonds, annuity certificates, savings certificates, and other certificates issued by the Central Government
02. Interest on securities held by the issue department of the Central Bank of Ceylon constituted under the Ceylon Monetary Law Act, 1949
03. Interest payable to any bank incorporated in a country outside India and authorised to perform central banking functions in that country on any deposits made by it, with the approval of the Reserve Bank of India, with any scheduled bank
04. Interest payable by Government or a local authority on money borrowed by it, including hedging charges on currency fluctuation
05. Interest on Gold Deposit Bonds
06. Interest on deposits for Bhopal Gas victims
07. Interest on bonds of local authorities
08. Tax Free Bonds and Tax Free Infrastructure Bonds which are eligible for investment for securing exemption from Capital Gains
09. Interest received by a non-resident or non-ordinarily person on deposits made with an Off-shore Banking Unit
10. Interest from Tax Free Infrastructure Bonds
11. Bank interest of a girl child from the Sukanya Samridhi Scheme

content_sections.heading: Scholarships and Awards
content_sections.content: Scholarship granted to meet the cost of education and certain awards is exempt from income tax.  Also, the amount provided as pension and family pension of Gallantry Award Winners like Paramvir Chakra, Mahavir Chakra, and Vir Chakra and also other Gallantry Award winners notified by the Central Government are exempt.

content_sections.heading: Dividends on Shares and Mutual Funds
content_sections.content: Dividend income and income of units of Mutual Funds are completely exempt from income tax.

content_sections.content: The capital gains received on 1 is eligible for exemption. However, the land should have been used in the past two years for agricultural purposes. Also, the proceeds should be reinvested in agricultural land again.

However, the transaction should have been subjected to a Securities Transaction Tax (STT). Thus, if the shares of any company listed in the stock exchange are sold after holding it for a minimum period of one year, then there will be no liability to payment of capital gains. content_sections.content:
[Gifts](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/income-tax-gift)

received from a relative and gifts received during the assessee's wedding are fully exempt from income tax without any limit. Gift received from any other person is taxable subject to an exemption for up to a limit of fifty thousand rupees.

content_sections.content:
Transfer of a capital asset in a transaction of

[reverse mortgage](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/reverse-mortgage-loan-scheme)

for senior citizens would not attract capital gains tax. Further, the loan amount is also exempt from tax.

Are there any income sources that are completely tax-free in India?

Yes, the article highlights several types of income that are fully exempt from income tax in India. These include agricultural income, receipts from Hindu Undivided Family, share from a partnership firm or LLP, certain incomes for NRIs and foreigners, gratuities, commutation of pension, leave salary, voluntary retirement payments, and income from life insurance policies and provident funds.

Is agricultural income taxable in India?

According to the article, agricultural income is fully exempt from income tax under Section 10(1) of the Income Tax Act. However, for individuals and HUFs, an agricultural income of more than Rs.5000 is added to the total income for the purpose of determining the applicable income tax slab rate on other income sources.

Are scholarships and awards taxable in India?

No, the article states that scholarship granted to meet the cost of education and certain awards are exempt from income tax. Additionally, the pension and family pension of Gallantry Award Winners like Paramvir Chakra, Mahavir Chakra, and Vir Chakra, as well as other Gallantry Award winners notified by the Central Government, are also exempt.

Is dividend income from shares and mutual funds taxable?

No, the article clearly mentions that dividend income and income from units of Mutual Funds are completely exempt from income tax in India.

Are capital gains from the transfer of agricultural land taxable?

According to the article, capital gains received on the transfer of agricultural land are eligible for exemption, provided that the land has been used for agricultural purposes in the past two years and the proceeds are reinvested in agricultural land.

Is income from tax-free bonds taxable?

No, the article specifically mentions that interest income from Tax Free Bonds and Tax Free Infrastructure Bonds, which are eligible for investment for securing exemption from Capital Gains, is exempt from income tax.

Are gifts received taxable in India?

The article states that gifts received from relatives and gifts received during the assessee's wedding are fully exempt from income tax without any limit. However, gifts received from any other person are taxable, subject to an exemption of up to Rs. 50,000.

Is the interest income on bank deposits taxable?

According to the article, certain types of interest income are exempt from income tax under Section 10(15) of the Income Tax Act. This includes interest income from deposits made with an Off-shore Banking Unit by a non-resident or non-ordinarily resident person, and interest from the Sukanya Samridhi Scheme for a girl child.

Are voluntary retirement or separation payments taxable?

The article states that any amount received by an employee of a public sector company, local authority, statutory authority, cooperative society, or university at the time of voluntary retirement or voluntary separation is completely exempt from tax, subject to a maximum exemption of Rs. 5 lakh.

Is income from reverse mortgage schemes taxable?

No, the article mentions that the transfer of a capital asset in a transaction of reverse mortgage for senior citizens would not attract capital gains tax, and the loan amount is also exempt from tax.

content_sections.heading: 12A Registration
content_sections.content:
12A registration is a one-time registration which is granted by the Income Tax Department to trusts and other not for profit organisations. The purpose of the registration is to be exempted from the payment of income tax. 12A registration is generally applied for immediately after incorporation.

[Section 8 Companies](https://www.indiafilings.com/section-8-company-registration), Trusts and NGOs which have obtained 12A registration enjoy exemption from paying income tax on their surplus income. The 12A registration facility is available for all non-profit entities. Hence, it is necessary for all Trusts, NGOs and other Not-for-Profit organisations to be aware of Section 12A of the Income Tax Act. The purpose of the present article is to discuss the procedure for obtaining 12A registration.

content_sections.heading: Benefits of 12A Registration
content_sections.content:
The benefits of Section 12A Registration are the following:

- The fund used for charitable or religious purposes is considered to be the application of the income. The income application refers to the expenses used for charitable or religious purposes for calculating the taxable income of the not-for-profit organisation.
- The income received will be free from the charge of Income Tax.
- The person who is registered under Section 12A can avail benefits for accumulating or setting aside income. However, the income which is set aside should not be more than 15% of the amount applied towards charitable or other non-commercial purposes.
- The accumulation of income which is considered to be the income application shall not be included in the assessee's total income.
- NGOs are entitled to receive grants as funds from domestic and international sources. These agencies are entitled to provide grants to NGOs which have obtained registration under this section.
- The registration which is granted under Section 12A shall be treated as a one-time registration. Once the registration is made, the registration will be active until the date of cancellation.
- There is no requirement to renew the registration periodically. Hence, the registration benefits can be claimed NGO as and when the requirement arises.

content_sections.heading: Eligibility for 12A Registration
content_sections.content:
- In order to qualify for registration under Section 12A, the organisation should meet the definition of charitable purpose as defined in the Income Tax Act. Charitable purpose means relief to the poor, education, medical relief and activities undertaken with the objective of preserving the environment. The pursuit of any other objective of a public utility will also qualify for a charitable purpose.
- The primary qualifying criterion will be to check whether there is any profit motive involved in the activities carried on by the assessee. In the absence of a profit motive, registration shall be granted.
- If the assessee is carrying on activities related to trade or commerce, then the facility granted under this section is restricted. In such cases, registration is granted exclusively if the receipts from the trade activity are less than twenty per cent of the total receipts of the assessee.
- Also, it may be noted that 12A Registration is not applicable for Private or Family Trusts. The activities of the assessee should be genuinely for the benefit of the public.

content_sections.heading: Form 10A
content_sections.content:
Form 10A is a form which should be filed by entities which wish to nake a registration under Section 12A. The process for applying for Section 12A registration and the process of Form 10A filing has been made exclusively online. The process of making online filing is possible only with a

[digital signature](https://www.indiafilings.com/digital-signature). For making an application under Section 12A, the digital signature of the founder or author of the trust should be affixed. To obtain registration under Section 12A, an application in [Form 10A](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/form-10a) for registration of a charitable or religious trust or institution can be made. The application should compulsorily be made in the online mode. The application shall be addressed to the Commissioner of Income Tax along with the necessary documents.

content_sections.heading: Documents Required for 12A Registration
content_sections.content:
1. A self-certified copy of the instrument which was used to create the trust or establish the institution shall be submitted.
2. The institution or trust may have been created otherwise than by way of drafting and registering an instrument. In such cases, a self-certified copy of the document evidencing the creation of the trust, or establishment of the institution should be submitted to the Income Tax Department.
3. It is necessary to submit a self-certified copy of the registration, which was made with the applicable body. The applicable body may be the Registrar of Companies, the Registrar of Firms and Societies or Registrar of Public Trusts.
4. A self-certified copy of the documents which provide evidence for adoption or modification of the objectives of the entity shall be submitted.
5. Annual financial statements for three preceding financial years
6. Note on the activities conducted by the entity
7. In certain cases, the Income Tax department may cancel the registration granted under this section. After rectifying the default, the assessee is allowed to make a subsequent application. In such cases, it is necessary to submit a self-certified copy of the existing order granting registration.
8. The assessee may have previously applied for registration under this section. The application may have been rejected. In such cases, a self-certified copy of the order of rejection should be attached with the application.

content_sections.heading: Procedure for Obtaining 12A Registration
content_sections.content:
- The assessee is required to submit the application in the required format online. After the application has been submitted, the Commissioner may request the applicant to submit additional information or documents as needed. The Commissioner may make the request in case there is a need to satisfy the Income Tax Department about the genuineness of the activities undertaken by the trust.
- The Commissioner may be satisfied with the application. In such cases, the Commissioner will pass a written order mentioning that the assessee is eligible to obtain registration under the section. The written order is forwarded to the assessee. On receipt of the order, the assessee can obtain the privilege of registration under the section.
- The commissioner may not be satisfied with the application. In such cases, the right is available with the Commissioner to reject the application. The assessee should be informed in writing of the reason for the rejection.

content_sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
content_sections.content:
Common questions about12A Registration.

What is 12A registration?

12A registration is a one-time registration granted by the Income Tax Department to trusts and other not-for-profit organizations. It exempts them from paying income tax on their surplus income, provided they meet certain criteria related to their purpose and activities.

Who can apply for 12A registration?

Any non-profit entity, such as a trust, NGO, or Section 8 company, engaged in charitable or religious purposes without any profit motive can apply for 12A registration. However, private or family trusts are not eligible.

What are the benefits of 12A registration?

The key benefits include exemption from income tax on surplus funds used for charitable or religious purposes, ability to accumulate or set aside up to 15% of income for future use, and eligibility to receive grants from domestic and international sources.

What documents are required for 12A registration?

The applicant must submit self-certified copies of the trust deed or document evidencing its creation, registration certificate (if applicable), documents showing adoption or modification of objectives, and annual financial statements for the preceding three years, among other documents.

How can an organization apply for 12A registration?

The application process for 12A registration is online. The applicant must file Form 10A with the required documents and a digital signature of the founder or trustee.

Is 12A registration permanent?

Yes, the 12A registration granted by the Income Tax Department is a one-time registration and does not need to be renewed periodically, unless it is canceled by the department for specific reasons.

Can an organization's 12A registration be canceled?

Yes, the Income Tax Department has the authority to cancel an organization's 12A registration if it finds that the organization has violated the conditions or purposes for which the registration was granted.

What is the eligibility criteria for 12A registration?

To be eligible for 12A registration, an organization's activities must qualify as "charitable purpose" as defined in the Income Tax Act, which includes relief of the poor, education, medical relief, environmental preservation, and other objectives of public utility. Additionally, the organization should not have any profit motive.

Can an organization engaged in trade or commerce obtain 12A registration?

Yes, an organization engaged in trade or commerce can obtain 12A registration if its receipts from such activities are less than 20% of its total receipts.

Is there a time limit for applying for 12A registration after an organization's establishment?

No, there is no specific time limit mentioned in the article for applying for 12A registration after an organization's establishment. However, it is generally advisable to apply for 12A registration immediately after incorporation or establishment.

content_sections.heading: Noc - No Objection Certificate
content_sections.content: RTO No objection Certificate (NOC) is an official document issued by the local Regional Transport Office (RTO) to allow re-registration of the vehicle with another RTO in a different state. Also, it is a document certifying that there are no pending dues of tax on the concerned vehicle. In this article, we look at the procedure for obtaining No Objection Certificate (NOC) in detail. _Also, read about [Driving Licence Address Change](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/driving-licence-address-change)_

content_sections.heading: Purpose of Obtaining NOC
content_sections.content: As per the Motor Vehicle Act, the owner of a vehicle must obtain NOC if he or she desires to remove or sell his/her vehicle to the other state. However, an application for change of address and registration needs a NOC from the local RTO where you got your vehicle registered.

content_sections.heading: Service Charge
content_sections.content: The prescribed fee of Rs.50/- for all class of vehicle will be charged in the issuance of NOC.

content_sections.heading: Documents Required
content_sections.content:
The following are the documents to be furnished along with the application form:

- Copy of Police certificate from NCRB
- Copy of Registration certificate
- Copy of Insurance certificate
- [Valid tax](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/tamil-nadu-vehicle-tax) details

content_sections.heading: Offline Application Procedure for NOC
content_sections.content:
The No Objection Certificate (NOC) can be obtained using the form no. 28 that the applicant needs to fill with the required details and submit at the Regional Transport Office (RTO) along with the documents required to issue NOC. Once the application form is submitted will be checked by the concerned authority of the RTO in order to obtain the report of the vehicle from the police authority to verify that the vehicle is involved under any criminal case or stolen.On verification, if there is no DSA cases pending or outstanding dues against the vehicle, then the receipt of clearance can be obtained, and No Objection Certificate (NOC) is issued.Note: The application form for the No Objection Certificate (NOC) is given below in the pdf format.

content_sections.heading: Online Application Procedure for NOC

To obtain NOC from the RTO, follow the procedure which is mentioned below:**Step 1:** The applicant needs to access the  of Ministry of Road Transport & Highways.**Step 2:** Select the state from the list of states as given below.![No Objection Certificate (NOC) - Image 1](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2019/09/No-Objection-Certificate-NOC-Image-1.png) No Objection Certificate (NOC) - Image 1

**Step 3:** Click on "Apply Online" and select "Services on Driving Licence" to apply for NOC.![No Objection Certificate (NOC) - Image 2](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2019/09/No-Objection-Certificate-NOC-Image-2.png) No Objection Certificate (NOC) - Image 2

**Step 4:** Now, read the following instructions carefully and click on the "Continue" button to move further.![No Objection Certificate (NOC) - Image 3](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2019/09/No-Objection-Certificate-NOC-Image-3.png) No Objection Certificate (NOC) - Image 3

What is a No Objection Certificate (NOC) and why is it required?

A No Objection Certificate (NOC) is an official document issued by the Regional Transport Office (RTO) to allow re-registration of a vehicle in another state. It is required when the vehicle owner wants to sell or transfer their vehicle to another state or change the address and registration of the vehicle.

How much does it cost to obtain an NOC?

The prescribed fee for obtaining an NOC is Rs. 50 for all classes of vehicles, as mentioned in the article.

What documents are required to apply for an NOC?

The documents required to apply for an NOC include a copy of the police certificate from NCRB, copy of the registration certificate, copy of the insurance certificate, and valid tax details.

Can I apply for an NOC online?

Yes, the article provides a detailed step-by-step procedure for applying for an NOC online through the official portal of the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways.

How long is an NOC valid for?

# Noc - No Objection Certificate

RTO No objection Certificate (NOC) is an official document issued by the local Regional Transport Office (RTO) to allow re-registration of the vehicle with another RTO in a different state. Also, it is a document certifying that there are no pending dues of tax on the concerned vehicle. In this article, we look at the procedure for obtaining No Objection Certificate (NOC) in detail. _Also, read about [Driving Licence Address Change](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/driving-licence-address-change)_

## Purpose of Obtaining NOC

As per the Motor Vehicle Act, the owner of a vehicle must obtain NOC if he or she desires to remove or sell his/her vehicle to the other state. However, an application for change of address and registration needs a NOC from the local RTO where you got your vehicle registered.

## Service Charge

The prescribed fee of Rs.50/- for all class of vehicle will be charged in the issuance of NOC.

## Documents Required

The following are the documents to be furnished along with the application form:

- Copy of Police certificate from NCRB
- Copy of Registration certificate
- Copy of Insurance certificate
- [Valid tax](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/tamil-nadu-vehicle-tax) details

## Offline Application Procedure for NOC

The No Objection Certificate (NOC) can be obtained using the form no. 28 that the applicant needs to fill with the required details and submit at the Regional Transport Office (RTO) along with the documents required to issue NOC. Once the application form is submitted will be checked by the concerned authority of the RTO in order to obtain the report of the vehicle from the police authority to verify that the vehicle is involved under any criminal case or stolen.On verification, if there is no DSA cases pending or outstanding dues against the vehicle, then the receipt of clearance can be obtained, and No Objection Certificate (NOC) is issued.Note: The application form for the No Objection Certificate (NOC) is given below in the pdf format.

content_sections.heading: ISO Certification in India
content_sections.content:
ISO (International Organization for Standardization) as the name implies it’s an independent international organisation, develops International Standards, such as ISO 9001 and ISO 14001, but they are not involved in the ISO certification and do not issue ISO certificates. External certification bodies in India perform the ISO certification process.In this article we will look at ISO Certification process in detail.

_Need to apply for ISO Certification? Get help from IndiaFilings experts to obtain your ISO certificate effortlessly!_

content_sections.heading: Objective of ISO certification
content_sections.content: The aim of getting ISO certification is to advance the improvement of standardisation in the technology of an organisation.

content_sections.heading: Advantages of ISO Certification
content_sections.content:
- International credibility: ISO Certification plays a vital role in helping the organisation to build credibility in overseas business.
- Customer Satisfaction: ISO standards are intended to make organisations to serve their customers in a better way that would simultaneously increase customers’ satisfaction
- Government Tenders: ISO Certification is quite essential to bid for Government Tenders.
- Business Efficiency: Functional efficiency of organisations is improved by obtaining ISO Certification. SOP (Standard Operating Procedures) and work instructions can be developed with the help of ISO Certification Agency. Implementation of ISO in an organisation manages the resources efficiently.
- Product Quality: By obtaining ISO Certification, the product quality matches up the international standards, it will reduce the risk of product order rejections that may occur due to the flawed products.
- Marketability: ISO Certification improves the business credibility, and it helps the business marketing directly.

content_sections.heading: Applicable Fee for ISO Certification
content_sections.content:
Fee for ISO certification in India varies from organisation to organisation. The ISO certification body will compute the fee for ISO certification by considering the below mentioned different parameters:

- Size of an organisation
- Number of employees
- Processes of Organization
- Level of risk associated with the scope of services of the organisation
- The complexity of the management system
- The number of working shifts

content_sections.heading: ISO Certification Processing Time
content_sections.content: ISO certification processing time also varies from organisation to organisation. The ISO certification body will notify the details processing time for completion of ISO certification after assessing the size of an organisation.

content_sections.heading: Prerequisite
content_sections.content: The precondition for processing ISO certification or ISO registration is explained in detail below:

content_sections.heading: Selecting the Type of ISO Certification
content_sections.content:
First of all, the entrepreneur needs to choose the type of ISO certification required for the business. There are various types of ISO certification are available such as listed below:

- ISO 9001:2008- Quality Management System
- OHSAS 18001 – Occupational Health & Safety Management System
- ISO 37001 - Anti-bribery management systems
- ISO 31000 – Risk Management
- ISO 27001 – Information Security Management System
- ISO 10002 – Compliant Management System
- ISO 14001:2015 – Environment Management System
- ISO 26000 – Social Responsibility
- ISO 28000 – Security Management
- ISO 22008 – Food Safety Management
- SA 8000 – Social accountability
- EnMS EN 16001 ISO 50001 – Energy Management
- SO/IEC 17025 - Testing and calibration laboratories
- SO 13485 - Medical devices
- ISO 639 - Language codes
- ISO 4217 - Currency codes
- ISO 3166 - Country codes
- ISO 8601 - Date and time format
- ISO 20121 - Sustainable events
- SO/IEC 27001 - Information security management

content_sections.heading: Selecting an ISO Certification Body (ISO Registrar)
content_sections.content:
As stated above ISO does not provide companies’ certification. It needs to be done by the external certification bodies. Thus it is mandatory to recognise the credible certification body. When selecting a certification body, the entrepreneur has to follow the things listed below.

- Evaluate several certification bodies
- Check if the certification body uses the relevant CASCO standards
- Check whether the certification body is accredited.

Note: Accreditation is not compulsory; however, the companies should meet the ISO accreditation bodies’ requirements.To find an accredited certification body in our country, contact the National Board of Accreditation(NBA), India.

content_sections.heading: ISO Certification Process in India
content_sections.content: The process for obtaining ISO certification in India is explained in detail below:

content_sections.heading: Make an Application
content_sections.content: Once the entrepreneur or application has selected the ISO standard and ISO certification body, need to make an application in a prescribed form (depends on the ISO registrar). The application should contain rights and obligations of entrepreneur and certification body parties and includes liability issues, confidentiality, and access rights.

content_sections.heading: Documents Review by Registrar
content_sections.content: The ISO certification body will review all the quality manuals and documents related to various policies and procedures being followed in the organisation. Review of existing works will help the ISO registrar to identify the possible gaps against the requirements stipulated in the ISO standards.

content_sections.heading: Determination of Pre-assessment Needs
content_sections.content: The Pre-assessment is an initial review of the Quality Management System in an organisation to identify any significant weakness or omissions in the system and registrar will provide the organisation with an opportunity to correct the deficiencies before the regular registration assessment is conducted.

content_sections.heading: Prepare an Action Plan
content_sections.content: After the ISO registrar notified the existing gaps in the organisation, the applicant or entrepreneur has to prepare an action plan to eliminate these gaps. The action plan should contain the list of the required tasks to be performed to meet the Quality Management SystemNote: The entrepreneur may need giving training to employees to work efficiently to achieve quality management system. Make all the employees in the organisation to aware of the ISO standards concerning work efficiency and quality standards.

content_sections.heading: Onsite Inspection or Audit
content_sections.content:
The ISO registrar will conduct a physical onsite inspection to audit the changes made in the organisation.During the audit, if the registrar finds anything that does not meet with the requirements of the ISO standards, registrar determines the severity and issue findings. Audit findings are usually called as nonconformities and fall into one of two categories depending on severity.

- A Minor Non-conformance – It deals with minor infractions of procedures or minor failures of the system in meeting the ISO standards.
- A Major Non-conformance – It deals with issues where the nonconforming products are likely to reach the customers or where there is a breakdown in the quality system that results in an inefficient system in meeting the requirements of the standards.

content_sections.heading: Final audit
content_sections.content: The registration cannot proceed until all significant nonconformities are closed and verified by the Registrar.  This usually involves a re-audit of the affected areas and, of course, the associated costs.Note: Minor nonconformities require a corrective action plan and that will be closed at the first surveillance.

content_sections.heading: Get ISO Certificate
content_sections.content: After all, non-conformities are addressed, and all the findings are updated in the ISO audit report, the registrar will grant the ISO certification.

content_sections.heading: Surveillance Audits
content_sections.content:
Surveillance audit will be conducted primarily to ensure that the organisation is maintaining ISO quality standards. It will be performed from time to time.

content_sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
content_sections.content:
Common questions aboutISO Certification in India.

What is the objective of getting ISO certification?

The main objective of obtaining ISO certification is to enhance the standardization of processes and improve the overall quality management system within an organization. It helps businesses establish credibility, increase customer satisfaction, and facilitate better operational efficiency.

What are the advantages of ISO certification?

Some key advantages of ISO certification include international credibility, improved customer satisfaction, eligibility for government tenders, increased business efficiency, better product quality, and enhanced marketability for the organization.

How is the fee for ISO certification determined?

The fee for ISO certification in India varies from organization to organization. It is calculated by the certification body based on factors such as the size of the organization, number of employees, processes, level of risk associated with the scope of services, complexity of the management system, and the number of working shifts.

What is the prerequisite for obtaining ISO certification?

The main prerequisite for obtaining ISO certification is selecting the appropriate type of ISO certification required for the business, such as ISO 9001 for Quality Management System, ISO 14001 for Environmental Management System, or others based on the specific needs of the organization.

How to choose an ISO certification body (registrar)?

When selecting an ISO certification body, it is important to evaluate several bodies, check if they use relevant CASCO standards, and ensure they are accredited. Organizations can contact the National Board of Accreditation (NBA) in India to find an accredited certification body.

What is the process for obtaining ISO certification in India?

The process for obtaining ISO certification in India typically involves making an application, document review by the registrar, determining pre-assessment needs, preparing an action plan, onsite inspection or audit, addressing any non-conformities, final audit, and finally obtaining the ISO certificate.

What are surveillance audits in the context of ISO certification?

Surveillance audits are periodic audits conducted by the certification body to ensure that the organization is maintaining the ISO quality standards and adhering to the requirements of the certification even after obtaining the certificate.

How long does the ISO certification process take?

The processing time for ISO certification can vary from organization to organization. The certification body will notify the details of the processing time after assessing the size of the organization and other relevant factors.

Is accreditation mandatory for an ISO certification body?

Accreditation is not compulsory for an ISO certification body, but it is highly recommended. Organizations should ensure that the certification body meets the requirements of ISO accreditation bodies, which helps establish credibility and trust in the certification process.

Can an organization get ISO certified directly from the International Organization for Standardization (ISO)?

No, the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) does not directly provide certifications to organizations. ISO develops and publishes international standards, but the certification process is carried out by external, accredited certification bodies.

content_sections.heading: Tamil Nadu Factory Registration
content_sections.content: Tamil Nadu [Factory Registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/factory-establishment-in-rajasthan) is mandated by the Factories Act, 1948, to ensure that the factory complies with the stipulated rules and safety guidelines. Upon registering the factory, the Government of Tamil Nadu issues a factory license. This license is a document of authorisation for granting permission to regulate and carry out manufacturing pursuits from a particular locality. In this article, we look at the Tamil Nadu Factory Registration procedure in detail.

content_sections.heading: Factories Act, 1948
content_sections.content:
According to the Factories Act, any person who wants to construct or extend a factory in Tamil Nadu has to get prior permission from the respective authority in advance before the commencement of the business.The Factories Act is established with the objective of ensuring the installation of adequate safety measures and promoting the health and welfare of the workers employed in factories. Also, it strives to curtail the hazardous growth of factories. To complete the Tamil Nadu Factory Registration and to obtain a factory license, you need to follow three steps:

- Get plan approval and permission to construct or extend a building as a factory
- Registration of Factory
- Get a license under the Factories Act

content_sections.heading: Eligibility Criteria

After construction, the factory owner or the manager has to register the factory under the Tamil Nadu Factories Act, 1948.

content_sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
content_sections.content:
Common questions aboutTamil Nadu Factory Registration.

What is the purpose of Tamil Nadu Factory Registration?

The purpose of Tamil Nadu Factory Registration is to ensure that the factory complies with the stipulated rules and safety guidelines under the Factories Act, 1948. It aims to promote the health and welfare of the workers employed in factories and curtail the hazardous growth of factories.

Who needs to register a factory in Tamil Nadu?

According to the Factories Act, 1948, any person who wants to construct, extend, or take into use any building as a factory in Tamil Nadu needs to register it. Factories employing ten or more workers with power or twenty or more workers without power in the manufacturing process need to be registered.

What are the steps involved in Tamil Nadu Factory Registration?

The three main steps involved in Tamil Nadu Factory Registration are: 1) Getting plan approval and permission to construct or extend a building as a factory, 2) Registration of the factory, and 3) Obtaining a license under the Factories Act.

What is the validity period of the Tamil Nadu Factory License?

The factory license granted to carry out business in Tamil Nadu is valid for ten years from the date of issue. After the expiry of this period, the license needs to be renewed.

Who is the licensing authority for Tamil Nadu Factory Registration?

The Directorate of Industrial Safety and Health, Government of Tamil Nadu, facilitates the process of Tamil Nadu Factory Registration. The licensing authority varies based on the number of workers employed and the nature of operations.

What documents are required for Tamil Nadu Factory Registration?

Some of the documents required for Tamil Nadu Factory Registration include Topo Plan, Site plan, Detailed plan of buildings, Sale deed/Lease deed, Proof of Identity and Address of Occupier, Manager, and Owner of premises, Memorandum of articles of Association, and List of Machinery with Horse Power details.

How long does it take to complete Tamil Nadu Factory Registration?

The total time for closing the application for Tamil Nadu Factory Registration will be 30 days from the date of successful submission of the application. The certificate for factory registration will be issued within 30 days of the successful submission of the application.

What is the process for renewing the Tamil Nadu Factory License?

The occupier or manager should apply for the renewal of the Tamil Nadu Factory License not less than two months before the date of expiry of the license. The renewal application can be submitted through the online portal along with the payment of prescribed fees.

Is there a fee for Tamil Nadu Factory Registration?

Yes, the applicant has to pay a prescribed fee for Tamil Nadu Factory Registration as per the proposed schedule. The nature of factory-wise fees is provided in the document attached with the article.

What is the validity period of the factory plan approval license in Tamil Nadu?

The factory plan approval license granted under the factories act to construct, extend, or use any building as a factory in Tamil Nadu is valid for a lifetime from the date of issue.

# Tamil Nadu Factory Registration

Tamil Nadu [Factory Registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/factory-establishment-in-rajasthan) is mandated by the Factories Act, 1948, to ensure that the factory complies with the stipulated rules and safety guidelines. Upon registering the factory, the Government of Tamil Nadu issues a factory license. This license is a document of authorisation for granting permission to regulate and carry out manufacturing pursuits from a particular locality. In this article, we look at the Tamil Nadu Factory Registration procedure in detail.

## Factories Act, 1948

According to the Factories Act, any person who wants to construct or extend a factory in Tamil Nadu has to get prior permission from the respective authority in advance before the commencement of the business.The Factories Act is established with the objective of ensuring the installation of adequate safety measures and promoting the health and welfare of the workers employed in factories. Also, it strives to curtail the hazardous growth of factories. To complete the Tamil Nadu Factory Registration and to obtain a factory license, you need to follow three steps:

- Get plan approval and permission to construct or extend a building as a factory
- Registration of Factory
- Get a license under the Factories Act

## Eligibility Criteria

Factories in which ten or more workers are employed with power being used in the manufacturing process and factories which are engaging twenty or more workers without using power in manufacturing process need to be registered under the Factories Act, 1948.Any Person (Owner of the factory, occupier) who wants to construct, extend or take into use any building as a factory in Tamil Nadu need to get plan and permission approval to construct, extend or to use any building as a factory. After construction, the factory owner or the manager has to register the factory under the Tamil Nadu Factories Act, 1948.

## When to Apply?

### Application for Factories Plan Approval

Before starting construction of a factory or in case of expansion of the factory, Occupier of the factory needs to apply for approval of plan and permission.

### Application for Factory Registration and License

If the application for approval of the factory plan and permission to construct a building as the factory has been successfully accepted and before starting the construction of a factory or in case of expansion of the factory, you can register the factory in Tamil Nadu and apply for a factory license.

## Licensing Authority

The Directorate of Industrial Safety and Health, Government of Tamil Nadu, facilitates the process of Tamil Nadu Factory Registration.

|     |     |     |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **S.No.** | **Employees** | **Approved by** |
| 1 | Factories employing 200 or less workers except those engaged in dangerous operations | Deputy Chief Inspector of Factories |
| 2 | Factories employing above 200 workers up to 1000 workers, except those engaged in dangerous operations | Joint Chief Inspector of Factories |
| 3 | Factories employing more than 1000 workers and all factories engaged in dangerous operations | Chief Inspector of Factories |

Factories Plan Approval

- Director of Industrial Safety and Health, Additional Director ISH and Joint Director ISH

Tamil Nadu Factory Registration

- Additional Director ISH - for allotment of Registration number to the New Factory
- Joint Director ISH - the issue of license

Note: This factory license is a certificate which grants permission to carry on the particular manufacturing business for which it is granted. It does not confer the ownership of property or land or permission for any other activities than for which it is issued.

## Processing Time

The total time for closing the application from the date of application for Tamil Nadu Factory Registration will be 30 days from the date of successful submission of the application. The certificate for factory registration will be issued within 30 days of the successful submission of the application.

## Applicable Fee

## Frequently Asked Questions

Common questions aboutTamil Nadu Factory Registration.

What is the purpose of Tamil Nadu Factory Registration?

The purpose of Tamil Nadu Factory Registration is to ensure that the factory complies with the stipulated rules and safety guidelines under the Factories Act, 1948. It aims to promote the health and welfare of the workers employed in factories and curtail the hazardous growth of factories.

Who needs to register a factory in Tamil Nadu?

According to the Factories Act, 1948, any person who wants to construct, extend, or take into use any building as a factory in Tamil Nadu needs to register it. Factories employing ten or more workers with power or twenty or more workers without power in the manufacturing process need to be registered.

What are the steps involved in Tamil Nadu Factory Registration?

The three main steps involved in Tamil Nadu Factory Registration are: 1) Getting plan approval and permission to construct or extend a building as a factory, 2) Registration of the factory, and 3) Obtaining a license under the Factories Act.

What is the validity period of the Tamil Nadu Factory License?

The factory license granted to carry out business in Tamil Nadu is valid for ten years from the date of issue. After the expiry of this period, the license needs to be renewed.

Who is the licensing authority for Tamil Nadu Factory Registration?

The Directorate of Industrial Safety and Health, Government of Tamil Nadu, facilitates the process of Tamil Nadu Factory Registration. The licensing authority varies based on the number of workers employed and the nature of operations.

What documents are required for Tamil Nadu Factory Registration?

Some of the documents required for Tamil Nadu Factory Registration include Topo Plan, Site plan, Detailed plan of buildings, Sale deed/Lease deed, Proof of Identity and Address of Occupier, Manager, and Owner of premises, Memorandum of articles of Association, and List of Machinery with Horse Power details.

How long does it take to complete Tamil Nadu Factory Registration?

The total time for closing the application for Tamil Nadu Factory Registration will be 30 days from the date of successful submission of the application. The certificate for factory registration will be issued within 30 days of the successful submission of the application.

What is the process for renewing the Tamil Nadu Factory License?

The occupier or manager should apply for the renewal of the Tamil Nadu Factory License not less than two months before the date of expiry of the license. The renewal application can be submitted through the online portal along with the payment of prescribed fees.

Is there a fee for Tamil Nadu Factory Registration?

Yes, the applicant has to pay a prescribed fee for Tamil Nadu Factory Registration as per the proposed schedule. The nature of factory-wise fees is provided in the document attached with the article.

What is the validity period of the factory plan approval license in Tamil Nadu?

The factory plan approval license granted under the factories act to construct, extend, or use any building as a factory in Tamil Nadu is valid for a lifetime from the date of issue.
