blogs.title: Find Complete Details of GST Registration Procedure

content_sections.heading: Find Complete Details of GST Registration Procedure
content_sections.content:
GST registration applies to all individuals and entities supplying goods or services in India. [GST registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-registration) becomes mandatory when the aggregate value of supplying goods exceeds Rs.40 lakh. The Ministry of Finance (MoF) has simplified the GST registration process to ease the tax filing process. If the entity operates in a special category state, GST registration becomes applicable if the value exceeds Rs.20 lakh p.a.  In this article, let us look at the eligibility to engage in the GST registration process under GST. The article also covers the documents required as well as the GST registration procedure online.

_**Simplify the GST registration process with IndiaFilings expert assistance!!**_

[Register Now!](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-registration)

content_sections.heading: Latest Update: [GST Registration within 3 Days: India’s New Auto-Approval System to Begin Nov. 1, 2025](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-registration/3-days-auto-approval-november-2025)
What is the Eligibility Criteria for GST Registration?
content_sections.content: The following mentions the categories and eligibility for GST registration and can go through the procedure for registration under GST:

content_sections.heading: [Aggregate Turnover](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/gst-turnover-limit)
content_sections.content: Any service provider who provides a service value of more than Rs. 20 Lakhs aggregate in a year is required to obtain GST registration. In the special category states, this limit is Rs. 10 lakhs. Any entity engaged in the exclusive supply of goods whose aggregate turnover crosses Rs.40 lakhs is required to obtain GST registration.

content_sections.heading: [Inter-state Business](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/gst-interstate-intrastate-meaning)
content_sections.content: An entity shall register for GST if they supply goods inter state, i.e., from one state to another irrespective of their aggregate turnover. Inter state service providers need to obtain GST registration only if their annual turnover exceeds Rs. 20 lakhs. (In special category states, this limit is Rs. 10 lakhs).

content_sections.heading: [E-commerce Platform](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/gst-ecommerce)
content_sections.content: Any individual supplying goods or services through an e-commerce platform shall apply for GST registration. The individual shall register irrespective of the turnover. Hence, sellers on Flipkart, Amazon and other e-commerce platforms must obtain registration to commence activity.

content_sections.heading: [Casual Taxable Persons](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/casual-taxable-persons-gst-registration)
content_sections.content: Any individual undertaking supply of goods, services seasonally or intermittently through a temporary stall or shop must apply for GST. The individual shall apply irrespective of the annual aggregate turnover.

content_sections.heading: Voluntary Registration
content_sections.content: Any entity can obtain GST registration voluntarily. Earlier, any entity who obtained GST voluntarily could not surrender the registration for up to a year. However, after revisions, voluntary GST registration can be surrendered by the applicant at any time.

content_sections.heading: Types of GST Registration
content_sections.content: The following details the types of GST registration which are essential to understand to follow through procedure for registration under GST, properly:

content_sections.heading: Normal Taxpayer
content_sections.content: This category of GST registration applies to taxpayers operating a business in India. Taxpayers registering for normal taxpayer does not require a deposit and also provided with unlimited validity date.

content_sections.heading: Composition Taxpayer
content_sections.content: To register as a Composition Taxpayer, the individual should enroll under GST Composition Scheme. Taxpayers enrolled under the Composition Scheme can pay a flat GST rate. However, the taxpayer would not be allowed to claim the input tax credit.

content_sections.heading: Casual Taxable Person
content_sections.content: Any taxpayer establishing a stall or seasonal shop shall register under Casual Taxable Person. To register as a casual taxable person, the taxpayer shall pay a deposit equal to the amount of GST liability. The liability should match the active registration periods. The registration remains active for a period of 3 months.

content_sections.heading: Non-Resident Taxable Person
content_sections.content:
The category non-resident taxable person applies to individuals located outside of India. The taxpayers can supply taxable goods or services to residents in India only after obtaining registration. To register as a non-resident taxable person, the taxpayer shall pay a deposit equal to the amount of GST liability. The liability should match the active registration periods. The registration remains active for a period of 3 months.

The following details the types of GST registration process:

- [GST Registration for Non-Resident Online Service Provider](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/gst-registration-non-resident-taxable-person)
- UN Body /Embassy/Other Notified Person
- Special Economic Zone Developer
- [Special Economic Zone Unit (SEZ)](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/supply-to-sez-under-gst)
- GST TDS Deductor-Government Entities
- GST TCS Collector -E-commerce Companies

content_sections.heading: What is the List of Documents Required for the GST Registration Procedure?
content_sections.content:
Before understanding how to do GST registration, let's look at the following checklist of documents required for obtaining GST registration:

|     |     |
| --- | --- |
| Proof of Constitution of Business (Any One) | Certificate of Incorporation |
| A passport-sized photo of the applicant | Passport-size photo of Promoter/Partner |
| Photo of the Authorised Signatory | Photo |
| Proof of Appointment of Authorised Signatory (Any One) | Letter of Authorisation |
|  | Copy of Resolution passed by BoD/ Managing Committee and Acceptance letter |
| Proof of Principal Place of business (Any One) | Electricity Bill |
|  | Legal ownership document |
|  | Municipal Khata Copy |
|  | Property Tax Receipt |
| Proof of Details of Bank Accounts (Any One) | The first page of Pass Book |
|  | Bank Statement |
|  | Cancelled Cheque |

[Click here to get the complete GST Registration Documents](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/documents-required-for-gst-registration)

content_sections.heading: Step-by-step Guide On the GST Registration Process Online
content_sections.content: The MoF has simplified the online procedure for registration under GST. The applicant can process of GST registration through the GST Portal. After submission of the application, the portal generates GST ARN immediately. Using the GST ARN, the applicant can check the application status and post queries if necessary. Within 7 days of ARN generation, the taxpayer shall receive a [GST registration certificate](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst/registration-certificate) and [GSTIN](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-registration). The following GST registration process guides you through on how to do GST registration clearly.

content_sections.heading: Step 1: Go to the GST Portal
content_sections.content:
Access the GST Portal ->/ > Services -> Registration > New Registration option.

![Content image](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/GST-Registration-Step-1.png)

content_sections.heading: Step 2: Generate a TRN by Completing OTP Validation
content_sections.content:
The new GST registration page is displayed. Select the New Registration option. If the GST registration application remains incomplete, the applicant shall continue filling the application using the TRN number.

- Select the Taxpayer type from the options provided.
- Choose the state as per the requirement.
- Enter the legal name of the business/entity, as mentioned in the PAN database. As the portal verifies the PAN automatically, the applicant should provide details as mentioned in the card.
- In the [Permanent Account Number (PAN)](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/pan-permanent-account-number) field, enter the PAN of the business or the PAN of the Proprietor. GST registration is linked to PAN. Hence, in the case of a company or LLP, enter the PAN of the company or LLP.
- Provide the email address of the Primary Authorised Signatory. (Will be verified in next step)
- Click the PROCEED button.

![Content image](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/GST-Registration-Step-2.png)

content_sections.heading: Step 3: OTP Verification & TRN Generation
content_sections.content:
On submission of the above information, the OTP Verification page is displayed. OTP will be valid only for 10 minutes. Hence, enter the two separate OTP sent to validate the email and mobile number.

- In the Mobile OTP field, enter the OTP.
- In the Email OTP field, enter the OTP.

content_sections.heading: Step 4: TRN Generated
content_sections.content:
On completing OTP verification, a TRN will be generated. TRN will now be used to complete and submit the GST registration application.

![Content image](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/GST-Registration-Step-3.png)

content_sections.heading: Step 5: Log in with TRN
content_sections.content:
Upon receiving the TRN, the applicant shall begin the process of GST registration. In the Temporary Reference Number (TRN) field on the GST Portal, enter the TRN generated and enter the captcha text as shown on the screen. Complete the OTP verification on mobile and email.

![Content image](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/GST-Registration-Step-4.png)

Click on the icon marked in red to start the process of GST registration.

content_sections.heading: Step 6: Submit Business Information
content_sections.content:
Various information must be submitted to navigate how to do GST registration properly. In the first tab, business details must be submitted.

- In the Trade Name field, enter the trade name of the business.
- Input the Constitution of the Business from the drop-down list.
- Enter the District and Sector/ Circle / Ward / Charge/ Unit from the drop-down list.
- In the Commissionerate Code, Division Code and Range Code drop-down lists, select the appropriate choice.
- Opt for the Composition Scheme, if necessary
- Input the date of commencement of business.
- Select the Date on whichthe  liability to register arises. This is the day the business crossed the aggregate turnover threshold for GST registration. Taxpayers are required to file the application for new GST registration within 30 days from the date on which the liability to register arises.

![Content image](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/GST-Registration-Business-Information.jpg)

content_sections.heading: Rule 14A: Opt-in for Simplified GST Registration (if eligible)

If you estimate that your monthly output tax liability on B2B supplies (i.e., to GST-registered customers) will not exceed ₹2.5 lakh, you can opt for simplified registration under Rule 14A.    - Select “Yes” for “Option for Registration under Rule 14A” (visible at the end of the Business Details tab). - This option is voluntary and triggers Aadhaar authentication-based fast-track processing.     Note: Once opted, Aadhaar authentication for the Primary Authorised Signatory and at least one Promoter/Partner becomes mandatory, and only one registration per State/UT per PAN is allowed under Rule 14A.    [Click here to know more about  Rule 14A](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-registration/simplified-gst-registration-scheme-rule-14a)
Step 7: Submit Promoter Information
content_sections.content:
In the next tab, provide promoters and directors information. In case of [proprietorship](https://www.indiafilings.com/proprietorship), the proprietors' information must be submitted. Details of up to 10 Promoters or Partners can be submitted in a GST registration application.

The following details must be submitted for the promoters:

- Personal details of the stakeholder like name, date of birth, address, mobile number, email address and gender.
- Designation of the promoter.
- DIN of the Promoter, only for the following types of applicants:


  - Private Limited Company
  - Public Limited Company
  - Public Sector Undertaking
  - Unlimited Company
  - Foreign Company registered in India

- Details of citizenship
- PAN & Aadhaar
- Residential address

In case the applicant provides Aadhaar, the applicant can use Aadhaar e-sign for filing GST returns instead of a [digital signature.](https://www.indiafilings.com/digital-signature)

![Content image](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/GST-Registration-Promoter-Information.jpg)

content_sections.heading: Step 8: Submit Authorised Signatory Information
content_sections.content: An authorised signatory is a person nominated by the promoters of the company. The nominated person shall hold responsibility for filing GST returns of the company. Further, the person shall also maintain the necessary compliance of the company. The authorised signatory will have full access to the GST Portal. The person shall undertake a wide range of transactions on behalf of the promoters.

content_sections.heading: Step 9: Principal Place of Business
content_sections.content:
In this section of the GST registration procedure, the applicant shall provide the details of the principal place of business. The Principal Place of Business acts as the primary location within the State where the taxpayer operates the business. It generally addresses the books of accounts and records. Hence, in the case of a company or LLP, the principal place of business shall be the registered office.

For the principal place of business, enter the following:

- Address of the principal place of business.
- Official contact such as Email address, telephone number (with STD Code), mobile number field and fax number (with STD Code).
- Nature of possession of the premises.

If the principal place of business is located in SEZ or the applicant acts as SEZ developer, the necessary documents/certificates issued by the Government of India are required to be uploaded by choosing ‘Others’ value in Nature of possession of premises drop-down and uploading the document.

In this section, upload documents to provide proof of ownership or occupancy of the property as follows:

- Own premises – Any document in support of the ownership of the premises, like the Latest Property Tax Receipt or Municipal Khata copy or a copy of the Electricity Bill.
- Rented or Leased premises – A copy of the valid Rent / Lease Agreement with any document in support of the ownership of the premises of the Lessor, like the Latest Property Tax Receipt or Municipal Khata copy or a copy of the Electricity Bill.
- Premises not covered above – A copy of the Consent Letter with any document in support of the ownership of the premises of the Consenter, like Municipal Khata copy or Electricity Bill copy. For shared properties, also, the same documents may also be uploaded.

![Content image](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/GST-Registration-Place-of-Business.jpg)

content_sections.heading: Step 10: Additional Place of Business
content_sections.content: Upon having an additional place of business, enter the details of the property in this tab. For instance, if the applicant is a seller on Flipkart or another e-commerce portal and uses the seller's warehouse, that location can be added as an additional place of business.

content_sections.heading: Step 11: Details of Goods and Services
content_sections.content:
In this section, the taxpayer must provide details of the top 5 goods and services supplied by the applicant. For goods supplied, provide the HSN code, and for services, provide the SAC code.

Click here to know more about the [HSN](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/hsn-code) code and [SAC code.](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/sac-codes)

![Content image](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/GST-Registration-Goods-Services-Supplied.png)

content_sections.heading: Step 12: Details of Bank Account
content_sections.content:
In this section, enter the number of bank accounts held by the applicant. If there are 5 accounts, enter 5. Then provide details of the bank account like account number, IFSC code and type of account. Finally, upload a copy of the bank statement or passbook in the place provided.

![Content image](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/GST-Registration-Bank-Account.jpg)

content_sections.heading: Step 13: Verification of Application
content_sections.content: In this step, verify the details submitted in the application before submission. Once verification is complete, select the verification checkbox. In the Name of Authorised Signatory drop-down list, select the name of the authorised signatory. Enter the place where the form is filled. Finally, digitally sign the application using a Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)/ E-Signature or EVC. Digitally signing using DSC is mandatory in the case of LLPs and Companies.

content_sections.heading: Rule 9A: Automatic Registration within 3 Days
content_sections.content:
In addition to Rule 14A, Rule 9A enables automatic approval of your registration application within 3 working days, based on system-generated risk analysis.

If your application is low-risk (based on data validation, PAN/Aadhaar match, etc.), the system may auto-approve your GSTIN — even if you haven’t opted for Rule 14A.This benefits all applicants, including those applying under regular GST registration rules (Rules 8, 12, 17).

- Date of Commencement of Business: The actual date when your business started operations.
- Date on which liability to register arises: This is the date your turnover crossed the prescribed threshold (e.g., ₹20L/₹40L depending on business type and state).
-  You must apply for registration within 30 days from this date.

[Click here to know more about Rule 9A: Automatic Registration Within 3 Working Days](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-registration/3-days-auto-approval-november-2025)

content_sections.heading: Step 14: ARN Generated
content_sections.content: On signing the application, the success message is displayed. The acknowledgement shall be received in the registered e-mail address and mobile phone number. The Application Reference Number (ARN) receipt is sent to the e-mail address and mobile phone number. Using the GST ARN Number, the status of the application can be tracked. This 14-step process can help you with how to do GST registration.

content_sections.heading: Do businesses need separate GST registrations for each state of operation?
content_sections.content:
Yes, businesses need separate GST registrations for each state where they have a place of business and supply goods or services. This is because GST is state-specific, and each state's operations are treated as distinct entities for compliance purposes.

content_sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
content_sections.content:
Common questions aboutGST Registration Procedure.

What is the aggregate turnover limit for mandatory GST registration?

For businesses supplying goods, GST registration becomes mandatory if the aggregate turnover exceeds Rs. 40 lakhs. For service providers or businesses operating in special category states, the aggregate turnover limit for mandatory GST registration is Rs. 20 lakhs.

Do e-commerce sellers need to obtain GST registration?

Yes, any individual or entity supplying goods or services through an e-commerce platform, such as Flipkart or Amazon, is required to obtain GST registration, regardless of their turnover.

What is the validity period for GST registration as a Casual Taxable Person?

GST registration for Casual Taxable Persons, who undertake supply of goods or services seasonally or intermittently through temporary stalls or shops, is valid for a period of 3 months.

Can a business voluntarily obtain GST registration even if their turnover is below the threshold?

Yes, any entity can voluntarily obtain GST registration, even if their turnover is below the mandatory threshold. After the revisions, voluntary GST registration can be surrendered by the applicant at any time.

What documents are required for GST registration?

Some of the key documents required for GST registration include proof of business constitution (like certificate of incorporation), passport-sized photographs, proof of principal place of business, proof of bank account details, and authorization documents for the signatory.

How long does it take to obtain a GST registration certificate after applying?

Within 7 days of generating the Application Reference Number (ARN), the taxpayer should receive the GST registration certificate and GSTIN (GST Identification Number) from the GST portal.

Is a separate GST registration required for each state of operation?

Yes, businesses need to obtain separate GST registrations for each state where they have a place of business and supply goods or services, as GST is state-specific.

What is the process for submitting the GST registration application online?

The GST registration process online involves generating a Temporary Reference Number (TRN) after OTP verification, logging in with the TRN, providing business details, promoter information, authorized signatory details, and submitting the application after digital signature or e-signature.

Is it mandatory to provide Aadhaar details during GST registration?

While providing Aadhaar details is optional during GST registration, if the applicant provides Aadhaar, they can use Aadhaar e-sign for filing GST returns instead of a digital signature.

What happens if a business fails to obtain GST registration within the prescribed timeline?

If a business fails to obtain GST registration within 30 days from the date on which the liability to register arises, they may be liable to pay late fees and penalties as prescribed under the GST laws.

# Find Complete Details of GST Registration Procedure

GST registration applies to all individuals and entities supplying goods or services in India. [GST registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-registration) becomes mandatory when the aggregate value of supplying goods exceeds Rs.40 lakh. The Ministry of Finance (MoF) has simplified the GST registration process to ease the tax filing process. If the entity operates in a special category state, GST registration becomes applicable if the value exceeds Rs.20 lakh p.a.  In this article, let us look at the eligibility to engage in the GST registration process under GST. The article also covers the documents required as well as the GST registration procedure online.

_**Simplify the GST registration process with IndiaFilings expert assistance!!**_

[Register Now!](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-registration)

### Latest Update: [GST Registration within 3 Days: India’s New Auto-Approval System to Begin Nov. 1, 2025](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-registration/3-days-auto-approval-november-2025)

## **What is the Eligibility Criteria for GST Registration?**

The following mentions the categories and eligibility for GST registration and can go through the procedure for registration under GST:

### [Aggregate Turnover](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/gst-turnover-limit)

Any service provider who provides a service value of more than Rs. 20 Lakhs aggregate in a year is required to obtain GST registration. In the special category states, this limit is Rs. 10 lakhs. Any entity engaged in the exclusive supply of goods whose aggregate turnover crosses Rs.40 lakhs is required to obtain GST registration.

### [Inter-state Business](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/gst-interstate-intrastate-meaning)

An entity shall register for GST if they supply goods inter state, i.e., from one state to another irrespective of their aggregate turnover. Inter state service providers need to obtain GST registration only if their annual turnover exceeds Rs. 20 lakhs. (In special category states, this limit is Rs. 10 lakhs).

### [E-commerce Platform](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/gst-ecommerce)

Any individual supplying goods or services through an e-commerce platform shall apply for GST registration. The individual shall register irrespective of the turnover. Hence, sellers on Flipkart, Amazon and other e-commerce platforms must obtain registration to commence activity.

### [Casual Taxable Persons](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/casual-taxable-persons-gst-registration)

Any individual undertaking supply of goods, services seasonally or intermittently through a temporary stall or shop must apply for GST. The individual shall apply irrespective of the annual aggregate turnover.

### Voluntary Registration

Any entity can obtain GST registration voluntarily. Earlier, any entity who obtained GST voluntarily could not surrender the registration for up to a year. However, after revisions, voluntary GST registration can be surrendered by the applicant at any time.

## Types of GST Registration

The following details the types of GST registration which are essential to understand to follow through procedure for registration under GST, properly:

### Normal Taxpayer

This category of GST registration applies to taxpayers operating a business in India. Taxpayers registering for normal taxpayer does not require a deposit and also provided with unlimited validity date.

### Composition Taxpayer

To register as a Composition Taxpayer, the individual should enroll under GST Composition Scheme. Taxpayers enrolled under the Composition Scheme can pay a flat GST rate. However, the taxpayer would not be allowed to claim the input tax credit.

### Casual Taxable Person

Any taxpayer establishing a stall or seasonal shop shall register under Casual Taxable Person. To register as a casual taxable person, the taxpayer shall pay a deposit equal to the amount of GST liability. The liability should match the active registration periods. The registration remains active for a period of 3 months.

### Non-Resident Taxable Person

The category non-resident taxable person applies to individuals located outside of India. The taxpayers can supply taxable goods or services to residents in India only after obtaining registration. To register as a non-resident taxable person, the taxpayer shall pay a deposit equal to the amount of GST liability. The liability should match the active registration periods. The registration remains active for a period of 3 months.

The following details the types of GST registration process:

- [GST Registration for Non-Resident Online Service Provider](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/gst-registration-non-resident-taxable-person)
- UN Body /Embassy/Other Notified Person
- Special Economic Zone Developer
- [Special Economic Zone Unit (SEZ)](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/supply-to-sez-under-gst)
- GST TDS Deductor-Government Entities
- GST TCS Collector -E-commerce Companies

## **What is the List of Documents Required for the GST Registration Procedure?**

Before understanding how to do GST registration, let's look at the following checklist of documents required for obtaining GST registration:

|     |     |
| --- | --- |
| Proof of Constitution of Business (Any One) | Certificate of Incorporation |
| A passport-sized photo of the applicant | Passport-size photo of Promoter/Partner |
| Photo of the Authorised Signatory | Photo |
| Proof of Appointment of Authorised Signatory (Any One) | Letter of Authorisation |
|  | Copy of Resolution passed by BoD/ Managing Committee and Acceptance letter |
| Proof of Principal Place of business (Any One) | Electricity Bill |
|  | Legal ownership document |
|  | Municipal Khata Copy |
|  | Property Tax Receipt |
| Proof of Details of Bank Accounts (Any One) | The first page of Pass Book |
|  | Bank Statement |
|  | Cancelled Cheque |

[Click here to get the complete GST Registration Documents](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/documents-required-for-gst-registration)

## **Step-by-step Guide On the GST Registration Process Online**

The MoF has simplified the online procedure for registration under GST. The applicant can process of GST registration through the GST Portal. After submission of the application, the portal generates GST ARN immediately. Using the GST ARN, the applicant can check the application status and post queries if necessary. Within 7 days of ARN generation, the taxpayer shall receive a [GST registration certificate](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst/registration-certificate) and [GSTIN](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-registration). The following GST registration process guides you through on how to do GST registration clearly.

### Step 1: Go to the GST Portal

Access the GST Portal ->/ > Services -> Registration > New Registration option.

![Content image](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/GST-Registration-Step-1.png)

### Step 2: Generate a TRN by Completing OTP Validation

The new GST registration page is displayed. Select the New Registration option. If the GST registration application remains incomplete, the applicant shall continue filling the application using the TRN number.

- Select the Taxpayer type from the options provided.
- Choose the state as per the requirement.
- Enter the legal name of the business/entity, as mentioned in the PAN database. As the portal verifies the PAN automatically, the applicant should provide details as mentioned in the card.
- In the [Permanent Account Number (PAN)](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/pan-permanent-account-number) field, enter the PAN of the business or the PAN of the Proprietor. GST registration is linked to PAN. Hence, in the case of a company or LLP, enter the PAN of the company or LLP.
- Provide the email address of the Primary Authorised Signatory. (Will be verified in next step)
- Click the PROCEED button.

![Content image](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/GST-Registration-Step-2.png)

### Step 3: OTP Verification & TRN Generation

On submission of the above information, the OTP Verification page is displayed. OTP will be valid only for 10 minutes. Hence, enter the two separate OTP sent to validate the email and mobile number.

- In the Mobile OTP field, enter the OTP.
- In the Email OTP field, enter the OTP.

### Step 4: TRN Generated

On completing OTP verification, a TRN will be generated. TRN will now be used to complete and submit the GST registration application.

![Content image](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/GST-Registration-Step-3.png)

### Step 5: Log in with TRN

Upon receiving the TRN, the applicant shall begin the process of GST registration. In the Temporary Reference Number (TRN) field on the GST Portal, enter the TRN generated and enter the captcha text as shown on the screen. Complete the OTP verification on mobile and email.

![Content image](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/GST-Registration-Step-4.png)

Click on the icon marked in red to start the process of GST registration.

### Step 6: Submit Business Information

Various information must be submitted to navigate how to do GST registration properly. In the first tab, business details must be submitted.

- In the Trade Name field, enter the trade name of the business.
- Input the Constitution of the Business from the drop-down list.
- Enter the District and Sector/ Circle / Ward / Charge/ Unit from the drop-down list.
- In the Commissionerate Code, Division Code and Range Code drop-down lists, select the appropriate choice.
- Opt for the Composition Scheme, if necessary
- Input the date of commencement of business.
- Select the Date on whichthe  liability to register arises. This is the day the business crossed the aggregate turnover threshold for GST registration. Taxpayers are required to file the application for new GST registration within 30 days from the date on which the liability to register arises.

![Content image](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/GST-Registration-Business-Information.jpg)

### Rule 14A: Opt-in for Simplified GST Registration (if eligible)

### If you estimate that your monthly output tax liability on B2B supplies (i.e., to GST-registered customers) will not exceed ₹2.5 lakh, you can opt for simplified registration under Rule 14A.    - Select “Yes” for “Option for Registration under Rule 14A” (visible at the end of the Business Details tab). - This option is voluntary and triggers Aadhaar authentication-based fast-track processing.     Note: Once opted, Aadhaar authentication for the Primary Authorised Signatory and at least one Promoter/Partner becomes mandatory, and only one registration per State/UT per PAN is allowed under Rule 14A.    [Click here to know more about  Rule 14A](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-registration/simplified-gst-registration-scheme-rule-14a)

### Step 7: Submit Promoter Information

In the next tab, provide promoters and directors information. In case of [proprietorship](https://www.indiafilings.com/proprietorship), the proprietors' information must be submitted. Details of up to 10 Promoters or Partners can be submitted in a GST registration application.

The following details must be submitted for the promoters:

- Personal details of the stakeholder like name, date of birth, address, mobile number, email address and gender.
- Designation of the promoter.
- DIN of the Promoter, only for the following types of applicants:


  - Private Limited Company
  - Public Limited Company
  - Public Sector Undertaking
  - Unlimited Company
  - Foreign Company registered in India

- Details of citizenship
- PAN & Aadhaar
- Residential address

In case the applicant provides Aadhaar, the applicant can use Aadhaar e-sign for filing GST returns instead of a [digital signature.](https://www.indiafilings.com/digital-signature)

![Content image](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/GST-Registration-Promoter-Information.jpg)

### Step 8: Submit Authorised Signatory Information

An authorised signatory is a person nominated by the promoters of the company. The nominated person shall hold responsibility for filing GST returns of the company. Further, the person shall also maintain the necessary compliance of the company. The authorised signatory will have full access to the GST Portal. The person shall undertake a wide range of transactions on behalf of the promoters.

### Step 9: Principal Place of Business

In this section of the GST registration procedure, the applicant shall provide the details of the principal place of business. The Principal Place of Business acts as the primary location within the State where the taxpayer operates the business. It generally addresses the books of accounts and records. Hence, in the case of a company or LLP, the principal place of business shall be the registered office.

For the principal place of business, enter the following:

- Address of the principal place of business.
- Official contact such as Email address, telephone number (with STD Code), mobile number field and fax number (with STD Code).
- Nature of possession of the premises.

If the principal place of business is located in SEZ or the applicant acts as SEZ developer, the necessary documents/certificates issued by the Government of India are required to be uploaded by choosing ‘Others’ value in Nature of possession of premises drop-down and uploading the document.

In this section, upload documents to provide proof of ownership or occupancy of the property as follows:

- Own premises – Any document in support of the ownership of the premises, like the Latest Property Tax Receipt or Municipal Khata copy or a copy of the Electricity Bill.
- Rented or Leased premises – A copy of the valid Rent / Lease Agreement with any document in support of the ownership of the premises of the Lessor, like the Latest Property Tax Receipt or Municipal Khata copy or a copy of the Electricity Bill.
- Premises not covered above – A copy of the Consent Letter with any document in support of the ownership of the premises of the Consenter, like Municipal Khata copy or Electricity Bill copy. For shared properties, also, the same documents may also be uploaded.

![Content image](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/GST-Registration-Place-of-Business.jpg)

### Step 10: Additional Place of Business

Upon having an additional place of business, enter the details of the property in this tab. For instance, if the applicant is a seller on Flipkart or another e-commerce portal and uses the seller's warehouse, that location can be added as an additional place of business.

### Step 11: Details of Goods and Services

In this section, the taxpayer must provide details of the top 5 goods and services supplied by the applicant. For goods supplied, provide the HSN code, and for services, provide the SAC code.

Click here to know more about the [HSN](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/hsn-code) code and [SAC code.](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/sac-codes)

![Content image](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/GST-Registration-Goods-Services-Supplied.png)

### Step 12: Details of Bank Account

In this section, enter the number of bank accounts held by the applicant. If there are 5 accounts, enter 5. Then provide details of the bank account like account number, IFSC code and type of account. Finally, upload a copy of the bank statement or passbook in the place provided.

![Content image](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/GST-Registration-Bank-Account.jpg)

### Step 13: Verification of Application

In this step, verify the details submitted in the application before submission. Once verification is complete, select the verification checkbox. In the Name of Authorised Signatory drop-down list, select the name of the authorised signatory. Enter the place where the form is filled. Finally, digitally sign the application using a Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)/ E-Signature or EVC. Digitally signing using DSC is mandatory in the case of LLPs and Companies.

### Rule 9A: Automatic Registration within 3 Days

In addition to Rule 14A, Rule 9A enables automatic approval of your registration application within 3 working days, based on system-generated risk analysis.

If your application is low-risk (based on data validation, PAN/Aadhaar match, etc.), the system may auto-approve your GSTIN — even if you haven’t opted for Rule 14A.This benefits all applicants, including those applying under regular GST registration rules (Rules 8, 12, 17).

- Date of Commencement of Business: The actual date when your business started operations.
- Date on which liability to register arises: This is the date your turnover crossed the prescribed threshold (e.g., ₹20L/₹40L depending on business type and state).
-  You must apply for registration within 30 days from this date.

[Click here to know more about Rule 9A: Automatic Registration Within 3 Working Days](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-registration/3-days-auto-approval-november-2025)

### Step 14: ARN Generated

On signing the application, the success message is displayed. The acknowledgement shall be received in the registered e-mail address and mobile phone number. The Application Reference Number (ARN) receipt is sent to the e-mail address and mobile phone number. Using the GST ARN Number, the status of the application can be tracked. This 14-step process can help you with how to do GST registration.

## Do businesses need separate GST registrations for each state of operation?

Yes, businesses need separate GST registrations for each state where they have a place of business and supply goods or services. This is because GST is state-specific, and each state's operations are treated as distinct entities for compliance purposes.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Common questions aboutGST Registration Procedure.

What is the aggregate turnover limit for mandatory GST registration?

For businesses supplying goods, GST registration becomes mandatory if the aggregate turnover exceeds Rs. 40 lakhs. For service providers or businesses operating in special category states, the aggregate turnover limit for mandatory GST registration is Rs. 20 lakhs.

Do e-commerce sellers need to obtain GST registration?

Yes, any individual or entity supplying goods or services through an e-commerce platform, such as Flipkart or Amazon, is required to obtain GST registration, regardless of their turnover.

What is the validity period for GST registration as a Casual Taxable Person?

GST registration for Casual Taxable Persons, who undertake supply of goods or services seasonally or intermittently through temporary stalls or shops, is valid for a period of 3 months.

Can a business voluntarily obtain GST registration even if their turnover is below the threshold?

Yes, any entity can voluntarily obtain GST registration, even if their turnover is below the mandatory threshold. After the revisions, voluntary GST registration can be surrendered by the applicant at any time.

What documents are required for GST registration?

Some of the key documents required for GST registration include proof of business constitution (like certificate of incorporation), passport-sized photographs, proof of principal place of business, proof of bank account details, and authorization documents for the signatory.

How long does it take to obtain a GST registration certificate after applying?

Within 7 days of generating the Application Reference Number (ARN), the taxpayer should receive the GST registration certificate and GSTIN (GST Identification Number) from the GST portal.

Is a separate GST registration required for each state of operation?

Yes, businesses need to obtain separate GST registrations for each state where they have a place of business and supply goods or services, as GST is state-specific.

What is the process for submitting the GST registration application online?

The GST registration process online involves generating a Temporary Reference Number (TRN) after OTP verification, logging in with the TRN, providing business details, promoter information, authorized signatory details, and submitting the application after digital signature or e-signature.

Is it mandatory to provide Aadhaar details during GST registration?

While providing Aadhaar details is optional during GST registration, if the applicant provides Aadhaar, they can use Aadhaar e-sign for filing GST returns instead of a digital signature.

What happens if a business fails to obtain GST registration within the prescribed timeline?

If a business fails to obtain GST registration within 30 days from the date on which the liability to register arises, they may be liable to pay late fees and penalties as prescribed under the GST laws.

blogs.title: GST Registration Issues - Problems & Solutions

content_sections.heading: GST Registration Issues - Problems & Solutions
content_sections.content: Nearly 1 crore businesses have obtained GST registrations in India. GST registration can be obtained through India Filings with Expert Support or you can do it yourself on the Government GST Portal. In this article, we look at some of the issues faced by many taxpayers along with the solutions.

content_sections.heading: No Provisional ID
content_sections.content:
**Problem:** You do not have a provisional ID or username to start the GST registration process.

**Solution:** All taxpayers applying for new GST Registration must first provide their name, business name, PAN, email and mobile number for starting the registration process. The process for GST registration starts at /registration/ . Make sure you start from this page. Once you provide the information mentioned above, an OTP is sent to the email id and mobile number for verification. On successful completion, the temporary reference number is provided to start the GST registration process.

In case your are a [non-resident taxable person](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/gst-registration-non-resident-taxable-person) under GST and do not have an Indian mobile number for receiving OTP, use the mobile number of the Authorised Signatory. All non-resident taxable persons must appoint a person in India to act as an Authorised Signatory.

content_sections.heading: Provisional ID Cancelled (Applicable for GST Migrations Only)
content_sections.content:
**Problem**: Your RC or Provisional ID is Cancelled.

In case you are migrating to GST from a VAT or Service Tax registration, you will have to follow the process for completing GST migration. During GST migration, if you had not filed service tax or VAT returns for a long-time, your GST registration could have been cancelled. In such cases, you will have to visit the nearest GST Seva Kendra and request the assistance of a GST officer for moving forward the provisional ID to a GSTIN, manually.

content_sections.heading: Unable to Select Range Code
content_sections.content:
**Problem:** No Range Code available

During the GST registration process, you will be required to select the applicable GST jurisdiction based on Range Code. In some cases, the drop-down list containing the range code would not populate. In such cases, make sure that your browser is compatible with the GST Portal.

GST portal is best viewed in 1024 x 768 resolution in Internet Explorer 10+, Google Chrome 49+, Firefox 45+ and Safari 6+. In case of lower resolution, the above issue could arise. Try refreshing the page or try accessing the GST registration application form using a different computer.

content_sections.heading: Digital Signature Errors
content_sections.content:
**Problem:** You are having a problem with the digital signature required for GST registration.

**Solution:** Digital signature is mandatory for the following types of GST registration applicants :

- Public Limited Company
- [Private Limited Company](https://www.indiafilings.com/company-registration)
- Unlimited Company
- Foreign Company
- [Limited Liability Partnership (LLP)](https://www.indiafilings.com/llp-registration)
- Foreign Limited Liability Partnership
- Public Sector Undertaking

Hence, before starting the GST registration process, ensure that you have obtained a

[class 2 or class 3 digital signature](https://www.indiafilings.com/digital-signature) for the authorised signatory. After obtaining the digital signature, you should install emSigner and register the DSC on the GST Portal. You can download emSigner using the link below :  /help/docsigner

Once the emSigner is installed and initialized, you will have to follow the steps below to register the DSC on the GST Portal. Then try the GST registration process again to solve the issue.

content_sections.heading: Step 1 : Log in to GST Portal
content_sections.content:

**Solution:** While registering for GST, you will have to provide PAN of the authorised signatory and the promoters. The PAN details provided on the GST portal must match the PAN database. content_sections.content:
Common questions aboutGST Registration Issues.

What should I do if I don't have a provisional ID to start the GST registration process?

If you don't have a provisional ID or username, you need to provide your name, business name, PAN, email, and mobile number to start the GST registration process. Once you submit these details, an OTP will be sent to your email and mobile number for verification. After successful verification, a temporary reference number will be provided to start the GST registration process.

How can I resolve the issue of a cancelled provisional ID during GST migration?

If your provisional ID or RC is cancelled during GST migration from a VAT or Service Tax registration, you will need to visit the nearest GST Seva Kendra and request assistance from a GST officer to manually move forward the provisional ID to a GSTIN.

What should I do if I cannot select the Range Code during GST registration?

If the drop-down list for selecting the Range Code is not populating, ensure that your browser is compatible with the GST Portal. The GST portal works best in 1024 x 768 resolution with Internet Explorer 10+, Google Chrome 49+, Firefox 45+, and Safari 6+. Try refreshing the page or accessing the application form from a different computer.

How can I resolve digital signature errors during GST registration?

To resolve digital signature errors, ensure that you have obtained a class 2 or class 3 digital signature for the authorized signatory before starting the GST registration process. Install emSigner, register the DSC on the GST Portal, and follow the steps provided in the article to register the DSC successfully.

What should I do if I have provided incorrect PAN details during GST registration?

The PAN details provided on the GST portal are immediately verified against the PAN database. If there is a discrepancy, the application will not proceed. In case your PAN has wrong information, you will need to change the PAN data first, following the process outlined in the article.

What should I do if I haven't received the ARN number after submitting the GST registration application?

If you have submitted all the information correctly but haven't received the ARN number, contact the GST Helpdesk at 0124-4688999 or 1800-1200-232 for assistance.

How can I obtain the GST registration certificate if I haven't received it after 5-10 days of application submission?

If you haven't received the GST registration certificate within 5-10 days of submission, check if the GST Officer has raised any queries on the GST Portal using the Temporary Reference Number. If there are no queries, the registration is deemed to be issued after 10 working days. You can also contact the GST Helpdesk or GST Seva Kendra for additional support.

What should I do if I have received a GST registration certificate with incorrect information?

If you have received a GST registration certificate with incorrect information, contact the GST Helpdesk or GST Seva Kendra for assistance. If you need to change the GST mobile number or email ID, follow the guides provided in the article.

Can I get expert support for GST registration and return filing?

Yes, you can simplify the GST registration and GST return filing process by seeking expert support from IndiaFilings.

How can I change my GST email ID or mobile number?

To change your GST email ID or mobile number, refer to the guides provided in the article on how to change the GST email ID and how to change the GST mobile number.

# GST Registration Issues - Problems & Solutions

Nearly 1 crore businesses have obtained GST registrations in India. GST registration can be obtained through India Filings with Expert Support or you can do it yourself on the Government GST Portal. In this article, we look at some of the issues faced by many taxpayers along with the solutions.

## No Provisional ID

**Problem:** You do not have a provisional ID or username to start the GST registration process.

**Solution:** All taxpayers applying for new GST Registration must first provide their name, business name, PAN, email and mobile number for starting the registration process. The process for GST registration starts at /registration/ . Make sure you start from this page. Once you provide the information mentioned above, an OTP is sent to the email id and mobile number for verification. On successful completion, the temporary reference number is provided to start the GST registration process.

In case your are a [non-resident taxable person](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/gst-registration-non-resident-taxable-person) under GST and do not have an Indian mobile number for receiving OTP, use the mobile number of the Authorised Signatory. All non-resident taxable persons must appoint a person in India to act as an Authorised Signatory.

## Provisional ID Cancelled (Applicable for GST Migrations Only)

**Problem**: Your RC or Provisional ID is Cancelled.

In case you are migrating to GST from a VAT or Service Tax registration, you will have to follow the process for completing GST migration. During GST migration, if you had not filed service tax or VAT returns for a long-time, your GST registration could have been cancelled. In such cases, you will have to visit the nearest GST Seva Kendra and request the assistance of a GST officer for moving forward the provisional ID to a GSTIN, manually.

## Unable to Select Range Code

**Problem:** No Range Code available

During the GST registration process, you will be required to select the applicable GST jurisdiction based on Range Code. In some cases, the drop-down list containing the range code would not populate. In such cases, make sure that your browser is compatible with the GST Portal.

GST portal is best viewed in 1024 x 768 resolution in Internet Explorer 10+, Google Chrome 49+, Firefox 45+ and Safari 6+. In case of lower resolution, the above issue could arise. Try refreshing the page or try accessing the GST registration application form using a different computer.

## Digital Signature Errors

**Problem:** You are having a problem with the digital signature required for GST registration.

**Solution:** Digital signature is mandatory for the following types of GST registration applicants :

- Public Limited Company
- [Private Limited Company](https://www.indiafilings.com/company-registration)
- Unlimited Company
- Foreign Company
- [Limited Liability Partnership (LLP)](https://www.indiafilings.com/llp-registration)
- Foreign Limited Liability Partnership
- Public Sector Undertaking

Hence, before starting the GST registration process, ensure that you have obtained a

[class 2 or class 3 digital signature](https://www.indiafilings.com/digital-signature) for the authorised signatory. After obtaining the digital signature, you should install emSigner and register the DSC on the GST Portal. You can download emSigner using the link below :  /help/docsigner

Once the emSigner is installed and initialized, you will have to follow the steps below to register the DSC on the GST Portal. Then try the GST registration process again to solve the issue.

### Step 1 : Log in to GST Portal

Login to the GST Portal using the temporary reference number and select My Profile.

![Step 1 - My Profile](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2017/10/Step-1-My-Profile-1024x210.png) Step 1 - My Profile

### Step 2: Register DSC

Select Register or Update DSC on the My Profile page.

![Step 2 - Register DSC](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2017/10/Step-2-Register-DSC-1024x339.png) Step 2 - Register DSC

### Step 3: Select PAN

Select PAN of the authorised signatory for whom DSC was earlier obtained.

![Step 3 - Select PAN](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2017/10/Step-3-Select-PAN.png) Step 3 - Select PAN

### Step 4: Select DSC Certificate

Select DSC certificate of the authorised signatory from emSigner.

![Step 4 - Select DSC from emSigner](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2017/10/Step-4-Select-DSC-from-emSigner.png) Step 4 - Select DSC from emSigner

### Step 5: DSC Registered

On submission, DSC would be registered, if the steps above are followed.

![Step 5 - Successfully Saved](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2017/10/Step-5-Successfully-Saved.png) Step 5 - Successfully Saved

## Incorrect PAN Details

**Problem:** Incorrect PAN details.

**Solution:** While registering for GST, you will have to provide PAN of the authorised signatory and the promoters. The PAN details provided on the GST portal must match the PAN database. The data submitted on GST portal is immediately verified against the PAN database. Hence, if there is any discrepancy, the application would not be able to proceed.

In case your PAN has wrong information and you wish to insert correct data in GST registration application, you will first have to change PAN data.

[Process for changing PAN data is provided in this article.](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/pan-card-name-change)

## ARN Number Not Received

If you had submitted all the information correctly and you have not received any ARN number, contact the GST Helpdesk at:

**GST helpdesk 0124-4688999 or at 1800-1200-232**

## GST Registration Certificate Not Received

In case you have not received GST registration certificate after about 5 - 10 days of submission of application, check whether the GST Officer has raised any queries on the GST Portal by accessing with the Temporary Reference Number.

In case, there are no queries and you have not received GST registration certificate or GSTIN, the registration would be deemed to be issued after 10 working days.

You can also contact the GST helpdesk or GST Seva Kendra for additional support in obtaining the

[GST registration certificate.](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/gst-registration-certificate)

## Incorrect Information on GST Registration Certificate

If you have received a GST registration certificate with incorrect information, you can contact the GST helpdesk or GST Seva Kendra. In case you would like to change GST mobile number or email id, check out the following guides:

blogs.title: Deposit for GST Registration

content_sections.heading: Deposit for GST Registration
content_sections.content: All individuals involved in businesses and not-for-profits engaged in the supply of goods and services to persons or entities in India. GST registration can be broadly be classified into three different types, namely GST registration for regular taxpayers, GST registration for casual taxable persons and GST registration for non-resident taxable persons. Under the GST Act, casual taxable persons or non-resident taxable persons should mandatorily obtain GST registration, irrespective of aggregate annual turnover. In this article, let us look at the deposit requirement for those registering for GST as a casual taxable person or non-resident taxable person.

content_sections.heading: Amount of Deposit for GST Registration
content_sections.content:
All casual taxable persons and

[non-resident taxable persons applying for GST registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/gst-registration-for-foreign-companies) are required to make an advance deposit of tax equal to the estimated tax liability of the taxpayer for the period for which the registration is sought. After depositing the GST payment in advance, the taxpayer shall receive the credit in the electronic cash ledger to use against payment of GST liability, fee, penalty or other charges. Further, all temporary GST registration for a casual taxable person shall detail the expiry date of registration. In case the taxpayer needs an extension of temporary GST registration, then additional tax must be deposited as per the amount of tax liability expected to get an extension of the GST registration.

For example, if a casual taxable person estimates a GST liability of Rs.18 lakhs for a period of 2 months during the Diwali season, then the concerned individual shall deposit Rs.18 lakhs in advance while applying for GST registration.

It is important to note that GST registration for casual taxable persons and non-resident taxable persons are provided for a period of less than 90 days or the period requested in the GST registration application. To lighten the process of GST registration for casual taxable persons and non-residents taxable persons, the authorized officer can extend the registration period for 90 days.

![Paying Deposit for GST Registration](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2017/06/Paying-Deposit-for-GST-Registration-1024x745.png) Paying Deposit for GST Registration

content_sections.heading: Casual Taxable Persons under GST
content_sections.content: A [casual taxable person](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/casual-taxable-persons-gst-registration) under GST means a person who occasionally undertakes transactions involving the supply of goods or services or both in the course or furtherance of business, whether as principal, agent or in any other capacity, in a State or a Union territory where he has no fixed place of business. An example of a casual taxable person under GST; firework shops set up during Diwali times or shops set up in temporary exhibitions.

content_sections.heading: Non-Resident Taxable Persons under GST
content_sections.content: Non-resident taxable person means any person who occasionally undertakes transactions involving the supply of goods or services or both, whether as principal or agent or in any other capacity, but who has no fixed place of business or residence in India.

content_sections.heading: Regular Taxpayers
content_sections.content:
As per GST rules, no regular taxpayers shall pay any deposit for the advanced tax while applying for GST registration. However, after obtaining GST registration, all regular taxpayers would be required to f

[ile monthly GST returns](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-return-filing) regularly or pay the penalty as per the GST Act. Penalty for late filing of GST returns is Rs.100 per day, with a maximum penalty of Rs.5000, per each instance of default.

content_sections.heading: Procedure for Paying Deposit for GST Registration
content_sections.content:
Upon filing a GST registration application for a casual taxable person or non-resident taxable person, the system generates a temporary reference number for making an advance deposit of tax into the electronic cash ledger. After the completion of the process for the advance tax payment, the portal shall generate an acknowledgement for the payment made. After the acknowledgement, the completes the GST registration.

India Filings can help to

[obtain GST Registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-registration), talk to an India Filings Business Advisor today.

content_sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
content_sections.content:
Common questions aboutGST Registration Deposit for Casual and Non Resident Taxpayers.

What is the purpose of paying a deposit for GST registration?

The deposit for GST registration is an advance payment of the estimated tax liability that casual taxable persons and non-resident taxable persons must make. This deposit is required to obtain GST registration and the amount is credited to the electronic cash ledger, which can be used to pay GST, fees, penalties, or other charges.

Who needs to pay the deposit for GST registration?

Casual taxable persons and non-resident taxable persons are required to pay the deposit for GST registration, irrespective of their aggregate annual turnover. Regular taxpayers are not required to pay this deposit.

How is the amount of deposit for GST registration determined?

The deposit amount is equal to the estimated tax liability of the taxpayer for the period for which the registration is sought. For example, if a casual taxable person estimates a GST liability of Rs. 18 lakhs for 2 months, they must deposit Rs. 18 lakhs as the deposit.

What happens if the registration period needs to be extended?

If a casual taxable person or non-resident taxable person needs to extend their temporary GST registration beyond the initial period, they must deposit additional tax based on their expected tax liability for the extended period.

Can the GST registration period be extended for casual taxable persons and non-resident taxable persons?

Yes, the authorized officer can extend the registration period for casual taxable persons and non-resident taxable persons for up to 90 days.

What is a casual taxable person under GST?

# Deposit for GST Registration

All individuals involved in businesses and not-for-profits engaged in the supply of goods and services to persons or entities in India. GST registration can be broadly be classified into three different types, namely GST registration for regular taxpayers, GST registration for casual taxable persons and GST registration for non-resident taxable persons. Under the GST Act, casual taxable persons or non-resident taxable persons should mandatorily obtain GST registration, irrespective of aggregate annual turnover. In this article, let us look at the deposit requirement for those registering for GST as a casual taxable person or non-resident taxable person.

## Amount of Deposit for GST Registration

All casual taxable persons and

[non-resident taxable persons applying for GST registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/gst-registration-for-foreign-companies) are required to make an advance deposit of tax equal to the estimated tax liability of the taxpayer for the period for which the registration is sought. After depositing the GST payment in advance, the taxpayer shall receive the credit in the electronic cash ledger to use against payment of GST liability, fee, penalty or other charges. Further, all temporary GST registration for a casual taxable person shall detail the expiry date of registration. In case the taxpayer needs an extension of temporary GST registration, then additional tax must be deposited as per the amount of tax liability expected to get an extension of the GST registration.

For example, if a casual taxable person estimates a GST liability of Rs.18 lakhs for a period of 2 months during the Diwali season, then the concerned individual shall deposit Rs.18 lakhs in advance while applying for GST registration.

It is important to note that GST registration for casual taxable persons and non-resident taxable persons are provided for a period of less than 90 days or the period requested in the GST registration application. To lighten the process of GST registration for casual taxable persons and non-residents taxable persons, the authorized officer can extend the registration period for 90 days.

### Casual Taxable Persons under GST

A [casual taxable person](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/casual-taxable-persons-gst-registration) under GST means a person who occasionally undertakes transactions involving the supply of goods or services or both in the course or furtherance of business, whether as principal, agent or in any other capacity, in a State or a Union territory where he has no fixed place of business. An example of a casual taxable person under GST; firework shops set up during Diwali times or shops set up in temporary exhibitions.

### Non-Resident Taxable Persons under GST

Non-resident taxable person means any person who occasionally undertakes transactions involving the supply of goods or services or both, whether as principal or agent or in any other capacity, but who has no fixed place of business or residence in India.

### Regular Taxpayers

As per GST rules, no regular taxpayers shall pay any deposit for the advanced tax while applying for GST registration. However, after obtaining GST registration, all regular taxpayers would be required to f

[ile monthly GST returns](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-return-filing) regularly or pay the penalty as per the GST Act. Penalty for late filing of GST returns is Rs.100 per day, with a maximum penalty of Rs.5000, per each instance of default.

## Procedure for Paying Deposit for GST Registration

Upon filing a GST registration application for a casual taxable person or non-resident taxable person, the system generates a temporary reference number for making an advance deposit of tax into the electronic cash ledger. After the completion of the process for the advance tax payment, the portal shall generate an acknowledgement for the payment made. After the acknowledgement, the completes the GST registration.

Who needs to pay the deposit for GST registration?

Casual taxable persons and non-resident taxable persons are required to pay the deposit for GST registration, irrespective of their aggregate annual turnover. Regular taxpayers are not required to pay this deposit.

The deposit amount is equal to the estimated tax liability of the taxpayer for the period for which the registration is sought. For example, if a casual taxable person estimates a GST liability of Rs. 18 lakhs for 2 months, they must deposit Rs. 18 lakhs as the deposit.

If a casual taxable person or non-resident taxable person needs to extend their temporary GST registration beyond the initial period, they must deposit additional tax based on their expected tax liability for the extended period.

Yes, the authorized officer can extend the registration period for casual taxable persons and non-resident taxable persons for up to 90 days.

Is there a penalty for late filing of GST returns for regular taxpayers?

content_sections.heading: New GST Registration after Cancellation
content_sections.content:
GST officers have been bestowed upon with the powers, vide section 29 (2) of the Central Goods and Service Tax Act, 2017, to cancel

[GST registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-registration) of a concerned person on account of non-compliance of the statutory provisions / non-filing of [GST returns](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-return-filing). If after cancellation a person wants to continue his/her business, he/she is required to apply for revocation of cancellation of the registration.

In case of new GST registration after the [cancellation of GST registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/gst-registration-cancellation) on account of non-compliance of the statutory provisions and applying for revocation thereon, the registered person applying for revocation would be required to pay all the pending tax liabilities.

However, in order to avoid payment of pending tax liabilities, it has been noted by the Government that cases wherein the GST registration has been cancelled by the proper officer, on account of non-compliance of the statutory provisions - the concerned registered person, instead of applying for revocation of cancellation of registration is applying for fresh registration under GST.

Vide circular no. 95/14/2019-GST dated 28th March, 2019, the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs has clarified the consequence the taxpayer has to face in case of non-revocation of cancelled registration and applying for new registration which is being summarized in the present article.

content_sections.heading: Section 29(2) of the CGST Act
content_sections.content:
Section 29(2) of the CGST Act declares the provisions and powers available to the concerned GST officer to cancel the registration under the following cases :

- If the taxpayer has contravened provisions of the GST Act or rules made therein.
- If the taxpayer under Section 10 has made taxable supplies and holds registration but has not filed a return for a consecutive period of three years.
- If the taxpayer is a registered taxpayer, who has not furnished any tax return for the consecutive 6 six months.
- If the taxpayer has opted for voluntary registration but has not commenced his business within 6 months from the date of registration.
- If the taxpayer has obtained registration by means of fraud, wilful misstatement or through suppression of facts.

Note: The notification issued by the GST Council on 28th March 2019, allows all taxpayers whose registrations were cancelled can now apply for fresh registration in GST instead of applying for revocation.

As per the new rules, the proper officer is responsible for granting new registrations to the taxpayers whose

[GST registrations](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-registration) were cancelled previously and has applied for revocation. The tax officers have been issued with guidelines to verify the reasons for previous cancellations and unauthorized holding of new GST registrations along with existing registration in the same state.

content_sections.heading: New Process
content_sections.content: In order to protect revenue due to modus operandi adopted by errant taxpayers, as mentioned above, proper officer would exercise extra caution while processing of the application of a tax payer opting for another registration within the same State.

content_sections.heading: Vetting of New Registration Application
Consequences of Not Applying for Revocation
content_sections.content:
In case there is a cancellation of registration and the taxpayer has not applied for

[revocation of cancellation of registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/revocation-of-gst-registration-cancellation) and non-compliance still continues, then, it shall be deemed to be a ‘deficiency’ within the meaning of rule 9 (2) of the Central Goods and Service Tax Rules, 2017 and the officer may consider the same as a ground for rejection of application for fresh registration.

**Thus, in the coming days, taxpayers who have not complied with GST return filing regulations will find it extremely hard to obtain GST registration again.**

content_sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
content_sections.content:
Common questions aboutGST Registration After Cancellation in Financial Services.

What is the consequence of applying for a new GST registration instead of revocation of cancelled registration?

If a taxpayer's GST registration has been cancelled due to non-compliance of statutory provisions and they apply for a new registration instead of revocation, it will be considered a 'deficiency' under Rule 9(2) of the Central Goods and Service Tax Rules, 2017. This could lead to rejection of the application for fresh registration.

Can a taxpayer apply for a new GST registration in the same state after cancellation of their previous registration?

Yes, as per the notification issued by the GST Council on 28th March 2019, taxpayers whose registrations were cancelled can now apply for fresh registration in GST instead of applying for revocation of the cancelled registration.

What steps will the proper officer take while processing an application for a new registration from a taxpayer whose previous registration was cancelled?

The proper officer will analyze whether the existing registration continues or is being cancelled, the reason for cancellation (non-filing of returns for a specific period), and whether the taxpayer has applied for revocation of cancellation of registration.

Under what circumstances can the proper officer reject an application for a new GST registration?

If a taxpayer's registration was cancelled due to non-compliance of Section 29(2) of the CGST Act, and they have not applied for revocation of cancellation, the proper officer may consider this as a ground for rejection of the application for fresh registration.

What is the significance of Section 29(2) of the CGST Act in the context of new GST registration after cancellation?

Section 29(2) of the CGST Act provides the provisions and powers available to the GST officer to cancel the registration under specific cases, such as contravention of the GST Act or rules, non-filing of returns for a specified period, or obtaining registration through fraud or misstatement.

Can the proper officer cancel a newly issued GST registration if the taxpayer has defaulted under Section 29 or any other provisions of the Act?

Yes, the notification empowers the proper officer to cancel the new registration if there is any default in respect of Section 29 or any other provisions of the Act.

What is the significance of the circular no. 95/14/2019-GST dated 28th March 2019 in the context of new GST registration after cancellation?

This circular clarifies the consequences a taxpayer has to face in case of not applying for revocation of cancelled registration and instead applying for a fresh registration under GST.

What is the purpose of the guidelines issued to tax officers regarding new GST registrations after cancellation?

The guidelines instruct tax officers to verify the reasons for previous cancellations and unauthorized holding of new GST registrations along with existing registration in the same state. This is to protect revenue due to modus operandi adopted by errant taxpayers.

What is the significance of the term 'deficiency' in the context of new GST registration after cancellation?

If a taxpayer's registration was cancelled due to non-compliance of statutory provisions, and they apply for a new registration without revocation, it shall be deemed to be a 'deficiency' within the meaning of Rule 9(2) of the Central Goods and Service Tax Rules, 2017. This could lead to rejection of the application for fresh registration.

What is the purpose of the notification issued by the GST Council on 28th March 2019 regarding new GST registration after cancellation?

The purpose of this notification is to allow taxpayers whose registrations were cancelled to apply for fresh registration in GST instead of applying for revocation of the cancelled registration. It also provides guidelines to tax officers to verify and prevent misuse of this provision.

The tax officers have been issued with guidelines to verify the reasons for previous cancellations and unauthorized holding of new GST registrations along with existing registration in the same state.

## **New Process**

In order to protect revenue due to modus operandi adopted by errant taxpayers, as mentioned above, proper officer would exercise extra caution while processing of the application of a tax payer opting for another registration within the same State.

## **Vetting of New Registration Application**

If a tax payer already having one registration, applies for another registration within the same state, the proper officer would undertake the following analysis –

- Whether existing registration continues or is being cancelled;
- If the existing registration is cancelled, then it would be analyzed whether the registration is cancelled on account of violation of provisions of section 29 (2) (b) \[composition dealer has not furnished returns for 3 consecutive tax period\] or section 29 (2) (c) \[registered taxpayer has not furnished returns for a continuous period of 6 months\];
- If the registration is cancelled, whether the taxpayer has opted/filed application for revocation of cancellation of registration.

## **Consequences of Not Applying for Revocation**

In case there is a cancellation of registration and the taxpayer has not applied for

[revocation of cancellation of registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/revocation-of-gst-registration-cancellation) and non-compliance still continues, then, it shall be deemed to be a ‘deficiency’ within the meaning of rule 9 (2) of the Central Goods and Service Tax Rules, 2017 and the officer may consider the same as a ground for rejection of application for fresh registration.

**Thus, in the coming days, taxpayers who have not complied with GST return filing regulations will find it extremely hard to obtain GST registration again.**
