## Frequently Asked Questions

Common questions aboutGST Registration After Cancellation in Financial Services.

What is the consequence of applying for a new GST registration instead of revocation of cancelled registration?

If a taxpayer's GST registration has been cancelled due to non-compliance of statutory provisions and they apply for a new registration instead of revocation, it will be considered a 'deficiency' under Rule 9(2) of the Central Goods and Service Tax Rules, 2017. This could lead to rejection of the application for fresh registration.

Can a taxpayer apply for a new GST registration in the same state after cancellation of their previous registration?

Yes, as per the notification issued by the GST Council on 28th March 2019, taxpayers whose registrations were cancelled can now apply for fresh registration in GST instead of applying for revocation of the cancelled registration.

What steps will the proper officer take while processing an application for a new registration from a taxpayer whose previous registration was cancelled?

The proper officer will analyze whether the existing registration continues or is being cancelled, the reason for cancellation (non-filing of returns for a specific period), and whether the taxpayer has applied for revocation of cancellation of registration.

Under what circumstances can the proper officer reject an application for a new GST registration?

If a taxpayer's registration was cancelled due to non-compliance of Section 29(2) of the CGST Act, and they have not applied for revocation of cancellation, the proper officer may consider this as a ground for rejection of the application for fresh registration.

What is the significance of Section 29(2) of the CGST Act in the context of new GST registration after cancellation?

Section 29(2) of the CGST Act provides the provisions and powers available to the GST officer to cancel the registration under specific cases, such as contravention of the GST Act or rules, non-filing of returns for a specified period, or obtaining registration through fraud or misstatement.

Can the proper officer cancel a newly issued GST registration if the taxpayer has defaulted under Section 29 or any other provisions of the Act?

Yes, the notification empowers the proper officer to cancel the new registration if there is any default in respect of Section 29 or any other provisions of the Act.

What is the significance of the circular no. 95/14/2019-GST dated 28th March 2019 in the context of new GST registration after cancellation?

This circular clarifies the consequences a taxpayer has to face in case of not applying for revocation of cancelled registration and instead applying for a fresh registration under GST.

What is the purpose of the guidelines issued to tax officers regarding new GST registrations after cancellation?

The guidelines instruct tax officers to verify the reasons for previous cancellations and unauthorized holding of new GST registrations along with existing registration in the same state. This is to protect revenue due to modus operandi adopted by errant taxpayers.

What is the significance of the term 'deficiency' in the context of new GST registration after cancellation?

If a taxpayer's registration was cancelled due to non-compliance of statutory provisions, and they apply for a new registration without revocation, it shall be deemed to be a 'deficiency' within the meaning of Rule 9(2) of the Central Goods and Service Tax Rules, 2017. This could lead to rejection of the application for fresh registration.

What is the purpose of the notification issued by the GST Council on 28th March 2019 regarding new GST registration after cancellation?

The purpose of this notification is to allow taxpayers whose registrations were cancelled to apply for fresh registration in GST instead of applying for revocation of the cancelled registration. It also provides guidelines to tax officers to verify and prevent misuse of this provision.

What is the GST registration requirement for transporters, godowns, and warehouses?

GST registration is mandatory for transporters, godowns, and warehouses to ensure that the movement and storage of goods within India are accounted for and monitored under the GST regime. The unique enrollment number generated for godowns, warehouses, and transporters upon GST registration is used for identification and tracking purposes under the GST regime. It ensures that the movement and storage of goods are properly accounted for and monitored.

What is the aggregate turnover criteria for obtaining GST registration in general?

For most states, any person doing business with an aggregate turnover exceeding Rs. 20 lakhs in a financial year must obtain GST registration. For special category states, the GST aggregate turnover threshold is Rs. 10 lakhs.

Yes, irrespective of their aggregate turnover, any business involved in inter-state supply of goods or services must obtain GST registration.

Yes, any business that becomes liable to pay GST under the reverse charge mechanism must obtain GST registration, irrespective of their turnover.

No, GST registration is mandatory for all transporters, godowns, and warehouses, regardless of their turnover or whether they are already registered for GST or not. They must obtain GST registration by filing Form GST ENR-01 to operate legally under the GST regime.

content_sections.heading: GST Registration Applicability for One Person Company (OPC)
content_sections.content:
- According to the GST Act, any person, including companies and LLPs, must register under GST if their total turnover is more than Rs. 20 lakh (Rs. 10 lakhs for special category states in hill states and North-Eastern states).
- If your turnover is currently above 20 lakhs or expected to reach that point, it's necessary to process the online GST registration.
- GST registration is mandatory for the OPC companies which supply goods or services outside the state, regardless of annual turnover. For example, GST registration is necessary if an OPC company registered in Assam supplies goods to Gujarat.
- Existing OPCs with service tax, VAT, or Excise registration must enrol for GST Registration. The GST department initially provides a provisional ID and Password for GST Migration. GST registration is necessary for existing OPCs with service tax, VAT, or Excise registration.
- An OPC company that supplies goods or services through e-commerce platforms must apply for GST registration. For example, an OPC company supplying goods on e-commerce platforms like Amazon, eBay, or Flipkart must register for GST, especially for work contracts in India.
- The registration process can be done digitally without the need for manual intervention or physical paper submissions.
- The registration is usually completed within  4-6 working days, and the supplier will get a 15-digit GSTIN (GST identification number) along with a registration certificate from the GST department.

content_sections.heading: Benefits of GST Registration for OPC in India
content_sections.content:
- **Legal Recognition**: OPC GST registration provides legal recognition to the business entity, making it a legitimate and compliant organization. It signals the authority to the customers.
- **Trust and Credibility:** GST registration shows the credibility and trustworthiness of the OPC in the eyes of customers, suppliers, and other stakeholders.
- **Access to Input Tax Credit (ITC**): Registered OPCs can utilise Input Tax Credit on the GST paid on goods and services. It can reduce the overall tax liability.
- **Interstate Business Facilitation**: GST registration is necessary for interstate trade businesses. It helps the OPCs to expand their market reach and engage in business transactions across state borders.
- **Compliance with Government Regulations**: GST registration ensures compliance with government tax regulations, minimizing the risk of penalties or legal actions. It provides the space to run a business without the disturbance of legal problems.
- **Claiming Refunds**: In certain cases, registered OPCs can claim GST refunds, especially if they deal with exports or zero-rated supplies
- **Streamlined Tax Compliance**: GST registration enables OPCs to streamline their tax compliance processes and meet reporting requirements efficiently.

content_sections.heading: List of Documents Required GST Registration for OPC
content_sections.content:
Ensure you have the following documents before the One Person Company Registration GST registration.

- PAN Card of the OPC
- Aadhar Card and PAN card of the sole proprietor or director
- Proof of Business Registration (Certificate of Incorporation)
- Address Proof for the registered office – Copy of electricity bill/ water bill/ landline bill/ municipal khata copy/ property tax receipt from your registered office. If it is a rented office, the owner's no-objection certificate (NOC) is required.
- Bank Account Details - Canceled cheque or bank statement
- Memorandum of Association (MOA) and Articles of Association (AOA)
- Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)
- Authorization Letter (if applicable)
- Board Resolution passed by the Board of Directors of the OPC
- Passport-sized Photographs of the sole proprietor or director

content_sections.heading: GST Registration Process for One-Person Company
content_sections.content:
Use the following step-by-step instructions to register under the Goods and Services Tax (GST).

01. Login to the GST official website
02. Fill out the Part-A submission form (Email address, mobile no, PAN, legal name of the business, etc.)
03. The GST portal will verify your details through Email/OTP
04. Upload all the necessary documents
05. Access and fill the Part-B form carefully using the Temporary reference number (TRN).
06. Then, you will get the Application Reference Number (ARN)
07. GST officers will start to verify your submitted documents
08. GST officer will either accept or reject your application within seven working days
09. If further clarifications or proofs are required for the verification, you must provide the same.
10. After completing all the clarifications, you will be allotted a GSTN number.

blogs.title: IGST - Integrated Tax under GST

content_sections.heading: IGST - Integrated Tax under GST
content_sections.content:
India’s GST is levied in three forms, namely

[Central Goods and Services Tax (CGST), State Goods and Services Tax (SGST) and Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGST)](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/guide-to-cgst-sgst-and-igst). While CGST and SGST are levied on the intra-state supply of goods and/or services, the latter is levied on the inter-state supply of goods and/or services. In addition to it, IGST is levied on the import and export of goods and/or services. Akin to CGST and unlike SGST, this form of tax is entirely collected by the Central Government. The article explores the provisions pertaining to integrated tax under GST.

content_sections.heading: CST and IGST – a Comparison
content_sections.content:
Under the previous tax regime, inter-state trade or commerce was regulated by the Central Sales Tax Act, 1956 wherein the taxes were collected and retained from the state of dispatch of goods and/or service, or in other words, the state of manufacture of goods. This was against the norm of indirect tax, wherein taxes are levied on the consumer. Factors such as the cascading of taxes in the absence of

[Input Tax Credit (ITC)](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/gst-input-tax-credit), increasing compliance costs due to the filing of various accounting forms, etc., complicated the tax system of those days.

Here’s how IGST has changed it:

- IGST, in contrast to CST, is a destination-based tax. As a result, the SGST component accrues to the State of the consumer.
- The tax system maintains the integrity of ITC chains in inter-state supplies.

content_sections.heading: Inter-State Supply
content_sections.content: A supply of goods and/or services is classified as inter-state if the location of the supplier and the place of supply are in two different states; two different union territories; or in case of a transaction between a state and a union territory. Moreover, the import of goods into the country is also treated as inter-state trade or commerce.

content_sections.heading: Export of Services
content_sections.content:
A supply is considered as an export if:

- The supplier of service is located in India.
- The recipient of service is located outside India.
- The place of supply of service is located outside India.
- The payment of such services has been received by the Indian supplier in convertible foreign exchange.
- The supplier of services and the recipient of services are not mere establishments of a distinct person.

content_sections.heading: Import of Services
content_sections.content:
A supply is classified as an import if:

- The supplier of the service is located outside India.
- The recipient of the service is located in India.
- The place of supply of service is in India.

Wonder how to calculate IGST on imports?

[Here's your guide](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/igst-on-imports).

content_sections.heading: Location
content_sections.content: For tax purposes, the location of a supplier could be a registered place of business or a fixed establishment of the supplier. To qualify as a location, a premise has to be either a regular place of business or a fixed establishment and must hold an essential degree of performance and suitable structure in terms of human and technical resources.

content_sections.heading: Place of Supply
content_sections.content:
The concept of place of supply stakes a vital claim in the realms of

[GST](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-registration). Its provisions have been framed in accordance with the principle of destination or consumption. The provisions related to the place of supply of goods and services has been explained below:

content_sections.heading: Place of Supply of Goods – Domestic Supplies
content_sections.content:
|     |     |     |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **S. No.** | **Nature of Supply** | **Place of Supply** |
| 1 | If the supply entails the movement of goods, whether by the supplier, recipient or any other person | Destination of supply of goods |
| 2 | Delivery of goods to the recipient or any person as per the discretion of a third person through the transfer of title or other means | The third person, as it is deemed that the third person has received the goods |
| 3 | Movement of goods either by the supplier or recipient | The place of destination of supply |
| 4 | If the goods are assembled or installed at the site. | The place where the goods were assembled or installed |
| 5 | Goods supplied onboard a conveyance like a vessel, aircraft, train or motor vehicle | The place of destination of supply |
| 6 | If the place of supply cannot be ascertained | It shall be determined in the manner as prescribed |

content_sections.heading: Place of Supply of Goods – Imports and Exports
content_sections.content:
|     |     |     |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **S. No.** | **Nature of Supply of Goods** | **Place of Supply** |
| 1 | Import | Location of the Importer |
| 2 | Export | Location of the exporter |

content_sections.heading: Place of Supply of Services – Domestic Supplies
content_sections.content:
For the awareness of the taxpayers, the place of supply of the below-listed services is determined with reference to a proxy, while the likes of the remaining are governed by a default provision. | | | | | --- | --- | --- | | **S. No.** | **Nature of Service** | **Place of Supply** | | 1 | Immovable property pertaining to services | Location of the recipient | | 2 | Restaurant and catering, personal grooming, fitness, beauty treatment and health services | The location of performance of service | | 3 | Training and performance appraisal | 1.       Location of the registered person (for B2B supplies)
2.       Location of the performance of service (for B2C supplies) | | 4 | Admission to an event or amusement park | The location of the event or the location of the park or affiliated places | | 5 | Organization of an event | 1.       Location of the registered person (for B2B supplies)
2.       Location at which such goods were dispatched for transportation (for B2C supplies) | | 6 | Transportation of goods | Same as above | | 7 | Passenger transportation | 1.       Location of the registered person (for B2B supplies)
2.       Place where the passenger boards the conveyance for a continuous journey (for B2C supplies) | | 8 | Services on board a conveyance | Location of the initial scheduled point of departure of the conveyance for the particular voyage | | 9 | Banking and other financial services | The location of the recipient as per the records of the supplier. In the absence of such records, the location of a supplier will be considered as the place of supply | | 10 | Insurance Services | 1.       Location of such person (for B2B supplies)
2.       Location of the recipient of services as per the records of the supplier | | 11 | Advertisement and services to the Government | The place of supply will be taken as located in each of such states | | 12 | Telecommunication services | 1.       For mobile/internet post-paid services – the billing address of the recipient
2.       For sale of pre-paid voucher – the place of sale of such vouchers
3.       In other cases – the address of the recipient |

content_sections.content:
The following services qualify for a default provision. | | | | | --- | --- | --- | | **S.NO.** | **Nature of Supply** | **Place of Supply** | | 1 | B2B | Location of such registered person | | 2 | B2C | 1.       Location of the registered person if the address on record exists
2.       If not, the location of the supplier of services |

content_sections.content:
Here again, the place of supply for the below-listed services is determined with reference to proxy, while the rest are governed by a default provision. | | | | | --- | --- | --- | | **S. No.** | **Nature of Service** | **Place of Supply** | | 1 | Supply of service for goods which needs to be made physically available from a remote location through electronic means (except for those goods that are temporarily imported into India for repairs and exported) | The location of performance of service or the location where the goods are held | | 2 | Services supplied to individuals, the likes of which requires the physical presence of the receiver | The location of performance of the service | | 3 | Services connected with immovable property | The location of immovable property | | 4 | Admission to or organization of an event | The location of the event | | 5 | If the following services are supplied at multiple locations (explained individually below):
·         Goods and individual related.
·         Immovable property related.
·         Event-related | | | 5 (1) | At multiple locations, including that of a taxable territory | The location in the taxable territory where greater proportions of the service were provided | | 5(2) | In multiple states | Each of the states. The levy will be based on the quantum of services provided to these states. | | 6 | Banking, financial institutions, NBC Intermediary services, the hiring of vehicles, and other affiliated services | The location of the supplier | | 7 | Transportation of goods | The destination of supply | | 8 | Passenger transportation | The location where the passenger embarks on the conveyance for a continuous journey | | 9 | Services onboard a conveyance | The first scheduled point of departure of their conveyance for the journey | | 10 | Online information and database access or retrieval services | The location of the recipient |

content_sections.heading: Default Provision for Other Services
content_sections.content:
|     |     |     |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **S. No.** | **Nature of Supply** | **Place of Supply** |
| 1 | Any | Location of the recipient. In the absence of the recipient’s address, the location of the supplier. |

content_sections.heading: Supplies in Territorial Waters
content_sections.content:
|     |     |     |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **S. No.** | **Location of Supplier** | **Place of Supply** |
| 1 | If the location of the supplier is in territorial waters | The location of the supplier |
| 2 | If the destination of supply is in territorial waters | The coastal state or union territory where the nearest point of the appropriate baseline is located |

content_sections.heading: Cross-Utilization of Credits
content_sections.content: Cross-utilization is a mechanism wherein the credits of a tax component is utilized against the other. With respect to GST, the sum of ITC on account of IGST could be utilized for the remittance of IGST, CGST and SGST respectively. Likewise, the sum of ITC on account of CGST could be utilized for the remittance of CGST (but not SGST) and IGST respectively. Also, the sum of ITC on account of SGST could be utilized for the remittance of SGST (but not CGST) and IGST respectively.

content_sections.heading: Zero Rated Supply
content_sections.content:
[Zero-rated supplies](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/zero-rated-supply-under-gst) refer to the exports and supplies to Special Economic Zones (SEZ’s), the likes of which are tax exempt. However, the provision of ITC is allowed, provided that the prescribed conditions, safeguards and procedures are followed. Refunds on such supplies are claimable through any of the following options:

- By making supplies without the payment of IGST under bond and claiming the refund of unbilled ITC.
- By making supplies on the payment of IGST and claiming a refund of the same.

content_sections.heading: Refund of IGST on Supplies Made to Foreign Tourists
content_sections.content:
The integrated tax for foreign tourists follows a similar pattern to that of exports, given that an international tourist is considered as a non-resident of India who makes a visit to the country for a period not exceeding six months. The Indian tax laws facilitate the refund of IGST paid to an international tourist leaving India on goods being taken outside the country, subject to the prescribed conditions and safeguards.

[Know more.](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/gst-refund-tourists-visiting-india)

content_sections.heading: Refund on Mistaken Payment
content_sections.content:
Taxpayers who have remitted payments to another tax head, i.e., SGST or CGST instead of IGST and vice versa, would be refunded. Such taxpayers must make a re-deposit of the sum in the respective tax head.

[Know more.](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/how-to-get-gst-refund)

[Back to Learn](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn)

content_sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
content_sections.content:
Common questions aboutIGST.

What is IGST under GST in India?

IGST or Integrated Goods and Services Tax is a form of GST levied on the inter-state supply of goods and/or services, as well as on imports and exports. It is collected by the Central Government and aims to maintain the integrity of Input Tax Credit (ITC) chains in inter-state supplies.

How is IGST different from the earlier Central Sales Tax (CST)?

Unlike CST, which was a origin-based tax, IGST is a destination-based tax. This means that the SGST component of IGST accrues to the state where the goods or services are consumed, as opposed to the state of manufacture or supply.

What qualifies as an inter-state supply under IGST?

A supply of goods and/or services is considered inter-state if the location of the supplier and the place of supply are in different states, different union territories, or if the transaction is between a state and a union territory. Imports are also treated as inter-state supplies under IGST.

How is the place of supply determined for goods under IGST?

For domestic supplies of goods, the place of supply is generally the destination where the goods are delivered or where the goods are assembled or installed. For imports, it is the location of the importer, and for exports, it is the location of the exporter.

How is the place of supply determined for services under IGST?

The place of supply for services under IGST is determined based on the nature of the service and whether it is a B2B or B2C supply. For certain specified services, proxy rules are used, while for others, a default provision based on the location of the supplier or recipient applies.

What is the significance of the place of supply under IGST?

The place of supply is crucial under IGST as it determines the chargeability of IGST, CGST, and SGST. The principle of destination or consumption is followed, which means that the taxes accrue to the state where the goods or services are consumed.

Can IGST credits be utilized for payment of other GST components?

Yes, the credits of IGST can be cross-utilized for payment of IGST, CGST, and SGST respectively. Similarly, CGST credits can be used for payment of CGST and IGST, while SGST credits can be used for payment of SGST and IGST.

What are zero-rated supplies under IGST?

Zero-rated supplies refer to exports and supplies to Special Economic Zones (SEZs), which are exempt from IGST. However, the provision of ITC is allowed for such supplies, subject to certain conditions and procedures.

Can international tourists claim a refund of IGST paid on goods?

Yes, international tourists who are non-residents visiting India for a period not exceeding six months can claim a refund of IGST paid on goods being taken out of the country, subject to prescribed conditions and safeguards.

Can taxpayers claim a refund if IGST is paid mistakenly instead of CGST or SGST?

Yes, taxpayers who have mistakenly paid IGST instead of CGST or SGST, or vice versa, can claim a refund by re-depositing the amount in the correct tax head, following the prescribed procedures.

It is collected by the Central Government and aims to maintain the integrity of Input Tax Credit (ITC) chains in inter-state supplies. How is IGST different from the earlier Central Sales Tax (CST)? Unlike CST, which was a origin-based tax, IGST is a destination-based tax. This means that the SGST component of IGST accrues to the state where the goods or services are consumed, as opposed to the state of manufacture or supply. What qualifies as an inter-state supply under IGST? A supply of goods and/or services is considered inter-state if the location of the supplier and the place of supply are in different states, different union territories, or if the transaction is between a state and a union territory. Imports are also treated as inter-state supplies under IGST. How is the place of supply determined for goods under IGST? For domestic supplies of goods, the place of supply is generally the destination where the goods are delivered or where the goods are assembled or installed. For imports, it is the location of the importer, and for exports, it is the location of the exporter. How is the place of supply determined for services under IGST? The place of supply for services under IGST is determined based on the nature of the service and whether it is a B2B or B2C supply. For certain specified services, proxy rules are used, while for others, a default provision based on the location of the supplier or recipient applies. What is the significance of the place of supply under IGST? The place of supply is crucial under IGST as it determines the chargeability of IGST, CGST, and SGST. The principle of destination or consumption is followed, which means that the taxes accrue to the state where the goods or services are consumed. Can IGST credits be utilized for payment of other GST components? Yes, the credits of IGST can be cross-utilized for payment of IGST, CGST, and SGST respectively. Similarly, CGST credits can be used for payment of CGST and IGST, while SGST credits can be used for payment of SGST and IGST. What are zero-rated supplies under IGST? Zero-rated supplies refer to exports and supplies to Special Economic Zones (SEZs), which are exempt from IGST. However, the provision of ITC is allowed for such supplies, subject to certain conditions and procedures. Can international tourists claim a refund of IGST paid on goods? Yes, international tourists who are non-residents visiting India for a period not exceeding six months can claim a refund of IGST paid on goods being taken out of the country, subject to prescribed conditions and safeguards. Can taxpayers claim a refund if IGST is paid mistakenly instead of CGST or SGST? Yes, taxpayers who have mistakenly paid IGST instead of CGST or SGST, or vice versa, can claim a refund by re-depositing the amount in the correct tax head, following the prescribed procedures. ### content_sections.heading: GSTR-1 Filing for Taxpayers with annual Turnover of above Rs.1.5 Crore
content_sections.content: GSTR-1 filing applies to all the individuals who have registered for GST. The individual shall file on the 10th of every month if the annual turnover exceeds Rs.1.5 crores. However, if the taxpayer holds less than Rs.1.5 crore as annual income, the individual shall process the GSTR-1 filing every quarter. GSTR-1 or return of outward supply would contain item wise detail of goods and services supplied with 1 and supply with respect to all B2B transactions. Further, it shall also include details of all inter-state supplies of B2C transactions above Rs.2.5 lakhs and all other invoices of less than Rs.2.50 lakhs. The list shall detail with state wise summary of all B2C transactions. In this article, we look at GSTR-1 in detail.

content_sections.heading: Import of E-Way Bill Data
content_sections.content:
It is essential for taxpayers to validate the data of their transactions before proceeding with the process of filing returns. Hence it saves time and processing unnecessary data entry. To cater to this purpose, the MoF introduced E-way Bill Portal (EWB). The taxpayer can access the E-way Bill Portal (EWB) through the GST portal. The integration enables the users to import the B2B and B2C invoice sections. In addition, it also displays the HSN-wise-summary of the outward supplies section. Using these details, the taxpayers may verify the data and complete the filing.

The feature shall analyze the major data gaps between self-declared liability in Form GSTR 1 and Form GSTR 3B. A similar rule also applies to Input Tax Credit (ITC) claimed in GSTR 3B to compared with the credit available in Form GSTR 2A.

The following tabs of the portal shall provide support for Data validation and comparison:

- Liability other than export/reverse charge
- ITC credit claimed and due
- Liability due to reverse charge
- Liability due to export and SEZ supplies.

content_sections.heading: E-Way Bill
content_sections.content:
The newly launched facility takes away the taxpayer’s need to make specifications connected with the

[e-way bill](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/e-way-bill-applicability) as specified in GSTR 3B. Hence, it allows the taxpayers to import data in Form GSTR 1 for all invoices. The particulars so imported would include the details of the supplier, receiver, and also invoice number. In addition, it also includes the date of the invoice, type, quantity of goods, the HSN Code, and others. The GST portal transfers the details and classifies into three categories in GSTR 1. The following details the categories:

- Business to Business Supplies (B2B),
- Business to Consumer (B2C) supplies (covering values of above Rs.2.5 lakhs) and
- HSN (Harmonized System of Nomenclature Codes for goods and services) wise consolidated supply data.

Taxpayers with more than 50 invoices but not more than 500 may download the data of the sections mentioned above in the ‘CSV’ file format. The portal provides the option to import the invoices into the GSTR1 offline tool. The individual shall add sufficient data and generate a JSON file for GSTR-1 filing.

If the number of invoices exceeds 500, the taxpayer can import the invoice details from the ‘Return’ Dashboard on the GST portal as a zip file. The individual can later unzip to three files and extract the details in Excel format. The taxpayer shall then add more invoices and fill the other sheets to upload in the offline tool.

content_sections.heading: Requirement for GSTR-1 Filing
content_sections.content: According to Section 32 of the GST Model Law,  all GST registered persons except an input service distributor, should process GSTR-1 filing electronically. The exceptions also apply to a non-resident taxable person and a person paying tax as per Section 9, Section 46, or Section 56. The individual shall process GSTR-1 filing detailing outward supplies of goods or services effected, during a tax period on or before the tenth day of the month as prescribed.

content_sections.heading: GSTR-1 Filing Not Required
content_sections.content: So as per the above rule of the GST Law, Input Service Distributor, Non-Resident Taxable Person, and Persons paying tax under Section 9, Section 46 and Section 56 are not required to file GSTR-1 filing as per the above terms. However, they are still required to file GST returns as per other terms mentioned in the relevant section.

content_sections.heading: Input Service Distributor
content_sections.content:
According to the GST Model Law, Input Service Distributor is defined as an office of the supplier of goods and/or services which receives tax invoices issued under section 28 towards receipt of input services and issues a prescribed document for the purposes of distributing the credit of CGST (SGST in State Acts) and/or IGST paid on the said services to a supplier of taxable goods and/or services having same PAN as that of the office referred to above".

All Input Service Distributors who are taxable persons registered as an Input Service Distributor are required to file GST return within thirteen days after the end of such a month.

content_sections.heading: Non-Resident Taxable Person
content_sections.content:
According to the GST Model Law, Non-Resident Taxable Person is a taxable person who occasionally undertakes transactions involving the supply of goods and/or services, whether as principal or agent or in any other capacity but who has no fixed place of business in India.

All GST registered non-resident taxable person for every calendar month are required to file GST return, electronically, within twenty days after the end of a calendar month or within seven days after the last day of the validity period of registration, whichever is earlier.

content_sections.heading: Section 9 - Composition Levy
content_sections.content:
Section 9 of the GST Model Law pertains to composition levy, wherein a taxable person having less than Rs.50 lakh aggregate turnover in the previous financial year can pay GST liability by paying an amount calculated at a rate as prescribed by the Government, but not less than 2.5% in case of a manufacturer and 1% in any other case, of the turnover in a State during the year.

Such persons falling under Section 9 are required to file GST Returns as prescribed, electronically, of inward supplies of goods or services, tax payable, and tax paid within eighteen days after the end of such quarter.

content_sections.heading: Section 46 - Tax Collection at Source
content_sections.content: All GST registered taxpayers falling under Section 46, who are required to deduct tax at source, are required to file GST return for the month in which such deductions have been made along with the payment of tax so deducted within ten days after the end of such month.

content_sections.heading: How to File GSTR-1
content_sections.content:
All registered taxpayers can file GSTR-1 electronically through the GST Common Portal or through the GST facilitation Centre. GSTR-1 return must contain details like:

- Invoice wise details of all:


  - Inter-State and intra-State supplies made to registered persons;
  - Inter-State supplies with invoice value more than two and a half lakh rupees made to unregistered persons;

- Consolidated details of all:


  - Intra-State supplies made to unregistered persons for each rate of tax; and
  - State-wise inter-State supplies with invoice value less than two and a half lakh rupees made to unregistered persons for each rate of tax; and

- Debit and credit notes, if any issued during the month for invoices issued previously.

Once GSTR-1 is filed, the details of outward supplies furnished by the supplier would be made available automatically to the concerned recipient mentioned in the invoice to facilitate the matching of records with Part A of FORM GSTR- 2A, in FORM GSTR-4A and in FORM GSTR-6A. Also, the details of inward supplies added, corrected, or deleted by the recipient in his FORM GSTR-2 under section 38 of FORM GSTR-4 under section 39 are made available to the supplier electronically in FORM GSTR-1A through the Common Portal for acceptance or rejection or modification.

content_sections.heading: Update for Filing GSTR-1 in 2020
content_sections.content:
Due to the impact of the Corona Virus worldwide, many people across the world stay in lockdown period to support the Governments' measure to curb the Corona Virus. To avoid the financial burden on the people at a time like these, the Government of India (GoI), implemented various schemes such as Companies Fresh Start Scheme 2020 to avail benefits for taxpayers who either failed to pay taxes on time or unable to pay the penalty and stopped filing. To ensure smooth operation of the business, the GoI also implemented several waive off for penalty in non-filing or registration compliance. This shall also apply for filing GSTR-1.

On 3rd April 2020, the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs implemented waving off the GSTR-1 through the Notification No.33/2020. The CBIC states that through the powers of Section 128 of Central Goods and Services Tax 2017, any late fee payable for the month of March 2020, April 2020, May 2020 and for the quarter ending 31st March 2020 shall stand waived off. It shall apply to all the registered taxpayers who failed to furnish the details of the outward supplies in Form GSTR-1 in the above-mentioned months by the end of the due date.

content_sections.heading: Update on extended due date for GSTR-1 filing for November 2022 in a few districts in Tamil Nadu
content_sections.content:
As per the latest notification on 13

th December 2022 from the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC), the GSTR-1 filing deadline for the month of November 2022 has been extended in several districts of Tamil Nadu. The due date has been extended in the following districts of Chennai, Tiruvallur, Chengalpattu, Kancheepuram, Tiruvannamalai, Ranipet, Vellore, Villupuram, Cuddalore, Thiruvarur, Nagapattinam, Mayiladuthurai and Thanjavur till 13th December.

The exact text of the notification is provided below:

_“T_ _he time limit for furnishing the details of outward supplies in FORM GSTR-1 of_ _the said rules for the tax period November, 2022, for the registered persons required to furnish return under sub-_ _section (1) of section 39 of the said Act whose principal place of business is in the districts of Chennai,_ _Tiruvallur, Chengalpattu, Kancheepuram, Tiruvannamalai, Ranipet, Vellore, Villupuram, Cuddalore,_ _Thiruvarur, Nagapattinam, Mayiladuthurai and Thanjavur in the State of Tamil Nadu, shall be extended till the_ _thirteenth day of the month succeeding the said tax period_ _.”_

content_sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
content_sections.content:
Common questions aboutGSTR-1 Filing for Businesses Over Rs.1.5 Crore Turnover.

What is GSTR-1?

GSTR-1 is a return of outward supplies that a registered taxpayer has to file every month or quarter, depending on their annual turnover. It contains details of all supplies made to registered and unregistered persons, along with debit and credit notes issued during the period.

Who needs to file GSTR-1?

All GST registered persons, except an input service distributor, non-resident taxable person, and those paying tax under Sections 9, 46, or 56 of the GST Act, are required to file GSTR-1.

What is the due date for GSTR-1 filing?

For taxpayers with an annual turnover exceeding Rs. 1.5 crores, GSTR-1 needs to be filed by the 11th of the succeeding month. For those with an annual turnover below Rs. 1.5 crores, GSTR-1 needs to be filed quarterly by the last day of the month following the quarter.

What details are required to be furnished in GSTR-1?

GSTR-1 requires invoice-wise details of all B2B supplies, inter-state B2C supplies above Rs. 2.5 lakhs, and consolidated details of intra-state B2C supplies and inter-state B2C supplies below Rs. 2.5 lakhs, along with debit and credit notes issued during the period.

How can taxpayers file GSTR-1?

Taxpayers can file GSTR-1 electronically through the GST Common Portal or through a GST Facilitation Centre. They can also import data from the e-way bill portal to reduce manual data entry.

What is the benefit of filing GSTR-1?

Once GSTR-1 is filed, the details of outward supplies furnished by the supplier are made available to the respective recipients, facilitating reconciliation and matching of records with their GSTR-2A or GSTR-4A.

What is the recent update regarding GSTR-1 filing?

The Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) has waived off the late fee for GSTR-1 filing for the months of March, April, and May 2020, and for the quarter ending 31st March 2020, due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

What is the extension for GSTR-1 filing in certain districts of Tamil Nadu?

The CBIC has extended the due date for GSTR-1 filing for the tax period of November 2022 till 13th December 2022 for registered persons whose principal place of business is in certain districts of Tamil Nadu, including Chennai, Tiruvallur, and Chengalpattu.

What is the importance of validating data before GSTR-1 filing?

It is essential for taxpayers to validate the data of their transactions before filing GSTR-1 to ensure accuracy and avoid unnecessary data entry. The e-way bill portal can be used to import invoice details, reducing manual effort.

What is the process for GSTR-1 filing for taxpayers with more than 500 invoices?

For taxpayers with more than 500 invoices, the invoice details can be imported from the 'Return' Dashboard on the GST portal as a zip file, which can be unzipped to extract the details in Excel format. Additional invoices can be added, and the offline tool can be used to generate a JSON file for GSTR-1 filing.

### E-Way Bill

The newly launched facility takes away the taxpayer’s need to make specifications connected with the

[e-way bill](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/e-way-bill-applicability) as specified in GSTR 3B. Hence, it allows the taxpayers to import data in Form GSTR 1 for all invoices. The particulars so imported would include the details of the supplier, receiver, and also invoice number. In addition, it also includes the date of the invoice, type, quantity of goods, the HSN Code, and others. The GST portal transfers the details and classifies into three categories in GSTR 1. The following details the categories:

- Business to Business Supplies (B2B),
- Business to Consumer (B2C) supplies (covering values of above Rs.2.5 lakhs) and
- HSN (Harmonized System of Nomenclature Codes for goods and services) wise consolidated supply data.

Taxpayers with more than 50 invoices but not more than 500 may download the data of the sections mentioned above in the ‘CSV’ file format. The portal provides the option to import the invoices into the GSTR1 offline tool. The individual shall add sufficient data and generate a JSON file for GSTR-1 filing.

If the number of invoices exceeds 500, the taxpayer can import the invoice details from the ‘Return’ Dashboard on the GST portal as a zip file. The individual can later unzip to three files and extract the details in Excel format. The taxpayer shall then add more invoices and fill the other sheets to upload in the offline tool.

## Requirement for GSTR-1 Filing

According to Section 32 of the GST Model Law,  all GST registered persons except an input service distributor, should process GSTR-1 filing electronically. The exceptions also apply to a non-resident taxable person and a person paying tax as per Section 9, Section 46, or Section 56. The individual shall process GSTR-1 filing detailing outward supplies of goods or services effected, during a tax period on or before the tenth day of the month as prescribed.

### GSTR-1 Filing Not Required

So as per the above rule of the GST Law, Input Service Distributor, Non-Resident Taxable Person, and Persons paying tax under Section 9, Section 46 and Section 56 are not required to file GSTR-1 filing as per the above terms. However, they are still required to file GST returns as per other terms mentioned in the relevant section.

#### Input Service Distributor

According to the GST Model Law, Input Service Distributor is defined as an office of the supplier of goods and/or services which receives tax invoices issued under section 28 towards receipt of input services and issues a prescribed document for the purposes of distributing the credit of CGST (SGST in State Acts) and/or IGST paid on the said services to a supplier of taxable goods and/or services having same PAN as that of the office referred to above".

All Input Service Distributors who are taxable persons registered as an Input Service Distributor are required to file GST return within thirteen days after the end of such a month.

#### Non-Resident Taxable Person

According to the GST Model Law, Non-Resident Taxable Person is a taxable person who occasionally undertakes transactions involving the supply of goods and/or services, whether as principal or agent or in any other capacity but who has no fixed place of business in India.

All GST registered non-resident taxable person for every calendar month are required to file GST return, electronically, within twenty days after the end of a calendar month or within seven days after the last day of the validity period of registration, whichever is earlier.

#### Section 9 - Composition Levy

Section 9 of the GST Model Law pertains to composition levy, wherein a taxable person having less than Rs.50 lakh aggregate turnover in the previous financial year can pay GST liability by paying an amount calculated at a rate as prescribed by the Government, but not less than 2.5% in case of a manufacturer and 1% in any other case, of the turnover in a State during the year.

Such persons falling under Section 9 are required to file GST Returns as prescribed, electronically, of inward supplies of goods or services, tax payable, and tax paid within eighteen days after the end of such quarter.

#### Section 46 - Tax Collection at Source

All GST registered taxpayers falling under Section 46, who are required to deduct tax at source, are required to file GST return for the month in which such deductions have been made along with the payment of tax so deducted within ten days after the end of such month.

## How to File GSTR-1

All registered taxpayers can file GSTR-1 electronically through the GST Common Portal or through the GST facilitation Centre. GSTR-1 return must contain details like:

- Invoice wise details of all:


  - Inter-State and intra-State supplies made to registered persons;
  - Inter-State supplies with invoice value more than two and a half lakh rupees made to unregistered persons;

- Consolidated details of all:


  - Intra-State supplies made to unregistered persons for each rate of tax; and
  - State-wise inter-State supplies with invoice value less than two and a half lakh rupees made to unregistered persons for each rate of tax; and

- Debit and credit notes, if any issued during the month for invoices issued previously.

Once GSTR-1 is filed, the details of outward supplies furnished by the supplier would be made available automatically to the concerned recipient mentioned in the invoice to facilitate the matching of records with Part A of FORM GSTR- 2A, in FORM GSTR-4A and in FORM GSTR-6A. Also, the details of inward supplies added, corrected, or deleted by the recipient in his FORM GSTR-2 under section 38 of FORM GSTR-4 under section 39 are made available to the supplier electronically in FORM GSTR-1A through the Common Portal for acceptance or rejection or modification.

!["<yoastmark](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2017/05/GSTR-1-Filing-on-GST-Common-Portal.png)

## Update for Filing GSTR-1 in 2020

Due to the impact of the Corona Virus worldwide, many people across the world stay in lockdown period to support the Governments' measure to curb the Corona Virus. To avoid the financial burden on the people at a time like these, the Government of India (GoI), implemented various schemes such as Companies Fresh Start Scheme 2020 to avail benefits for taxpayers who either failed to pay taxes on time or unable to pay the penalty and stopped filing. To ensure smooth operation of the business, the GoI also implemented several waive off for penalty in non-filing or registration compliance. This shall also apply for filing GSTR-1.

On 3rd April 2020, the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs implemented waving off the GSTR-1 through the Notification No.33/2020. The CBIC states that through the powers of Section 128 of Central Goods and Services Tax 2017, any late fee payable for the month of March 2020, April 2020, May 2020 and for the quarter ending 31st March 2020 shall stand waived off. It shall apply to all the registered taxpayers who failed to furnish the details of the outward supplies in Form GSTR-1 in the above-mentioned months by the end of the due date.

## Update on extended due date for GSTR-1 filing for November 2022 in a few districts in Tamil Nadu

As per the latest notification on 13

th December 2022 from the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC), the GSTR-1 filing deadline for the month of November 2022 has been extended in several districts of Tamil Nadu. ## Frequently Asked Questions

Common questions aboutGSTR-1 Filing for Businesses Over Rs.1.5 Crore Turnover.

What is GSTR-1?

GSTR-1 is a return of outward supplies that a registered taxpayer has to file every month or quarter, depending on their annual turnover. It contains details of all supplies made to registered and unregistered persons, along with debit and credit notes issued during the period.

Who needs to file GSTR-1?

All GST registered persons, except an input service distributor, non-resident taxable person, and those paying tax under Sections 9, 46, or 56 of the GST Act, are required to file GSTR-1.

What is the due date for GSTR-1 filing?

For taxpayers with an annual turnover exceeding Rs. 1.5 crores, GSTR-1 needs to be filed by the 11th of the succeeding month. For those with an annual turnover below Rs. 1.5 crores, GSTR-1 needs to be filed quarterly by the last day of the month following the quarter.

What details are required to be furnished in GSTR-1?

GSTR-1 requires invoice-wise details of all B2B supplies, inter-state B2C supplies above Rs. 2.5 lakhs, and consolidated details of intra-state B2C supplies and inter-state B2C supplies below Rs. 2.5 lakhs, along with debit and credit notes issued during the period.

How can taxpayers file GSTR-1?

Taxpayers can file GSTR-1 electronically through the GST Common Portal or through a GST Facilitation Centre. They can also import data from the e-way bill portal to reduce manual data entry.

What is the benefit of filing GSTR-1?

Once GSTR-1 is filed, the details of outward supplies furnished by the supplier are made available to the respective recipients, facilitating reconciliation and matching of records with their GSTR-2A or GSTR-4A.

What is the recent update regarding GSTR-1 filing?

The Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) has waived off the late fee for GSTR-1 filing for the months of March, April, and May 2020, and for the quarter ending 31st March 2020, due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

What is the extension for GSTR-1 filing in certain districts of Tamil Nadu?

The CBIC has extended the due date for GSTR-1 filing for the tax period of November 2022 till 13th December 2022 for registered persons whose principal place of business is in certain districts of Tamil Nadu, including Chennai, Tiruvallur, and Chengalpattu.

What is the importance of validating data before GSTR-1 filing?

It is essential for taxpayers to validate the data of their transactions before filing GSTR-1 to ensure accuracy and avoid unnecessary data entry. The e-way bill portal can be used to import invoice details, reducing manual effort.

What is the process for GSTR-1 filing for taxpayers with more than 500 invoices?

For taxpayers with more than 500 invoices, the invoice details can be imported from the 'Return' Dashboard on the GST portal as a zip file, which can be unzipped to extract the details in Excel format. Additional invoices can be added, and the offline tool can be used to generate a JSON file for GSTR-1 filing.

However, if the taxpayer holds less than Rs.1.5 crore as annual income, the individual shall process the GSTR-1 filing every quarter. GSTR-1 or return of outward supply would contain item wise detail of goods and services supplied with 1 and supply with respect to all B2B transactions. Further, it shall also include details of all inter-state supplies of B2C transactions above Rs.2.5 lakhs and all other invoices of less than Rs.2.50 lakhs. The list shall detail with state wise summary of all B2C transactions. In this article, we look at GSTR-1 in detail.

blogs.title: GSTR-3B: Due Date, Late Fee, Format, Return Filing, Eligibility, Rules

content_sections.heading: GSTR-3B: Due Date, Late Fee, Format, Return Filing, Eligibility, Rules
content_sections.content: Navigating the complexities of GST compliance is crucial for businesses in India, and understanding GSTR-3B is an essential part of this process. GSTR-3B is a monthly self-declaration that every registered taxpayer must file. It plays a significant role in summarizing the details of input tax credits and taxes paid on outward supplies. In this article, we will explore what GSTR-3B is, delve into the specifics of its due dates, and provide insights into its filing process to ensure you remain compliant with GST regulations.

content_sections.heading: 11th April 2025
content_sections.content:
GSTN issued an advisory regarding the reporting of values in Table 3.2 of GSTR-3B. Starting April 2025, the auto-populated figures for inter-state supplies made to unregistered persons, composition taxpayers, and UIN holders in Table 3.2 will be non-editable.

Taxpayers must correct any inaccuracies by filing amendments through Form GSTR-1A or Form GSTR-1/IFF in subsequent tax periods.

content_sections.heading: 10th January 2025
content_sections.content: The due dates for filing GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B (both monthly and quarterly) for December 2024 have been extended by two days, as notified in CGST Notifications 01/2025 and 02/2025.

content_sections.heading: 29th September 2024
content_sections.content: In response to persistent demand from the trade, GSTN has restored access to the return data for July 2017 and August 2017, which had been archived earlier on 1st August and 1st September, respectively. This data will remain available until further notice.

content_sections.heading: 24th September 2024
content_sections.content: As per GSTN’s data archival policy, data for September 2017 will be removed from the GST portal on 1st October 2024. This follows the policy of retaining return data on the portal for a period of 7 years.

content_sections.heading: What is GSTR 3B?
content_sections.content: GSTR-3B is a self-declared summary GST return that all taxpayers must file monthly (or quarterly under the QRMP scheme). This return summarizes the sales details, the Input Tax Credit (ITC) claimed, and the net tax payable. Each GSTIN must file a separate GSTR-3B and any GST liability must be paid by the filing date or its due date, whichever comes first. Once submitted, GSTR-3B cannot be revised. It's important to note that filing GSTR-3B is mandatory, even if there is no tax liability for that period.

content_sections.heading: Who Should File GSTR-3B?
content_sections.content: - **Regular Taxpayers**: Any individual or entity registered under the GST regime and not covered by any specific exceptions must file GSTR-3B. This includes manufacturers, traders, service providers, and others who conduct taxable activities.

content_sections.heading: Who is Exempt from Filing GSTR-3B?
content_sections.content:
- **Composition Scheme Taxpayers**: Businesses that have opted for the GST Composition Scheme, which allows them to pay GST at a fixed turnover rate and reduces compliance burdens, are exempt from filing GSTR-3B.
- **Input Service Distributors (ISDs)**: ISDs are not required to file GSTR-3B because they have a different mechanism for distributing the credit of input services to branches.
- **Non-resident Taxable Persons**: Individuals or businesses that reside outside India but make taxable supplies in India. They have different filing requirements tailored to non-residents.
- **Non-resident Suppliers of OIDAR Services**: These businesses outside India provide Online Information and Database Access or Retrieval (OIDAR) services to non-taxable online recipients in India. They are subject to simplified registration and compliance mechanisms.

content_sections.heading: GSTR-3B Due Date
content_sections.content:
![Uploaded Image](https://img.indiafilings.com/guides/GSTR-3B-Filing-Due-Dates.webp)

**Up to December 2019**: The due date for filing GSTR-3B was the **20th of the subsequent month**

content_sections.heading: Current Due Date s
content_sections.content:
- GSTR 3b due date monthly: **From January 2020**: The due dates have been changed. For monthly filers, the due date is either the **20th of every month**.
- GSTR 3b due date for quarterly return: For quarterly filers under the QRMP scheme starting from 1st January 2021, the due date is the **22nd or 24th of the month following the quarter**, depending on the State/UT of the principal place of business.

  - **Group 1 States/UTs**: The due date is the 22nd of the month following the end of the quarter. This group typically includes states and UTs in the northern and western parts of India.
  - **Group 2 States/UTs**: The due date is the 24th of the month following the end of the quarter. This group generally includes states and UTs in the southern and eastern parts of India.

content_sections.heading: GSTR-3B Due Date Extension for December 2024
content_sections.content:
The due date for filing monthly GSTR-3B for December 2024 has been extended to January 22, 2025, from the original deadline of January 20, 2025. For taxpayers opting for quarterly filing under the QRMP scheme, the last date for filing GSTR-3B for the October-December 2024 quarter has been extended as follows: January 24, 2025, for certain states, and January 26, 2025, for other states. This extension allows businesses additional time to ensure accurate and timely compliance with GST filing requirements.

_To get detailed information, read [GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B Due Date Extension](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/gstr1-and-gstr3b-due-date-extension)_

content_sections.heading: Key Compliance Notes
content_sections.content:
- **Timely Payment and Filing**: Taxes must be paid and GSTR-3B filed within the specified deadline to avoid penalties.
- **Penalties for Late Filing**: A late fee and interest at 18% per annum are applicable for delayed filings.
- **Late Fee and Interest Charges**: These charges apply even if the tax was paid on time but the GSTR-3B was filed after the deadline.
- **Monthly Filing Requirement**: Even taxpayers who file quarterly GSTR-1 returns are required to pay tax and file GSTR-3B monthly, unless opting for the QRMP scheme.

content_sections.heading: Late Fees and Interest Penalties for Delayed GSTR-3B Filing
content_sections.content:
A late fee applies if GSTR-3B is filed after its due date, calculated as follows:

- Rs. 50 per day of delay for general cases.
- Rs. 20 per day of delay for taxpayers with no monthly tax liability.

Additionally, if GST dues are not paid by the due date, interest is charged at 18% per annum on the outstanding tax amount.

content_sections.heading: Prerequisites for Filing GSTR-3B
content_sections.content:
Businesses required to file monthly GST returns, such as GSTR-1, GSTR-2, and GSTR-3, must also submit the GSTR-3B form. This form can be filed online via the GSTN portal. Payment of tax due can be made using challans at banks or through online payment methods.To verify and submit your GSTR-3B, you will need:

- An OTP is sent to your registered mobile number for verification using an Electronic Verification Code (EVC),
- A Class 2 or higher Digital Signature Certificate (DSC),
- Or, you can opt to use an Aadhaar-based e-signature to file your GST returns.

content_sections.heading: Details Featured in GSTR-3B
content_sections.content:
The GSTR-3B form consists of six tables that capture various types of transactions and tax details required from taxpayers. Here is a breakdown of what each table entails:

- **Table** **1:** This table captures information on inward supplies (purchases) and outward supplies (sales) that are liable to reverse charge.
- **Table 2:** Details of interstate supplies made to unregistered persons, Unique Identification Number (UIN) holders, and composition dealers are recorded here.
- **Table 3:** This table is dedicated to the Input Tax Credit (ITC), detailing credits received and utilized.
- **Table** **4:** This includes information on nil-rated, exempt, and non-GST inward supplies.
- **Table 5:** Payment of tax: this table summarizes the tax payable and the tax paid during the period, including segregation by tax type (CGST, SGST, IGST, Cess).
- **Table 6:** This table is for capturing the credit received from Tax Collected at Source (TCS) and Tax Deducted at Source (TDS).

content_sections.heading: GSTR-3B vs GSTR-2A & GSTR-2B
content_sections.content:
- **GSTR-3B** is a summary GST return filed monthly that includes details of sales and input tax credits (ITC). Reconciliation with **GSTR-2A** and **GSTR-2B** is crucial:
- **GSTR-2A**: A real-time dynamic report that reflects ITC as suppliers upload invoices. Reconciliation helps:

  - Avoid notices from tax authorities by preventing excess ITC claims.
  - Ensure no eligible ITC is missed.
  - Encourage suppliers to upload their invoices if missing, enhancing compliance.

- **GSTR-2B**: A static monthly statement that provides a snapshot of ITC available and not available for a given month. Using GSTR-2B for reconciliation ensures:

  - Accurate ITC claims in GSTR-3B.
  - Improved compliance and GST compliance rating.

By regularly comparing GSTR-3B with GSTR-2A and GSTR-2B, businesses can maintain accurate tax records and avoid discrepancies that could lead to penalties or missed credits.

content_sections.heading: Information Preparation for Filing GSTR 3B
content_sections.content: Before filing GSTR 3B return on the GST portal, the taxpayer must prepare the following information.

content_sections.heading: Step 1: Prepare details of outward taxable supplies
content_sections.content: ![GSTR 3B Details of Outward Supplies](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2017/08/GSTR-3B-Details-of-Outward-Supplies-1024x267.png)GSTR 3B Details of Outward SuppliesIn the first table, details of outward supplies and inward supplies liable to reverse charge must be provided. You can prepare this information by compiling details from all sales invoices issued during the month of July for the GSTR 3B return due in August. In case you are using LEDGERS GST software, this information will be auto-populated for you.

content_sections.heading: Outward taxable supplies (other than zero-rated, nil rated and exempted)
content_sections.content: In this row, the registered user shall provide information about all invoices issued by the company that is NOT zero-rated, nil rated and exempted. Hence, this row will contain details of all invoices for which GST was levied. The information about GST must be broken down further into taxable value, integrated tax, central tax, state tax and cess.In the field for taxable value, mention the total bill amount. If IGST was payable on the taxable value, mention the same in the field for integrated tax. If CGST and SGST was applicable, it must be mentioned in the fields for central tax and state tax. Finally, if any cess was applicable, it must be mentioned in the [GST cess](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/gst-cess) field.**Important:** The supplier is liable for payment of GST on the issuance of invoice, so the fields need to be completed based on the invoices issued and not based on payment received.

content_sections.heading: Outward taxable supplies (zero-rated)
content_sections.content: Exports and sales to SEZ units are zero rated. Hence, in this row details relating to exports and supplies made to SEZ units must be mentioned. As mentioned above, the details must be categorised by taxable value, integrated tax, central tax and cess.

content_sections.heading: Other outward supplies (Nil rated, exempted)
content_sections.content: In this field, Nil rated and exempted supplies must be mentioned. Hence, goods or services which attract nil or 0% GST rate should be mentioned. As IGST, CGST and SGST component are not be applicable for exempt supplies, it would be zero, while the taxable value of such invoices issued must be mentioned.

content_sections.heading: Inward supplies (liable to reverse charge)
content_sections.content: In this row, details of all inward supplies for which the business is liable to pay GST must be mentioned. Inward supplies liable for reverse charge are transactions wherein the recipient of the supply is made liable for payment of GST. You can break down inward supplies liable for a reverse charge by taxable amount, integrated tax, central tax, state tax and cess.

content_sections.heading: Non-GST outward supplies
content_sections.content: Some goods, such as petroleum crude, motor spirit (petrol), high-speed diesel, natural gas, and aviation turbine fuel, have been kept out of GST. This row must mention details of outward supplies of such goods, along with the taxable amount.

content_sections.heading: Step 2: Prepare supplies to unregistered persons, composition dealers and UIN holders
content_sections.content: ![GSTR 3B - Supplies made to unregistered persons](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2017/08/GSTR-3B-Supplies-made-to-unregistered-persons-1024x229.png)GSTR 3B - Supplies made to unregistered persons

content_sections.heading: Supplies made to Unregistered Persons
content_sections.content: In this table, inter-state supplies made to unregistered persons must be provided. Hence, the portal shall list all the aggregate level details of all B2C transactions. As this table shows the supply breakup in the above table, the value in the first table shall always exceed the value of other tables.In supplies made to unregistered persons, the concerned State should mention the amount of taxable value and integrated tax. The taxpayer can alter the rows based on the number of states the taxpayer provided supplies to the customers.

content_sections.heading: Supplies made to Composition Taxable Persons
content_sections.content: In this table, the taxpayer shall mention the supplies made to composition taxable persons along with the state, taxable value, and amount of integrated tax. Composition taxable persons are persons who have GST registration but are not eligible to collect GST.

content_sections.heading: Supplies made to UIN holders
content_sections.content: UIN or GST Unique ID is provided to Consulates, Embassies, and UN Bodies. If the taxpayer made supplies to UIN holders outside the state, such details must be provided in this row.**Important: This table contains details of interstate supplies ONLY. Hence, only information must be provided in this table if supplies were made outside of the state. If all the supplies were intrastate** **, then this table would be filled with zeros.**

content_sections.heading: Step 3: Prepare details of input tax credit
content_sections.content:
Persons registered under GST are eligible to claim [input tax credit](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/gst-input-tax-credit-guide) for setting off GST liability. To claim input tax credit, the taxpayer must properly enter purchase invoices and track expenditures. In LEDGERS, if you had updated all your purchase invoice details, the following table would be auto-populated.

![GSTR 3B Input Tax Credit Availed](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2017/08/GSTR-3B-Input-Tax-Credit-Availed-1024x469.png)GSTR 3B Input Tax Credit Availed

content_sections.heading: Input Tax Credit Available from Import of Goods
content_sections.content: Import of goods is subject to levy of IGST on import. Taxpayers registered under GST can claim the input tax credit for IGST paid on imports. In this table, the taxpayer should mention all the details of all imports of goods for which GST under IGST, CGST, SGST and Cess is paid along with customs duty.

content_sections.heading: Input Tax Credit Available from Import of Services
content_sections.content: Import of services into India is also subject to levy of IGST. In this row, the taxpayer should mention the details of the amount paid for the import of services for IGST.

content_sections.heading: Inward Supplies Liable to Reverse Charge
content_sections.content: Some types of inward supplies, like OIDAR services, are liable for the reverse charge, wherein the recipient of the goods or service is liable for payment of GST. The taxpayer shall mention the details of any GST payment liable for any such inward supplies.

content_sections.heading: Inward Supplies from ISD
content_sections.content: In this row, the taxpayer should mention the input tax credit availed from input service distributors. Hence, the taxpayers can allot Input service distributors to distribute input tax credit. This row would be applicable only for taxpayers who have registered as an input service distributor.

content_sections.heading: All Other Input Tax Credit
content_sections.content: Any taxpayer who purchased or received the invoices for goods and services during the month of July shall provide details on this row. The taxpayer shall provide information on integrated tax, central tax, state tax and cess paid based on the details of the taxpayer. To complete this field, it is important to compile all invoices received and calculate the amount of GST tax paid in the month of July.

content_sections.heading: Input Tax Credit Reversed
content_sections.content: The input tax credit cannot be availed fully for certain supplies which are used partly for business purposes and partly for other purposes. For such input tax credit, the taxpayer shall reverse the input tax credit as per Rule 42 and Rule 43 of the CGST Rules. Details of input tax credit so reversed must be provided in this row.

content_sections.heading: All Other Input Tax Credit Reversed
content_sections.content: In case of reversal of input tax credit for any other reason, the user can provide the details of such reversal in this row with break up of integrated tax, state tax, central tax and cess.

content_sections.heading: Net Input Tax Credit Availed
content_sections.content: Based on the information provided above, the GST Portal automatically calculates the net input tax credit available to the taxpayer in row C.

content_sections.heading: Ineligible Input Tax Credit
content_sections.content: Certain items like food, beverages, life insurance, health club memberships and more are [ineligible forGST input tax credit](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/items-not-eligible-input-tax-credit). Details of such items that were not eligible for the input tax credit must be mentioned in row D.

content_sections.heading: Step 4: Prepare Inward Supplies Exempt from GST
content_sections.content:
![GSTR 3B Inward Supplies Exempt from GST](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2017/08/GSTR-3B-Inward-Supplies-Exempt-from-GST-1024x162.jpg)GSTR 3B Inward Supplies Exempt from GST

In this table, details of inward supplies that were exempt from GST must be provided.In the first row, the taxpayer shall provide the total value of all supplies received from a composition scheme taxable person + purchases of goods or services exempted from GST + goods and services purchased with nil GST rate. The individual shall divide the details between inter-state supplies and intra-state supplies.In the second row, the taxpayer can mention the details on purchases of all non-GST goods and services, if any. For most taxpayers, this row would be nil.

content_sections.heading: Step 5: Prepare details of GST paid
content_sections.content:
![GSTR 3B Payment of Tax](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2017/08/GSTR-3B-Payment-of-Tax-1024x229.png)GSTR 3B Payment of Tax

In this table, the taxpayer shall provide the details of tax payable and GST tax paid. The Government portal, auto-populates the tax payable based on the information provided in the previous tables. The taxpayer can also calculate the total tax payable by adding all integrated tax, central tax, state tax and cess payable.After providing the total tax payable, the GST Portal auto-populates the input tax credit available after calculating in Step 3. If the taxpayer paid any GST, details of such tax payment can be provided in column 8. Interest and late fees will be zero if GSTR 3B is filed on time with GST payment.

content_sections.heading: Step 6: Details of TDS and TCS
content_sections.content:
![TDS & TCS Credit](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2017/08/GSTR-3B-TDS-TCS-Credit-1024x126.png)GSTR 3B TDS & TCS Credit

In this table, the input has been disabled on the GST portal as TDS and TCS provisions have not come into effect. Hence, taxpayers need not worry about calculating TDS or TCS for the GSTR 3B return to be filed in August.

content_sections.heading: Step 7: Filing GSTR 3B on GST Portal
content_sections.content: After providing the above-mentioned details manually or through GST software, the user can file GSTR 3B on the GST portal within a few minutes. In case you use LEDGERS GST software, the software shall calculate all of the information above based on the invoices and purchase invoices you generated. Hence, you can simply enter the information provided by us into the GST Portal and click on submit. _In case you do not use LEDGERS, you would have to prepare the above information manually to file the same on the GST portal._ _[Also Read - "How to File GSTR 3b online in GST Portal?"](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/how-to-file-gstr-3b)_

content_sections.heading: LEDGERS GST Software
content_sections.content: Using [LEDGERS GST software](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-software), you can prepare and file a GSTR 3B return in a few clicks. If you are not using LEDGERS GST Software, follow the steps below to calculate and file the GSTR 3B return.

content_sections.heading: Difference between GSTR1 and GSTR 3b
content_sections.content:
GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B are both crucial forms under India's Goods and Services Tax (GST) system, but they serve different purposes and contain different information. Here’s a breakdown of the key differences between GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B:

**GSTR-1** is detailed, covering all outward supplies of goods and services. It is filed monthly or quarterly, depending on the taxpayer's turnover. This form serves primarily for reconciling outward supplies.

**GSTR-3B**, in contrast, is a summary return filed monthly by all taxpayers. It provides a consolidated overview of sales and purchases and is crucial for calculating and paying net GST.

The reconciliation of GSTR-3B and GSTR-1 is essential for verifying that the data reported in both returns are consistent. This process is a compliance measure and a crucial check to prevent any mismatches that could result in penalties or interest due to inaccuracies.

In summary, while GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B serve different purposes—one for detailed transaction reporting and the other for summary tax liability—both are integral to GST compliance.

[_Click here to learn more about the Difference Between GSTR 1 and GSTR 3b_](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/difference-between-gstr-1-and-gstr-3b)

content_sections.content:

[Click here to start with IndiaFilings and simplify your GST filing process with LEDGERS](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-return-filing).
