# GSTR-3A - Notice for Not Filing GST Return

GSTR-3A is a notice for not filing GST returns issued under the GST regulations. Taxable persons registered under GST shall file GST returns periodically. The due date and the type of return to be filed varies based on the type of

[GST registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-registration) obtained by the taxpayers. Regular taxpayers registered under GST have to file 3 GST returns a month namely, GSTR-1, GSTR-2, and GSTR-3. Casual taxable persons, non-resident taxable persons, and taxpayers registered under the Composition scheme have to file different types of GST returns on due dates, as shown below.

![GST Return Filing Due Dates](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2017/06/GST-Return-Filing-Due-Dates-1024x841.png) GST Return Filing Due Dates

## GSTR-3A: Notice for Not Filing GST Return

Upon failure to file the GST returns on a regular basis, the GST department issues GSTR-3A to the taxpayer. The following is a sample GSTR-3A tax notice:

![Sample GSTR-3A](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2017/08/Sample-GSTR-3A.png) Sample GSTR-3A



GSTR-3A can be classified under two categories as follows:

## Notice to File Pending GST Return

In the first type of GSTR-3A notice, the GST department provides an opportunity for the taxpayer to file any pending GST returns with penalty or interest and regularize the GST compliance. The following reasons shall apply for issuing the notice:

Being a registered taxpayer, you are required to furnish return for the supplies made or received and to discharge resultant tax liability for the aforesaid tax period by due date. It has been noticed that you have not filed the said return till date.

1. > You are, therefore, requested to furnish the said return within 15 days failing which the tax liability will be assessed u/s 62 of the Act, based on the relevant material available with this office. Please note that in addition to tax so assessed, you will also be liable to pay interest and [penalty](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/penalty-late-filing-gst-return) as per provisions of the Act.

2. > Please note that no further communication will be issued for assessing the liability.

3. > The notice shall be deemed to have been withdrawn in case the return referred above, is filed by you before issue of the assessment order.


### Responding to notice to file GST return

The taxpayer should file for GST returns even if the business stops the operation or no transactions for the month. Hence, the taxpayer should always file any pending GST returns immediately after receiving the notice from the GST department. After filing the GST returns and clearing any tax liabilities, the taxpayer can apply for cancellation. In the case of nil transactions, the taxpayer shall apply to discontinue the GST compliance.

In any case, if the taxpayer regularizes GST compliance within 15 days, then the GST registration would be valid. In case the taxpayer fails to respond to the above notice, the department shall cancel the GST registration and issue the following notice:

## Notice of Cancellation of GST Registration

If a taxpayer after receiving a notice requesting GST return filing has not complied or filed GST returns within 15 days of notice, the following notice in Form GST REG-17 can be issued by the GST department with show-cause notice for cancellation of GST registration.

![Sample GST REG-17](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2017/08/GST-REG-17.png) Sample GST REG-17



In such a case, the taxpayer must immediately file the overdue GST returns within 7 days, provide a written reply to the tax office about the reason for the delay in filing of GST returns and appear before the concerned officer in person on the date and time mentioned in the show-cause notice.

In case the taxpayer is not able to file GST returns, a reply citing reasons for the delay in filing GST returns along with a request for extension can be submitted in writing. The authorised person under GST will also have to appear before the tax officer for the personal hearing and decide on a course of action.

[gst registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/gst-registration-branches) to read on GST Registration for Branches & Business Verticals

## Notice to File GST Final Return - GSTR-10

After the cancellation or surrender of a GST registration,  the taxpayer must file GSTR-10 return within 3 months. In case the taxpayer failed to file GSTR-10, then the following notice would be issued by the GST department.

> The taxpayer should provide the final return in Form GSTR-10 as per Section 45 of the Act when surrendering or canceling the GST registration for the following reasons:

> - It has been noticed that you have not filed the final return by the due date.
> - You are, therefore, requested to furnish the final return as specified under section 45 of the Act within 15 days failing which your tax liability for the aforesaid tax period will be determined in accordance with the provisions of the Act based on the relevant material available with or gathered by this office. Please note that in addition to tax so assessed, you will also be liable to pay interest as per provisions of the Act. This notice shall be deemed to be withdrawn in case the return is filed by you before
> - This notice shall be deemed to be withdrawn in case the return is filed by you before issue of the assessment order.

### Responding to Notice to File GSTR-10 Return

In case the above notice has been issued by the GST department, it is advisable to immediately file GSTR-10 return within 15 days along with any penalty or fines, as applicable. In case the taxpayer fails to respond to the above tax notice, the GST department could levy additional fines or penalty on the taxpayer for non-compliance.

[Back to Learn](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn)

## Frequently Asked Questions

Common questions aboutGSTR-3A Notice.

What is GSTR-3A?

GSTR-3A is a notice issued by the GST department to taxpayers who have failed to file their GST returns within the prescribed due dates. It serves as a reminder and warning for non-compliance with GST return filing obligations.

Why is GSTR-3A issued?

GSTR-3A is issued when a registered taxpayer under GST fails to file the required GST returns (GSTR-1, GSTR-2, GSTR-3, or other applicable returns) within the stipulated due dates. It is a mechanism to ensure timely compliance with GST return filing requirements.

What are the two types of GSTR-3A notices?

The two types of GSTR-3A notices are: 1) Notice to file pending GST returns, and 2) Notice of cancellation of GST registration. The first type provides an opportunity to file pending returns, while the second is issued if the taxpayer fails to respond to the first notice.

How much time is given to respond to the notice to file pending GST returns?

The notice to file pending GST returns typically gives the taxpayer 15 days to file the overdue GST returns. Failure to comply within this period may lead to the issuance of a notice for cancellation of GST registration.

What happens if a taxpayer fails to respond to the notice of cancellation of GST registration?

If a taxpayer fails to respond to the notice of cancellation of GST registration (GST REG-17) within the given timeframe (usually 7 days), the GST department may proceed with canceling the taxpayer's GST registration.

What is GSTR-10, and when is it required to be filed?

GSTR-10 is the final GST return that a taxpayer must file within 3 months of cancellation or surrender of their GST registration. Failure to file GSTR-10 may result in the issuance of a notice from the GST department to file the final return.

Can a taxpayer request an extension for filing GST returns after receiving GSTR-3A?

Yes, if a taxpayer is unable to file the overdue GST returns within the specified timeframe after receiving GSTR-3A, they can submit a written request for an extension, citing valid reasons for the delay, and appear before the concerned officer for a personal hearing.

What are the consequences of not responding to GSTR-3A notices?

If a taxpayer fails to respond to GSTR-3A notices, the GST department may proceed with canceling the taxpayer's GST registration, assessing tax liability based on available information, and imposing interest and penalties as per the GST Act.

Can a taxpayer file nil GST returns if there are no transactions in a particular period?

Yes, even if there are no transactions or business operations in a particular period, the taxpayer must file nil GST returns to maintain compliance with GST regulations. Failing to do so may result in the issuance of GSTR-3A notices.

What should a taxpayer do if they receive a notice to file GSTR-10 after cancellation of GST registration?

If a taxpayer receives a notice to file GSTR-10 (final GST return) after cancellation of their GST registration, they should file the GSTR-10 return within 15 days, along with any applicable penalties or fines. Failure to do so may result in further penalties or assessments by the GST department.

content_sections.heading: GST Registration Online: A Guide
content_sections.content:
For GST registration online, the taxpayers shall upload the required documents to the GST portal.  The registration applies to individuals required to collect GST or a person required to collect Tax at Source or a person providing online information and database access or retrieval services (

[OIDAR Service](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/service-tax-online-services)) from a place outside India to a non-taxable online recipient is required to obtain GST registration in India. In this article, we look at a detailed procedure for obtaining GST Registration in India with a list of information and documents required.

content_sections.heading: How to Apply for GST Registration
content_sections.content:
The taxpayer shall process the GST Registration application through Form GST REG-01 on the India Filings platform, GST Common Portal, or through a GST Facilitation Centre. To begin the GST Registration process, the applicant must provide his/her PAN, mobile number, email address, and also the state of registration.

After providing the information online, the Common Portal validates the PAN of the applicant from the database maintained by the Central Board of Direct Taxes. Further, an OTP is sent to the mobile number and email address mentioned in the registration form along with a temporary reference number. Using the temporary reference number, the applicant must then complete Part-B of the FORM GST REG-01 along with that is duly signed application and documents. The application form can be submitted electronically through the GST Common Platform or through a GST Facilitation Centre.

content_sections.heading: Information Required in GST Registration Application
content_sections.content:
The applicant can submit the following information online through the GST Common Portal or through a GST Facilitation Centre or India Filings.

![GST-Registration-Page](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2017/05/GST-Registration-Application-Page-1.png) GST-Registration-Page



![GST-Registration-Page](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2017/05/GST-Registration-Application-Page-2.png)!["<yoastmark](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2017/05/GST-Registration-Application-Page-3.png)!["<yoastmark](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2017/05/GST-Registration-Application-Page-4.png)!["<yoastmark](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2017/05/GST-Registration-Application-Page-5.png)!["<yoastmark](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2017/05/GST-Registration-Application-Page-6.png)!["<yoastmark](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2017/05/GST-Registration-Application-Page-7.png)!["<yoastmark](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2017/05/GST-Registration-Application-Page-8.png)

content_sections.heading: Photographs of the Promoters
content_sections.content:
- - In case of Proprietary Concern – Proprietor's Photo
  - Partnership Firm / LLP – Managing or Authorized or Designated Partner's Photo. Photos of up to 10 partners.
  - Hindu Undivided Family (HUF) - Karta
  - Company – Managing Director or the Authorised Person
  - Trust – Managing Trustee
  - Association of Persons (AoP) or Body of Individuals (BoI) – Members of the Managing Committee. Photos of up to ten members, including that of Chairman, are to be submitted.
  - Local Authority – CEO or his equivalent
  - Statutory Body – CEO or his equivalent
  - For all Others – Person in Charge

content_sections.heading: Constitution of Business or Registration Certificate
content_sections.content:
- - Partnership Firm - Partnership Deed
  - Society, Trust, Club, Government Department, Association of Persons or Body of Individuals, Local Authority, Statutory Body and Others - Registration Certificate or Proof of Constitution
  - LLP - Incorporation Certificate
  - Company - Incorporation Certificate

content_sections.heading: Proof of Principal Place of Business
content_sections.content:
- - In case of own premises – Any document in support of the ownership of the premises like the latest Property Tax Receipt or Municipal Khata copy or copy of Electricity Bill.
  - Rented or Leased premises – A copy of the valid Rent / Lease Agreement with any document in support of the ownership of the premises of the Lessor like Latest Property Tax Receipt or Municipal Khata copy or copy of Electricity Bill.
  - Upon non-availability of Rent or lease agreement for the Rented or leased premises - An affidavit to that effect along with any document in support of the possession of the premises like a copy of Electricity Bill.
  - For all other cases including shared properties - A copy of the Consent Letter with any document in support of the ownership of the premises of the Consenter like Municipal Khata copy or Electricity Bill copy.
  - In case the location of the principal place of business established as SEZ or the applicant registered as an SEZ developer - the applicant shall upload the necessary documents or certificates as issued by the Government of India.

content_sections.heading: Bank Account Related Proof
content_sections.content: - - Scanned copy of the first page of Bank passbook or the relevant page of Bank Statement or Scanned copy of a canceled cheque containing the name of the Proprietor or Business entity, Bank Account No., MICR, IFSC and Branch details including code.

content_sections.heading: GST Authorisation Form
content_sections.content:
The following GST Authorisation Form must be executed by the Managing Director or Board of Directors, authorizing the authorized signatory signing the GST registration application.

> #### Declaration for Authorised Signatory
>
> Provide details of Proprietor/all Partners/Karta/Managing Directors and whole time Director/Members of Managing Committee of Associations/Board of Trustees etc.)
>
> I/We, (Name) of Partners/Karta/Directors/Trustees/CEO) being (Partners/Karta/Managing Directors and whole time Director/Members of Managing Committee of Associations/Board of Trustees etc.) of (GST Applicant Name), hereby solemnly affirm and declare that (Name of Authorised Signatory) is hereby authorized, vide resolution no (Board Resolution Number, if applicable) dated (Board Resolution Date, if applicable) (copy submitted herewith), to act as an authorized signatory for the business (Name of the Business / GST Applicant Name) for which application for registration is being filed under the Act. All his actions in relation to this business will be binding on me/us.
>
> Signature of the person(s) competent to sign
>
> Name:
>
> Designation/Status:
>
> (Name of the proprietor/Business Entity)

content_sections.heading: Digitally Signing the GST Registration Application
content_sections.content:
Once the above information and documents are provided, the application for GST registration must be digitally signed by the person mentioned in the table below :

- Proprietorship - Proprietor
- Partnership - Managing / Authorized Partners
- Hindu Undivided Family - Karta
- Private Limited Company - Managing / Whole-time Directors
- Public Limited Company - Managing / Whole-time Directors
- Society/ Club/Trust/AOP - Members of Managing Committee
- Government Department - Person In Charge
- Public Sector Undertaking - Managing / Whole-time Director
- Unlimited Company - Managing/ Whole-time Director
- Limited Liability Partnership - Designated Partners
- Local Authority - Chief Executive Officer (CEO) or Equivalent
- Statutory Body - Chief Executive Officer (CEO) or Equivalent
- Foreign Company - Authorized Person in India
- Foreign Limited Liability Partnership - Authorized Person in India
- Others (specify) - Person In-charge

content_sections.heading: GST Registration Application Receipt
content_sections.content:
The portal provides the GST Registration Application after submitting the required information and documents :

![GST Registration Application Acknowledgement](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2017/05/GST-Registration-Application-Acknowledgement.png) GST Registration Application Acknowledgement

content_sections.heading: GST Registration Application Processing by the Government
content_sections.content:
For the verification process, the concerned Officer receives the information and documents for the GST Registration application from the system. After successful verification, the Officer shall grant the certificate to the applicant within three working days from the date of submission of application.

In case of any deficiencies with the application or information or documents submitted, the Officer shall provide a notice to the applicant electronically in FORM GST REG-03 within three working days from the date of submission of application. On receiving the details of deficiencies, the applicant shall submit the clarification or information or documents to the concerned Officer in FORM GST REG-04, within seven working days from the date of receipt of such notice.

content_sections.heading: Non-Submission of Clarification
content_sections.content: If the applicant fails to respond to the deficiencies in application noted by the Officer within seven days or the clarification provided by the applicant fails to meet the requirement, the Officer will reject the application with a reason for registration in writing.

content_sections.heading: Automatic GST Registration
content_sections.content: The individual shall consider the registration process as approved if the Officer fails to take any actions within the stipulated period. The approval process applies upon failure of action within three working days from the date of submission of application, or within seven working days from the date of receipt of clarification, information or documents furnished by the applicant.

content_sections.heading: GST Registration
content_sections.content:
After successful verification by the Officer for the

[GST registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/change-gst-registration-information) application furnished by the applicant, he/she may approve the grant of registration to the applicant within seven working days from the date of receipt of such clarification or information or documents. The following model describes the GST Registration Certificate :

![Model GST Registration Certificate](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2017/05/Model-GST-Registration-Certificate.png) Model GST Registration Certificate

The GST Registration Certificate would show the name of the business and the principal place of business. In addition, it also shows the type of entity, validity period, and a Goods and Services Tax Identification Number (GSTIN). The 15 digit GSTIN is provided in the following format :

Two characters for the State code, ten characters for the PAN or;

The Tax Deduction and Collection Account Number, two characters for the entity code, and one checksum character.

Know more about [GST Return Filing](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-return-filing) post obtaining GST Registration on India Filings GST Portal.

[Back to Learn](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn)

content_sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
content_sections.content:
Common questions aboutGST Registration Online: Process and Requirements.

What is the process to apply for GST registration online?

To apply for GST registration online, the taxpayer needs to fill out Form GST REG-01 on the GST Common Portal, India Filings platform, or through a GST Facilitation Centre. They will need to provide details like PAN, mobile number, email address, and state of registration. After submitting the initial details, they must complete the remaining sections of the form and submit the required documents.

What documents are required for GST registration?

Some key documents required for GST registration include photographs of promoters/partners/directors, proof of business constitution (partnership deed, registration certificate, etc.), proof of principal place of business (property tax receipt, rent agreement, etc.), bank account details, and authorization form for the authorized signatory.

Who can digitally sign the GST registration application?

The GST registration application must be digitally signed by the proprietor (in case of proprietorship), managing/authorized partners (partnership firm), karta (Hindu Undivided Family), managing/whole-time directors (private/public limited company), members of managing committee (society/club/trust/AOP), or the person in-charge (for other entities).

How does the government process the GST registration application?

The concerned officer verifies the information and documents submitted with the GST registration application. If everything is in order, they grant the registration certificate within 3 working days. If there are any deficiencies, the officer issues a notice, and the applicant has 7 working days to provide clarification or additional documents.

What happens if the applicant fails to provide clarification for GST registration?

If the applicant fails to respond to the deficiency notice within 7 working days or the clarification provided is unsatisfactory, the officer can reject the GST registration application with a written reason.

What is the validity period of the GST registration certificate?

The GST registration certificate issued by the government does not mention any specific validity period. It is presumed to be valid until it is surrendered, canceled, or revoked.

What information is included in the GST registration certificate?

The GST registration certificate displays the name of the business, principal place of business, type of entity, validity period (if any), and the 15-digit Goods and Services Tax Identification Number (GSTIN).

How is the GSTIN generated for GST registration?

The 15-digit GSTIN is generated in the following format: 2 characters for state code, 10 characters for PAN or Tax Deduction and Collection Account Number, 2 characters for entity code, and 1 checksum character.

Can an individual apply for GST registration if providing online database services from outside India?

Yes, the article mentions that a person providing online information and database access or retrieval services (OIDAR Service) from a place outside India to a non-taxable online recipient is required to obtain GST registration in India.

Is there an option for automatic GST registration approval?

Yes, if the concerned officer fails to take any action (approve or raise deficiency notice) within 3 working days from the date of application submission or 7 working days from the date of receiving clarification, the GST registration is considered approved automatically.

# GST Registration Online: A Guide

For GST registration online, the taxpayers shall upload the required documents to the GST portal.  The registration applies to individuals required to collect GST or a person required to collect Tax at Source or a person providing online information and database access or retrieval services (

[OIDAR Service](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/service-tax-online-services)) from a place outside India to a non-taxable online recipient is required to obtain GST registration in India. In this article, we look at a detailed procedure for obtaining GST Registration in India with a list of information and documents required.

## How to Apply for GST Registration

The taxpayer shall process the GST Registration application through Form GST REG-01 on the India Filings platform, GST Common Portal, or through a GST Facilitation Centre. To begin the GST Registration process, the applicant must provide his/her PAN, mobile number, email address, and also the state of registration.

After providing the information online, the Common Portal validates the PAN of the applicant from the database maintained by the Central Board of Direct Taxes. Further, an OTP is sent to the mobile number and email address mentioned in the registration form along with a temporary reference number. Using the temporary reference number, the applicant must then complete Part-B of the FORM GST REG-01 along with that is duly signed application and documents. The application form can be submitted electronically through the GST Common Platform or through a GST Facilitation Centre.

## Information Required in GST Registration Application

The applicant can submit the following information online through the GST Common Portal or through a GST Facilitation Centre or India Filings.

![GST-Registration-Page](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2017/05/GST-Registration-Application-Page-1.png) GST-Registration-Page



![GST-Registration-Page](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2017/05/GST-Registration-Application-Page-2.png)!["<yoastmark](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2017/05/GST-Registration-Application-Page-3.png)!["<yoastmark](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2017/05/GST-Registration-Application-Page-4.png)!["<yoastmark](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2017/05/GST-Registration-Application-Page-5.png)!["<yoastmark](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2017/05/GST-Registration-Application-Page-6.png)!["<yoastmark](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2017/05/GST-Registration-Application-Page-7.png)!["<yoastmark](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2017/05/GST-Registration-Application-Page-8.png)

## Documents Required for GST Registration

#### **Photographs of the Promoters**

- - In case of Proprietary Concern – Proprietor's Photo
  - Partnership Firm / LLP – Managing or Authorized or Designated Partner's Photo. Photos of up to 10 partners.
  - Hindu Undivided Family (HUF) - Karta
  - Company – Managing Director or the Authorised Person
  - Trust – Managing Trustee
  - Association of Persons (AoP) or Body of Individuals (BoI) – Members of the Managing Committee. Photos of up to ten members, including that of Chairman, are to be submitted.
  - Local Authority – CEO or his equivalent
  - Statutory Body – CEO or his equivalent
  - For all Others – Person in Charge

#### Constitution of Business or Registration Certificate

- - Partnership Firm - Partnership Deed
  - Society, Trust, Club, Government Department, Association of Persons or Body of Individuals, Local Authority, Statutory Body and Others - Registration Certificate or Proof of Constitution
  - LLP - Incorporation Certificate
  - Company - Incorporation Certificate

#### Proof of Principal Place of Business

- - In case of own premises – Any document in support of the ownership of the premises like the latest Property Tax Receipt or Municipal Khata copy or copy of Electricity Bill.
  - Rented or Leased premises – A copy of the valid Rent / Lease Agreement with any document in support of the ownership of the premises of the Lessor like Latest Property Tax Receipt or Municipal Khata copy or copy of Electricity Bill.
  - Upon non-availability of Rent or lease agreement for the Rented or leased premises - An affidavit to that effect along with any document in support of the possession of the premises like a copy of Electricity Bill.
  - For all other cases including shared properties - A copy of the Consent Letter with any document in support of the ownership of the premises of the Consenter like Municipal Khata copy or Electricity Bill copy.
  - In case the location of the principal place of business established as SEZ or the applicant registered as an SEZ developer - the applicant shall upload the necessary documents or certificates as issued by the Government of India.

#### **Bank Account Related Proof**

- - Scanned copy of the first page of Bank passbook or the relevant page of Bank Statement or Scanned copy of a canceled cheque containing the name of the Proprietor or Business entity, Bank Account No., MICR, IFSC and Branch details including code.


## GST Authorisation Form

The following GST Authorisation Form must be executed by the Managing Director or Board of Directors, authorizing the authorized signatory signing the GST registration application.

> #### Declaration for Authorised Signatory
>
> Provide details of Proprietor/all Partners/Karta/Managing Directors and whole time Director/Members of Managing Committee of Associations/Board of Trustees etc.)
>
> I/We, (Name) of Partners/Karta/Directors/Trustees/CEO) being (Partners/Karta/Managing Directors and whole time Director/Members of Managing Committee of Associations/Board of Trustees etc.) of (GST Applicant Name), hereby solemnly affirm and declare that (Name of Authorised Signatory) is hereby authorized, vide resolution no (Board Resolution Number, if applicable) dated (Board Resolution Date, if applicable) (copy submitted herewith), to act as an authorized signatory for the business (Name of the Business / GST Applicant Name) for which application for registration is being filed under the Act. All his actions in relation to this business will be binding on me/us.
>
> Signature of the person(s) competent to sign
>
> Name:
>
> Designation/Status:
>
> (Name of the proprietor/Business Entity)

## Digitally Signing the GST Registration Application

Once the above information and documents are provided, the application for GST registration must be digitally signed by the person mentioned in the table below :

- Proprietorship - Proprietor
- Partnership - Managing / Authorized Partners
- Hindu Undivided Family - Karta
- Private Limited Company - Managing / Whole-time Directors
- Public Limited Company - Managing / Whole-time Directors
- Society/ Club/Trust/AOP - Members of Managing Committee
- Government Department - Person In Charge
- Public Sector Undertaking - Managing / Whole-time Director
- Unlimited Company - Managing/ Whole-time Director
- Limited Liability Partnership - Designated Partners
- Local Authority - Chief Executive Officer (CEO) or Equivalent
- Statutory Body - Chief Executive Officer (CEO) or Equivalent
- Foreign Company - Authorized Person in India
- Foreign Limited Liability Partnership - Authorized Person in India
- Others (specify) - Person In-charge

## GST Registration Application Receipt

The portal provides the GST Registration Application after submitting the required information and documents :

![GST Registration Application Acknowledgement](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2017/05/GST-Registration-Application-Acknowledgement.png) GST Registration Application Acknowledgement

## GST Registration Application Processing by the Government

For the verification process, the concerned Officer receives the information and documents for the GST Registration application from the system. After successful verification, the Officer shall grant the certificate to the applicant within three working days from the date of submission of application.

In case of any deficiencies with the application or information or documents submitted, the Officer shall provide a notice to the applicant electronically in FORM GST REG-03 within three working days from the date of submission of application. On receiving the details of deficiencies, the applicant shall submit the clarification or information or documents to the concerned Officer in FORM GST REG-04, within seven working days from the date of receipt of such notice.

### Non-Submission of Clarification

If the applicant fails to respond to the deficiencies in application noted by the Officer within seven days or the clarification provided by the applicant fails to meet the requirement, the Officer will reject the application with a reason for registration in writing.

### Automatic GST Registration

The individual shall consider the registration process as approved if the Officer fails to take any actions within the stipulated period. The approval process applies upon failure of action within three working days from the date of submission of application, or within seven working days from the date of receipt of clarification, information or documents furnished by the applicant.

## GST Registration

After successful verification by the Officer for the

[GST registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/change-gst-registration-information) application furnished by the applicant, he/she may approve the grant of registration to the applicant within seven working days from the date of receipt of such clarification or information or documents. The following model describes the GST Registration Certificate :

![Model GST Registration Certificate](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2017/05/Model-GST-Registration-Certificate.png) Model GST Registration Certificate

The GST Registration Certificate would show the name of the business and the principal place of business. In addition, it also shows the type of entity, validity period, and a Goods and Services Tax Identification Number (GSTIN). The 15 digit GSTIN is provided in the following format :

Two characters for the State code, ten characters for the PAN or;

The Tax Deduction and Collection Account Number, two characters for the entity code, and one checksum character.

Know more about [GST Return Filing](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-return-filing) post obtaining GST Registration on India Filings GST Portal.

[Back to Learn](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn)

## Frequently Asked Questions

Common questions aboutGST Registration Online: Process and Requirements.

What is the process to apply for GST registration online?

To apply for GST registration online, the taxpayer needs to fill out Form GST REG-01 on the GST Common Portal, India Filings platform, or through a GST Facilitation Centre. They will need to provide details like PAN, mobile number, email address, and state of registration. After submitting the initial details, they must complete the remaining sections of the form and submit the required documents.

What documents are required for GST registration?

Some key documents required for GST registration include photographs of promoters/partners/directors, proof of business constitution (partnership deed, registration certificate, etc.), proof of principal place of business (property tax receipt, rent agreement, etc.), bank account details, and authorization form for the authorized signatory.

Who can digitally sign the GST registration application?

The GST registration application must be digitally signed by the proprietor (in case of proprietorship), managing/authorized partners (partnership firm), karta (Hindu Undivided Family), managing/whole-time directors (private/public limited company), members of managing committee (society/club/trust/AOP), or the person in-charge (for other entities).

How does the government process the GST registration application?

The concerned officer verifies the information and documents submitted with the GST registration application. If everything is in order, they grant the registration certificate within 3 working days. If there are any deficiencies, the officer issues a notice, and the applicant has 7 working days to provide clarification or additional documents.

What happens if the applicant fails to provide clarification for GST registration?

If the applicant fails to respond to the deficiency notice within 7 working days or the clarification provided is unsatisfactory, the officer can reject the GST registration application with a written reason.

What is the validity period of the GST registration certificate?

The GST registration certificate issued by the government does not mention any specific validity period. It is presumed to be valid until it is surrendered, canceled, or revoked.

What information is included in the GST registration certificate?

The GST registration certificate displays the name of the business, principal place of business, type of entity, validity period (if any), and the 15-digit Goods and Services Tax Identification Number (GSTIN).

How is the GSTIN generated for GST registration?

The 15-digit GSTIN is generated in the following format: 2 characters for state code, 10 characters for PAN or Tax Deduction and Collection Account Number, 2 characters for entity code, and 1 checksum character.

Can an individual apply for GST registration if providing online database services from outside India?

Yes, the article mentions that a person providing online information and database access or retrieval services (OIDAR Service) from a place outside India to a non-taxable online recipient is required to obtain GST registration in India.

Is there an option for automatic GST registration approval?

Yes, if the concerned officer fails to take any action (approve or raise deficiency notice) within 3 working days from the date of application submission or 7 working days from the date of receiving clarification, the GST registration is considered approved automatically.

blogs.title: GST Demand Notice

content_sections.heading: GST Demand Notice
content_sections.content:
The Goods & Service Tax (GST) is payable on self-assessment basis i.e. assessee himself has to determine it’s tax lability. If the determination of assessee goes wrong i.e. assessee has short paid any taxes or not paid any taxes or has wrong availed and utilized
any

[input tax credit](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/gst-input-tax-credit) or has erroneously been refunded, than, under such circumstances demand would be raised by the GST officials. In this article, we look at GST demand notice and cases wherein demand would be raised, interest and penalty payable on such demand etc.

content_sections.heading: Types of Demand under GST
content_sections.content:
The GST demand notice can be issued by the GST officials for short payment or non-payment of GST in following two different situations:

1. When there is no reason of fraud or wilful misstatement or suppression of facts
2. When there is reason of fraud or wilful misstatement or suppression of facts

content_sections.heading: Section 73 of GST Act - No Fraud or Misrepresentation
content_sections.content:
When there is no reason of fraud or wilful misstatement or suppression of facts, demand notice is issued under Section 73 of the GST Act.

Section 73 of the CGST Act, deals with the cases where any taxes has not been paid or short paid or erroneously refunded, or where input tax credit has been wrongly availed or utilised for any reason, other than the reason of fraud or any wilful misstatement or suppression of facts to evade tax.

content_sections.heading: Time Limit for Issue of Notice and Adjudication under Section 73
content_sections.content:
If there is any non-payment, short payment, or where input credit has been wrongly availed or utilized for any reason other than fraud or willful misstatement or suppression of facts, than, the adjudication of the case should be done within 3 years from the date of filing of annual

[GST return](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-registration) for the relevant financial year.

If the assessee received an erroneous refund, the case must be adjudicated within 3 years from the date on which such refund was credited to the assessee’s account.

The officer should issue notice for recovery of tax at least 3 months prior to the limit of adjudication or issue of order.

The officer should issue order of adjudication within 3 years from the due date for furnishing of annual return for the financial year for the relevant period of dispute

Once the above notice has been issued within the time limit, the proper officer can serve a statement, with details of any unpaid tax/wrong refund etc. for other periods not covered in the notice. A separate notice does not have to be issued for each tax period.

Finally, an assessee can voluntarily pay taxes along with interest before issue of notice / statement and inform the departmental officer about the same in writing. The departmental officer, if satisfied, will not issue notice in that respect.

content_sections.heading: Payment of Tax on Receiving GST Demand Notice
content_sections.content: If a demand notice is issued under Section 73 and the taxpayer makes payment, the following would be the penalty under Section 73 of the GST Act:

content_sections.heading: Penalty under Section 73 of the GST Act
content_sections.content:
| | | | --- | --- | | Payment of Penalty | Amount of Penalty | | Dues paid before issuance of show cause
notice. | No penalty | | Dues paid within 30 days of issuance of
show cause notice. | No penalty | | Dues paid after 30 days of issuance of
Order. | 10% of tax dues or INR 10,000
Whichever is higher. | | Any other case | 10% of tax dues or INR 10,000
Whichever is higher. |

content_sections.heading: Section 74 of GST Act  - Fraud or Misrepresentation
content_sections.content:
When there is reason of fraud or wilful misstatement or suppression of facts, GST demand notice is issued under Section 74 of the GST Act.

Section 74 of the CGST Act, deals with the cases where any tax has not been paid or short paid or erroneously refunded, or where input tax credit has been wrongly  availed or utilised by reason of fraud or any wilful misstatement or suppression of
facts to evade tax.

content_sections.heading: Time Limit for Issue of Notice and Adjudication under Section 74
content_sections.content:
If there is any non-payment, short payment, or where input credit has been wrongly availed or utilized with the reason of fraud or willful misstatement or suppression of facts, than, the adjudication of the case should be done within 5 years from
the date of filing of annual return for the relevant financial year.

If the assessee received an erroneous refund, the case must be adjudicated within 5 years from the date on which such refund was credited to the assessee’s account.

The officer should issue notice for recovery of Tax at least 6 months before the deadline for adjudication of case or issue of order.

The officer should issue order of adjudication within 5 years from the due date for furnishing of annual return for the financial year for the relevant period of dispute.

Please note that, once the notice has been issued, the proper officer can serve a statement, with details of any unpaid tax/wrong refund etc. for other periods not covered in the notice. A separate notice does not have to be issued for each tax period.
Taxes paid before issue of show cause notice/

Finally, an assessee can voluntarily pay taxes along with interest and 15% penalty before issue of notice/statement and inform the departmental officer about the same in writing. The departmental officer, if satisfied, will not issue notice in that respect.

content_sections.heading: Penalty under Section 74 of GST Act
content_sections.content:
| | | | --- | --- | | **Payment of Penalty** | **Amount of Penalty** | | Dues paid before issuance of show cause
notice. | 15% of tax amount due | | Dues paid within 30 days of issuance of
show cause notice. | 25% of tax amount due | | Dues paid after 30 days of issuance of
Order. | 50% of tax amount due | | Any other case. | 100% of tax amount due |

content_sections.heading: Section 75 of GST Act
content_sections.content: Section 75 of the CGST Act, deals with the general provisions relating to determination of tax and demand under GST. The following are some of the important provisions under Section 75 of GST Act.

content_sections.heading: Stay of Notice
content_sections.content: If the service of notice or issuance of order is stayed by an order of Court or Appellate Tribunal, the period of stay will be excluded in computing the period 3 years or 5 years  - the time limit for issue of notice or adjudication.

content_sections.heading: No Fraud or Wilful Misrepresentation
content_sections.content: If any Appellate Authority or Appellate Tribunal or Court concludes that the notice issued under Section 74 is not sustainable for the reason that the charges of fraud or willful misstatement or suppression of facts to evade tax has not been established, the officer shall determine the tax payable deeming as if the notice were issued under Section 73.

content_sections.heading: Time Limit for Passing Order
content_sections.content: Where any order is required to be issued in pursuance of the direction of the Appellate Authority or Appellate Tribunal or a court, such order should be issued within 2 years from the date of communication of the said direction.

content_sections.heading: Opportunity for Being Heard
content_sections.content: An opportunity of hearing should be granted where a request is received in writing from the person chargeable with tax or penalty, or where any adverse decision is proposed against such person.

content_sections.heading: Maximum Adjournments Allowed
content_sections.content: The officer can, if sufficient cause is shown by the person chargeable with tax, adjourn the hearing for reasons to be recorded in writing. Adjournment will be allowed for maximum of 3 times.

content_sections.heading: Passing Order
content_sections.content: The officer, in his order, should set out the relevant facts and the basis of his decision.

content_sections.heading: Limitations
content_sections.content:
The amount of tax, interest and penalty demanded in the order should not be in excess of the amount specified in the notice and no demand can be confirmed on the grounds other than the grounds specified in the notice.

Further, where any penalty is imposed u/s 73 or section 74, no penalty for the same act or omission can be imposed on the same person under any other provision of this Act.

Finally, if the order is not issued with 3 years or 5 years as provided u/s 73 and 74, respectively, then it shall be deemed that the adjudication proceedings are completed and no order can be issued afterwards.

content_sections.heading: Applicability of Interest
content_sections.content:
The interest on the tax short paid or not paid should be payable whether or not specified in the order determining the tax liability.

content_sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
content_sections.content:
Common questions aboutGST Demand Notice: Understand Sections 73, 74 & 75 Regulations.

What is a GST demand notice?

A GST demand notice is issued by the GST officials when there is short payment or non-payment of GST. It can be issued in cases of fraud or willful misstatement/suppression of facts, or in cases where there was no such fraud or misrepresentation.

When is a demand notice issued under Section 73 of the GST Act?

A demand notice under Section 73 of the GST Act is issued when there is short payment or non-payment of GST, or wrong availment or utilization of input tax credit, but there is no reason of fraud, willful misstatement, or suppression of facts.

What is the time limit for issuing a demand notice under Section 73?

The time limit for issuing a demand notice under Section 73 is 3 years from the due date of filing the annual GST return for the relevant financial year. The officer must issue the notice at least 3 months before this time limit.

What is the penalty for non-payment of dues after receiving a demand notice under Section 73?

If the dues are paid after 30 days of issuance of the order under Section 73, a penalty of 10% of the tax dues or INR 10,000, whichever is higher, is payable.

When is a demand notice issued under Section 74 of the GST Act?

A demand notice under Section 74 of the GST Act is issued when there is short payment or non-payment of GST, or wrong availment or utilization of input tax credit, due to fraud, willful misstatement, or suppression of facts to evade tax.

What is the time limit for issuing a demand notice under Section 74?

The time limit for issuing a demand notice under Section 74 is 5 years from the due date of filing the annual GST return for the relevant financial year. The officer must issue the notice at least 6 months before this time limit.

What is the penalty for non-payment of dues after receiving a demand notice under Section 74?

If the dues are paid within 30 days of issuance of the show cause notice under Section 74, a penalty of 25% of the tax amount due is payable. If the dues are paid after 30 days of issuance of the order, a penalty of 50% of the tax amount due is payable.

Can the demand notice be stayed by a court or tribunal order?

Yes, if the service of notice or issuance of order is stayed by an order of a Court or Appellate Tribunal, the period of stay will be excluded from computing the time limit for issuing the notice or adjudicating the case.

Can the taxpayer voluntarily pay taxes before receiving a demand notice?

Yes, an assessee can voluntarily pay taxes along with interest before the issue of a notice or statement, and inform the departmental officer in writing. If the officer is satisfied, no notice will be issued in that respect.

What is the maximum number of adjournments allowed during the hearing process?

The officer can adjourn the hearing for reasons to be recorded in writing, but the maximum number of adjournments allowed is 3 times.

IndiaFilings Expert Published on: **Jul 30, 2026** # GST Demand Notice The Goods & Service Tax (GST) is payable on self-assessment basis i.e. assessee himself has to determine it’s tax lability. If the determination of assessee goes wrong i.e. assessee has short paid any taxes or not paid any taxes or has wrong availed and utilized any [input tax credit](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/gst-input-tax-credit) or has erroneously been refunded, than, under such circumstances demand would be raised by the GST officials. In this article, we look at GST demand notice and cases wherein demand would be raised, interest and penalty payable on such demand etc. ## Types of Demand under GST The GST demand notice can be issued by the GST officials for short payment or non-payment of GST in following two different situations: 1. When there is no reason of fraud or wilful misstatement or suppression of facts 2. When there is reason of fraud or wilful misstatement or suppression of facts ## Section 73 of GST Act - No Fraud or Misrepresentation When there is no reason of fraud or wilful misstatement or suppression of facts, demand notice is issued under Section 73 of the GST Act. Section 73 of the CGST Act, deals with the cases where any taxes has not been paid or short paid or erroneously refunded, or where input tax credit has been wrongly availed or utilised for any reason, other than the reason of fraud or any wilful misstatement or suppression of facts to evade tax. ### Time Limit for Issue of Notice and Adjudication under Section 73 If there is any non-payment, short payment, or where input credit has been wrongly availed or utilized for any reason other than fraud or willful misstatement or suppression of facts, than, the adjudication of the case should be done within 3 years from the date of filing of annual [GST return](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-registration) for the relevant financial year. If the assessee received an erroneous refund, the case must be adjudicated within 3 years from the date on which such refund was credited to the assessee’s account. The officer should issue notice for recovery of tax at least 3 months prior to the limit of adjudication or issue of order. The officer should issue order of adjudication within 3 years from the due date for furnishing of annual return for the financial year for the relevant period of dispute Once the above notice has been issued within the time limit, the proper officer can serve a statement, with details of any unpaid tax/wrong refund etc. for other periods not covered in the notice. A separate notice does not have to be issued for each tax period. Finally, an assessee can voluntarily pay taxes along with interest before issue of notice / statement and inform the departmental officer about the same in writing. The departmental officer, if satisfied, will not issue notice in that respect. ### Payment of Tax on Receiving GST Demand Notice If a demand notice is issued under Section 73 and the taxpayer makes payment, the following would be the penalty under Section 73 of the GST Act: ### Penalty under Section 73 of the GST Act | | | | --- | --- | | Payment of Penalty | Amount of Penalty | | Dues paid before issuance of show cause
notice. | No penalty | | Dues paid within 30 days of issuance of
show cause notice. | No penalty | | Dues paid after 30 days of issuance of
Order. | 10% of tax dues or INR 10,000
Whichever is higher. | | Any other case | 10% of tax dues or INR 10,000
Whichever is higher. | ## Section 74 of GST Act  - Fraud or Misrepresentation When there is reason of fraud or wilful misstatement or suppression of facts, GST demand notice is issued under Section 74 of the GST Act. Section 74 of the CGST Act, deals with the cases where any tax has not been paid or short paid or erroneously refunded, or where input tax credit has been wrongly  availed or utilised by reason of fraud or any wilful misstatement or suppression of facts to evade tax. ### Time Limit for Issue of Notice and Adjudication under Section 74 If there is any non-payment, short payment, or where input credit has been wrongly availed or utilized with the reason of fraud or willful misstatement or suppression of facts, than, the adjudication of the case should be done within 5 years from the date of filing of annual return for the relevant financial year. If the assessee received an erroneous refund, the case must be adjudicated within 5 years from the date on which such refund was credited to the assessee’s account. The officer should issue notice for recovery of Tax at least 6 months before the deadline for adjudication of case or issue of order. The officer should issue order of adjudication within 5 years from the due date for furnishing of annual return for the financial year for the relevant period of dispute. Please note that, once the notice has been issued, the proper officer can serve a statement, with details of any unpaid tax/wrong refund etc. for other periods not covered in the notice. A separate notice does not have to be issued for each tax period. Taxes paid before issue of show cause notice/ Finally, an assessee can voluntarily pay taxes along with interest and 15% penalty before issue of notice/statement and inform the departmental officer about the same in writing. The departmental officer, if satisfied, will not issue notice in that respect. ### Penalty under Section 74 of GST Act | | | | --- | --- | | **Payment of Penalty** | **Amount of Penalty** | | Dues paid before issuance of show cause
notice. | 15% of tax amount due | | Dues paid within 30 days of issuance of
show cause notice. | 25% of tax amount due | | Dues paid after 30 days of issuance of
Order. | 50% of tax amount due | | Any other case. | 100% of tax amount due | ## Section 75 of GST Act Section 75 of the CGST Act, deals with the general provisions relating to determination of tax and demand under GST. The following are some of the important provisions under Section 75 of GST Act. ### Stay of Notice If the service of notice or issuance of order is stayed by an order of Court or Appellate Tribunal, the period of stay will be excluded in computing the period 3 years or 5 years  - the time limit for issue of notice or adjudication. ### No Fraud or Wilful Misrepresentation If any Appellate Authority or Appellate Tribunal or Court concludes that the notice issued under Section 74 is not sustainable for the reason that the charges of fraud or willful misstatement or suppression of facts to evade tax has not been established, the officer shall determine the tax payable deeming as if the notice were issued under Section 73. ### Time Limit for Passing Order Where any order is required to be issued in pursuance of the direction of the Appellate Authority or Appellate Tribunal or a court, such order should be issued within 2 years from the date of communication of the said direction. ### Opportunity for Being Heard An opportunity of hearing should be granted where a request is received in writing from the person chargeable with tax or penalty, or where any adverse decision is proposed against such person. ### Maximum Adjournments Allowed The officer can, if sufficient cause is shown by the person chargeable with tax, adjourn the hearing for reasons to be recorded in writing. Adjournment will be allowed for maximum of 3 times. ### Passing Order The officer, in his order, should set out the relevant facts and the basis of his decision. ### Limitations The amount of tax, interest and penalty demanded in the order should not be in excess of the amount specified in the notice and no demand can be confirmed on the grounds other than the grounds specified in the notice. Further, where any penalty is imposed u/s 73 or section 74, no penalty for the same act or omission can be imposed on the same person under any other provision of this Act. Finally, if the order is not issued with 3 years or 5 years as provided u/s 73 and 74, respectively, then it shall be deemed that the adjudication proceedings are completed and no order can be issued afterwards. ### Applicability of Interest The interest on the tax short paid or not paid should be payable whether or not specified in the order determining the tax liability. [Back to Learn](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn) ## Frequently Asked Questions Common questions aboutGST Demand Notice: Understand Sections 73, 74 & 75 Regulations. What is a GST demand notice? A GST demand notice is issued by the GST officials when there is short payment or non-payment of GST. It can be issued in cases of fraud or willful misstatement/suppression of facts, or in cases where there was no such fraud or misrepresentation. When is a demand notice issued under Section 73 of the GST Act? A demand notice under Section 73 of the GST Act is issued when there is short payment or non-payment of GST, or wrong availment or utilization of input tax credit, but there is no reason of fraud, willful misstatement, or suppression of facts. What is the time limit for issuing a demand notice under Section 73? The time limit for issuing a demand notice under Section 73 is 3 years from the due date of filing the annual GST return for the relevant financial year. The officer must issue the notice at least 3 months before this time limit. What is the penalty for non-payment of dues after receiving a demand notice under Section 73? If the dues are paid after 30 days of issuance of the order under Section 73, a penalty of 10% of the tax dues or INR 10,000, whichever is higher, is payable. When is a demand notice issued under Section 74 of the GST Act? A demand notice under Section 74 of the GST Act is issued when there is short payment or non-payment of GST, or wrong availment or utilization of input tax credit, due to fraud, willful misstatement, or suppression of facts to evade tax. What is the time limit for issuing a demand notice under Section 74? The time limit for issuing a demand notice under Section 74 is 5 years from the due date of filing the annual GST return for the relevant financial year. The officer must issue the notice at least 6 months before this time limit. What is the penalty for non-payment of dues after receiving a demand notice under Section 74? If the dues are paid within 30 days of issuance of the show cause notice under Section 74, a penalty of 25% of the tax amount due is payable. If the dues are paid after 30 days of issuance of the order, a penalty of 50% of the tax amount due is payable. Can the demand notice be stayed by a court or tribunal order? Yes, if the service of notice or issuance of order is stayed by an order of a Court or Appellate Tribunal, the period of stay will be excluded from computing the time limit for issuing the notice or adjudicating the case. Can the taxpayer voluntarily pay taxes before receiving a demand notice? Yes, an assessee can voluntarily pay taxes along with interest before the issue of a notice or statement, and inform the departmental officer in writing. If the officer is satisfied, no notice will be issued in that respect. What is the maximum number of adjournments allowed during the hearing process? The officer can adjourn the hearing for reasons to be recorded in writing, but the maximum number of adjournments allowed is 3 times. ### Popular Searches [Company blogs.title: How to Download GST Notices?

content_sections.heading: How to Download GST Notices?
content_sections.content:
Receiving a [GST notice](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-notice) is a common occurrence for business owners, but many find it challenging to understand the nuances of handling these notices. GST notices are issued by the Goods and Services Tax (GST) department to notify taxpayers about discrepancies, non-compliance, or routine audits. It is crucial to take timely action when you receive a notice to avoid penalties or other legal complications.

One of the first steps in managing your GST notices is understanding how to access them. In this article, we will walk you through a detailed process on how to download GST notices and demand orders issued by the tax officer from the official GST portal.

content_sections.heading: What is a GST Notice?
content_sections.content:
A GST notice is an official communication from the GST department to inform the taxpayer of various discrepancies in their filings or non-compliance with GST rules. These notices can be issued for various reasons, such as:

- [Non-filing of GST returns](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/consequence-of-non-filing-late-filing-of-form-gstr-1-and-form-gstr-3b)
- Mismatched GST details
- Short payment of taxes or under-reporting
- Request for clarification on discrepancies in GST returns
- GST audits or investigations

The GST notices typically request the taxpayer to provide additional information, make corrections, pay any overdue taxes, or attend an audit or investigation.

content_sections.heading: Types of GST Notices
content_sections.content:
Before diving into the process of downloading GST notices, it is essential to understand the different types of notices you may receive from the GST department:

- Notice for Non-Filing of Returns: This notice is issued when a taxpayer fails to file their GST returns within the specified due dates.
- Notice for Mismatch in GST Returns: A notice is issued when there is a mismatch between the GSTR-1 (sales return) and GSTR-3B (monthly returns) filed by the taxpayer. The department compares the returns and issues a notice in case of discrepancies.
- Notice for Short Payment of Taxes: If the GST department detects any underpayment or short payment of taxes, they will issue a notice requiring the taxpayer to pay the outstanding amount along with interest or penalties.
- Show Cause Notice (SCN): If the tax department finds serious issues or irregularities in your GST filings, they may issue a show cause notice requiring you to explain the discrepancies.
- Audit or Investigation Notice: This is issued when the tax department decides to audit your GST records or investigate your financial transactions to check for any potential violations or discrepancies.
- Demand Notice: A demand notice is issued when the GST authorities request the taxpayer to pay the due taxes, penalties, or interest.

content_sections.heading: Why Do You Need to Download GST Notices?
content_sections.content:
GST notices typically include detailed information about the discrepancies found in your tax filings or issues that need attention. Downloading the notice is crucial because:

- To understand the issue: The notice will provide a detailed explanation of the discrepancies, along with the required actions.
- To respond promptly: In case the notice requires you to submit additional information or pay overdue taxes, you must act quickly to avoid penalties or legal action.
- For record-keeping: A downloaded copy of the notice can serve as a reference for future audits or investigations.
- For transparency: The notice helps ensure transparency in your communication with the GST department, showing that you are taking steps to comply.

content_sections.heading: How to View or Download Notices and Demand Orders Issued by GST Tax Officer
content_sections.content: If you need to view or download notices and demand orders issued by a GST tax officer, follow these simple steps:

content_sections.heading: Step 1: Access the GST Portal
content_sections.content: Open your browser and visit the official GST portal. The GST home page will be displayed.

content_sections.heading: Step 2: Login to the GST Portal
content_sections.content:
- Click on the "Login" button in the top-right corner.
- Enter your valid credentials (i.e., GSTIN and Password).
- Click on "Login".

content_sections.heading: Step 3: Access the Notices and Orders Tab
content_sections.content:
Once you’ve logged in, there are two options to access your notices and orders:

Option 1: Navigate via the Services Tab

- From the top menu, click on "Services". Then, go to "User Services" and select "View Notices and Orders".

![Download GST Notices](https://img.indiafilings.com/guides/How-to-Download-GST-Notices-1-1738921055.jpg)

Option 2: Directly From the Dashboard

- On your dashboard, you will see a button labeled "View Notices and Orders". Click on this button to access your notices and orders.

![Download GST Notices](https://img.indiafilings.com/guides/How-to-Download-GST-Notices-2-1738921080.jpg)

content_sections.heading: Step 4: View Notices and Orders
content_sections.content:
After clicking on "View Notices and Orders", all notices and demand orders issued to you in the last year will be displayed on the screen in chronological order (Descending). By default, you will see the "Notices and Orders" tab. If you wish to see older notices or additional types of orders, you can select the "Additional Notices/Orders" tab.

![Download GST Notices](https://img.indiafilings.com/guides/How-to-Download-GST-Notices-3.jpg)

content_sections.heading: Step 5: Download the Notice/Order
content_sections.content:
- Click on the "Download" option next to the notice or order you want to access. The document will be downloaded in PDF format, which you can save or print for your records.
- By following these steps, you will be able to easily view and download any GST-related notices or demand orders issued by the tax officer.

content_sections.heading: How to View Additional Orders/Notices Issued by the Tax Officer
content_sections.content: To view additional orders or notices issued by the GST tax officer, follow these steps:

content_sections.heading: Step 1: Access the GST Portal
content_sections.content: Open your browser and go to the official GST portal. The GST Home page will be displayed.

content_sections.heading: Step 2: Login to the GST Portal
content_sections.content: Click on the "Login" button in the top-right corner. Enter your GSTIN and Password. Click "Login" to proceed.

content_sections.heading: Step 3: Navigate to the Additional Notices/Orders Page
content_sections.content:
From the Dashboard, go to the top menu and click on "Services". Under the "Services" tab, select "User Services". Choose "View Additional Notices/Orders" from the available options.

![Download GST Notices](https://img.indiafilings.com/guides/How-to-Download-GST-Notices-4.jpg)

content_sections.heading: Step 4: View Additional Orders and Notices
content_sections.content:
- The Additional Notices and Orders page will be displayed, listing all the orders/notices issued by the tax officer.
- These notices and orders are shown in descending order, starting with the most recent.
- Use the navigation buttons provided at the bottom of the page to search for specific notices or orders.

content_sections.heading: Step 5: Access the Case Details
content_sections.content:
To view the details of a specific notice/order, click on the "View" hyperlink next to the relevant entry. This will open the Case Details page for that particular order/notice.

![Download GST Notices](https://img.indiafilings.com/guides/How-to-Download-GST-Notices-5.png)

content_sections.heading: Step 6: View and Download Case Details
content_sections.content:
On the Case Details page, you will see different tabs on the left-hand side. Click on the relevant tab to view and download specific details related to the notice/order.

By following these steps, you can easily view and download additional notices and orders issued by the GST tax officer, ensuring you stay informed about any updates or actions required from your side.

content_sections.heading: Common Reason for Receiving GST Notices
content_sections.content:
- Mismatched Data: One of the most common reasons for a GST notice is mismatched data between your GSTR-1 (Sales) and GSTR-3B (Monthly Returns). The GST department automatically checks for discrepancies between these forms and will issue a notice if discrepancies are found.
- Delayed Filing: If you fail to file your GST returns on time, the department will issue a notice for non-filing, and you will be required to file missing returns.
- Tax Short Payment: If you haven’t paid the correct amount of GST, the department may issue a demand notice requesting payment of the outstanding dues.

content_sections.heading: What to Do After Downloading a GST Notice?
content_sections.content: After downloading a GST notice from the GST portal, it's important to take the right steps to address the issue raised by the GST department. Ignoring the notice can lead to penalties, interest charges, or even legal action. Here’s a step-by-step guide on what you should do after downloading your GST notice:

content_sections.heading: Carefully Read and Understand the Notice
content_sections.content:
The first step is to thoroughly read the GST notice to understand the issue raised by the department. The notice will typically include:

- Nature of the discrepancy or issue (e.g., non-filing, underpayment, mismatch in returns)
- Notice reference number and date
- Details of the non-compliance or action required (e.g., filing missing returns, paying outstanding taxes, providing additional documentation)

Make sure to identify the specific concern addressed in the notice.

content_sections.heading: Identify the Reason Behind the Notice
content_sections.content:
Understand the reason for the GST notice by checking the details. Some common reasons for receiving a notice include:

- Non-filing of GST returns (e.g., [GSTR-3B](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/gstr1-and-gstr3b-due-date-extension), GSTR-1)
- Mismatch in GST returns (e.g., discrepancies between [GSTR-1](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/gstr-1-filing) and GSTR-3B)
- Short payment of GST taxes
- Request for additional clarification or documents in case of audits or investigations

Once you understand the cause, you can take the necessary steps to resolve it.

content_sections.heading: Review Your GST Returns and Records
content_sections.content:
- Cross-check your GST returns to verify the details and figures mentioned in the notice.
- Compare the GSTR-1 (sales return) and GSTR-3B (monthly summary return) to ensure there are no discrepancies.
- If there are any errors or omissions, rectify them in your records before responding.

content_sections.heading: Correct the Discrepancies
content_sections.content:
If the notice highlights discrepancies such as under-reporting, short payment, or missing returns, take immediate steps to correct them:

- File missing returns (GSTR-1, GSTR-3B, etc.)
- Pay any outstanding tax dues, along with applicable interest or penalties.
- Update your GST records to reflect accurate information.

content_sections.heading: Respond to the Notice
content_sections.content:
If the notice requires you to provide further information, clarification, or documents, prepare a response that includes:

- Explanation of the issue (if it was due to an error or technical problem)
- Details of the corrective actions taken (e.g., payment of taxes, filing of returns)
- Supporting documents (e.g., payment receipts, invoices, bank statements, etc.)

Ensure your reply is clear, concise, and compliant with the instructions mentioned in the notice.

content_sections.heading: Submit Your Response on the GST Portal
content_sections.content:
Once you’ve prepared your response, you need to submit it to the GST department. You can do this through:

- The GST portal: Navigate to the "View Notices and Orders" section, select the notice, and click "Reply" to submit your response.
- Physical submission: In certain cases, the department may require you to submit documents or responses in person or by mail.

content_sections.heading: Monitor for Further Communication
content_sections.content: After submitting your response, regularly check the GST portal for updates or additional communication from the department. If the issue is resolved, you will be notified. You will receive another notice requesting additional information if further clarification is required.

content_sections.heading: Seek Professional Help if Needed
content_sections.content:
If you're unsure about how to respond or if the issue is complex, it’s advisable to consult a GST expert or tax consultant. They can help you:

- Understand the notice in detail
- Prepare and submit an accurate response
- Ensure compliance with all applicable GST rules and regulations

content_sections.content: Downloading and reviewing your GST notices is a crucial step in staying compliant with the GST regulations. By following the simple steps outlined above, you can easily access and download any notices or demand orders issued by the GST department. Timely action on these notices is essential to avoid penalties, interest, or further legal actions.

content_sections.heading: FAQs: How to Download GST Notices?
1\. How do I download my GST notice from the GST portal?
content_sections.content: To download your GST notice, log in to the GST portal using your GSTIN and password. Then, navigate to Services > User Services > View Notices and Orders. From there, you can view and download your GST notices or demand orders.

content_sections.heading: 2\. What types of GST notices can I receive?
content_sections.content:
You can receive various types of GST notices, including:

- Notice for non-filing of returns
