# How to Download GST Notices?

Receiving a [GST notice](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-notice) is a common occurrence for business owners, but many find it challenging to understand the nuances of handling these notices. GST notices are issued by the Goods and Services Tax (GST) department to notify taxpayers about discrepancies, non-compliance, or routine audits. It is crucial to take timely action when you receive a notice to avoid penalties or other legal complications.

One of the first steps in managing your GST notices is understanding how to access them. In this article, we will walk you through a detailed process on how to download GST notices and demand orders issued by the tax officer from the official GST portal.

## What is a GST Notice?

A GST notice is an official communication from the GST department to inform the taxpayer of various discrepancies in their filings or non-compliance with GST rules. These notices can be issued for various reasons, such as:

- [Non-filing of GST returns](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/consequence-of-non-filing-late-filing-of-form-gstr-1-and-form-gstr-3b)
- Mismatched GST details
- Short payment of taxes or under-reporting
- Request for clarification on discrepancies in GST returns
- GST audits or investigations

The GST notices typically request the taxpayer to provide additional information, make corrections, pay any overdue taxes, or attend an audit or investigation.

## Types of GST Notices

Before diving into the process of downloading GST notices, it is essential to understand the different types of notices you may receive from the GST department:

- Notice for Non-Filing of Returns: This notice is issued when a taxpayer fails to file their GST returns within the specified due dates.
- Notice for Mismatch in GST Returns: A notice is issued when there is a mismatch between the GSTR-1 (sales return) and GSTR-3B (monthly returns) filed by the taxpayer. The department compares the returns and issues a notice in case of discrepancies.
- Notice for Short Payment of Taxes: If the GST department detects any underpayment or short payment of taxes, they will issue a notice requiring the taxpayer to pay the outstanding amount along with interest or penalties.
- Show Cause Notice (SCN): If the tax department finds serious issues or irregularities in your GST filings, they may issue a show cause notice requiring you to explain the discrepancies.
- Audit or Investigation Notice: This is issued when the tax department decides to audit your GST records or investigate your financial transactions to check for any potential violations or discrepancies.
- Demand Notice: A demand notice is issued when the GST authorities request the taxpayer to pay the due taxes, penalties, or interest.

## Why Do You Need to Download GST Notices?

GST notices typically include detailed information about the discrepancies found in your tax filings or issues that need attention. Downloading the notice is crucial because:

- To understand the issue: The notice will provide a detailed explanation of the discrepancies, along with the required actions.
- To respond promptly: In case the notice requires you to submit additional information or pay overdue taxes, you must act quickly to avoid penalties or legal action.
- For record-keeping: A downloaded copy of the notice can serve as a reference for future audits or investigations.
- For transparency: The notice helps ensure transparency in your communication with the GST department, showing that you are taking steps to comply.

## How to View or Download Notices and Demand Orders Issued by GST Tax Officer

If you need to view or download notices and demand orders issued by a GST tax officer, follow these simple steps:

### Step 1: Access the GST Portal

Open your browser and visit the official GST portal. The GST home page will be displayed.

### Step 2: Login to the GST Portal

- Click on the "Login" button in the top-right corner.
- Enter your valid credentials (i.e., GSTIN and Password).
- Click on "Login".

### Step 3: Access the Notices and Orders Tab

Once you’ve logged in, there are two options to access your notices and orders:

Option 1: Navigate via the Services Tab

- From the top menu, click on "Services". Then, go to "User Services" and select "View Notices and Orders".

![Download GST Notices](https://img.indiafilings.com/guides/How-to-Download-GST-Notices-1-1738921055.jpg)

Option 2: Directly From the Dashboard

- On your dashboard, you will see a button labeled "View Notices and Orders". Click on this button to access your notices and orders.

![Download GST Notices](https://img.indiafilings.com/guides/How-to-Download-GST-Notices-2-1738921080.jpg)

### Step 4: View Notices and Orders

After clicking on "View Notices and Orders", all notices and demand orders issued to you in the last year will be displayed on the screen in chronological order (Descending). By default, you will see the "Notices and Orders" tab. If you wish to see older notices or additional types of orders, you can select the "Additional Notices/Orders" tab.

![Download GST Notices](https://img.indiafilings.com/guides/How-to-Download-GST-Notices-3.jpg)

### Step 5: Download the Notice/Order

- Click on the "Download" option next to the notice or order you want to access. The document will be downloaded in PDF format, which you can save or print for your records.
- By following these steps, you will be able to easily view and download any GST-related notices or demand orders issued by the tax officer.

## How to View Additional Orders/Notices Issued by the Tax Officer

To view additional orders or notices issued by the GST tax officer, follow these steps:

### Step 1: Access the GST Portal

Open your browser and go to the official GST portal. The GST Home page will be displayed.

### Step 2: Login to the GST Portal

Click on the "Login" button in the top-right corner. Enter your GSTIN and Password. Click "Login" to proceed.

### Step 3: Navigate to the Additional Notices/Orders Page

From the Dashboard, go to the top menu and click on "Services". Under the "Services" tab, select "User Services". Choose "View Additional Notices/Orders" from the available options.

![Download GST Notices](https://img.indiafilings.com/guides/How-to-Download-GST-Notices-4.jpg)

### Step 4: View Additional Orders and Notices

- The Additional Notices and Orders page will be displayed, listing all the orders/notices issued by the tax officer.
- These notices and orders are shown in descending order, starting with the most recent.
- Use the navigation buttons provided at the bottom of the page to search for specific notices or orders.

### Step 5: Access the Case Details

To view the details of a specific notice/order, click on the "View" hyperlink next to the relevant entry. This will open the Case Details page for that particular order/notice.

![Download GST Notices](https://img.indiafilings.com/guides/How-to-Download-GST-Notices-5.png)

### Step 6: View and Download Case Details

On the Case Details page, you will see different tabs on the left-hand side. Click on the relevant tab to view and download specific details related to the notice/order.

By following these steps, you can easily view and download additional notices and orders issued by the GST tax officer, ensuring you stay informed about any updates or actions required from your side.

## Common Reason for Receiving GST Notices

- Mismatched Data: One of the most common reasons for a GST notice is mismatched data between your GSTR-1 (Sales) and GSTR-3B (Monthly Returns). The GST department automatically checks for discrepancies between these forms and will issue a notice if discrepancies are found.
- Delayed Filing: If you fail to file your GST returns on time, the department will issue a notice for non-filing, and you will be required to file missing returns.
- Tax Short Payment: If you haven’t paid the correct amount of GST, the department may issue a demand notice requesting payment of the outstanding dues.

## What to Do After Downloading a GST Notice?

After downloading a GST notice from the GST portal, it's important to take the right steps to address the issue raised by the GST department. Ignoring the notice can lead to penalties, interest charges, or even legal action. Here’s a step-by-step guide on what you should do after downloading your GST notice:

### Carefully Read and Understand the Notice

The first step is to thoroughly read the GST notice to understand the issue raised by the department. The notice will typically include:

- Nature of the discrepancy or issue (e.g., non-filing, underpayment, mismatch in returns)
- Notice reference number and date
- Details of the non-compliance or action required (e.g., filing missing returns, paying outstanding taxes, providing additional documentation)

Make sure to identify the specific concern addressed in the notice.

### Identify the Reason Behind the Notice

Understand the reason for the GST notice by checking the details. Some common reasons for receiving a notice include:

- Non-filing of GST returns (e.g., [GSTR-3B](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/gstr1-and-gstr3b-due-date-extension), GSTR-1)
- Mismatch in GST returns (e.g., discrepancies between [GSTR-1](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/gstr-1-filing) and GSTR-3B)
- Short payment of GST taxes
- Request for additional clarification or documents in case of audits or investigations

Once you understand the cause, you can take the necessary steps to resolve it.

### Review Your GST Returns and Records

- Cross-check your GST returns to verify the details and figures mentioned in the notice.
- Compare the GSTR-1 (sales return) and GSTR-3B (monthly summary return) to ensure there are no discrepancies.
- If there are any errors or omissions, rectify them in your records before responding.

### Correct the Discrepancies

If the notice highlights discrepancies such as under-reporting, short payment, or missing returns, take immediate steps to correct them:

- File missing returns (GSTR-1, GSTR-3B, etc.)
- Pay any outstanding tax dues, along with applicable interest or penalties.
- Update your GST records to reflect accurate information.

### Respond to the Notice

If the notice requires you to provide further information, clarification, or documents, prepare a response that includes:

- Explanation of the issue (if it was due to an error or technical problem)
- Details of the corrective actions taken (e.g., payment of taxes, filing of returns)
- Supporting documents (e.g., payment receipts, invoices, bank statements, etc.)

Ensure your reply is clear, concise, and compliant with the instructions mentioned in the notice.

### Submit Your Response on the GST Portal

Once you’ve prepared your response, you need to submit it to the GST department. You can do this through:

- The GST portal: Navigate to the "View Notices and Orders" section, select the notice, and click "Reply" to submit your response.
- Physical submission: In certain cases, the department may require you to submit documents or responses in person or by mail.

### Monitor for Further Communication

After submitting your response, regularly check the GST portal for updates or additional communication from the department. If the issue is resolved, you will be notified. You will receive another notice requesting additional information if further clarification is required.

## Seek Professional Help if Needed

If you're unsure about how to respond or if the issue is complex, it’s advisable to consult a GST expert or tax consultant. They can help you:

- Understand the notice in detail
- Prepare and submit an accurate response
- Ensure compliance with all applicable GST rules and regulations

## Conclusion

Downloading and reviewing your GST notices is a crucial step in staying compliant with the GST regulations. By following the simple steps outlined above, you can easily access and download any notices or demand orders issued by the GST department. Timely action on these notices is essential to avoid penalties, interest, or further legal actions.

### 1\. How do I download my GST notice from the GST portal?

To download your GST notice, log in to the GST portal using your GSTIN and password. Then, navigate to Services > User Services > View Notices and Orders. From there, you can view and download your GST notices or demand orders.

### 2\. What types of GST notices can I receive?

You can receive various types of GST notices, including:

- Notice for non-filing of returns
- Notice for mismatch in GST returns (GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B)
- Notice for short payment of taxes
- Show cause notices (SCN)
- Audit or investigation notices

After downloading a GST notice, read it carefully to understand the issue. Verify the details in your GST returns, correct any discrepancies, and respond with the required documents or payment. Submit your response through the GST portal or in person if needed.

### 4\. Can I view additional GST notices or orders on the GST portal?

Yes, to view additional GST notices or orders, log in to the GST portal and go to Services > User Services > View Additional Notices/Orders. This will display all additional notices/orders issued to you, where you can view and download the details.

### 5\. What happens if I ignore a GST notice?

Ignoring a GST notice can lead to penalties, interest, or even legal action. It's important to respond promptly to resolve the issue and avoid complications like audits, further penalties, or suspension of GST registration.

blogs.title: GSTR-1 Filing: Meaning, Eligibility, Due Dates, & Penalty

content_sections.heading: GSTR-1 Filing: Meaning, Eligibility, Due Dates, & Penalty
content_sections.content:
GSTR-1 means a monthly or quarterly sales return filed by every GST-registered taxpayer to report details of all outward supplies of goods and services during a particular tax period. The GSTR-1 return contains details of sales invoices, debit and credit notes, and other outward supply details. Taxpayers must ensure a valid GSTIN is filled in while entering sales invoice details. It can be filed through the GST portal by entering all the details in the 13 sections of the GSTR-1 form. Registered dealers’ annual aggregate turnover limit determines whether they are eligible for monthly or quarterly returns. In this article, you will learn about GSTR-1, its meaning, eligibility, due dates, tax period, sales invoice details, and penalties for late filing.

_**IndiaFilings experts streamline your GSTR-1 return filing with expert guidance!!**_

[File Now!](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-return-filing)

content_sections.heading: What is GSTR-1?
content_sections.content: GSTR-1 stands for Goods and Services Tax Return 1. It's a monthly (or quarterly for eligible taxpayers) filing mandated by the Indian government for businesses registered under the Goods and Services Tax (GST) system. In simpler terms, it's a report submitted to the GST authorities that details all the outward supplies of goods and services you made during a specific tax period. This includes sales to registered businesses, unregistered customers, and any credit or debit notes issued. By filing GSTR-1, you provide the government with a record of your taxable transactions, which helps them track and collect GST efficiently.

content_sections.heading: GSTR-1 Due Date
content_sections.content:
The due date for filing GSTR-1 depends on the taxpayer's annual aggregate turnover and whether they have opted for the QRMP (Quarterly Return Monthly Payment) scheme.

- Monthly Filing: Taxpayers with an annual aggregate turnover exceeding ₹5 crore, or those who have not opted for the QRMP scheme, must file GSTR-1 on a monthly basis. The due date for monthly filing is the 11th of the following month.
- Quarterly Filing: Taxpayers with an annual aggregate turnover of up to ₹5 crore and who have opted for the QRMP scheme can file GSTR-1 quarterly. For quarterly filers, the due date is the 13th of the month following the relevant quarter.

Below, we provided the table capturing the GSTR-1 Filing Due Dates at a Glance:

|     |     |     |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Category | Annual Aggregate Turnover | Due Date |
| Monthly Filers | More than ₹5 crore (or not opted for QRMP) | 11th of the following month |
| Quarterly Filers (QRMP scheme) | Up to ₹5 crore | 13th of the month following the relevant quarter |

Note: Double-check and ensure the filled details are correct. The GST framework doesn't allow the revision of filed GSTR-1 returns. However, mistakes can be rectified in the GSTR-1 for the following filing period (month or quarter). For instance, if you find a mistake in your July 2024 GSTR-1, you can rectify it in the August 2024 GSTR-1 or any subsequent month's filing.

content_sections.heading: Who can file GSTR 1?
content_sections.content:
Every registered dealer is liable to file GSTR 1 regardless of sales and turnover for a particular month, which means that even when there is no sale or transaction (

[Nil GSTR-1](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/file-nil-gstr1-return)), a registered dealer has to file GSTR 1.

Here is the list of people who are exempt from filing the GSTR 1:
**[An Input Service Distributor](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/input-service-distributor-registration):** If your business receives invoices for services used by your branches, then you are in the category of the Input Service Distributor under GST.
[Composition Scheme Dealer](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/gst-filing-payment-composition-scheme-dealers): If you have registered under the Composition scheme, you are a composition scheme dealer and are not required to file this GST return.
A supplier of online Information, database access, or retrieval services.
**Non-resident taxable person:** If you import goods and services from outside India or manage the business on behalf of a Non-Resident Indian.
A Taxpayer who is liable for collecting Tax at Source or a taxpayer for deducting Tax at sources ( [TDS](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/tds-tax-deducted-at-source-all-you-need-to-know)).

content_sections.heading: Requirements for GSTR-1 filing
content_sections.content:
It is necessary to have the documents that are mentioned below and the information that is ready with you:

- A valid Goods and Service Tax Identification Number
- The User ID and Password to sign in to the portal.
- A valid Digital Signature Certificate and Password to sign the form
- Aadhar Number if you are going to e-sign the form.
- Access to the Mobile Number mentioned on the Aadhar Card.

content_sections.heading: Details to be Reported in the GSTR-1 Filing
content_sections.content:
In the table below, we list down all 13 sections of the return along with the information to be submitted respectively,

|     |     |
| --- | --- |
| Table No. | Details to be Reported |
| 1, 2 & 3 | GSTIN, legal name, trade name, and aggregate turnover of the previous financial year |
| 4 | Taxable outward supplies made to registered persons (including UIN holders), excluding zero-rated supplies and deemed exports |
| 5 | Taxable outward inter-state supplies made to unregistered persons where the invoice value exceeds ₹2.5 lakh |
| 6 | Zero-rated supplies and deemed exports |
| 7 | Taxable supplies made to unregistered persons (other than those reported in Table 5), net of debit and credit notes |
| 8 | Outward supplies that are nil-rated, exempt, or non-GST in nature |
| 9 | Amendments to outward taxable supplies reported in Tables 4, 5, and 6 of previous GSTR-1 returns (including debit notes, credit notes, and refund vouchers issued in the current period) |
| 10 | Debit notes and credit notes issued to unregistered persons |
| 11 | Details of advances received or adjusted in the current tax period and amendments of previously reported advances |
| 12 | Summary of outward supplies based on HSN codes |
| 13 | List of documents issued during the tax period |
| 14 | For suppliers — Reporting GSTIN-wise sales through e-commerce operators (ECO) on which the ECO is liable to collect TCS under section 52 or pay tax under section 9(5) of the CGST Act |
| 14A | For suppliers — Amendments to details reported in Table 14 |

content_sections.content: GSTR-1 is a monthly or quarterly return that contains details of all outward supplies (sales) made by a registered taxpayer during a specific tax period. It includes invoices, debit/credit notes, and other sales-related details.

content_sections.heading: 2\. What is the turnover limit for GSTR-1?
content_sections.content: Taxpayers with an annual turnover of up to ₹5 crore in the preceding financial year can opt for quarterly filing. Taxpayers exceeding this limit must file GSTR-1 monthly.

content_sections.heading: 3\. Who cannot file GSTR-1?
content_sections.content:
The following taxpayers are exempt from filing GSTR-1:

- Composition scheme taxpayers
- Input Service Distributors
- Non-resident taxable persons
- Tax deductors (TDS) and collectors (TCS)
- Online information database access and retrieval (OIDAR) service providers.

content_sections.heading: 4\. Is GSTR-1 sales or purchase?
content_sections.content: GSTR-1 pertains to sales and outward supplies made by the taxpayer during the tax period.

content_sections.heading: 5\. How do I file GSTR-1 in Excel?
content_sections.content: You can use the GST Offline Tool to prepare GSTR-1 in Excel format and upload it to the GST portal. The tool allows you to enter invoice details offline and generate a JSON file for submission.

content_sections.heading: 6\. What is the due date for filing GSTR-1?
content_sections.content:
The due date is:

- 11th of the succeeding month for monthly filers.
- 13th of the month following the quarter for quarterly filers.

content_sections.heading: 7\. Is HSN compulsory in GSTR-1?
content_sections.content: Yes, HSN (Harmonized System of Nomenclature) codes are mandatory for reporting outward supplies. From January 2025, taxpayers must select HSN codes from a dropdown menu on the GST portal.

content_sections.heading: 8\. Is GSTR-1 monthly or quarterly?
content_sections.content: GSTR-1 can be filed either monthly or quarterly, depending on the taxpayer's turnover and preference.

content_sections.heading: 9\. What happens if GSTR-1 is filed late?
content_sections.content: A late fee of ₹50 per day (₹25 each for CGST and SGST) is applicable, capped at ₹10,000 per return. For nil returns, the late fee is ₹20 per day (₹10 each for CGST and SGST).

content_sections.heading: 10\. How to calculate GSTR-1?
content_sections.content:
GSTR-1 includes:

- Invoice-level details of B2B supplies
- Summary of B2C supplies
- Export details
- Debit/credit notes
- Adjustments for advances received

Ensure accurate data entry from invoices and other documents to calculate total taxable value and tax liability.

content_sections.heading: 11\. How to fill GSTR-1 step by step?
content_sections.content:
Steps to file GSTR-1:

- Log in to the GST portal.
- Navigate to "Returns Dashboard" and select the tax period.
- Enter invoice-wise details of outward supplies.
- Validate data and click "Submit."
- File using DSC or EVC after confirming details.

content_sections.heading: 12\. What is the maximum late fee for GSTR-1?
content_sections.content: The maximum late fee is ₹10,000 per return (₹5,000 each for CGST and SGST).

content_sections.heading: 13\. Can GSTR-1 be filed monthly or quarterly?
content_sections.content: Yes, taxpayers can choose between monthly or quarterly filing based on their turnover and preference.

content_sections.heading: 14\. Who will file GSTR-1?
content_sections.content: All registered taxpayers making outward supplies are required to file GSTR-1, except those exempted (e.g., composition taxpayers).

content_sections.heading: 15\. What is the rule for GSTR-1?
content_sections.content: GSTR-1 must include all details of outward supplies made during a tax period, even if there are no transactions (nil return). It must be filed by the due date based on filing frequency.

content_sections.heading: 16\. Is it compulsory to file GSTR-1?
content_sections.content: Yes, filing GSTR-1 is mandatory for all eligible taxpayers, even if there are no sales during the tax period (nil return).

content_sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
content_sections.content:
Common questions aboutGSTR-1 Filing.

What is GSTR-1?

GSTR-1 is a monthly or quarterly return that registered taxpayers under the Goods and Services Tax (GST) system must file. It contains details of all outward supplies of goods and services, including sales to registered and unregistered customers, debit notes, and credit notes issued during a specific tax period.

Who is eligible to file GSTR-1?

Every GST-registered taxpayer is required to file GSTR-1, except for certain categories like composition scheme dealers, Input Service Distributors, non-resident taxable persons, tax deductors/collectors, and suppliers of online information and database access or retrieval services.

What is the due date for filing GSTR-1?

The due date for filing GSTR-1 depends on the taxpayer's annual aggregate turnover and whether they have opted for the QRMP (Quarterly Return Monthly Payment) scheme. For monthly filers, the due date is the 11th of the following month, while for quarterly filers, it is the 13th of the month after the relevant quarter.

What details are required to be reported in GSTR-1?

GSTR-1 requires taxpayers to report various details, including GSTIN, legal name, trade name, aggregate turnover of the previous financial year, outward supplies made to registered and unregistered persons, zero-rated supplies, deemed exports, amendments to previous returns, and HSN-wise summary of outward supplies.

What is the penalty for late filing of GSTR-1?

The late fee for GSTR-1 filing depends on the taxpayer's annual turnover and whether it is a regular or nil return. For regular returns, the late fee is Rs. 50 per day, subject to a maximum cap based on the turnover slab. For nil returns, the late fee is Rs. 20 per day, capped at Rs. 500.

Can GSTR-1 be revised after filing?

No, GSTR-1 cannot be revised once filed. However, any mistakes or omissions can be rectified in the GSTR-1 for the subsequent filing period (month or quarter).

Is HSN code mandatory for GSTR-1 filing?

Yes, reporting outward supplies using the Harmonized System of Nomenclature (HSN) codes is mandatory in GSTR-1. From January 2025, taxpayers will be required to select HSN codes from a dropdown menu on the GST portal.

Can GSTR-1 be filed offline?

Yes, taxpayers can use the GST Offline Tool to prepare GSTR-1 in Excel format offline and then upload the JSON file to the GST portal for submission.

What is the significance of GSTR-1?

GSTR-1 is crucial as it provides the government with a record of a taxpayer's taxable transactions, enabling efficient tracking and collection of GST. It also serves as the basis for matching input tax credit claims made by recipients in their GSTR-2A.

Can a third-party service provider assist with GSTR-1 filing?

Yes, taxpayers can seek assistance from third-party service providers like IndiaFilings to streamline their GSTR-1 filing process and ensure compliance with GST regulations.

# GSTR-1 Filing: Meaning, Eligibility, Due Dates, & Penalty

GSTR-1 means a monthly or quarterly sales return filed by every GST-registered taxpayer to report details of all outward supplies of goods and services during a particular tax period. The GSTR-1 return contains details of sales invoices, debit and credit notes, and other outward supply details. Taxpayers must ensure a valid GSTIN is filled in while entering sales invoice details. It can be filed through the GST portal by entering all the details in the 13 sections of the GSTR-1 form. Registered dealers’ annual aggregate turnover limit determines whether they are eligible for monthly or quarterly returns. In this article, you will learn about GSTR-1, its meaning, eligibility, due dates, tax period, sales invoice details, and penalties for late filing.

_**IndiaFilings experts streamline your GSTR-1 return filing with expert guidance!!**_

[File Now!](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-return-filing)

## What is GSTR-1?

GSTR-1 stands for Goods and Services Tax Return 1. It's a monthly (or quarterly for eligible taxpayers) filing mandated by the Indian government for businesses registered under the Goods and Services Tax (GST) system. In simpler terms, it's a report submitted to the GST authorities that details all the outward supplies of goods and services you made during a specific tax period. This includes sales to registered businesses, unregistered customers, and any credit or debit notes issued. By filing GSTR-1, you provide the government with a record of your taxable transactions, which helps them track and collect GST efficiently.

## GSTR-1 Due Date

The due date for filing GSTR-1 depends on the taxpayer's annual aggregate turnover and whether they have opted for the QRMP (Quarterly Return Monthly Payment) scheme.

- Monthly Filing: Taxpayers with an annual aggregate turnover exceeding ₹5 crore, or those who have not opted for the QRMP scheme, must file GSTR-1 on a monthly basis. The due date for monthly filing is the 11th of the following month.
- Quarterly Filing: Taxpayers with an annual aggregate turnover of up to ₹5 crore and who have opted for the QRMP scheme can file GSTR-1 quarterly. For quarterly filers, the due date is the 13th of the month following the relevant quarter.

Below, we provided the table capturing the GSTR-1 Filing Due Dates at a Glance:

|     |     |     |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Category | Annual Aggregate Turnover | Due Date |
| Monthly Filers | More than ₹5 crore (or not opted for QRMP) | 11th of the following month |
| Quarterly Filers (QRMP scheme) | Up to ₹5 crore | 13th of the month following the relevant quarter |

Note: Double-check and ensure the filled details are correct. The GST framework doesn't allow the revision of filed GSTR-1 returns. However, mistakes can be rectified in the GSTR-1 for the following filing period (month or quarter). For instance, if you find a mistake in your July 2024 GSTR-1, you can rectify it in the August 2024 GSTR-1 or any subsequent month's filing.

## Who can file GSTR 1?

Every registered dealer is liable to file GSTR 1 regardless of sales and turnover for a particular month, which means that even when there is no sale or transaction (

[Nil GSTR-1](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/file-nil-gstr1-return)), a registered dealer has to file GSTR 1.

Here is the list of people who are exempt from filing the GSTR 1:
**[An Input Service Distributor](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/input-service-distributor-registration):** If your business receives invoices for services used by your branches, then you are in the category of the Input Service Distributor under GST.
[Composition Scheme Dealer](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/gst-filing-payment-composition-scheme-dealers): If you have registered under the Composition scheme, you are a composition scheme dealer and are not required to file this GST return.
A supplier of online Information, database access, or retrieval services.
**Non-resident taxable person:** If you import goods and services from outside India or manage the business on behalf of a Non-Resident Indian.
A Taxpayer who is liable for collecting Tax at Source or a taxpayer for deducting Tax at sources ( [TDS](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/tds-tax-deducted-at-source-all-you-need-to-know)).

## Requirements for GSTR-1 filing

It is necessary to have the documents that are mentioned below and the information that is ready with you:

- A valid Goods and Service Tax Identification Number
- The User ID and Password to sign in to the portal.
- A valid Digital Signature Certificate and Password to sign the form
- Aadhar Number if you are going to e-sign the form.
- Access to the Mobile Number mentioned on the Aadhar Card.

In the table below, we list down all 13 sections of the return along with the information to be submitted respectively,

| 1, 2 & 3 | GSTIN, legal name, trade name, and aggregate turnover of the previous financial year |

| 5 | Taxable outward inter-state supplies made to unregistered persons where the invoice value exceeds ₹2.5 lakh |

| 10 | Debit notes and credit notes issued to unregistered persons |
| 11 | Details of advances received or adjusted in the current tax period and amendments of previously reported advances |
| 12 | Summary of outward supplies based on HSN codes |
| 13 | List of documents issued during the tax period |
| 14 | For suppliers — Reporting GSTIN-wise sales through e-commerce operators (ECO) on which the ECO is liable to collect TCS under section 52 or pay tax under section 9(5) of the CGST Act |
| 14A | For suppliers — Amendments to details reported in Table 14 |

| 15A I | Amendments to Table 15 for B2B sales (sales to GST-registered persons) |

## FAQs on GSTR-1 Filing

### 1\. What is GSTR-1 filing?

GSTR-1 is a monthly or quarterly return that contains details of all outward supplies (sales) made by a registered taxpayer during a specific tax period. It includes invoices, debit/credit notes, and other sales-related details.

### 2\. What is the turnover limit for GSTR-1?

Taxpayers with an annual turnover of up to ₹5 crore in the preceding financial year can opt for quarterly filing. Taxpayers exceeding this limit must file GSTR-1 monthly.

### 3\. Who cannot file GSTR-1?

The following taxpayers are exempt from filing GSTR-1:

- Composition scheme taxpayers
- Input Service Distributors
- Non-resident taxable persons
- Tax deductors (TDS) and collectors (TCS)
- Online information database access and retrieval (OIDAR) service providers.

### 4\. Is GSTR-1 sales or purchase?

GSTR-1 pertains to sales and outward supplies made by the taxpayer during the tax period.

### 5\. How do I file GSTR-1 in Excel?

You can use the GST Offline Tool to prepare GSTR-1 in Excel format and upload it to the GST portal. The tool allows you to enter invoice details offline and generate a JSON file for submission.

### 6\. What is the due date for filing GSTR-1?

The due date is:

- 11th of the succeeding month for monthly filers.
- 13th of the month following the quarter for quarterly filers.

### 7\. Is HSN compulsory in GSTR-1?

Yes, HSN (Harmonized System of Nomenclature) codes are mandatory for reporting outward supplies. From January 2025, taxpayers must select HSN codes from a dropdown menu on the GST portal.

### 8\. Is GSTR-1 monthly or quarterly?

GSTR-1 can be filed either monthly or quarterly, depending on the taxpayer's turnover and preference.

### 9\. What happens if GSTR-1 is filed late?

A late fee of ₹50 per day (₹25 each for CGST and SGST) is applicable, capped at ₹10,000 per return. For nil returns, the late fee is ₹20 per day (₹10 each for CGST and SGST).

GSTR-1 includes:

- Invoice-level details of B2B supplies
- Summary of B2C supplies
- Export details
- Debit/credit notes
- Adjustments for advances received

Ensure accurate data entry from invoices and other documents to calculate total taxable value and tax liability.

### 11\. How to fill GSTR-1 step by step?

Steps to file GSTR-1:

- Log in to the GST portal.
- Navigate to "Returns Dashboard" and select the tax period.
- Enter invoice-wise details of outward supplies.
- Validate data and click "Submit."
- File using DSC or EVC after confirming details.

### 12\. What is the maximum late fee for GSTR-1?

The maximum late fee is ₹10,000 per return (₹5,000 each for CGST and SGST).

### 13\. Can GSTR-1 be filed monthly or quarterly?

Yes, taxpayers can choose between monthly or quarterly filing based on their turnover and preference.

### 14\. Who will file GSTR-1?

All registered taxpayers making outward supplies are required to file GSTR-1, except those exempted (e.g., composition taxpayers).

### 15\. What is the rule for GSTR-1?

GSTR-1 must include all details of outward supplies made during a tax period, even if there are no transactions (nil return). It must be filed by the due date based on filing frequency.

### 16\. Is it compulsory to file GSTR-1?

Yes, filing GSTR-1 is mandatory for all eligible taxpayers, even if there are no sales during the tax period (nil return).

Failure to file may result in penalties, late fees, and restricted ability to file subsequent GST returns like GSTR-3B.

Who is eligible to file GSTR-1?

Every GST-registered taxpayer is required to file GSTR-1, except for certain categories like composition scheme dealers, Input Service Distributors, non-resident taxable persons, tax deductors/collectors, and suppliers of online information and database access or retrieval services.

What is the due date for filing GSTR-1?

The due date for filing GSTR-1 depends on the taxpayer's annual aggregate turnover and whether they have opted for the QRMP (Quarterly Return Monthly Payment) scheme. What details are required to be reported in GSTR-1?

What is the penalty for late filing of GSTR-1?

The late fee for GSTR-1 filing depends on the taxpayer's annual turnover and whether it is a regular or nil return. For regular returns, the late fee is Rs. 50 per day, subject to a maximum cap based on the turnover slab. For nil returns, the late fee is Rs. 20 per day, capped at Rs. 500.

content_sections.heading: Foreign Non-Resident Taxpayer - GST Registration
content_sections.content: After the rollout of Goods and Services Tax (GST), the Government of India mandated GST registration for all foreign non-resident taxpayers supplying goods or services to residents in India. According to the GST Act, a "non-resident taxable person” is anyone who occasionally undertakes transactions involving the supply of goods or services, but does not have a fixed place of business or residence in India. In this article, we explore the GST registration process for foreign non-resident taxpayers and the essential documents required for obtaining GST registration in India.

content_sections.heading: Foreign Non-Resident Taxpayer - GST Registration Procedure
content_sections.content: All foreign non-resident taxpayers must obtain GST registration at least 5 days prior to commencing business or undertaking supply to residents in India. The following procedure can help non-resident taxpayers secure GST registration in India:

content_sections.heading: Step 1: Appoint an Authorized Signatory
content_sections.content: The application for GST registration as a non-resident taxable person must be signed by an authorized signatory who is a resident of India with a valid PAN. Therefore, it's crucial for foreign non-resident taxpayers to appoint an authorized signatory in India for GST registration and compliance purposes.

content_sections.heading: Step 2: Provide Authorization to Authorized Signatory
content_sections.content: The promoters or officers of the foreign company must prepare and sign a GST Declaration, validating the appointment of an authorized signatory in India and their acceptance of responsibility for complying with GST regulations on behalf of the foreign company.

content_sections.heading: Step 3: Apply for GST Registration
content_sections.content:
After processing all required documents and completing all steps, the non-resident taxable person should submit the application for GST registration. Upon submission, the Portal provides a temporary reference number for remitting the [GST deposit fees](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-registration-for-foreigners/fees).

India Filings can provide assistance with [GST registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-registration) for foreign non-resident taxpayers under GST.

content_sections.heading: Step 4: Pay GST Deposit
content_sections.content: Non-resident taxable persons are required to remit a deposit for obtaining GST registration. The [GST deposit amount](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-registration-for-foreigners/pricing) depends on the validity period of the GST registration requested and the expected GST liability during that period. Depending on these factors, the GST deposit must be deposited into the notified banks. Once the deposit is remitted, the taxpayer's electronic cash ledger will be credited. This deposit can then be used against any GST payments.

content_sections.heading: Step 5: GST Registration Certificate Issued
content_sections.content:
Upon remittance of the GST deposit and submission of the necessary documents, a GST registration certificate is issued. This certificate for foreign non-resident taxpayers and casual taxable persons has a fixed validity period. If a foreign non-resident taxpayer needs to extend this validity, they must submit an application for extension before the registration expires. The applicant must also pay the required tax liability occurred during the extension period.

![Paying Deposit for GST Registration](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2017/06/Paying-Deposit-for-GST-Registration-1024x745.png)

content_sections.heading: Documents Required for GST Registration
content_sections.content:
The documents required for GST registration can be classified into five major categories as represented in the following infographic:

![Documents Required for GST Registration](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2017/06/Documents-Required-for-GST-Registration-1024x772.png)

content_sections.heading: PAN or Tax Identification Number of the Applicant
content_sections.content: All regular taxpayers with residency in India should obtain a Permanent Account Number (PAN). However, foreign non-resident taxpayers can apply for GST registration, whether incorporated or established outside India, using their tax identification number or a unique number identified by their government. Therefore, PAN is not mandatory for foreign non-resident taxpayers.

content_sections.heading: Proof of Business Incorporation
content_sections.content: To validate the business, taxpayers need to provide proof of business incorporation or a certificate of incorporation from an appropriate authority of their foreign Government.

content_sections.heading: Identity & Address Proof of Promoters with Photographs
content_sections.content:
For GST registration, applicants must provide relevant identity and address proof of the business promoters. Foreign nationals must attach a scanned copy of their passport with VISA details along with other documents. For the authorized signatory in India, they need to provide PAN along with an acceptable address proof like a passport, driving license, or voter identity card.

Find a comprehensive list of [documents required for GST registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-registration-for-foreigners/document-required) for non-resident taxpayers.

content_sections.heading: Proof of Address
content_sections.content:
The taxpayer is required to provide proof of the principal place of business. The following documents are acceptable based on the ownership scenario:

- **Own premises** – Any document supporting the ownership of the premises, like a Latest Property Tax Receipt, Municipal Khata copy, or Electricity Bill copy.
- **Rented or Leased premises** – A copy of a valid Rent/Lease Agreement along with a document supporting the ownership of the premises of the Lessor.
- **Other scenarios** – A Consent Letter along with a document supporting the ownership of the premises of the Consenter, applicable also for shared properties.

content_sections.heading: Bank Account Statement
content_sections.content: Applicants must upload a scanned copy of the first page of the bank passbook, a relevant page of the bank statement, or a cancelled cheque that includes the business or proprietor's name, Bank Account Number, MICR, IFSC, and Branch details.

content_sections.heading: Class 2 Digital Signature
content_sections.content:
A [class 2 digital signature](https://www.indiafilings.com/digital-signature) is mandatory for the authorized signatory in India to apply for GST registration.

![GST Registration - Digital Signature for Authorised Signatory](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2017/06/GST-Registration-Digital-Signature-for-Authorised-Signatory-1024x767.png)

content_sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
content_sections.content:
Common questions aboutForeign Non Resident Taxpayer GST Registration Process in India.

What is the procedure for a foreign non-resident taxpayer to obtain GST registration in India?

The procedure for a foreign non-resident taxpayer to obtain GST registration in India involves the following steps: (1) Appoint an authorized signatory who is a resident of India with a valid PAN. (2) Provide authorization to the authorized signatory from the foreign company's promoters or officers. (3) Apply for GST registration online. (4) Pay the required GST deposit based on the validity period and expected tax liability. (5) Upon submission of documents and payment, the GST registration certificate will be issued.

What documents are required for a foreign non-resident taxpayer to obtain GST registration in India?

The key documents required for a foreign non-resident taxpayer to obtain GST registration in India include: (1) PAN or tax identification number of the applicant. (2) Proof of business incorporation or certificate of incorporation from the foreign government. (3) Identity and address proof of promoters with photographs. (4) Proof of address of the principal place of business. (5) Bank account statement or canceled cheque. (6) Class 2 digital signature for the authorized signatory in India.

Is it mandatory for a foreign non-resident taxpayer to have a PAN for GST registration in India?

No, it is not mandatory for a foreign non-resident taxpayer to have a PAN for GST registration in India. Instead, they can provide their tax identification number or unique number as identified by the government of their country, or PAN if available.

How much time in advance should a foreign non-resident taxpayer apply for GST registration before commencing business in India?

A foreign non-resident taxpayer is required to obtain GST registration at least 5 days prior to the commencement of business or undertaking any supply to residents in India.

What is the purpose of paying a GST deposit for a foreign non-resident taxpayer during registration?

All non-resident taxable persons are required to remit a deposit for obtaining GST registration. The amount of GST deposit depends on the validity period of GST registration requested and the expected GST liability during that period. This deposit can then be used against any GST payments that the taxpayer needs to make.

How is the validity period of GST registration determined for a foreign non-resident taxpayer?

The GST registration certificate for foreign non-resident taxpayers and casual taxable persons has a fixed validity period. If the foreign non-resident taxpayer needs to extend the validity period, they must submit an application for extension prior to the expiry of the existing registration, along with the required amount of tax liability for the extension period.

Can a foreign non-resident taxpayer appoint any authorized signatory in India for GST registration?

No, the authorized signatory appointed by a foreign non-resident taxpayer for GST registration and compliance purposes must be a person resident in India having a valid PAN.

What is the role of the authorized signatory appointed by a foreign non-resident taxpayer in India?

The authorized signatory appointed by a foreign non-resident taxpayer in India is responsible for signing the application for GST registration and complying with GST regulations on behalf of the foreign company.

What is the significance of obtaining a Class 2 digital signature for the authorized signatory in India?

A Class 2 digital signature must be obtained for the authorized signatory in India to apply for GST registration on behalf of the foreign non-resident taxpayer. This digital signature is required for electronic filing and authentication purposes.

Can a foreign non-resident taxpayer use their existing GST registration for multiple business transactions in India?

The article does not provide specific information on whether a single GST registration can be used for multiple business transactions by a foreign non-resident taxpayer in India. However, it does mention that the GST registration certificate has a fixed validity period, and an extension may be required for continued operations beyond the initial validity period.

For GST registration, applicants must provide relevant identity and address proof of the business promoters. Foreign nationals must attach a scanned copy of their passport with VISA details along with other documents. For the authorized signatory in India, they need to provide PAN along with an acceptable address proof like a passport, driving license, or voter identity card.

Find a comprehensive list of [documents required for GST registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-registration-for-foreigners/document-required) for non-resident taxpayers.

### Proof of Address

The taxpayer is required to provide proof of the principal place of business. The following documents are acceptable based on the ownership scenario:

- **Own premises** – Any document supporting the ownership of the premises, like a Latest Property Tax Receipt, Municipal Khata copy, or Electricity Bill copy.
- **Rented or Leased premises** – A copy of a valid Rent/Lease Agreement along with a document supporting the ownership of the premises of the Lessor.
- **Other scenarios** – A Consent Letter along with a document supporting the ownership of the premises of the Consenter, applicable also for shared properties.

### Bank Account Statement

Applicants must upload a scanned copy of the first page of the bank passbook, a relevant page of the bank statement, or a cancelled cheque that includes the business or proprietor's name, Bank Account Number, MICR, IFSC, and Branch details.

### Class 2 Digital Signature

A [class 2 digital signature](https://www.indiafilings.com/digital-signature) is mandatory for the authorized signatory in India to apply for GST registration.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Common questions aboutForeign Non Resident Taxpayer GST Registration Process in India.

What is the procedure for a foreign non-resident taxpayer to obtain GST registration in India?

The procedure for a foreign non-resident taxpayer to obtain GST registration in India involves the following steps: (1) Appoint an authorized signatory who is a resident of India with a valid PAN. (2) Provide authorization to the authorized signatory from the foreign company's promoters or officers. (3) Apply for GST registration online. (4) Pay the required GST deposit based on the validity period and expected tax liability. (5) Upon submission of documents and payment, the GST registration certificate will be issued.

What documents are required for a foreign non-resident taxpayer to obtain GST registration in India?

The key documents required for a foreign non-resident taxpayer to obtain GST registration in India include: (1) PAN or tax identification number of the applicant. (2) Proof of business incorporation or certificate of incorporation from the foreign government. (3) Identity and address proof of promoters with photographs. (4) Proof of address of the principal place of business. (5) Bank account statement or canceled cheque. (6) Class 2 digital signature for the authorized signatory in India.

Is it mandatory for a foreign non-resident taxpayer to have a PAN for GST registration in India?

No, it is not mandatory for a foreign non-resident taxpayer to have a PAN for GST registration in India. Instead, they can provide their tax identification number or unique number as identified by the government of their country, or PAN if available.

How much time in advance should a foreign non-resident taxpayer apply for GST registration before commencing business in India?

A foreign non-resident taxpayer is required to obtain GST registration at least 5 days prior to the commencement of business or undertaking any supply to residents in India.

What is the purpose of paying a GST deposit for a foreign non-resident taxpayer during registration?

All non-resident taxable persons are required to remit a deposit for obtaining GST registration. The amount of GST deposit depends on the validity period of GST registration requested and the expected GST liability during that period. This deposit can then be used against any GST payments that the taxpayer needs to make.

How is the validity period of GST registration determined for a foreign non-resident taxpayer?

The GST registration certificate for foreign non-resident taxpayers and casual taxable persons has a fixed validity period. If the foreign non-resident taxpayer needs to extend the validity period, they must submit an application for extension prior to the expiry of the existing registration, along with the required amount of tax liability for the extension period.

Can a foreign non-resident taxpayer appoint any authorized signatory in India for GST registration?

No, the authorized signatory appointed by a foreign non-resident taxpayer for GST registration and compliance purposes must be a person resident in India having a valid PAN.

What is the role of the authorized signatory appointed by a foreign non-resident taxpayer in India?

The authorized signatory appointed by a foreign non-resident taxpayer in India is responsible for signing the application for GST registration and complying with GST regulations on behalf of the foreign company.

What is the significance of obtaining a Class 2 digital signature for the authorized signatory in India?

A Class 2 digital signature must be obtained for the authorized signatory in India to apply for GST registration on behalf of the foreign non-resident taxpayer. This digital signature is required for electronic filing and authentication purposes.

Can a foreign non-resident taxpayer use their existing GST registration for multiple business transactions in India?

The article does not provide specific information on whether a single GST registration can be used for multiple business transactions by a foreign non-resident taxpayer in India. However, it does mention that the GST registration certificate has a fixed validity period, and an extension may be required for continued operations beyond the initial validity period.

content_sections.heading: Documents Required for GST Registration
content_sections.content: The following documents must be provided by the non-resident taxable person during the GST registration process:

content_sections.content:
- A scanned copy of the passport of the non-resident taxable person with VISA details. content_sections.content:
Non-resident taxable persons are required to appoint an authorised representative in India. An authorization or copy of the Resolution of the Managing Committee or Board of Directors authorising the authorised representative must be provided in the following format:

content_sections.heading: GST Deposit for Non-Resident Taxable Persons (NRI)
content_sections.content:
Non-resident taxable persons and casual taxable persons under GST are required to remit a deposit for GST registration. The amount of deposit for GST registration would equal the expected tax liability during the validity of the registration. Further, in case a non-resident taxable person requests for extension of GST registration, then tax must be deposited in advance based on the expected tax liability of the extension period.

Once the non-resident taxable person files the application for GST registration, the portal generates a reference number for the application on the payment of advance tax. On payment of tax, the system credits to the electronic cash ledger of the taxpayer and then provides the GST registration certificate. The illustration below shows the process of obtaining GST registration for non-resident taxable persons.

![Paying Deposit for GST Registration](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2017/06/Paying-Deposit-for-GST-Registration-1024x745.png) Paying Deposit for GST Registration

content_sections.heading: Validity of GST Registration for Non-Resident Taxable Persons (NRI)
content_sections.content: GST registration for casual taxable persons and non-resident taxable persons is provided with a validity period. The validity period would be based on the request of the taxable person and the amount of the GST deposit remitted. If a non-resident taxable person intends to extend the validity period of GST registration, the individual shall make an application in FORM GST REG-11 before the end of the validity of the registration.

content_sections.heading: Important Instructions for Non-Resident Taxpayers (NRI)
content_sections.content:
- The name of the Applicant should reflect the passport.
- It is mandatory for the applicant to apply for GST registration on the common portal by filing form GST REG-09 at least 5 days before commencement of the business.
- The applicant should submit the Tax identification number or unique identification number (as identified by the respective Government) or PAN (if applicable) along with the application in case of a business entity incorporated or
established outside India.
- The applicant shall provide the application duly signed or verified by EVC

In the case of NRI, in order to obtain GST registration, a two-step procedure needs to be followed:

- Provisional registration
- Final registration

content_sections.heading: Provisional Registration
content_sections.content:
The Non-resident taxable person (NRI) shall submit an application in Form GST REG-09 through online. The applicant shall also submit a self-attached copy of a valid passport along with the application.

The applicant shall submit the application 5 days prior to the commencement of business. In the case of foreign entity, the concerned individual shall submit the application for GST registration along with tax identification number or unique number or PAN (if applicable). Such advance payment of tax would be based on self-estimation. Hence, the applicant should mandatorily make the advance tax deposit along with the application.

content_sections.heading: Final Registration
content_sections.content:
The final registration of a Non-resident taxable person (NRI) would be carried out in the same line as that of the resident taxpayer in India. The following details the procedure:

- The applicant shall submit the FORM GST REG-26 electronically. In addition, the concerned applicant shall submit all the information related to tax and GST within a period of 3 months from the provisional registration.
- The applicant shall receive the GST certificate in FORM GST REG-06 upon providing accurate and complete details. Upon any discrepancies or incomplete information, the authorized may cancel the application for registration through FORM GST REG-28.
- However, if the applicant provides an appropriate reply to the show cause notice issued and the officer accepts the said reply, the officer shall cancel the show cause notice by issuing an order in FORM GST REG-20.
- The authorized signatory of the applicant should duly sign the application for registration. The said authorized signatory should be a person resident in India and he would have a valid PAN.

content_sections.content:
Common questions aboutGST Registration for Non Resident Taxable Person in India.

What is a non-resident taxable person (NRI) under GST?

A non-resident taxable person (NRI) under GST is any individual, business, or not-for-profit entity that occasionally undertakes transactions involving the supply of goods or services or both in India but does not have a fixed place of business or residence in the country.

Is GST registration mandatory for non-resident taxable persons (NRIs)?

Yes, all non-resident taxable persons are required to obtain GST registration in India, irrespective of their aggregate annual turnover or any other criteria. They must obtain GST registration 5 days prior to the commencement of business.

What is the procedure for applying for GST registration as a non-resident taxable person (NRI)?

To apply for GST registration, a non-resident taxable person must submit an application in FORM GST REG-09. They should also identify a person in India as their authorized representative for GST compliance and provide the necessary documents, such as proof of identity and business establishment.

What documents are required for GST registration as a non-resident taxable person (NRI)?

The main documents required include proof of principal place of business, identity proof (passport with visa details), tax identification number or unique number from the foreign country, bank account proof, and authorization for an authorized representative in India.

Is a deposit required for GST registration as a non-resident taxable person (NRI)?

Yes, non-resident taxable persons and casual taxable persons under GST are required to remit a deposit for GST registration. The deposit amount is equal to the expected tax liability during the validity of the registration.

What is the validity period of GST registration for non-resident taxable persons (NRIs)?

The validity period of GST registration for non-resident taxable persons is based on the request of the taxable person and the amount of GST deposit remitted. They can apply for an extension of the validity period before it expires.

Can a non-resident taxable person (NRI) appoint an authorized representative in India?

Yes, non-resident taxable persons are required to appoint an authorized representative in India for GST compliance purposes. They must provide an authorization or copy of the resolution authorizing the representative during the registration process.

Is there a special procedure for non-resident taxable persons (NRIs) providing OIDAR services?

Yes, in the case of a non-resident taxable person supplying online information and database access or retrieval (OIDAR) services to a non-taxable online recipient, they must submit an application in FORM GST REG-10 electronically.

What is the process for obtaining final GST registration as a non-resident taxable person (NRI)?

After obtaining provisional registration, the non-resident taxable person must submit FORM GST REG-26 electronically, along with all necessary information related to tax and GST within 3 months. Upon providing accurate and complete details, they will receive the final GST registration certificate in FORM GST REG-06.

Who can be an authorized signatory for a non-resident taxable person (NRI) during GST registration?

The authorized signatory for a non-resident taxable person during GST registration should be a person resident in India with a valid PAN. They should duly sign the application for registration on behalf of the non-resident taxable person.

![Paying Deposit for GST Registration](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2017/06/Paying-Deposit-for-GST-Registration-1024x745.png) Paying Deposit for GST Registration

## Validity of GST Registration for Non-Resident Taxable Persons (NRI)

GST registration for casual taxable persons and non-resident taxable persons is provided with a validity period. The validity period would be based on the request of the taxable person and the amount of the GST deposit remitted. If a non-resident taxable person intends to extend the validity period of GST registration, the individual shall make an application in FORM GST REG-11 before the end of the validity of the registration.

## Important Instructions for Non-Resident Taxpayers (NRI)

- The name of the Applicant should reflect the passport.
- It is mandatory for the applicant to apply for GST registration on the common portal by filing form GST REG-09 at least 5 days before commencement of the business.
- The applicant should submit the Tax identification number or unique identification number (as identified by the respective Government) or PAN (if applicable) along with the application in case of a business entity incorporated or
established outside India.
- The applicant shall provide the application duly signed or verified by EVC

In the case of NRI, in order to obtain GST registration, a two-step procedure needs to be followed:

- Provisional registration
- Final registration

### Provisional Registration

The Non-resident taxable person (NRI) shall submit an application in Form GST REG-09 through online. The applicant shall also submit a self-attached copy of a valid passport along with the application.

The applicant shall submit the application 5 days prior to the commencement of business. In the case of foreign entity, the concerned individual shall submit the application for GST registration along with tax identification number or unique number or PAN (if applicable). Such advance payment of tax would be based on self-estimation. Hence, the applicant should mandatorily make the advance tax deposit along with the application.

### Final Registration

The final registration of a Non-resident taxable person (NRI) would be carried out in the same line as that of the resident taxpayer in India. The following details the procedure:

- The applicant shall submit the FORM GST REG-26 electronically. In addition, the concerned applicant shall submit all the information related to tax and GST within a period of 3 months from the provisional registration.
- The applicant shall receive the GST certificate in FORM GST REG-06 upon providing accurate and complete details. Upon any discrepancies or incomplete information, the authorized may cancel the application for registration through FORM GST REG-28.
- However, if the applicant provides an appropriate reply to the show cause notice issued and the officer accepts the said reply, the officer shall cancel the show cause notice by issuing an order in FORM GST REG-20.
- The authorized signatory of the applicant should duly sign the application for registration. The said authorized signatory should be a person resident in India and he would have a valid PAN.

[Back to Learn](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn)

## Frequently Asked Questions

Common questions aboutGST Registration for Non Resident Taxable Person in India.

What is a non-resident taxable person (NRI) under GST?

A non-resident taxable person (NRI) under GST is any individual, business, or not-for-profit entity that occasionally undertakes transactions involving the supply of goods or services or both in India but does not have a fixed place of business or residence in the country.

Is GST registration mandatory for non-resident taxable persons (NRIs)?

Yes, all non-resident taxable persons are required to obtain GST registration in India, irrespective of their aggregate annual turnover or any other criteria. They must obtain GST registration 5 days prior to the commencement of business.

What is the procedure for applying for GST registration as a non-resident taxable person (NRI)?

To apply for GST registration, a non-resident taxable person must submit an application in FORM GST REG-09. They should also identify a person in India as their authorized representative for GST compliance and provide the necessary documents, such as proof of identity and business establishment.

What documents are required for GST registration as a non-resident taxable person (NRI)?

The main documents required include proof of principal place of business, identity proof (passport with visa details), tax identification number or unique number from the foreign country, bank account proof, and authorization for an authorized representative in India.

Is a deposit required for GST registration as a non-resident taxable person (NRI)?

Yes, non-resident taxable persons and casual taxable persons under GST are required to remit a deposit for GST registration. The deposit amount is equal to the expected tax liability during the validity of the registration.

What is the validity period of GST registration for non-resident taxable persons (NRIs)?

The validity period of GST registration for non-resident taxable persons is based on the request of the taxable person and the amount of GST deposit remitted. They can apply for an extension of the validity period before it expires.

Can a non-resident taxable person (NRI) appoint an authorized representative in India?

Yes, non-resident taxable persons are required to appoint an authorized representative in India for GST compliance purposes. They must provide an authorization or copy of the resolution authorizing the representative during the registration process.

Is there a special procedure for non-resident taxable persons (NRIs) providing OIDAR services?

Yes, in the case of a non-resident taxable person supplying online information and database access or retrieval (OIDAR) services to a non-taxable online recipient, they must submit an application in FORM GST REG-10 electronically.

What is the process for obtaining final GST registration as a non-resident taxable person (NRI)?

After obtaining provisional registration, the non-resident taxable person must submit FORM GST REG-26 electronically, along with all necessary information related to tax and GST within 3 months. Upon providing accurate and complete details, they will receive the final GST registration certificate in FORM GST REG-06.

Who can be an authorized signatory for a non-resident taxable person (NRI) during GST registration?

The authorized signatory for a non-resident taxable person during GST registration should be a person resident in India with a valid PAN. They should duly sign the application for registration on behalf of the non-resident taxable person.
