content_sections.heading: AOC-4
content_sections.content:
The financial statements of a company must be filed with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs every year. The MCA form for filing financial statements is AOC-4. Hence, Form AOC-4 is submitted with the MCA for each Financial Year within 30 days of a company's annual general meeting. Along with AOC-4 form, the documents such as Board’s report, Auditors’ report, Statement of subsidiaries in Form AOC-1, details of CSR policy etc. are filed. This form must be certified by a practising

[Chartered Accountant](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/aoc-4) or Company Secretary. In this article, we look at the procedure for filing AOC-4 in detail.

content_sections.heading: Documents to Be Filed in AOC-4
content_sections.content:
Financial Statements of a company includes Balance Sheet, Profit and Loss Account, Cash Flow statement (if applicable), statement of change in equity (if applicable) and any explanatory notes annexed to the financial statements. Financial statements along with Board Report must be filed for all companies registered in India (

[Private Limited Company](https://www.indiafilings.com/company-registration), One Person Company, Limited Company, Section 8 Company, etc.,) to provide the Shareholders, Government, Stakeholders and the Public a broad financial picture of the affairs of the company during a financial year.

The following is the complete list of documents that must be filed with AOC-4:

01. Copy of financial statements duly authenticated as per section 134 (including Board’s report, auditors’ report and other documents)
02. Statement of subsidiaries as per section 129 – Form AOC-1
03. Statement of the fact and reasons for not adopting Financial statements in the annual general meeting (AGM)
04. Statement of the fact and reasons for not holding the AGM
05. Approval letter of extension of financial year or AGM
06. Supplementary or test audit report under section 143
07. Company CSR policy as per sub-section (4) of section 135
08. Details of other entity(s)
09. Details of salient features and justification for entering into contracts/Arrangements/transactions with related parties as per Sub-section (1) of section 188 - Form AOC-2
10. Details of comments of CAG of India
11. Secretarial Audit Report
12. Directors’ report as per sub-section (3) of section 134
13. Details of remaining CSR activities
14. Optional attachment(s), if any.

content_sections.heading: Filing of Form AOC-4
content_sections.content:
Financial Statements of a company are required to be filed with the Registrar along with Form AOC-4 every year for each Financial Year. All the attachments including financial statements uploaded with Form AOC-4 must be signed as per the requirement of the Companies Act 2013. SD copies are not acceptable in case of AOC-4, hand signed copies are only accepted.

In case of the companies covered under XBRL requirement under the Companies (Filing of documents & Forms in Extensible Business Reporting Language) Rules, 2015, the financial statements must be uploaded on MCA portal in XBRL format. The following class of companies are required file their financial statements and other documents in e-Form AOC-4 XBRL on or after 1st April 2014:

- All companies listed with any Stock Exchange(s) in India & their Indian subsidiaries
- All companies having paid up capital of rupees five crore or above
- All companies having turnover of rupees hundred crore or above
- All companies which were hitherto covered under the companies (Filing of Documents & Forms in Extensible Business Reporting Language) Rules, 2011

content_sections.heading: Due Date for Filing AOC-4
content_sections.content:
All companies registered in India are required under the Companies Act, 2013 to file a copy of financial statements, including all the documents which are required to be or attached, duly adopted at the annual general meeting of the company, within thirty days of conducting an Annual General Meeting. Since,

[One Person Company](https://www.indiafilings.com/one-person-company) does not have an Annual General Meeting, One Person Company must file a copy of the financial statements duly adopted by its member, within 180 of closure of the financial year.

If the annual general meeting of a company for any year has not been held, the financial statements along with the documents required to be attached, duly signed along with the statement of facts and reasons for not holding the annual general meeting should be filed with the Registrar within 30 days of the last date before which the annual general meeting should have been held.

content_sections.heading: Government Fee for Filing AOC-4
content_sections.content:
The Government fee for submitting Form AOC-4 on or before the due date is as follows:

|     |     |
| --- | --- |
| **Company's Nominal Share Capital** | **Government Fee** |
| Upto Rs.1 lakh | Rs.200 |
| Rs. 1 lakh to Rs. 5 lakhs | Rs.300 |
| Rs. 5 lakhs to Rs. 25 lakhs | Rs.400 |
| Rs. 25 lakhs to Rs. 1 crore | Rs.500 |
| Rs. 1 crore and more | Rs.600 |

For companies not having nominal share capital, the government fee for filing Form AOC-4 is Rs.200.

content_sections.heading: Penalty for Late Filing AOC-4
content_sections.content:
If a company fails to file  along this form with a copy of the financial statements before the due date, the company will be punishable with fine of one thousand rupees for every day during which the failure continues up to a maximum amount of Rs.10 lakhs. Further, the Managing Director, Directors and the Chief Financial Officer of the company, could be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months or with fine which will not be less than Rs.1 and upto Rs.5 lakhs.

In addition to the above penalty, the Government fee for filing AOC-4 would also be increased as follows:

|     |     |
| --- | --- |
| **Number of Days Delayed** | **Penalty Amount for Late Filing** |
| Up to 30 days | 2 times of normal filing fees |
| More than 30 days and up to 60 days | 4 times of normal filing fees |
| More than 60 days and up to 90 days | 6 times of normal filing fees |
| More than 90 days and up to 180 days | 10 times of normal filing fees |
| More than 180 days and up to 270 days | 12 times of normal filing fees |

content_sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
content_sections.content:
Common questions aboutAOC-4 Filing.

What is AOC-4?

AOC-4 is the form prescribed by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) for filing financial statements of a company every year. It must be submitted within 30 days of the company's Annual General Meeting (AGM) along with various other documents like the Board's report, Auditor's report, and details of the company's corporate social responsibility (CSR) policy.

What documents need to be filed along with AOC-4?

The documents that must be filed along with AOC-4 include the company's financial statements (Balance Sheet, Profit & Loss Account, Cash Flow Statement, etc.), Board's report, Auditor's report, Statement of subsidiaries in Form AOC-1, CSR policy details, related party transactions in Form AOC-2, and any other relevant documents as per the Companies Act, 2013.

Is it mandatory for all companies to file AOC-4?

Yes, filing AOC-4 along with the financial statements is mandatory for all companies registered in India, including Private Limited Companies, One Person Companies, Limited Companies, and Section 8 Companies.

What is the due date for filing AOC-4?

The due date for filing AOC-4 is within 30 days of the company's Annual General Meeting (AGM). For One Person Companies, which do not have an AGM, the due date is within 180 days of the financial year's closure.

What is the government fee for filing AOC-4?

The government fee for filing AOC-4 varies based on the company's nominal share capital. It ranges from Rs. 200 for companies with share capital up to Rs. 1 lakh to Rs. 600 for companies with share capital of Rs. 1 crore or more.

What is the penalty for late filing of AOC-4?

If AOC-4 is not filed within the due date, the company may be liable to pay a fine of Rs. 1,000 per day, up to a maximum of Rs. 10 lakhs. Additionally, the company's directors and key managerial personnel may face imprisonment up to six months or a fine ranging from Rs. 1 lakh to Rs. 5 lakhs.

Do all companies need to file financial statements in XBRL format?

Companies listed on any stock exchange in India, companies with paid-up capital of Rs. 5 crore or more, companies with a turnover of Rs. 100 crore or more, and certain other classes of companies are required to file their financial statements in XBRL format.

What is the significance of filing AOC-4?

Filing AOC-4 along with the financial statements is crucial as it provides stakeholders, including shareholders, the government, and the public, with a comprehensive financial picture of the company's affairs during a financial year.

Can AOC-4 be filed without holding an AGM?

If a company fails to hold its Annual General Meeting (AGM) for any reason, it can still file AOC-4 along with the financial statements within 30 days of the last date by which the AGM should have been held. However, the company must provide a statement explaining the reasons for not holding the AGM.

Who can certify the documents filed with AOC-4?

The documents filed with AOC-4, including the financial statements, must be certified by a practicing Chartered Accountant or Company Secretary.

[Chartered Accountant](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/aoc-4) or Company Secretary. In this article, we look at the procedure for filing AOC-4 in detail.

## Documents to Be Filed in AOC-4

Financial Statements of a company includes Balance Sheet, Profit and Loss Account, Cash Flow statement (if applicable), statement of change in equity (if applicable) and any explanatory notes annexed to the financial statements. Financial statements along with Board Report must be filed for all companies registered in India (

[Private Limited Company](https://www.indiafilings.com/company-registration), One Person Company, Limited Company, Section 8 Company, etc.,) to provide the Shareholders, Government, Stakeholders and the Public a broad financial picture of the affairs of the company during a financial year.

The following is the complete list of documents that must be filed with AOC-4:

01. Copy of financial statements duly authenticated as per section 134 (including Board’s report, auditors’ report and other documents)
02. Statement of subsidiaries as per section 129 – Form AOC-1
03. Statement of the fact and reasons for not adopting Financial statements in the annual general meeting (AGM)
04. Statement of the fact and reasons for not holding the AGM
05. Approval letter of extension of financial year or AGM
06. Supplementary or test audit report under section 143
07. Company CSR policy as per sub-section (4) of section 135
08. Details of other entity(s)
09. Details of salient features and justification for entering into contracts/Arrangements/transactions with related parties as per Sub-section (1) of section 188 - Form AOC-2
10. Details of comments of CAG of India
11. Secretarial Audit Report
12. Directors’ report as per sub-section (3) of section 134
13. Details of remaining CSR activities
14. Optional attachment(s), if any.

## Filing of Form AOC-4

Financial Statements of a company are required to be filed with the Registrar along with Form AOC-4 every year for each Financial Year. All the attachments including financial statements uploaded with Form AOC-4 must be signed as per the requirement of the Companies Act 2013. SD copies are not acceptable in case of AOC-4, hand signed copies are only accepted.

In case of the companies covered under XBRL requirement under the Companies (Filing of documents & Forms in Extensible Business Reporting Language) Rules, 2015, the financial statements must be uploaded on MCA portal in XBRL format. The following class of companies are required file their financial statements and other documents in e-Form AOC-4 XBRL on or after 1st April 2014:

- All companies listed with any Stock Exchange(s) in India & their Indian subsidiaries
- All companies having paid up capital of rupees five crore or above
- All companies having turnover of rupees hundred crore or above
- All companies which were hitherto covered under the companies (Filing of Documents & Forms in Extensible Business Reporting Language) Rules, 2011

## Due Date for Filing AOC-4

All companies registered in India are required under the Companies Act, 2013 to file a copy of financial statements, including all the documents which are required to be or attached, duly adopted at the annual general meeting of the company, within thirty days of conducting an Annual General Meeting. Since,

[One Person Company](https://www.indiafilings.com/one-person-company) does not have an Annual General Meeting, One Person Company must file a copy of the financial statements duly adopted by its member, within 180 of closure of the financial year.

If the annual general meeting of a company for any year has not been held, the financial statements along with the documents required to be attached, duly signed along with the statement of facts and reasons for not holding the annual general meeting should be filed with the Registrar within 30 days of the last date before which the annual general meeting should have been held.

## Penalty for Late Filing AOC-4

If a company fails to file  along this form with a copy of the financial statements before the due date, the company will be punishable with fine of one thousand rupees for every day during which the failure continues up to a maximum amount of Rs.10 lakhs. Further, the Managing Director, Directors and the Chief Financial Officer of the company, could be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months or with fine which will not be less than Rs.1 and upto Rs.5 lakhs.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Common questions aboutAOC-4 Filing.

What is AOC-4?

AOC-4 is the form prescribed by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) for filing financial statements of a company every year. It must be submitted within 30 days of the company's Annual General Meeting (AGM) along with various other documents like the Board's report, Auditor's report, and details of the company's corporate social responsibility (CSR) policy.

What documents need to be filed along with AOC-4?

The documents that must be filed along with AOC-4 include the company's financial statements (Balance Sheet, Profit & Loss Account, Cash Flow Statement, etc.), Board's report, Auditor's report, Statement of subsidiaries in Form AOC-1, CSR policy details, related party transactions in Form AOC-2, and any other relevant documents as per the Companies Act, 2013.

Is it mandatory for all companies to file AOC-4?

Yes, filing AOC-4 along with the financial statements is mandatory for all companies registered in India, including Private Limited Companies, One Person Companies, Limited Companies, and Section 8 Companies.

What is the due date for filing AOC-4?

The due date for filing AOC-4 is within 30 days of the company's Annual General Meeting (AGM). For One Person Companies, which do not have an AGM, the due date is within 180 days of the financial year's closure.

What is the government fee for filing AOC-4?

The government fee for filing AOC-4 varies based on the company's nominal share capital. It ranges from Rs. 200 for companies with share capital up to Rs. 1 lakh to Rs. 600 for companies with share capital of Rs. 1 crore or more.

What is the penalty for late filing of AOC-4?

If AOC-4 is not filed within the due date, the company may be liable to pay a fine of Rs. 1,000 per day, up to a maximum of Rs. 10 lakhs. Additionally, the company's directors and key managerial personnel may face imprisonment up to six months or a fine ranging from Rs. 1 lakh to Rs. 5 lakhs.

Do all companies need to file financial statements in XBRL format?

Companies listed on any stock exchange in India, companies with paid-up capital of Rs. 5 crore or more, companies with a turnover of Rs. 100 crore or more, and certain other classes of companies are required to file their financial statements in XBRL format.

What is the significance of filing AOC-4?

Filing AOC-4 along with the financial statements is crucial as it provides stakeholders, including shareholders, the government, and the public, with a comprehensive financial picture of the company's affairs during a financial year.

Can AOC-4 be filed without holding an AGM?

If a company fails to hold its Annual General Meeting (AGM) for any reason, it can still file AOC-4 along with the financial statements within 30 days of the last date by which the AGM should have been held. However, the company must provide a statement explaining the reasons for not holding the AGM.

Who can certify the documents filed with AOC-4?

The documents filed with AOC-4, including the financial statements, must be certified by a practicing Chartered Accountant or Company Secretary.

content_sections.heading: Annual Return Filing
content_sections.content: The Annual Return is a comprehensive document encompassing crucial elements like a company's share capital, debts, directors, and shareholders. According to the Companies Act of 2013, it is obligatory for companies to prepare and submit their Annual Returns to the Registrar of Companies (RoC) annually. This filing requirement is necessary to avoid substantial penalties.The Annual Return must be validated and signed by the Director and the Company Secretary, utilizing their [Digital Signatures.](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/basics-digital-signature) In cases where the company hasn't employed a Company Secretary, the signature can be obtained from a practicing Company Secretary. However, the Director's signature is sufficient for [One Person Companies (OPC)](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/what-is-a-opc-company) or small companies. This mandatory Annual Return filing is executed through Form MGT-7, which comprehensively outlines the company's pertinent details.

content_sections.heading: What is Form MGT-7
content_sections.content: The Annual Return: Form MGT-7 is a document registered companies in India must file annually. It contains essential information about the company, such as its registered office, details of shareholders, directors, and more. This form provides a comprehensive snapshot of the company's status as of the end of the financial year,The purpose of filing Form MGT-7 is to ensure transparency and compliance with regulatory requirements. It helps regulatory authorities and stakeholders understand the company's structure, activities, and key personnel. Companies must complete and submit this form within a specified timeframe, and the filing fee varies based on the company's nominal share capital. The form is submitted electronically through the Ministry of Corporate Affairs portal, and any delays in filing can lead to penalties.

content_sections.heading: What is the purpose of e-Form MGT-7?
content_sections.content:
The e-Form MGT-7 is the repository for an annual return that every company must compile. This return encapsulates particulars that reflect the company's status at the culmination of the financial year. The encompassed details comprise:

- Registered office address, principal business activities, and information concerning holding, subsidiary, and associate companies.
- Shares, debentures, other securities, and the configuration of shareholding within the company.
- Indebtedness level of the company.
- Members and debenture-holders, incorporating any alterations since the preceding financial year's closure.
- Promoters, directors, key managerial personnel, and any modifications to their status since the prior financial year's end.
- Records of meetings involving members or specific classes, the Board, and its assorted committees, alongside attendance records.
- Remuneration details for directors and key managerial personnel.
- Notable penalties or sanctions imposed on the company, its directors, or officers, including compounding offenses and appeals against such penalties or punishments.
- Matters concerning certifications of compliance and prescribed disclosures.
- Overview of the company's shareholding pattern.
- Any other stipulated matters as required by the form.

The e-Form MGT-7 comprehensively captures these vital aspects, offering a comprehensive snapshot of the company's activities and structure at the close of the financial year.

content_sections.heading: Which attachments are necessary when filing this form?
content_sections.content:
When completing this e-form, including scanned copies of documents as attachments is essential. These attachments will be uploaded at the form's conclusion under the designated section. The required attachments encompass the following:

- List of shareholders and debenture holders.
- Approval letter about extending the [Annual General Meeting (AGM).](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/guide-to-annual-general-meeting)
- Copy of MGT-8.
- Any optional attachment(s), if applicable.

content_sections.heading: When should this form be submitted?
content_sections.content: Form MGT-7 must be filed within 60 days after the company's Annual General Meeting. The deadline for convening the annual general meeting falls on or before the 30th day of September following the conclusion of each financial year.Hence, the typical due date for filing form MGT-7 is November 29th annually.

content_sections.heading: Procedure for Filing Form MGT-7
content_sections.content:
The process of submitting Form MGT-7 or MGT-7A on the MCA portal can be accomplished through the following steps:

- **Access the Official Website**: Visit the Ministry of Corporate Affairs' official website and log in to the portal. Once logged in, proceed to upload Form MGT-7.
- **Enter Corporate Identity Number (CIN):** Upon logging in, provide a valid [Corporate Identity Number (CIN)](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/cin-number-meaning) for tasks such as canceling unused issued shares of one class and increasing share capital.
- **Choose Purpose and Provide Details:** From the drop-down menu, select the purpose of the eForm. If "Others" is set, provide entity details in the description box.
- **Declaration and Designation:** Opt for one of the available options from the drop-down list for representation. Digitally sign Form MGT-7/7A accordingly.
  - If the person signing digitally is a Director, provide the approved DIN.
  - If the person signing digitally is a Manager, input the approved DIN or valid income-tax PAN.
  - When a Company Secretary signs digitally, enter the membership number.
- **Upload Documents:** Utilize the attach button to upload the required documents. Proceed to make the fee payment by clicking on the payment button.
- **Form Submission and Processing:** After successfully submitting Form MGT-7, the Registrar of Companies office will process the eForm.
- **SRN Generation:** A Service Request Number (SRN) will be generated and presented to the applicant upon successful submission. This SRN will be essential for future interactions with the MCA.
- **Challan Generation:** A challan will be generated after submission, displaying the fee details paid by the user to the Ministry. This serves as an acknowledgment that Form MGT-7 has been filed.
- **Acknowledgment:** Following complete processing by the authority, an acknowledgment will be sent to the company's official email address regarding Form MGT-7.

Filing Form MGT-7 or MGT-7A can be effectively completed by following these steps, ensuring compliance with the regulatory requirements.

content_sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
content_sections.content:
Common questions aboutCompany Annual Return Filing.

What is Form MGT-7, and why is it important?

Form MGT-7 is an annual return that every registered company in India must file with the Registrar of Companies (RoC). It provides crucial details about the company, such as its registered office address, principal business activities, shareholding pattern, directors, key managerial personnel, and any changes since the previous financial year. Filing this form is mandatory for maintaining transparency and complying with regulatory requirements.

Who is required to file Form MGT-7?

Every registered company in India, whether private or public, is obligated to file Form MGT-7 annually. However, One Person Companies (OPCs) and Small Companies are required to file Form MGT-7A, which is a condensed version of the MGT-7 form specifically designed for their needs.

When is the due date for filing Form MGT-7?

Form MGT-7 must be filed within 60 days after the company's Annual General Meeting (AGM). Since the AGM must be held on or before September 30th following the end of each financial year, the typical due date for filing Form MGT-7 is November 29th annually.

What are the consequences of not filing Form MGT-7 on time?

Failure to file Form MGT-7 within the stipulated time can result in substantial penalties. The penalty for non-filing has been increased to Rs. 100 (One Hundred Rupees) per day of non-compliance, making it crucial to ensure timely submission of the annual return.

What information is required to be disclosed in Form MGT-7?

Form MGT-7 requires companies to disclose various details, including registered office address, principal business activities, shareholding pattern, information about promoters, directors, key managerial personnel, remuneration details, penalties or sanctions imposed, certifications of compliance, and any other prescribed matters.

What are the attachments required when filing Form MGT-7?

When filing Form MGT-7, companies must attach scanned copies of documents such as the list of shareholders and debenture holders, approval letter for extending the AGM (if applicable), a copy of MGT-8 (if applicable), and any other relevant attachments.

How can I file Form MGT-7 on the MCA portal?

To file Form MGT-7 on the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) portal, you need to log in with your company's Corporate Identity Number (CIN), select the purpose of the form, provide the required details, digitally sign the form, upload necessary documents, and make the fee payment. After successful submission, a Service Request Number (SRN) and challan will be generated.

What are the fees for filing Form MGT-7?

The fees for filing Form MGT-7 vary based on the company's nominal share capital. The fees range from Rs. 200 for companies with a share capital of less than Rs. 1,00,000 to Rs. 600 for companies with a share capital of Rs. 1,00,00,000 or more. Companies without share capital are required to pay a fee of Rs. 200.

Can I seek professional assistance for filing Form MGT-7?

Yes, you can seek professional assistance from service providers like IndiaFilings to simplify the process of filing Form MGT-7. Their experienced team can ensure seamless and error-free submission of the annual return, allowing you to focus on your core business operations while ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements.

How can I ensure timely and accurate filing of Form MGT-7?

To ensure timely and accurate filing of Form MGT-7, you can maintain a calendar reminder for the due date, gather all required information and documents well in advance, and consider seeking professional assistance from reliable service providers like IndiaFilings. # Complete Guide to Company Annual Return Filing using Form MGT-7

Following[company registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/private-limited-company-registration-in-india), every company must submit a return to the [Registrar of Companies (ROC)](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/registrar-of-companies-roc) annually. This report encompasses fundamental details about the company, its shareholders, directors, and more, as of the concluding day of the fiscal year – specifically, March 31st. Compliance with this requirement is compulsory for all registered companies, necessitating the completion and submission of Form MGT-7. Form MGT-7 is an electronic document furnished by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs to all corporate entities. It facilitates the comprehensive disclosure of their annual return particulars. The Registrar of Companies manages this electronic form digitally and relies on the accuracy attested to by the company's statement of correctness.Simplify[Company Compliance](https://www.indiafilings.com/company-annual-filing) Filing with IndiaFilings. Contact us today to file your company's annual return hassle-free. [Get Started!](https://www.indiafilings.com/company-annual-filing)

## Annual Return Filing

The Annual Return is a comprehensive document encompassing crucial elements like a company's share capital, debts, directors, and shareholders. According to the Companies Act of 2013, it is obligatory for companies to prepare and submit their Annual Returns to the Registrar of Companies (RoC) annually. This filing requirement is necessary to avoid substantial penalties.The Annual Return must be validated and signed by the Director and the Company Secretary, utilizing their [Digital Signatures.](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/basics-digital-signature) In cases where the company hasn't employed a Company Secretary, the signature can be obtained from a practicing Company Secretary. However, the Director's signature is sufficient for [One Person Companies (OPC)](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/what-is-a-opc-company) or small companies. This mandatory Annual Return filing is executed through Form MGT-7, which comprehensively outlines the company's pertinent details.

## What is Form MGT-7

The Annual Return: Form MGT-7 is a document registered companies in India must file annually. It contains essential information about the company, such as its registered office, details of shareholders, directors, and more. This form provides a comprehensive snapshot of the company's status as of the end of the financial year,The purpose of filing Form MGT-7 is to ensure transparency and compliance with regulatory requirements. It helps regulatory authorities and stakeholders understand the company's structure, activities, and key personnel. Companies must complete and submit this form within a specified timeframe, and the filing fee varies based on the company's nominal share capital. The form is submitted electronically through the Ministry of Corporate Affairs portal, and any delays in filing can lead to penalties.

## Who is Required to Submit the MGT-7 Form?

Every registered company in India, irrespective of whether it is a private or public company, is obligated to file this e-form annually. The company's filing of the MGT-7 form pertains to its annual return.

### Form No. MGT-7 - Annual Return (Excluding OPCs and Small Companies)

By the Companies (Management and Administration) Amendment Rules, 2021, each company must submit its annual return using Form No. MGT-7, except for One Person Companies (OPCs) and Small Companies.Form No. MGT-7 is reproduced below for ready reference:

### Form No.MGT-7A – Annual Return for OPCs and Small Companies

Introducing Form No. MGT-7A - Condensed Annual Return for OPCs and Small Companies Starting from the fiscal year 2020-2021, both One Person Companies and Small Companies must submit their annual return using Form No. MGT-7A.Therefore, it is incumbent upon every company, including OPCs, to complete and submit Form MGT-7 as part of their annual return filing process.

## Due date of filing Form MGT-7/MGT-7A

Form MGT-7 should be submitted within 60 days from the company's Annual General Meeting. The annual general meeting must be held on or before the 30th day of September, following the completion of each financial year. Consequently, the typical deadline for filing [form MGT-7/MGT-7A](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/mca-form-no-mgt-7-and-form-no-mgt-7a-2021)is usually November 29th each year.The last date for filing Form MGT 7 is November 29th, 2023, for the FY 2022-23

## MGT-7 (MCA) Form Filing Fees

The fee for filing a company's annual return through MGT-7 is determined based on the company's nominal share capital. The MGT-7 form filing fee commences at Rs 200 for companies with a Share Capital of less than 1,00,000. As the company's share capital increases, the fee amount escalates accordingly. A comprehensive list of fees can be found here. This fee will be remitted while submitting the annual return (MGT-7) to the Registrar of Companies (ROC). The MGT-7 Filing Fee stands at Rs 200 for companies without share capital.

| **Nominal Share Capital** | **Normal Fee (in Rupees)** |
| --- | --- |
| Less than 1,00,000 | INR 200 |
| 1,00,000 to 4,99,999 | INR 300 |
| 5,00,000 to 24,99,999 | INR 400 |
| 25,00,000 to 99,99,999 | INR 500 |
| 1,00,00,000 or more | INR 600 |
| No share capital | INR 200 |

Note: The fee for filing (for companies without share capital) is Rs 200.

| **Period of Delays** | **Fees** |
| --- | --- |
| Up to 30 days | Two times of regular fees |
| More than 30 days and up to 60 days | Four times of regular fees |
| More than 60 days and up to 90 days | Six times of regular fees |
| More than 90 days and up to 180 days | Ten times of regular fees |
| More than 180 days and up to 270 days | 12 times of normal fees |

## Penalty for Non-Filing of MGT-7/MGT-7A

The [penalty for the non-filing of an annual return](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/placing-of-companys-annual-return-on-the-website) was notably raised in 2018 to Rs. 100 (One Hundred Rupees) per day of non-compliance. As a result, it is imperative to guarantee that the annual return in this form is lodged before the stipulated due date.

## What is the purpose of e-Form MGT-7?

The e-Form MGT-7 is the repository for an annual return that every company must compile. This return encapsulates particulars that reflect the company's status at the culmination of the financial year. The encompassed details comprise:

- Registered office address, principal business activities, and information concerning holding, subsidiary, and associate companies.
- Shares, debentures, other securities, and the configuration of shareholding within the company.
- Indebtedness level of the company.
- Members and debenture-holders, incorporating any alterations since the preceding financial year's closure.
- Promoters, directors, key managerial personnel, and any modifications to their status since the prior financial year's end.
- Records of meetings involving members or specific classes, the Board, and its assorted committees, alongside attendance records.
- Remuneration details for directors and key managerial personnel.
- Notable penalties or sanctions imposed on the company, its directors, or officers, including compounding offenses and appeals against such penalties or punishments.
- Matters concerning certifications of compliance and prescribed disclosures.
- Overview of the company's shareholding pattern.
- Any other stipulated matters as required by the form.

The e-Form MGT-7 comprehensively captures these vital aspects, offering a comprehensive snapshot of the company's activities and structure at the close of the financial year.

## Which attachments are necessary when filing this form?

When completing this e-form, including scanned copies of documents as attachments is essential. These attachments will be uploaded at the form's conclusion under the designated section. The required attachments encompass the following:

- List of shareholders and debenture holders.
- Approval letter about extending the [Annual General Meeting (AGM).](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/guide-to-annual-general-meeting)
- Copy of MGT-8.
- Any optional attachment(s), if applicable.

## When should this form be submitted?

Form MGT-7 must be filed within 60 days after the company's Annual General Meeting. The deadline for convening the annual general meeting falls on or before the 30th day of September following the conclusion of each financial year.Hence, the typical due date for filing form MGT-7 is November 29th annually.

## Procedure for Filing Form MGT-7

The process of submitting Form MGT-7 or MGT-7A on the MCA portal can be accomplished through the following steps:

- **Access the Official Website**: Visit the Ministry of Corporate Affairs' official website and log in to the portal. Once logged in, proceed to upload Form MGT-7.
- **Enter Corporate Identity Number (CIN):** Upon logging in, provide a valid [Corporate Identity Number (CIN)](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/cin-number-meaning) for tasks such as canceling unused issued shares of one class and increasing share capital.
- **Choose Purpose and Provide Details:** From the drop-down menu, select the purpose of the eForm. If "Others" is set, provide entity details in the description box.
- **Declaration and Designation:** Opt for one of the available options from the drop-down list for representation. Digitally sign Form MGT-7/7A accordingly.
  - If the person signing digitally is a Director, provide the approved DIN.
  - If the person signing digitally is a Manager, input the approved DIN or valid income-tax PAN.
  - When a Company Secretary signs digitally, enter the membership number.
- **Upload Documents:** Utilize the attach button to upload the required documents. Proceed to make the fee payment by clicking on the payment button.
- **Form Submission and Processing:** After successfully submitting Form MGT-7, the Registrar of Companies office will process the eForm.
- **SRN Generation:** A Service Request Number (SRN) will be generated and presented to the applicant upon successful submission. This SRN will be essential for future interactions with the MCA.
- **Challan Generation:** A challan will be generated after submission, displaying the fee details paid by the user to the Ministry. This serves as an acknowledgment that Form MGT-7 has been filed.
- **Acknowledgment:** Following complete processing by the authority, an acknowledgment will be sent to the company's official email address regarding Form MGT-7.

Filing Form MGT-7 or MGT-7A can be effectively completed by following these steps, ensuring compliance with the regulatory requirements.

Our team of seasoned professionals specializes in ensuring a seamless and error-free submission of Form MGT-7, allowing you to dedicate your time and energy to your core business operations. ## Frequently Asked Questions

Common questions aboutCompany Annual Return Filing.

What is Form MGT-7, and why is it important?

Form MGT-7 is an annual return that every registered company in India must file with the Registrar of Companies (RoC). It provides crucial details about the company, such as its registered office address, principal business activities, shareholding pattern, directors, key managerial personnel, and any changes since the previous financial year. Filing this form is mandatory for maintaining transparency and complying with regulatory requirements.

Who is required to file Form MGT-7?

Every registered company in India, whether private or public, is obligated to file Form MGT-7 annually. However, One Person Companies (OPCs) and Small Companies are required to file Form MGT-7A, which is a condensed version of the MGT-7 form specifically designed for their needs.

When is the due date for filing Form MGT-7?

Form MGT-7 must be filed within 60 days after the company's Annual General Meeting (AGM). Since the AGM must be held on or before September 30th following the end of each financial year, the typical due date for filing Form MGT-7 is November 29th annually.

What are the consequences of not filing Form MGT-7 on time?

Failure to file Form MGT-7 within the stipulated time can result in substantial penalties. The penalty for non-filing has been increased to Rs. 100 (One Hundred Rupees) per day of non-compliance, making it crucial to ensure timely submission of the annual return.

What information is required to be disclosed in Form MGT-7?

Form MGT-7 requires companies to disclose various details, including registered office address, principal business activities, shareholding pattern, information about promoters, directors, key managerial personnel, remuneration details, penalties or sanctions imposed, certifications of compliance, and any other prescribed matters.

What are the attachments required when filing Form MGT-7?

When filing Form MGT-7, companies must attach scanned copies of documents such as the list of shareholders and debenture holders, approval letter for extending the AGM (if applicable), a copy of MGT-8 (if applicable), and any other relevant attachments.

How can I file Form MGT-7 on the MCA portal?

To file Form MGT-7 on the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) portal, you need to log in with your company's Corporate Identity Number (CIN), select the purpose of the form, provide the required details, digitally sign the form, upload necessary documents, and make the fee payment. After successful submission, a Service Request Number (SRN) and challan will be generated.

What are the fees for filing Form MGT-7?

The fees for filing Form MGT-7 vary based on the company's nominal share capital. The fees range from Rs. 200 for companies with a share capital of less than Rs. 1,00,000 to Rs. 600 for companies with a share capital of Rs. 1,00,00,000 or more. Companies without share capital are required to pay a fee of Rs. 200.

Can I seek professional assistance for filing Form MGT-7?

Yes, you can seek professional assistance from service providers like IndiaFilings to simplify the process of filing Form MGT-7. Their experienced team can ensure seamless and error-free submission of the annual return, allowing you to focus on your core business operations while ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements.

How can I ensure timely and accurate filing of Form MGT-7?

To ensure timely and accurate filing of Form MGT-7, you can maintain a calendar reminder for the due date, gather all required information and documents well in advance, and consider seeking professional assistance from reliable service providers like IndiaFilings. Their expertise in company compliance filing can streamline the process and minimize the risk of penalties or non-compliance.

content_sections.content:
Due to the unfortunate situation of many people affected directly or indirectly to the Corona Virus across the globe, many countries have implemented lock down situation to prevent spreading of the virus. This has ultimately hit the economy for India as well as for other countries. To retain financial stability during this situation the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) waived off the

**filing fee of Rs.5000 and Rs.10,000** for the DIN holders who have not filed DIN-3 KYC OR DIN-3 eKYC. The MCA implemented this wave-off through General Circular N0.11 on 24th March 2020 and through General Circular No. 12 on 30th March 2020. This wave-off of filing fee shall apply for the following only if:

- The status of the DIN holders marked as 'Deactivated' for non-filing DIN-3 KYC OR DIN-3 eKYC and
- The status of the Companies whose compliance has been marked as 'Active non-compliant' for not filing Active Company Tagging Identifies and Verification (ACTIVE) e-form.

**NOTE: The wave off period for the filing fee of Rs.5000 and Rs.10,000 shall apply only between 1st April 2020 to 30th September.** **Also read:** [Companies Fresh Start Scheme 2020](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/companies-fresh-start-scheme-2020)

content_sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
content_sections.content:
Common questions aboutDIR-3 eKYC.

What is the purpose of DIR-3 eKYC?

The DIR-3 eKYC is a new e-form introduced by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) to conduct annual Know Your Customer (KYC) verification for all directors of companies in India. It is mandatory for directors to file this form to update their personal details, including unique mobile number and email address, which will be verified through an OTP process.

Who needs to file DIR-3 eKYC?

Every director who has been allotted a Director Identification Number (DIN) on or before 31st March 2018 and whose DIN is in 'Approved' status, is required to file the DIR-3 eKYC form. This includes directors whose DINs have been marked as 'Disqualified' by the MCA.

What is the due date for filing DIR-3 eKYC?

Originally, the due date for filing DIR-3 eKYC was set as 31st August 2018. However, it was later extended to 15th September 2018 by the MCA. If the form is not filed by the due date, the respective DINs will be marked as 'Deactivated' by the MCA system.

Is there any fee for filing DIR-3 eKYC?

No fee is required for filing DIR-3 eKYC if it is submitted on or before the due date (initially 15th September 2018, later extended to 14th October 2019 for the financial year ending 31st March 2019). However, if the form is filed after the due date, a fee of Rs. 5,000 will be payable for reactivating the deactivated DIN.

How can I file DIR-3 eKYC?

The DIR-3 eKYC form must be filed using the director's own Digital Signature Certificate (DSC) and should be certified by a practicing professional (Chartered Accountant, Company Secretary, or Cost Accountant). The form requires mandatory disclosure of the director's unique personal mobile number and email address, which will be verified through an OTP process.

What happens if I don't file DIR-3 eKYC on time?

If a director fails to file the DIR-3 eKYC form by the due date, the MCA system will automatically deactivate their DIN with the reason 'Non-filing of DIR-3 KYC'. To reactivate a deactivated DIN, the director will need to file the DIR-3 eKYC form and pay a penalty fee of Rs. 5,000 or more, as specified by the MCA.

Is DIR-3 eKYC the same as DIR-3 form?

No, DIR-3 and DIR-3 eKYC are two different forms. DIR-3 is used for obtaining a Director Identification Number (DIN), while DIR-3 eKYC is an annual KYC form that directors need to file to update their personal details with the MCA.

Do I need to file DIR-3 eKYC every year?

Yes, the MCA notification states that the DIR-3 eKYC form will be required to be filed annually by all directors to update their KYC details with the ministry.

Can I file DIR-3 eKYC if my DIN is deactivated due to non-filing of annual returns?

Yes, even directors whose DINs have been marked as 'Disqualified' by the MCA for not filing annual returns are required to file the DIR-3 eKYC form. Failure to do so will attract an additional penalty of Rs. 5,000.

What is the purpose of the 2020 DIN eKYC waiver?

In light of the COVID-19 pandemic and its economic impact, the MCA has waived the filing fee of Rs. 5,000 and Rs. 10,000 for DIN holders who have not filed DIN-3 KYC or DIN-3 eKYC, and for companies whose compliance status is marked as 'Active non-compliant'. This waiver is applicable from 1st April 2020 to 30th September 2020 to provide financial relief during the crisis.

To reactivate a deactivated DIN, the director will need to file the DIR-3 eKYC form and pay a penalty fee of Rs. 5,000 or more, as specified by the MCA.

Is DIR-3 eKYC the same as DIR-3 form?

No, DIR-3 and DIR-3 eKYC are two different forms. DIR-3 is used for obtaining a Director Identification Number (DIN), while DIR-3 eKYC is an annual KYC form that directors need to file to update their personal details with the MCA.

Do I need to file DIR-3 eKYC every year?

Yes, the MCA notification states that the DIR-3 eKYC form will be required to be filed annually by all directors to update their KYC details with the ministry.

Can I file DIR-3 eKYC if my DIN is deactivated due to non-filing of annual returns?

Yes, even directors whose DINs have been marked as 'Disqualified' by the MCA for not filing annual returns are required to file the DIR-3 eKYC form. Failure to do so will attract an additional penalty of Rs. 5,000.

What is the purpose of the 2020 DIN eKYC waiver?

In light of the COVID-19 pandemic and its economic impact, the MCA has waived the filing fee of Rs. 5,000 and Rs. 10,000 for DIN holders who have not filed DIN-3 KYC or DIN-3 eKYC, and for companies whose compliance status is marked as 'Active non-compliant'. This waiver is applicable from 1st April 2020 to 30th September 2020 to provide financial relief during the crisis.

content_sections.heading: CBDT Notifies Revised ITR-6 Form for AY 2025–26
content_sections.content: The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) has officially released the updated ITR-6 form for Assessment Year 2025–26 via Notification No. 44/2025 dated May 6, 2025. This revised form incorporates significant changes aligning with the Finance Act, 2024 and aims to improve reporting accuracy for corporate taxpayers.

content_sections.heading: Key Changes in ITR-6 for AY 2025–26
content_sections.content:
- Capital Gains Reporting: The Schedule-CG has been updated to separately report capital gains accrued before and after July 23, 2024, in line with amendments introduced by the Finance Act, 2024.
- Buyback Loss Treatment: Capital losses on share buybacks are now allowed if the related dividend income is disclosed under ‘Income from Other Sources’—applicable for buybacks post October 1, 2024.
- New Section Reference – 44BBC: The form now includes a reference to Section 44BBC, relating to presumptive taxation for cruise shipping businesses.
- Schedule BP Update (Rule 10TIA): Profits from the sale of rough diamonds must now be declared as 4% or more of gross receipts by Foreign Companies.
- Enhanced Disclosure in Schedule-24(b): Taxpayers claiming interest deductions on housing loans under Section 24(b) will now be required to furnish additional details.
- Schedule-TDS Revision: A new field has been added to report the applicable TDS section code, ensuring more accurate linkage with Form 26AS and TDS returns.

content_sections.heading: Who Should File ITR-6?
content_sections.content:
All companies registered under the Companies Act, 2013 or the earlier Companies Act, 1956, are required to file their income tax return using Form ITR-6:

- Domestic companies
- Foreign companies
- Firms such as partnerships and limited liability partnerships (LLPs)

content_sections.heading: Who Cannot File ITR-6?
content_sections.content: Companies whose income is derived from property held for charitable or religious purposes—covered under Section 11—are exempt from filing ITR-6.

content_sections.heading: ITR 6 Due Date
content_sections.content: The due date for filing the ITR-6 Form depends on the audit requirements of the company. Below are the timelines as per the Income Tax Act:

content_sections.heading: 1\. If Accounts are Subject to Audit (Section 44AB):
content_sections.content: Due Date: 31st October of the Assessment Year.

content_sections.heading: 2\. If International or Specified Domestic Transactions Exist (Form 3CEB):
content_sections.content: Due Date: 30th November of the Assessment Year.

content_sections.heading: 3\. If No Audit is Required:
content_sections.content: Due Date: 31st July of the Assessment Year.

content_sections.heading: Mandatory Audit Filing for Companies
content_sections.content:
- If a company is required to undergo an audit under the Income Tax Act (Section 44AB) or any other applicable law (such as the Companies Act), the following must be ensured:
- Audit Report Submission: The audit report must be submitted electronically by the auditor through the Income Tax e-filing portal.
- Audit Form Requirements: Since companies are audited under the Companies Act, the audit report must be submitted in Form 3CA and Form 3CD.
- Details Required - The ITR-6 form must include:

  - Name and details of the auditor
  - Date of furnishing the audit report
  - Acknowledgement number of the electronically filed report

_[Click here to learn more about the requirements for Form 3CA and 3CD](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/form-3cb-3cd)_

content_sections.heading: What is the Structure of the ITR-6 Form?
content_sections.content: The ITR-6 Form is comprehensive and divided into two main parts along with multiple detailed schedules. Here's a breakdown:

content_sections.heading: Part A – General and Financial Information
content_sections.content:
- Part A: General Information
- Part A-BS: Balance Sheet as on 31st March
- Part A-BS-Ind AS: Balance Sheet as on 31st March or on the date of business combination (Ind AS compliant)
- Part A-Manufacturing Account: Manufacturing account for the financial year
- Part A-Trading Account: Trading account for the financial year
- Part A-P&L: Profit and Loss account for the financial year
- Part A-Manufacturing Account-Ind AS: Manufacturing account (Ind AS compliant)
- Part A-Trading Account Ind-AS: Trading account (Ind AS compliant)
- Part A-P&L Ind-AS: Profit and Loss account (Ind AS compliant)
- Part A-OI: Other Information
- Part A-QD: Quantitative Details
- Part A-OL: Receipts and Payments Account (for companies under liquidation)

content_sections.heading: Part B – Income and Tax Computation
content_sections.content:
- Part B-TI: Computation of Total Income
- Part B-TTI: Computation of Tax Liability on Total Income

content_sections.heading: Schedules in ITR-6 (Total: 46 Schedules)
content_sections.content:
- Schedule HP: Income from House Property
- Schedule BP: Profits and Gains from Business or Profession
- Schedule DPM: Depreciation on Plant and Machinery
- Schedule DOA: Depreciation on Other Assets
- Schedule DEP: Summary of Depreciation
- Schedule DCG: Deemed Capital Gains on Depreciable Assets
- Schedule ESR: Deduction under Section 35 (Scientific Research)
- Schedule CG: Capital Gains
- Schedule 112A: Sale of equity shares or units with STT under Section 112A
- Schedule 115AD(1)(b)(iii) - Proviso: Sale under Section 112A (for certain non-residents)
- Schedule VDA: Income from transfer of Virtual Digital Assets
- Schedule OS: Income from Other Sources
- Schedule CYLA: Set-off of Current Year’s Losses
- Schedule BFLA: Set-off of Unabsorbed Losses
- Schedule CFL: Losses to be Carried Forward
- Schedule UD: Unabsorbed Depreciation & Section 35(4) Allowances
- Schedule ICDS: Effect of Income Computation and Disclosure Standards
- Schedule 10AA: Deduction under Section 10AA
- Schedule 80G: Donations under Section 80G
- Schedule 80GGA: Donations for Scientific Research or Rural Development
- Schedule 80GGC: Contributions to Political Parties
- Schedule 80IAC: Deduction for Eligible Start-ups
- Schedule 80LA: IFSC/Offshore Banking Deduction
- Schedule RA: Donations to Research Associations
- Schedule 80IA: Deduction under Section 80IA
- Schedule 80IB: Deduction under Section 80IB
- Schedule 80IC/80IE: Deduction under Sections 80IC or 80IE
- Schedule VIA: Deductions under Chapter VIA
- Schedule SI: Income Chargeable at Special Rates
- Schedule IF: Investment in Unincorporated Entities
- Schedule EI: Exempt Income
- Schedule PTI: Pass-through Income from Trusts/Investment Funds
- Schedule MAT: Minimum Alternate Tax (Section 115JB)
- Schedule MATC: MAT Credit (Section 115JAA)
- Schedule BBS: Tax on Buy-back of Shares
- Schedule TPSA: Secondary Transfer Pricing Adjustments
- Schedule 115TD: Accreted Income under Section 115TD
- Schedule FSI: Foreign Source Income
- Schedule TR: Tax Relief for Foreign Taxes Paid
- Schedule FA: Foreign Assets and Income
- Schedule SH-1: Shareholding of Unlisted Companies
- Schedule SH-2: Shareholding of Startups
- Schedule AL-1: Assets and Liabilities (end of year)
- Schedule AL-2: Assets and Liabilities for Startups
- Schedule GST: GST Turnover/Gross Receipts
- Schedule FD: Foreign Currency Payment/Receipt Breakup

content_sections.heading: Tax Payment Details Included in the Form
content_sections.content:
- Advance Tax & Self-Assessment Tax
- TDS (Tax Deducted at Source)
- TCS (Tax Collected at Source)

content_sections.heading: Key Changes in ITR-6 Form – AY 2024-25
content_sections.content:
- Legal Entity Identifier (LEI): Mandatory disclosure of LEI information for companies involved in high-value transactions.
- New Schedule 115TD: Introduced for reporting tax payable on accreted income under Section 115TD.
- Capital Gains Accounts Scheme: Disclosure required if capital gains have been deposited under this scheme.
- Schedule 80GGC (New): Requires reporting of donations made to political parties.
- Schedule 80-IAC (New): Requires details in respect of eligible start-ups claiming deduction.
- Schedule 80LA (New): Requires information about offshore banking units or IFSC entities.
- MSME Dues Disclosure: Mandatory disclosure of amounts payable to Micro and Small Enterprises beyond the prescribed time limit.
- Online Gaming Winnings: Reporting of winnings from online games under the new Section 115BBJ.
- IFSC Dividends: Declaration of dividend income derived from units located in International Financial Services Centres (IFSC).
- Due Date of Return Filing: Companies must specify the applicable due date for filing their return.
- Audit Report Details: Furnishing of the Audit Report Acknowledgement Number and UDIN (Unique Document Identification Number).
- MSME Classification: The Company must disclose if it is recognised as a Micro or Small Enterprise.
- Reason for Tax Audit (Section 44AB): The reason for undergoing a tax audit must be specified.

content_sections.heading: Key Changes in ITR-6 Form – AY 2020-21
content_sections.content:
- Schedule 112A: Introduced for reporting long-term capital gains on sale of equity shares or units liable to STT.
- Section 92CE(2A): Details required on tax payable for secondary adjustments to transfer pricing.
- COVID Relief Reporting: Separate field for tax deduction claims on investments/payments/expenditures made between 1st April 2020 and 30th June 2020 (COVID-related relief period).

content_sections.heading: Key Changes in ITR-6 Form – AY 2019-20
content_sections.content:
- Startup Recognition: Requirement to disclose recognition status as a start-up by DPIIT (Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade).
- Form-2 Declaration: Disclosure of declarations filed in Form-2 (used by start-ups).
- Donation Details: Bifurcation of donations into cash and non-cash modes.
- GST Reporting: Disclosure of turnover or gross receipts as reported in GST returns.

content_sections.heading: How to Fill Out the ITR-6 Form
content_sections.content:
The Income Tax Department recommends the following sequence for completing the ITR-6 Form:

- Part A – Start by filling in General Information, Financial Statements, and Other Relevant Details.
- Schedules – Complete all applicable schedules based on your company’s income, deductions, and disclosures.
- Part B – Enter the computation of total income and tax liability.
- Verification – Finally, complete the verification section and digitally sign the form.

content_sections.heading: How to File ITR-6 Form?
content_sections.content: The applicant can do the online filing of ITR 6 for companies electronically on the e-filing web portal of the Income-tax Department and verify by way of a digital signature only. Here is the brief procedure for an ITR6 online filing:

content_sections.heading: Step 1: Login
content_sections.content:
- Visit the Income Tax Department's e-filing portal
- Enter your valid User ID (PAN) and password to log in. You'll need to do so if you haven't registered yet.

content_sections.heading: Step 2: Go to 'File Income Tax Return
content_sections.content: - Once logged in, locate the section for filing income tax returns. This might be labeled "e-File" or "Income Tax Return" depending on the portal's layout.

content_sections.heading: Step 3: Select the Assessment Year (AY)
content_sections.content: - Choose the relevant assessment year (AY) for filing the ITR. The AY is based on the financial year you're reporting income (previous year + 1). For example, if you file for income earned between April 1, 2023, and March 31, 2024, the AY would be 2024-25.

content_sections.heading: Step 4: Select Status and ITR Type
content_sections.content:
- Here, you'll specify your filing status. Since you're filing for a company, it likely won't be "Individual." It could be "Company" or another category, depending on your business structure.
- Then, choose the ITR form type. Select "ITR 6" from the available options.

content_sections.heading: Step 5: Reason for Filing
content_sections.content: Indicate the reason for filing the ITR. This could be "Original Return" if it's the first time you're filing for the AY, or "Revised Return" if you're correcting a previously filed return.

content_sections.heading: Step 6: Pre-filled Information
content_sections.content:
- The portal might pre-fill some information based on your previous filings or information received from third parties (like tax deducted at source - TDS). Carefully review this pre-filled data.
- Edit any pre-filled information that's inaccurate or incomplete.

content_sections.heading: Step 7: Fill ITR 6 Form
content_sections.content:
The applicant is required to furnish the following details in the income tax return Form-6 (ITR 6):

General & Company Information

- Basic company details (Name, PAN, Incorporation date, etc.)
- Filing and holding status
- Nature and type of company
- Shareholder and ownership details
- Business structure and nature of business

Audit & Financial Information

- Audit details (under Income Tax Act or other laws)
- Auditor information and audit report details (Form 3CA/3CD)
- Balance Sheet details
- Manufacturing and Trading account details
- Profit and Loss statement

Income Details

- Income from Business or Profession
- Income from House Property
- Capital Gains (including scrip-wise details under section 112A)
- Income from Other Sources
- Presumptive income under sections 44AE, 44B, 44BB, etc.
- Exempt Income
- Foreign Income

Depreciation & Adjustments

- Depreciation on assets (Plant, Machinery, etc.)
- Deemed capital gains on the sale of depreciable assets
- Unabsorbed depreciation and other allowances
- Income Computation Disclosure Standards (ICDS) adjustments

Deductions & Reliefs

- Deductions under Chapter VI-A (80G, 80IA, 80IB, 80IC, 80P, etc.)
- Dedications for donations (scientific research, rural development, political parties)
- Dedication for SEZ units, start-ups, and IFSCs
- Tax relief under the Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (DTAA)

Tax Computation

- Minimum Alternate Tax (MAT) under section 115JB
- Tax credits under section 115JAA
- Tax on distributed profits, share buy-backs, and dividends
- Income chargeable at special rates

Other Disclosures

- Shareholding information (including start-ups)
- Assets and liabilities (for both startups and other companies)
- Pass-through income from investment funds/business trusts
- GST turnover/revenue details
- Foreign currency transaction breakup

Tax Payments & Verification

- Advance Tax, Self-assessment Tax
- [Tax Deducted at Source (TDS)](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/tds-tax-deducted-at-source-all-you-need-to-know) and [Tax Collected at Source (TCS)](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/tax-collected-at-source-tcs)
- Verification and declaration of the return

content_sections.heading: Step 8: E-verification
content_sections.content:
- Once you've completed filling out the ITR6 form, you'll need to verify it electronically. The portal will provide various e-verification methods like Aadhaar OTP, digital signature certificates, etc.
- Choose a convenient method and follow the on-screen instructions to sign the ITR, making it a valid electronic submission.

content_sections.heading: Key Notes:
content_sections.content:
- You are not required to attach any documents with the ITR-6 form—this includes TDS certificates, audit reports, or financial statements. The form is fully self-contained.
- Before submitting the return, make sure to reconcile your tax details with [Form 26AS](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/form-26as)(Tax Credit Statement). This ensures that the taxes deducted, collected, or paid on your behalf match the official records.

content_sections.heading: 1\. What is ITR-6?
content_sections.content: ITR-6 is an income tax return form applicable to companies that do not claim exemptions under Section 11 (charitable or religious purposes). It is used to report income, claim deductions, and compute tax liability.

content_sections.heading: 2\. Who should file ITR-6?
content_sections.content: All domestic and foreign companies registered under the Companies Act, except those claiming exemption under Section 11, must file ITR-6.

content_sections.heading: 3\. When is the due date for filing ITR-6?
content_sections.content:
- 31st October: If the company’s accounts are subject to audit
- 30th November: If the company is required to furnish Form 3CEB (international/domestic transfer pricing)
- 31st July: For companies not subject to audit

content_sections.heading: 4\. How do I fill out the ITR-6 form?
content_sections.content:
You need to follow this sequence:

- Part A – General info & financials
- Schedules – Income, deductions, depreciation, etc.
- Part B – Tax computation
- Verification – With DSC (Digital Signature Certificate)

content_sections.heading: 5\. Can I file ITR-6 online?
content_sections.content: Yes. ITR-6 must be filed online, and it must be verified using a Digital Signature Certificate (DSC).

content_sections.heading: 6\. How do I upload ITR-6 on the income tax portal?
content_sections.content:
You need to:

- Log in to incometax.gov.in
- Prepare and validate the ITR-6 form using the Java or Excel utility
- Upload it under your company profile using a valid DSC

content_sections.heading: 7\. Where can I download the ITR-6 form?
content_sections.content: You can download the latest ITR-6 form (in Excel/Java format) from the official Income Tax e-Filing portal.

content_sections.heading: 8\. What are the key details required in ITR-6?
content_sections.content:
- Company’s PAN & registration details
- Balance sheet & profit/loss account
- Income from business/profession
- Deductions under various sections
- Depreciation & capital gains
- Foreign income & assets (if applicable)

content_sections.heading: 9\. Can I revise ITR-6 after submitting it?
content_sections.content: Yes, you can revise ITR-6 if there’s an error or omission, before the end of the assessment year. You can also revise to opt into the New Tax Regime, provided Forms 10IB/10IC/10ID were submitted on time.

content_sections.heading: 10\. Is ITR-6 applicable for LLPs or partnerships?
content_sections.content: No. LLPs and partnerships should file ITR-5, not ITR-6. ITR-6 is only for companies.

content_sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
content_sections.content:
Common questions aboutITR 6 Filing.

What is the purpose of the ITR-6 form?

The ITR-6 form is an income tax return form that companies registered under the Companies Act are required to file. Its purpose is to report the company's income, claim eligible deductions, and compute the tax liability for the assessment year.

Which companies are required to file ITR-6?

All domestic and foreign companies registered under the Companies Act, except those claiming exemption under Section 11 (for charitable or religious purposes), must file their income tax return using the ITR-6 form.

What is the due date for filing ITR-6?

The due date for filing ITR-6 depends on the company's audit requirements. If the company's accounts are subject to audit, the due date is October 31st of the assessment year. If the company is required to furnish Form 3CEB (related to international/domestic transfer pricing), the due date is November 30th of the assessment year. If no audit is required, the due date is July 31st of the assessment year.

What is the structure of the ITR-6 form?

The ITR-6 form is divided into two main parts: Part A (General and Financial Information) and Part B (Income and Tax Computation). Additionally, there are numerous schedules to report specific details such as income from business, capital gains, deductions claimed, and more.

How do I file the ITR-6 form?

The ITR-6 form must be filed online through the Income Tax Department's e-filing portal. The process involves logging in, selecting the assessment year and ITR form type, filling out the required details, and finally verifying and submitting the form using a Digital Signature Certificate (DSC).

What information is required to complete the ITR-6 form?

To fill out the ITR-6 form, you'll need to provide general company information, financial statements (balance sheet, profit and loss account, etc.), details of income sources, deductions claimed, depreciation calculations, foreign income and assets (if applicable), tax payments made, and more.

Can I revise the ITR-6 form after filing?

Yes, you can revise the ITR-6 form if there are any errors or omissions, as long as it's before the end of the assessment year. It's also possible to revise the form to opt for the New Tax Regime, provided the necessary forms (10IB/10IC/10ID) were submitted on time.

Is ITR-6 applicable for Limited Liability Partnerships (LLPs) or partnerships?

No, ITR-6 is not applicable for LLPs or partnerships. These business entities are required to file their income tax returns using the ITR-5 form, while ITR-6 is specifically for companies registered under the Companies Act.

What are the penalties for not filing or late filing of ITR-6?

Failing to file the ITR-6 form or filing it after the due date can attract penalties under the Income Tax Act. The penalties may include interest on the unpaid tax amount, late filing fees, and potential prosecution in case of repeated non-compliance.

Can I seek professional assistance for filing ITR-6?

Yes, you can seek professional assistance from tax consultants or service providers like IndiaFilings to ensure accurate and timely filing of the ITR-6 form. Their expertise can help you navigate the complexities of tax compliance and avoid potential errors or penalties.

# ITR-6: Meaning, Due Date, Applicability & Filing Guide for Companies

If you're a company registered under the [Companies Act](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/companies-act-2013) and not claiming exemptions under [Section 11](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/section-11-income-tax-act), ITR-6 is the form you need to file. From income reporting to tax calculations, this form is key to staying compliant. In this guide, we’ll explore everything about Form ITR-6—its due date, applicability, recent changes, and the step-by-step filing process.

_Not sure which ITR form is right for you? Our experts are here to help you choose the correct form and ensure a smooth filing process._

[Get Started!](https://www.indiafilings.com/income-tax-filing)

## CBDT Notifies Revised ITR-6 Form for AY 2025–26

The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) has officially released the updated ITR-6 form for Assessment Year 2025–26 via Notification No. 44/2025 dated May 6, 2025. This revised form incorporates significant changes aligning with the Finance Act, 2024 and aims to improve reporting accuracy for corporate taxpayers.

### Key Changes in ITR-6 for AY 2025–26

- Capital Gains Reporting: The Schedule-CG has been updated to separately report capital gains accrued before and after July 23, 2024, in line with amendments introduced by the Finance Act, 2024.
- Buyback Loss Treatment: Capital losses on share buybacks are now allowed if the related dividend income is disclosed under ‘Income from Other Sources’—applicable for buybacks post October 1, 2024.
- New Section Reference – 44BBC: The form now includes a reference to Section 44BBC, relating to presumptive taxation for cruise shipping businesses.
- Schedule BP Update (Rule 10TIA): Profits from the sale of rough diamonds must now be declared as 4% or more of gross receipts by Foreign Companies.
- Enhanced Disclosure in Schedule-24(b): Taxpayers claiming interest deductions on housing loans under Section 24(b) will now be required to furnish additional details.
- Schedule-TDS Revision: A new field has been added to report the applicable TDS section code, ensuring more accurate linkage with Form 26AS and TDS returns.
