## Who Should File ITR-6?

All companies registered under the Companies Act, 2013 or the earlier Companies Act, 1956, are required to file their income tax return using Form ITR-6:

- Domestic companies
- Foreign companies
- Firms such as partnerships and limited liability partnerships (LLPs)

## Who Cannot File ITR-6?

Companies whose income is derived from property held for charitable or religious purposes—covered under Section 11—are exempt from filing ITR-6.

## ITR 6 Due Date

The due date for filing the ITR-6 Form depends on the audit requirements of the company. Below are the timelines as per the Income Tax Act:

### 1\. If Accounts are Subject to Audit (Section 44AB):

Due Date: 31st October of the Assessment Year.

### 2\. If International or Specified Domestic Transactions Exist (Form 3CEB):

Due Date: 30th November of the Assessment Year.

### 3\. If No Audit is Required:

Due Date: 31st July of the Assessment Year.

### Mandatory Audit Filing for Companies

- If a company is required to undergo an audit under the Income Tax Act (Section 44AB) or any other applicable law (such as the Companies Act), the following must be ensured:
- Audit Report Submission: The audit report must be submitted electronically by the auditor through the Income Tax e-filing portal.
- Audit Form Requirements: Since companies are audited under the Companies Act, the audit report must be submitted in Form 3CA and Form 3CD.
- Details Required - The ITR-6 form must include:

  - Name and details of the auditor
  - Date of furnishing the audit report
  - Acknowledgement number of the electronically filed report

_[Click here to learn more about the requirements for Form 3CA and 3CD](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/form-3cb-3cd)_

## What is the Structure of the ITR-6 Form?

The ITR-6 Form is comprehensive and divided into two main parts along with multiple detailed schedules. Here's a breakdown:

### Part A – General and Financial Information

- Part A: General Information
- Part A-BS: Balance Sheet as on 31st March
- Part A-BS-Ind AS: Balance Sheet as on 31st March or on the date of business combination (Ind AS compliant)
- Part A-Manufacturing Account: Manufacturing account for the financial year
- Part A-Trading Account: Trading account for the financial year
- Part A-P&L: Profit and Loss account for the financial year
- Part A-Manufacturing Account-Ind AS: Manufacturing account (Ind AS compliant)
- Part A-Trading Account Ind-AS: Trading account (Ind AS compliant)
- Part A-P&L Ind-AS: Profit and Loss account (Ind AS compliant)
- Part A-OI: Other Information
- Part A-QD: Quantitative Details
- Part A-OL: Receipts and Payments Account (for companies under liquidation)

### Part B – Income and Tax Computation

- Part B-TI: Computation of Total Income
- Part B-TTI: Computation of Tax Liability on Total Income

### Schedules in ITR-6 (Total: 46 Schedules)

- Schedule HP: Income from House Property
- Schedule BP: Profits and Gains from Business or Profession
- Schedule DPM: Depreciation on Plant and Machinery
- Schedule DOA: Depreciation on Other Assets
- Schedule DEP: Summary of Depreciation
- Schedule DCG: Deemed Capital Gains on Depreciable Assets
- Schedule ESR: Deduction under Section 35 (Scientific Research)
- Schedule CG: Capital Gains
- Schedule 112A: Sale of equity shares or units with STT under Section 112A
- Schedule 115AD(1)(b)(iii) - Proviso: Sale under Section 112A (for certain non-residents)
- Schedule VDA: Income from transfer of Virtual Digital Assets
- Schedule OS: Income from Other Sources
- Schedule CYLA: Set-off of Current Year’s Losses
- Schedule BFLA: Set-off of Unabsorbed Losses
- Schedule CFL: Losses to be Carried Forward
- Schedule UD: Unabsorbed Depreciation & Section 35(4) Allowances
- Schedule ICDS: Effect of Income Computation and Disclosure Standards
- Schedule 10AA: Deduction under Section 10AA
- Schedule 80G: Donations under Section 80G
- Schedule 80GGA: Donations for Scientific Research or Rural Development
- Schedule 80GGC: Contributions to Political Parties
- Schedule 80IAC: Deduction for Eligible Start-ups
- Schedule 80LA: IFSC/Offshore Banking Deduction
- Schedule RA: Donations to Research Associations
- Schedule 80IA: Deduction under Section 80IA
- Schedule 80IB: Deduction under Section 80IB
- Schedule 80IC/80IE: Deduction under Sections 80IC or 80IE
- Schedule VIA: Deductions under Chapter VIA
- Schedule SI: Income Chargeable at Special Rates
- Schedule IF: Investment in Unincorporated Entities
- Schedule EI: Exempt Income
- Schedule PTI: Pass-through Income from Trusts/Investment Funds
- Schedule MAT: Minimum Alternate Tax (Section 115JB)
- Schedule MATC: MAT Credit (Section 115JAA)
- Schedule BBS: Tax on Buy-back of Shares
- Schedule TPSA: Secondary Transfer Pricing Adjustments
- Schedule 115TD: Accreted Income under Section 115TD
- Schedule FSI: Foreign Source Income
- Schedule TR: Tax Relief for Foreign Taxes Paid
- Schedule FA: Foreign Assets and Income
- Schedule SH-1: Shareholding of Unlisted Companies
- Schedule SH-2: Shareholding of Startups
- Schedule AL-1: Assets and Liabilities (end of year)
- Schedule AL-2: Assets and Liabilities for Startups
- Schedule GST: GST Turnover/Gross Receipts
- Schedule FD: Foreign Currency Payment/Receipt Breakup

### Tax Payment Details Included in the Form

- Advance Tax & Self-Assessment Tax
- TDS (Tax Deducted at Source)
- TCS (Tax Collected at Source)

## Key Changes in ITR-6 Form – AY 2024-25

- Legal Entity Identifier (LEI): Mandatory disclosure of LEI information for companies involved in high-value transactions.
- New Schedule 115TD: Introduced for reporting tax payable on accreted income under Section 115TD.
- Capital Gains Accounts Scheme: Disclosure required if capital gains have been deposited under this scheme.
- Schedule 80GGC (New): Requires reporting of donations made to political parties.
- Schedule 80-IAC (New): Requires details in respect of eligible start-ups claiming deduction.
- Schedule 80LA (New): Requires information about offshore banking units or IFSC entities.
- MSME Dues Disclosure: Mandatory disclosure of amounts payable to Micro and Small Enterprises beyond the prescribed time limit.
- Online Gaming Winnings: Reporting of winnings from online games under the new Section 115BBJ.
- IFSC Dividends: Declaration of dividend income derived from units located in International Financial Services Centres (IFSC).
- Due Date of Return Filing: Companies must specify the applicable due date for filing their return.
- Audit Report Details: Furnishing of the Audit Report Acknowledgement Number and UDIN (Unique Document Identification Number).
- MSME Classification: The Company must disclose if it is recognised as a Micro or Small Enterprise.
- Reason for Tax Audit (Section 44AB): The reason for undergoing a tax audit must be specified.

## Key Changes in ITR-6 Form – AY 2020-21

- Schedule 112A: Introduced for reporting long-term capital gains on sale of equity shares or units liable to STT.
- Section 92CE(2A): Details required on tax payable for secondary adjustments to transfer pricing.
- COVID Relief Reporting: Separate field for tax deduction claims on investments/payments/expenditures made between 1st April 2020 and 30th June 2020 (COVID-related relief period).

## Key Changes in ITR-6 Form – AY 2019-20

- Startup Recognition: Requirement to disclose recognition status as a start-up by DPIIT (Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade).
- Form-2 Declaration: Disclosure of declarations filed in Form-2 (used by start-ups).
- Donation Details: Bifurcation of donations into cash and non-cash modes.
- GST Reporting: Disclosure of turnover or gross receipts as reported in GST returns.

## How to Fill Out the ITR-6 Form

The Income Tax Department recommends the following sequence for completing the ITR-6 Form:

- Part A – Start by filling in General Information, Financial Statements, and Other Relevant Details.
- Schedules – Complete all applicable schedules based on your company’s income, deductions, and disclosures.
- Part B – Enter the computation of total income and tax liability.
- Verification – Finally, complete the verification section and digitally sign the form.

## How to File ITR-6 Form?

The applicant can do the online filing of ITR 6 for companies electronically on the e-filing web portal of the Income-tax Department and verify by way of a digital signature only. Here is the brief procedure for an ITR6 online filing:

### Step 1: Login

- Visit the Income Tax Department's e-filing portal
- Enter your valid User ID (PAN) and password to log in. You'll need to do so if you haven't registered yet.

### Step 2: Go to 'File Income Tax Return

- Once logged in, locate the section for filing income tax returns. This might be labeled "e-File" or "Income Tax Return" depending on the portal's layout.

### Step 3: Select the Assessment Year (AY)

- Choose the relevant assessment year (AY) for filing the ITR. The AY is based on the financial year you're reporting income (previous year + 1). For example, if you file for income earned between April 1, 2023, and March 31, 2024, the AY would be 2024-25.

### Step 4: Select Status and ITR Type

- Here, you'll specify your filing status. Since you're filing for a company, it likely won't be "Individual." It could be "Company" or another category, depending on your business structure.
- Then, choose the ITR form type. Select "ITR 6" from the available options.

### Step 5: Reason for Filing

Indicate the reason for filing the ITR. This could be "Original Return" if it's the first time you're filing for the AY, or "Revised Return" if you're correcting a previously filed return.

### Step 6: Pre-filled Information

- The portal might pre-fill some information based on your previous filings or information received from third parties (like tax deducted at source - TDS). Carefully review this pre-filled data.
- Edit any pre-filled information that's inaccurate or incomplete.

### Step 7: Fill ITR 6 Form

The applicant is required to furnish the following details in the income tax return Form-6 (ITR 6):

General & Company Information

- Basic company details (Name, PAN, Incorporation date, etc.)
- Filing and holding status
- Nature and type of company
- Shareholder and ownership details
- Business structure and nature of business

Audit & Financial Information

- Audit details (under Income Tax Act or other laws)
- Auditor information and audit report details (Form 3CA/3CD)
- Balance Sheet details
- Manufacturing and Trading account details
- Profit and Loss statement

Income Details

- Income from Business or Profession
- Income from House Property
- Capital Gains (including scrip-wise details under section 112A)
- Income from Other Sources
- Presumptive income under sections 44AE, 44B, 44BB, etc.
- Exempt Income
- Foreign Income

Depreciation & Adjustments

- Depreciation on assets (Plant, Machinery, etc.)
- Deemed capital gains on the sale of depreciable assets
- Unabsorbed depreciation and other allowances
- Income Computation Disclosure Standards (ICDS) adjustments

Deductions & Reliefs

- Deductions under Chapter VI-A (80G, 80IA, 80IB, 80IC, 80P, etc.)
- Dedications for donations (scientific research, rural development, political parties)
- Dedication for SEZ units, start-ups, and IFSCs
- Tax relief under the Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (DTAA)

Tax Computation

- Minimum Alternate Tax (MAT) under section 115JB
- Tax credits under section 115JAA
- Tax on distributed profits, share buy-backs, and dividends
- Income chargeable at special rates

Other Disclosures

- Shareholding information (including start-ups)
- Assets and liabilities (for both startups and other companies)
- Pass-through income from investment funds/business trusts
- GST turnover/revenue details
- Foreign currency transaction breakup

Tax Payments & Verification

- Advance Tax, Self-assessment Tax
- [Tax Deducted at Source (TDS)](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/tds-tax-deducted-at-source-all-you-need-to-know) and [Tax Collected at Source (TCS)](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/tax-collected-at-source-tcs)
- Verification and declaration of the return

### Step 8: E-verification

- Once you've completed filling out the ITR6 form, you'll need to verify it electronically. The portal will provide various e-verification methods like Aadhaar OTP, digital signature certificates, etc.
- Choose a convenient method and follow the on-screen instructions to sign the ITR, making it a valid electronic submission.

### Key Notes:

- You are not required to attach any documents with the ITR-6 form—this includes TDS certificates, audit reports, or financial statements. The form is fully self-contained.
- Before submitting the return, make sure to reconcile your tax details with [Form 26AS](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/form-26as)(Tax Credit Statement). This ensures that the taxes deducted, collected, or paid on your behalf match the official records.

## ITR-6 Frequently Asked Questions

### 1\. What is ITR-6?

ITR-6 is an income tax return form applicable to companies that do not claim exemptions under Section 11 (charitable or religious purposes). It is used to report income, claim deductions, and compute tax liability.

### 2\. Who should file ITR-6?

All domestic and foreign companies registered under the Companies Act, except those claiming exemption under Section 11, must file ITR-6.

### 3\. When is the due date for filing ITR-6?

- 31st October: If the company’s accounts are subject to audit
- 30th November: If the company is required to furnish Form 3CEB (international/domestic transfer pricing)
- 31st July: For companies not subject to audit

### 4\. How do I fill out the ITR-6 form?

You need to follow this sequence:

- Part A – General info & financials
- Schedules – Income, deductions, depreciation, etc.
- Part B – Tax computation
- Verification – With DSC (Digital Signature Certificate)

### 5\. Can I file ITR-6 online?

Yes. ITR-6 must be filed online, and it must be verified using a Digital Signature Certificate (DSC).

### 6\. How do I upload ITR-6 on the income tax portal?

You need to:

- Log in to incometax.gov.in
- Prepare and validate the ITR-6 form using the Java or Excel utility
- Upload it under your company profile using a valid DSC

### 7\. Where can I download the ITR-6 form?

You can download the latest ITR-6 form (in Excel/Java format) from the official Income Tax e-Filing portal.

### 8\. What are the key details required in ITR-6?

- Company’s PAN & registration details
- Balance sheet & profit/loss account
- Income from business/profession
- Deductions under various sections
- Depreciation & capital gains
- Foreign income & assets (if applicable)

### 9\. Can I revise ITR-6 after submitting it?

Yes, you can revise ITR-6 if there’s an error or omission, before the end of the assessment year. You can also revise to opt into the New Tax Regime, provided Forms 10IB/10IC/10ID were submitted on time.

### 10\. Is ITR-6 applicable for LLPs or partnerships?

No. LLPs and partnerships should file ITR-5, not ITR-6. ITR-6 is only for companies.

What is the purpose of the ITR-6 form?

The ITR-6 form is an income tax return form that companies registered under the Companies Act are required to file. Its purpose is to report the company's income, claim eligible deductions, and compute the tax liability for the assessment year.

Which companies are required to file ITR-6?

All domestic and foreign companies registered under the Companies Act, except those claiming exemption under Section 11 (for charitable or religious purposes), must file their income tax return using the ITR-6 form.

What is the due date for filing ITR-6?

The due date for filing ITR-6 depends on the company's audit requirements. If the company's accounts are subject to audit, the due date is October 31st of the assessment year. If the company is required to furnish Form 3CEB (related to international/domestic transfer pricing), the due date is November 30th of the assessment year. If no audit is required, the due date is July 31st of the assessment year.

What is the structure of the ITR-6 form?

The ITR-6 form is divided into two main parts: Part A (General and Financial Information) and Part B (Income and Tax Computation). Additionally, there are numerous schedules to report specific details such as income from business, capital gains, deductions claimed, and more.

How do I file the ITR-6 form?

The ITR-6 form must be filed online through the Income Tax Department's e-filing portal. The process involves logging in, selecting the assessment year and ITR form type, filling out the required details, and finally verifying and submitting the form using a Digital Signature Certificate (DSC).

What information is required to complete the ITR-6 form?

To fill out the ITR-6 form, you'll need to provide general company information, financial statements (balance sheet, profit and loss account, etc.), details of income sources, deductions claimed, depreciation calculations, foreign income and assets (if applicable), tax payments made, and more.

Can I revise the ITR-6 form after filing?

Yes, you can revise the ITR-6 form if there are any errors or omissions, as long as it's before the end of the assessment year. It's also possible to revise the form to opt for the New Tax Regime, provided the necessary forms (10IB/10IC/10ID) were submitted on time.

Is ITR-6 applicable for Limited Liability Partnerships (LLPs) or partnerships?

No, ITR-6 is not applicable for LLPs or partnerships. These business entities are required to file their income tax returns using the ITR-5 form, while ITR-6 is specifically for companies registered under the Companies Act.

What are the penalties for not filing or late filing of ITR-6?

Failing to file the ITR-6 form or filing it after the due date can attract penalties under the Income Tax Act. The penalties may include interest on the unpaid tax amount, late filing fees, and potential prosecution in case of repeated non-compliance.

Can I seek professional assistance for filing ITR-6?

Yes, you can seek professional assistance from tax consultants or service providers like IndiaFilings to ensure accurate and timely filing of the ITR-6 form. Their expertise can help you navigate the complexities of tax compliance and avoid potential errors or penalties.

What is the main purpose of company compliance?

The main purpose of company compliance is to ensure that a company follows all relevant laws and regulations applicable to its industry and operations, and to promote ethical and responsible behavior within the organization. Compliance helps create transparency, credibility, and enhances public confidence in the company.

Why is compliance important for a company?

Compliance is crucial for a company as it helps avoid hefty penalties and legal consequences arising from non-compliance. It also opens up investment opportunities, provides a competitive edge in the market, and maintains the active status of the company. Proper compliance ensures accurate data collection and builds trust among stakeholders.

How does compliance enhance a company's credibility?

Compliance enhances a company's credibility by demonstrating that the company is regularly reviewing its operations and adhering to applicable laws and regulations. This transparency and commitment to ethical practices instill confidence in the public, clients, and investors, making the company more credible and trustworthy.

What role does compliance play in attracting investments?

Investors are more likely to invest in companies that are well-compliant and have a strong track record of compliance. Before making any investment, investors thoroughly check the company's financial records and compliance status. Proper and timely compliance increases the company's credibility and makes it more attractive to potential investors.

How can compliance help a company avoid legal issues?

Non-compliance with laws and regulations can lead to legal consequences, such as notices or penalties from regulatory authorities like the Ministry of Corporate Affairs. By ensuring timely and accurate compliance filings, companies can avoid such legal troubles and maintain a clean record.

How does compliance contribute to a company's competitive edge?

Compliance can give a company a competitive advantage in the market. Companies can use their compliance record as an advertising strategy, assuring investors, customers, and stakeholders that the business has been conducted diligently and in accordance with regulations. This can differentiate the company from competitors and enhance its reputation.

Why is accurate data collection important for compliance?

Accurate data collection is essential for compliance because companies are required to disclose financial information and report on their operations truthfully. Annual compliance filings, such as financial returns, provide stakeholders with an accurate picture of the company's financial health and operational status.

How does compliance build trust with stakeholders?

Compliance helps build trust with various stakeholders, including suppliers, vendors, customers, and investors. When a company files compliance reports and discloses information on time, it is perceived as trustworthy and transparent. Stakeholders can have confidence in the company's operations and decision-making processes.

What role does compliance play in maintaining a company's active status?

Proper and timely compliance filings are essential for maintaining a company's active status. Failure to comply with regulatory requirements can result in the company's status being revoked or suspended, which can have severe consequences for its operations and reputation.

How can compliance help a company obtain financial aid and market credit?

Companies that have a strong compliance record and file their compliance reports on time are more likely to be viewed favorably by financial institutions and lenders. This credibility and transparency make it easier for the company to obtain financial aid, loans, or credit from the market, as compared to companies with inadequate compliance records.

content_sections.content:
Internal Compliance refers to an internally designed set of rules and regulations that the owners, employees, traders, and customers follow to maintain the quality of the services or products provided by the organization. These are created and sanctioned by senior professionals and are followed by everyone in the company. Some internal compliance is setting up a Board of Directors, Conducting regular meetings, and distributing stocks to shareholders.Other internal compliance rules you can include:

- Which employee activities you can monitor, and how.
- How to handle discrimination complaints.
- What forms of donations can you make on behalf of your business?
- The penalties for damaging a business resource or property.
- How to address conflicts of interest between employees.

An organization will comply with external requirements only when working in line with internal rules and regulations.

content_sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
content_sections.content:
Common questions aboutDifferent Types of Compliance.

What is compliance, and why is it important for businesses?

Compliance refers to adhering to the rules, laws, and regulations set by governing bodies or internal policies. It is crucial for businesses to maintain compliance as it helps avoid fines, penalties, and potential lawsuits, maintain a professional and secure work environment, and build trust and credibility with stakeholders and the public.

What are the two main types of compliance discussed in the article?

The article discusses two main types of compliance: external compliance and internal compliance. External compliance refers to following rules and regulations set by the government or regulatory bodies, while internal compliance involves adhering to policies and standards established within the organization.

Can you provide examples of external compliance requirements for businesses in India?

Yes, the article lists several statutory compliances that businesses in India must follow, such as the Employees Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provision Act, the Employees State Insurance Corporation Act, the Payment of Wages Act, and the Factories Act of 1948. It also mentions regulatory compliances like accounting and payroll standards, tax regulations, and corporate law requirements.

What are some benefits of maintaining internal compliance within an organization?

Maintaining internal compliance can help organizations set clear standards for what is and isn't acceptable behavior, ensure consistent quality of products or services, and provide a secure and professional environment for employees. Internal compliance policies also help organizations comply with external regulations more effectively.

How can compliance help a business build trust and credibility?

By adhering to relevant laws, regulations, and ethical standards, businesses demonstrate their commitment to operating responsibly and transparently. This can help them establish a positive reputation, build trust with customers, investors, and other stakeholders, and maintain a competitive position in their industry.

What are some examples of internal compliance policies that a business might implement?

Internal compliance policies can cover various aspects of operations, such as employee monitoring, handling discrimination complaints, guidelines for making donations or addressing conflicts of interest, and procedures for addressing damage to company property or resources.

Is compliance a one-time effort, or is it an ongoing process for businesses?

Compliance is an ongoing process for businesses, as laws, regulations, and industry standards are constantly evolving. Organizations need to continually review and update their compliance policies and procedures to ensure they remain compliant and avoid potential penalties or legal issues.

How can businesses ensure that their employees understand and follow compliance requirements?

Businesses can ensure compliance by providing regular training and education on relevant laws, regulations, and internal policies. They should also have clear reporting and enforcement mechanisms in place, as well as channels for employees to raise concerns or seek guidance on compliance matters.

What are the potential consequences of non-compliance for businesses?

Non-compliance can result in severe consequences for businesses, including hefty fines, legal penalties, damage to reputation and credibility, loss of customers or investors, and potential lawsuits or criminal charges in extreme cases.

Can compliance requirements vary across different industries or regions?

Yes, compliance requirements can vary significantly across different industries and regions. For example, businesses in the healthcare or financial sectors may face more stringent regulations related to data privacy and security, while companies in certain regions may need to comply with unique environmental or labor laws specific to their location.

content_sections.heading: Form MGT-7 - Annual Return
content_sections.content:
Form MGT-7 must be filed by all companies registered in India every year. Form MGT-7 is the form for filing annual returns by a company. The due date for filing MGT-7 is 60 days from the date of the

[Annual General Meeting](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/annual-general-meeting-notice-board-resolution-format)

. The due date for conducting annual general meeting is on or before the 30th of September following the end of the financial year. Hence, the due date for filing form MGT-7 is normally the 29th of November. In this article, we look at the procedure for filing Form MGT-7 in detail.

[Explore our article for detailed insights on Company Annual Return Filing through Form MGT-7.](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/complete-guide-to-company-annual-return-filing-using-form-mgt-7)

content_sections.heading: Information Filed in Form MGT-7
content_sections.content:
In Form MGT-7, the company would have to declare the following information about the financial year for which the form is filed:

01. Registered office, principal business activities, particulars of its holding, subsidiary, and associate companies.
02. Shares, debentures, and other securities and shareholding patterns.
03. Details of indebtedness.
04. Details of members and debenture-holders, along with changes therein since the close of the previous financial year
05. Promoters, directors, key managerial personnel, and changes therein since the close of the previous financial year.
06. Meetings of members or a class thereof, Board and its various committees along with attendance details.
07. Remuneration of directors and key managerial personnel.
08. Penalty or punishment imposed on the company, its directors or officers and details of compounding of offenses and appeals made against such penalty or punishment;
09. Matters relating to certification of compliances, disclosures as may be prescribed;
10. Shareholding pattern of the company; and such other matters as required.

To prepare and file form MGT-7, financial and operation information about the financial year would be required. Hence, before preparing MGT-7, a copy of the company's audited financial statement would be required.

content_sections.heading: Documents Filed in Form MGT-7
content_sections.content:

01. Registered office, principal business activities, particulars of its holding, subsidiary, and associate companies.
02. Shares, debentures, and other securities and shareholding patterns.
03. Details of indebtedness.
04. Details of members and debenture-holders, along with changes therein since the close of the previous financial year
05. Promoters, directors, key managerial personnel, and changes therein since the close of the previous financial year.
06. Meetings of members or a class thereof, Board and its various committees along with attendance details.
07. Remuneration of directors and key managerial personnel.
08. Penalty or punishment imposed on the company, its directors or officers and details of compounding of offenses and appeals made against such penalty or punishment;
09. Matters relating to certification of compliances, disclosures as may be prescribed;
10. Shareholding pattern of the company; and such other matters as required.

To prepare and file form MGT-7, financial and operation information about the financial year would be required. Hence, before preparing MGT-7, a copy of the company's audited financial statement would be required.

## Documents Filed in Form MGT-7

or a company secretary in practice.

## Section 92 of the Companies Act

Section 92(1) of the Companies Act deals with the filing of MGT-7 or company annual returns. Section 92 is reproduced below for reference:

**Section 92(1): Every company shall prepare a return (hereinafter referred to as the annual return) in the prescribed form containing the particulars as they stood on the close of the financial year regarding—**

(a) its registered office, principal business activities, particulars of its holding, subsidiary and associate companies;

(b) its shares, debentures, and other securities and shareholding pattern;

(c) its indebtedness;

(d) its members and debenture-holders, along with changes therein since the close of the previous financial year;

(e) its promoters, directors, and key managerial personnel, along with changes therein since the close of the previous financial year;

(f) meetings of members or a class thereof, Board and its various committees, along with attendance details;

(g) remuneration of directors and key managerial personnel;

(h) penalty or punishment imposed on the company, its directors or officers and details of compounding of offenses and appeals made against such penalty or punishment;

(i) matters relating to certification of compliances, disclosures as may be prescribed;

(j) details, as may be prescribed, in respect of shares held by or on behalf of the Foreign Institutional Investors indicating their names, addresses, countries of incorporation, registration, and percentage of shareholding held by them; and

(k) such other matters as may be prescribed and signed by a director and the company secretary, or where there is no company secretary, by a company secretary in practice:

Provided that in relation to One Person Company and small company, the company secretary shall sign the annual return, or where there is no company secretary, by the company director.

content_sections.heading: MCA Form MGT 14
content_sections.content: Running a successful business requires making timely and well-informed decisions. Whether it's a startup, a medium-scale enterprise, or a large corporation, the decisions taken in board meetings are pivotal. To ensure transparency and accountability in these decisions, the Indian Government, under the Companies Act 2013, mandated the filing of Form MGT-14. This form serves as a critical tool for documenting significant resolutions passed in various meetings and submitting them to the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

content_sections.heading: What is MGT 14?
content_sections.content: Form MGT-14, as mandated by the Companies Act 2013, is a crucial document that requires the registration of specific resolutions and agreements with the Registrar of Companies (ROC). This form must be filed following a board meeting once all necessary approvals from the members have been secured.

content_sections.heading: MGT 14 Form Purpose
content_sections.content: The purpose of Form MGT-14 is to ensure transparency and regulatory compliance in corporate governance by requiring companies to file specific resolutions and agreements with the Registrar of Companies (RoC). This form is critical for documenting significant corporate decisions and actions taken during meetings of the company's Board of Directors, shareholders, or creditors. MGT 14 must be filed within 30 days of the resolution's passing or the agreement's execution.

content_sections.heading: Law Governing Form MGT 14
content_sections.content:
eForm MGT-14 is mandated by Sections 94(1) and 117(1) of the Companies Act, 2013, as well as Section 192 of the Companies Act, 1956.

- Section 94(1) requires that registers and annual returns be kept at the company's registered office or another approved location if more than one-tenth of the members reside there, contingent on a special resolution and prior notification to the Registrar.
- Section 117(1) stipulates that a copy of every significant resolution or agreement, along with any explanatory statements, must be filed with the Registrar within 30 days of its approval. This includes resolutions altering the articles of association or any agreement referenced in subsection

Similarly, under the earlier Companies Act of 1956, Section 192 requires that every resolution or agreement be filed with the Registrar within the same timeframe, ensuring all documentation is recorded and compliant with the prescribed legal framework.Understanding the types of resolutions that need to be filed using Form MGT-14 is essential before delving into the details of the filing process and the required documents.MGT-14 is a form that companies in India need to file with the Registrar of Companies (ROC) to report certain resolutions and agreements. Here’s who needs to file it:

content_sections.heading: Types of Resolutions for Filing Form MGT 14
content_sections.content: The MCA Form MGT 14 is used to file three types of resolutions: board resolutions, special resolutions, and written resolutions. Each resolution must be appropriately categorized and filed under its respective type.

content_sections.heading: Ordinary Resolutions
content_sections.content: This resolution requires approval from at least 50% of the board members. Additionally, a majority of the shareholders must agree for the resolution to pass. It generally covers routine governance and operational decisions.

content_sections.heading: Special Resolutions
content_sections.content: These require the approval of at least 75% of the board members. Special resolutions are necessary for significant and extraordinary decisions that go beyond routine management, such as amendments to the company’s Articles of Association or major corporate restructuring.

content_sections.heading: Written Resolutions
content_sections.content:
Approval from at least 75% of the board members is needed for this type, and it must also be signed by all members or shareholders. Written resolutions are typically used when decisions need to be formalized without convening a meeting.Additionally, it's important to note that specific annexures must accompany these resolutions when filed:

- Annexure A is required for all Board Resolutions.
- Annexure B must accompany all Special Resolutions.
- Annexure C is necessary for all Ordinary Resolutions.

content_sections.heading: Applicability of MGT -14
content_sections.content: MGT-14 is a form that companies in India need to file with the Registrar of Companies (ROC) to report certain resolutions and agreements. Here’s who needs to file it:

content_sections.heading: Public Companies:
content_sections.content:
Must file MGT-14 for:

- Special resolutions (important decisions approved by shareholders).
- Key board resolutions (such as approving financial statements, mergers, issuing securities, and granting loans).

content_sections.heading: Private Companies:
content_sections.content:
- Must file MGT-14 for:

  - Special resolutions.

- **Exemptions:**

  - Do not need to file MGT-14 for certain board resolutions (like borrowing money, issuing securities, and making investments).

content_sections.heading: Applicability of MGT-14 for Private Companies
content_sections.content: MGT-14 is required to be submitted by companies to the Registrar of Companies (RoC) under Sections 94(1) and 117(1) of the Companies Act, 2013. However, private companies are exempt from filing certain board resolutions. Specifically, private companies are not required to file MGT-14 for matters listed under Section 179(3) of the Companies Act, 2013, as read with Rule 8 of the Companies (Meetings of Board and its Powers) Rules, 2014. Consequently, private companies do not need to submit e-Form MGT-14 to the RoC when exercising the board's powers as specified under Section 179(3) of the Companies Act 2013.

content_sections.heading: MGT-14 Form Resolutions
content_sections.content: The MGT-14 form is crucial for documenting significant resolutions in a company, categorized under three annexures:

content_sections.heading: Annexure A: Board Resolutions
content_sections.content:
Board resolutions included in Annexure A are:

- Inspection of subsidiary books and records.
- Authorization for political contributions.
- Approval for making investments, loans, guarantees, or security.
- Approval of related party transaction agreements.
- Appointment of whole-time key managerial personnel.
- Managing director appointment if they hold a similar position in another company.
- Approval of self-prospectus.
- Appointment or reappointment of a managing director and variation in terms.
- Calling unpaid share amounts from shareholders.
- Authorization for securities buy-back under Section 68.
- Issuance of securities in India or abroad.
- Borrowing money authorization.
- Approval of the Board’s report and financial statements.
- Business diversification approval.
- Approval for amalgamation, merger, or reconstruction.
- Acquisition of a controlling stake in another firm.

content_sections.heading: Annexure B: Special Resolutions
content_sections.content:
Special resolutions in Annexure B address:

- Adding entrenchment clauses to the Articles of Association.
- Relocating the registered office within the same state.
- Alterations to the Memorandum of Association.
- Changes to objectives when unutilized funds are involved.
- Alterations to the Articles of Association.
- Variations to contract terms or prospectus objectives.
- Issuance of depository receipts abroad.
- Variation of shareholder rights.
- Issuance of sweat equity shares.
- Employee stock options issuance.
- Private securities offerings.
- Convertible debentures or loan issues.
- Reduction of share capital.
- Purchase or subscription of shares for employee benefits.
- Shares buyback.
- Maintaining registers outside the registered office.
- Auditor removal before term expiry.
- Appointing more than 15 directors.
- Independent Director reappointment.
- Limiting directorships.
- Disposal of significant company assets.
- Investing amalgamation or merger compensations differently.
- Borrowing beyond paid-up capital and free reserves.
- Extending repayment time for directors' debts.
- Schemes for providing loans to directors.
- Exceeding prescribed investment limits.
- Appointing directors over the age of 70.
- Company operations investigation.
- Application for company name removal.
- Amalgamation schemes for sick companies.
- Company winding up through tribunal.
- Voluntary company winding up.
- Empowering the liquidator in property sale negotiations.
- Binding creditor arrangements during winding up.
- Empowering the company liquidator.
- Disposal of company documents upon dissolution.

content_sections.heading: Annexure C: Ordinary Resolutions
content_sections.content:
Ordinary resolutions in Annexure C include:

- The company name changed after the registrar's direction due to false information.
- Name change following central government direction due to trademark issues.
- Accepting public deposits.
- Corporate representation at company meetings.
- Representation at creditor meetings.
- Appointment of a statutory auditor other than the retiring one.
- Director removal before their term ends.
- Board power delegation under section 179(3) clauses (d) to (f).
- Non-cash transaction authorization for directors.
- Managing director, whole-time director, or manager appointments.
- Dissolution based on the Company Liquidator's report.
- Voluntary winding up due to term expiry or specific article conditions.
- Contracts with related parties involving significant amounts of capital.

These resolutions are crucial for corporate governance and compliance, detailing the scope and authority of the board in managing company affairs effectively.

content_sections.heading: When is there a Need to File MGT-14?
content_sections.content:
Form MGT-14 must be filed by any company registered under the Companies Act, 2013 or the Companies Act, 1956. The following events or transactions necessitate the filing of Form MGT-14:

- Alteration of the [Memorandum of Association (MOA)](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/memorandum-of-association-moa-a-fundamental-guide)includes changes to the company’s structure or operational purposes.
- Private Placement is when the company issues new securities to a select group of investors.
- Alteration of the [Articles of Association (AOA),](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/memorandum-of-association-moa-a-fundamental-guide) which involves changes to the internal governance rules of the company.
- Modification of the Object Clause in the MOA, which specifies the objectives and types of business activities a company can pursue.
- Utilization of Unspent Proceeds from a public offering as detailed in the issued prospectus.
- Conversion of a Private Company to a Public Limited Company, and vice versa.
- Issuing Additional Shares, either to existing shareholders, employees, or new investors.
- Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) issues, which allow employees to purchase shares at a set price.
- Reclassification of Shares, which might change share classifications or the rights attached to them.
- Issuance of Sweat Equity Shares, which are given to employees as a reward for their contributions to the company.
- Global Depository Receipts (GDR) issuance, involving shares held by a foreign depository that represents underlying shares of the issuing company.
- Legal Proceedings for Winding Up, either through a tribunal or court application.
- [Voluntary Winding Up](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/modes-of-winding-up-of-a-company) under section 304 of the Companies Act.

Each of these situations requires the company to document and file the appropriate resolutions through Form MGT-14 to maintain compliance and transparency with regulatory requirements.

content_sections.heading: MGt 14 Due Date
content_sections.content: The prescribed time period for filing Form MGT-14 is within thirty days from the date the resolution is duly passed and approved by the board members of the concerned company.

content_sections.heading: Documents Required for Form MGT-14
content_sections.content:
When submitting Form MGT-14 to the MCA (Ministry of Corporate Affairs), several essential documents must be included along with the form:

- **Copy of the Resolution or Agreement:** This is the primary document and should include the resolution that was passed concerning the Form MGT-14 being filed.
- **Explanatory Statement:** This document should contain a detailed description and particulars of the resolution passed, providing clarity on the nature and implications of the resolution.
- **Altered Articles:** In cases where there is an alteration or change in the Articles of Association as a result of the resolution, a copy of the amended articles should also be attached to the resolution or agreement.

content_sections.heading: Details Required for Filings MGT 14 Form
content_sections.content:
The MCA Form MGT-14 requires the inclusion of several important details to ensure comprehensive documentation and transparency regarding the resolutions passed by a company. Here are the specific details that need to be provided in the form:

- **[Corporate Identification Number (CIN)](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/cin-number-of-a-company-everything-you-need-to-know):** This is a unique identifier assigned to each company registered under the Registrar of Companies in India.
- **Company Details:** This includes the company's name, registered office address, email ID, and other relevant contact details.
- **Resolution Agreement Details:** Comprehensive information about the documents that need to be registered, particularly the resolution or agreement itself.
- **Dispatch Date:** The date on which the resolution was sent out to the members for approval.
- **Passing Date:** The actual date on which the resolution was approved by the requisite majority.
- Number of Resolutions: The total number of resolutions included in the filing.
- **Resolution Particulars:** Detailed information about each resolution, including its subject matter, purpose, and the authority under which the resolution is being passed.
- **Details on Company Wind-Up:** If applicable, detailed information regarding the decision to wind up the company must be included, outlining the reasons and the process to be followed.

Including all these details in Form MGT-14 ensures that the Registrar of Companies has a full understanding of the actions taken by the company and maintains a transparent record for public access and compliance monitoring.

content_sections.heading: Fee for filing MCA Form MGT-14
content_sections.content:
The fee for filing MCA Form MGT-14 varies based on the amount of share capital a company holds. Here is the detailed fee structure:

- Rs 200 per document for companies with share capital less than Rs 1,00,000.
- Rs 300 per document for companies with share capital between Rs 1,00,000 and Rs 4,99,999.
- Rs 400 per document for companies with share capital between Rs 5,00,000 and Rs 25,99,999.
- Rs 500 per document for companies with share capital between Rs 26,00,000 and Rs 99,99,999.
- Rs 600 per document for companies with share capital of Rs 1,00,00,000 and above.

Additionally, the filing fees increase depending on the delay in the registration process:If there is a delay of up to 30 days, the fees double. Beyond this initial period, the penalty escalates further, increasing the cost significantly the longer the delay continues.It's important for companies to file on time to avoid these steep penalties.

content_sections.heading: MGT 14 Penalty
content_sections.content:
If the company fails to file a resolution document within thirty days of passing, it will incur significant financial penalties. The initial fine for missing this deadline is Rs 1,00,000. Additionally, for each day the filing is delayed beyond the initial 30-day period, an extra charge of Rs 500 per day will be imposed until the document is finally submitted.

content_sections.heading: Procedure for Filing MCA Form MGT-14
content_sections.content: Follow these detailed steps to file MCA Form MGT-14:

content_sections.heading: Visit the MCA Website:
content_sections.content: Access the official website of the Ministry of Corporate Affairs official.

content_sections.heading: Log In to MCA Account:
content_sections.content:
- Click on the "Login" button located at the top right corner of the homepage.
- Enter your User ID and Password, then click on the "Login" button. If you do not have an account, you will need to create one by clicking on "Register" and following the registration process.

content_sections.heading: Download Form MGT-14:
content_sections.content: Before uploading, ensure you have downloaded and filled out Form MGT-14. You can download the form from the "Company Forms Download" section under the "MCA Services" tab.

content_sections.heading: Fill Out Form MGT-14:
content_sections.content: Complete the form with all the necessary details, including company information, resolution details, and explanatory statements. Ensure all mandatory fields are filled, and all required documents are attached.

content_sections.heading: Upload E-forms:
content_sections.content:
- Once logged in, navigate to the "E-Forms" section in the user dashboard.
- Select "Upload E-forms" from the options provided.

content_sections.heading: Select Normal Forms:
content_sections.content:
- Click on "Normal Forms," which will allow you to upload standard forms.
- Click on the "Browse" button to locate and select your saved Form MGT-14 from your computer.

content_sections.heading: Upload the Form:
content_sections.content: After selecting the form, click on the "Upload" button. The system will verify the form and check for any errors. Ensure that your internet connection is stable during this process to avoid interruptions.

content_sections.heading: Generate SRN:
content_sections.content: Once the form is successfully uploaded, the system will generate a Service Request Number (SRN). This SRN is a unique identifier for your form submission.Note down the SRN or save it for future reference, as it will be required for making the payment and tracking the status of your form.

content_sections.heading: Payment of Form Fees:
content_sections.content:
Navigate to the "Payments" section on the MCA portal.

- Enter the SRN generated during the upload process to proceed with the payment.
- Select the payment method (net banking, credit card, debit card, etc.) and complete the payment process. Ensure you receive a confirmation of payment.

content_sections.heading: Confirmation of Submission:
content_sections.content: After successful payment, a confirmation message will be displayed on the screen.You will also receive an acknowledgement receipt on your registered email ID confirming the submission and payment of Form MGT-14.

content_sections.heading: Processing of Form:
content_sections.content:
- The RoC will process the submitted form after the payment is confirmed.
- You can track the status of your form submission using the SRN on the MCA portal.

content_sections.heading: Download MGT Form 14
content_sections.content: You can download Form MGT-14 directly from the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) portal. Please visit the MCA website and navigate to the 'Company Forms Downloads' section to find and download the form.

content_sections.heading: Steps to Follow if  MGT-14 is Not Filed Within 300 Days of Passing a Resolution
content_sections.content:
If a company fails to file the e-form MGT-14 within 300 days of passing a resolution, it faces specific procedural requirements due to the delay. Since MGT-14 necessitates including the SRN (Service Request Number) of form INC-28 and INC-28 can only be submitted after receiving a condonation order from the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA), the company must take the following steps:

- **File Form CG-1 with MCA:** This is to request condonation for the delayed submission of e-form MGT-14.
- **Penalty Imposition:** MCA will issue a condonation order that includes a penalty, which the company must pay.
- **Submission of Proof:** After paying the penalty, the company must submit a copy of the condonation order and the penalty receipt using form INC-28 through the ROC software.
- **Filing of e-form MGT-14:** Once the above steps are completed, the company can submit e-form MGT-14, referencing the SRN of INC-28.

This process ensures that the company rectifies the failure to file on time by following the legal requirements set by the MCA.

content_sections.heading: Conclusion
content_sections.content:
In conclusion, it is mandatory for companies to submit resolutions passed in board meetings to the [Registrar of Companies (RoC)](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/registrar-of-companies-roc) using Form MGT-14. This requirement applies to three types of resolutions, and to avoid penalties, submissions must be made within 30 days of the resolution's approval or the agreement's execution. content_sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
content_sections.content:
Common questions aboutMGT-14.

What is Form MGT-14, and why is it important?

Form MGT-14 is a crucial document required to be filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC) under the Companies Act 2013. It serves to document and register significant resolutions passed during board meetings, shareholder meetings, or creditor meetings. Filing MGT-14 is essential for ensuring transparency and accountability in corporate governance, as it records important decisions made by the company.

What types of resolutions must be filed using Form MGT-14?

The three main types of resolutions that must be filed using Form MGT-14 are board resolutions (Annexure A), special resolutions (Annexure B), and ordinary resolutions (Annexure C). Board resolutions cover matters like appointment of key managerial personnel, approval of financial statements, and issuance of securities. Special resolutions pertain to significant decisions such as amendments to the Articles of Association or company restructuring. Ordinary resolutions include routine matters like the appointment of auditors or delegation of board powers.

Who is required to file Form MGT-14?

Public companies are required to file Form MGT-14 for all special resolutions and key board resolutions. Private companies must file MGT-14 for special resolutions, but they are exempted from filing certain board resolutions related to matters like borrowing money or issuing securities.

What is the deadline for filing Form MGT-14?

Form MGT-14 must be filed within 30 days from the date the resolution is passed or the agreement is executed. Failure to meet this deadline can result in significant penalties.

What documents are required to be submitted along with Form MGT-14?

When filing Form MGT-14, companies must attach a copy of the resolution or agreement, an explanatory statement providing details of the resolution, and a copy of the altered Articles of Association (if applicable).

What are the penalties for failing to file Form MGT-14 on time?

If a company fails to file Form MGT-14 within 30 days, it will incur a minimum penalty of Rs. 1,00,000. Additionally, there is a daily fine of Rs. 500 for each day the filing is delayed beyond the initial 30-day period, until the document is submitted.

How can companies file Form MGT-14 with the MCA?

Companies can file Form MGT-14 electronically through the MCA portal by following these steps: log in to the MCA account, download and fill out the form, upload the form, generate a Service Request Number (SRN), make the payment, and wait for confirmation of submission.

Is there a fee for filing Form MGT-14?

Yes, there is a fee for filing Form MGT-14, which varies based on the company's share capital. The fee ranges from Rs. 200 per document for companies with share capital less than Rs. 1,00,000 to Rs. 600 per document for companies with share capital of Rs. 1,00,00,000 and above.

What should a company do if it fails to file Form MGT-14 within 300 days of passing a resolution?

If a company fails to file Form MGT-14 within 300 days, it must first file Form CG-1 with the MCA to request condonation for the delayed submission. After paying the penalty imposed by the MCA and submitting proof, the company can then file Form MGT-14, referencing the SRN of Form INC-28.

Why is it essential for companies to comply with the MGT-14 filing requirements?

Complying with the MGT-14 filing requirements is crucial for companies to maintain transparency and accountability in their corporate governance practices. It ensures that significant resolutions and decisions are properly documented and registered with the regulatory authorities, promoting trust and confidence among stakeholders, including shareholders, creditors, and the general public.

# MCA Form MGT 14

Running a successful business requires making timely and well-informed decisions. Whether it's a startup, a medium-scale enterprise, or a large corporation, the decisions taken in board meetings are pivotal. To ensure transparency and accountability in these decisions, the Indian Government, under the Companies Act 2013, mandated the filing of Form MGT-14. This form serves as a critical tool for documenting significant resolutions passed in various meetings and submitting them to the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

## What is MGT 14?

Form MGT-14, as mandated by the Companies Act 2013, is a crucial document that requires the registration of specific resolutions and agreements with the Registrar of Companies (ROC). This form must be filed following a board meeting once all necessary approvals from the members have been secured.

## MGT 14 Form Purpose

The purpose of Form MGT-14 is to ensure transparency and regulatory compliance in corporate governance by requiring companies to file specific resolutions and agreements with the Registrar of Companies (RoC). This form is critical for documenting significant corporate decisions and actions taken during meetings of the company's Board of Directors, shareholders, or creditors. MGT 14 must be filed within 30 days of the resolution's passing or the agreement's execution.

## Law Governing Form MGT 14

eForm MGT-14 is mandated by Sections 94(1) and 117(1) of the Companies Act, 2013, as well as Section 192 of the Companies Act, 1956.

- Section 94(1) requires that registers and annual returns be kept at the company's registered office or another approved location if more than one-tenth of the members reside there, contingent on a special resolution and prior notification to the Registrar.
- Section 117(1) stipulates that a copy of every significant resolution or agreement, along with any explanatory statements, must be filed with the Registrar within 30 days of its approval. This includes resolutions altering the articles of association or any agreement referenced in subsection

Similarly, under the earlier Companies Act of 1956, Section 192 requires that every resolution or agreement be filed with the Registrar within the same timeframe, ensuring all documentation is recorded and compliant with the prescribed legal framework.Understanding the types of resolutions that need to be filed using Form MGT-14 is essential before delving into the details of the filing process and the required documents.MGT-14 is a form that companies in India need to file with the Registrar of Companies (ROC) to report certain resolutions and agreements. Here’s who needs to file it:

## Types of Resolutions for Filing Form MGT 14

The MCA Form MGT 14 is used to file three types of resolutions: board resolutions, special resolutions, and written resolutions. Each resolution must be appropriately categorized and filed under its respective type.

### Ordinary Resolutions

This resolution requires approval from at least 50% of the board members. Additionally, a majority of the shareholders must agree for the resolution to pass. It generally covers routine governance and operational decisions.

### Special Resolutions

These require the approval of at least 75% of the board members. Special resolutions are necessary for significant and extraordinary decisions that go beyond routine management, such as amendments to the company’s Articles of Association or major corporate restructuring.

### Written Resolutions

Approval from at least 75% of the board members is needed for this type, and it must also be signed by all members or shareholders. Written resolutions are typically used when decisions need to be formalized without convening a meeting.Additionally, it's important to note that specific annexures must accompany these resolutions when filed:

- Annexure A is required for all Board Resolutions.
- Annexure B must accompany all Special Resolutions.
- Annexure C is necessary for all Ordinary Resolutions.

## Applicability of MGT -14

MGT-14 is a form that companies in India need to file with the Registrar of Companies (ROC) to report certain resolutions and agreements. Here’s who needs to file it:

### Public Companies:

Must file MGT-14 for:

- Special resolutions (important decisions approved by shareholders).
- Key board resolutions (such as approving financial statements, mergers, issuing securities, and granting loans).

### Private Companies:

- Must file MGT-14 for:

  - Special resolutions.

- **Exemptions:**

  - Do not need to file MGT-14 for certain board resolutions (like borrowing money, issuing securities, and making investments).

### Applicability of MGT-14 for Private Companies

MGT-14 is required to be submitted by companies to the Registrar of Companies (RoC) under Sections 94(1) and 117(1) of the Companies Act, 2013. However, private companies are exempt from filing certain board resolutions. Specifically, private companies are not required to file MGT-14 for matters listed under Section 179(3) of the Companies Act, 2013, as read with Rule 8 of the Companies (Meetings of Board and its Powers) Rules, 2014. Consequently, private companies do not need to submit e-Form MGT-14 to the RoC when exercising the board's powers as specified under Section 179(3) of the Companies Act 2013.

## MGT-14 Form Resolutions

The MGT-14 form is crucial for documenting significant resolutions in a company, categorized under three annexures:

### Annexure A: Board Resolutions

Board resolutions included in Annexure A are:

- Inspection of subsidiary books and records.
- Authorization for political contributions.
- Approval for making investments, loans, guarantees, or security.
- Approval of related party transaction agreements.
- Appointment of whole-time key managerial personnel.
- Managing director appointment if they hold a similar position in another company.
- Approval of self-prospectus.
- Appointment or reappointment of a managing director and variation in terms.
- Calling unpaid share amounts from shareholders.
- Authorization for securities buy-back under Section 68.
- Issuance of securities in India or abroad.
- Borrowing money authorization.
- Approval of the Board’s report and financial statements.
- Business diversification approval.
- Approval for amalgamation, merger, or reconstruction.
- Acquisition of a controlling stake in another firm.

### Annexure B: Special Resolutions

Special resolutions in Annexure B address:

- Adding entrenchment clauses to the Articles of Association.
- Relocating the registered office within the same state.
- Alterations to the Memorandum of Association.
- Changes to objectives when unutilized funds are involved.
- Alterations to the Articles of Association.
- Variations to contract terms or prospectus objectives.
- Issuance of depository receipts abroad.
- Variation of shareholder rights.
- Issuance of sweat equity shares.
- Employee stock options issuance.
- Private securities offerings.
- Convertible debentures or loan issues.
- Reduction of share capital.
- Purchase or subscription of shares for employee benefits.
- Shares buyback.
- Maintaining registers outside the registered office.
- Auditor removal before term expiry.
- Appointing more than 15 directors.
- Independent Director reappointment.
- Limiting directorships.
- Disposal of significant company assets.
- Investing amalgamation or merger compensations differently.
- Borrowing beyond paid-up capital and free reserves.
- Extending repayment time for directors' debts.
- Schemes for providing loans to directors.
- Exceeding prescribed investment limits.
- Appointing directors over the age of 70.
- Company operations investigation.
- Application for company name removal.
- Amalgamation schemes for sick companies.
- Company winding up through tribunal.
- Voluntary company winding up.
- Empowering the liquidator in property sale negotiations.
- Binding creditor arrangements during winding up.
- Empowering the company liquidator.
- Disposal of company documents upon dissolution.

### Annexure C: Ordinary Resolutions

Ordinary resolutions in Annexure C include:

- The company name changed after the registrar's direction due to false information.
- Name change following central government direction due to trademark issues.
- Accepting public deposits.
- Corporate representation at company meetings.
- Representation at creditor meetings.
- Appointment of a statutory auditor other than the retiring one.

- Managing director, whole-time director, or manager appointments.
- Dissolution based on the Company Liquidator's report.
- Voluntary winding up due to term expiry or specific article conditions.
- Contracts with related parties involving significant amounts of capital.

These resolutions are crucial for corporate governance and compliance, detailing the scope and authority of the board in managing company affairs effectively.

- Alteration of the [Memorandum of Association (MOA)](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/memorandum-of-association-moa-a-fundamental-guide)includes changes to the company’s structure or operational purposes.
- Private Placement is when the company issues new securities to a select group of investors.

- **Resolution Particulars:** Detailed information about each resolution, including its subject matter, purpose, and the authority under which the resolution is being passed.
- **Details on Company Wind-Up:** If applicable, detailed information regarding the decision to wind up the company must be included, outlining the reasons and the process to be followed.

Including all these details in Form MGT-14 ensures that the Registrar of Companies has a full understanding of the actions taken by the company and maintains a transparent record for public access and compliance monitoring.

## Fee for filing MCA Form MGT-14

The fee for filing MCA Form MGT-14 varies based on the amount of share capital a company holds. Here is the detailed fee structure:

- Rs 200 per document for companies with share capital less than Rs 1,00,000.
- Rs 300 per document for companies with share capital between Rs 1,00,000 and Rs 4,99,999.
- Rs 400 per document for companies with share capital between Rs 5,00,000 and Rs 25,99,999.
- Rs 500 per document for companies with share capital between Rs 26,00,000 and Rs 99,99,999.
- Rs 600 per document for companies with share capital of Rs 1,00,00,000 and above.

Additionally, the filing fees increase depending on the delay in the registration process:If there is a delay of up to 30 days, the fees double. Beyond this initial period, the penalty escalates further, increasing the cost significantly the longer the delay continues.It's important for companies to file on time to avoid these steep penalties.

## MGT 14 Penalty

If the company fails to file a resolution document within thirty days of passing, it will incur significant financial penalties. The initial fine for missing this deadline is Rs 1,00,000. Additionally, for each day the filing is delayed beyond the initial 30-day period, an extra charge of Rs 500 per day will be imposed until the document is finally submitted.

|     |     |
| --- | --- |
| **Defaulting Party** | **Penalty Details** |
| Company | Minimum: Rs 1 lakhFor Continuing Failure: Rs 500 for each dayMaximum: Rs 25 lakh |
| Every Officer in Default (Including the Liquidator) | Minimum: Rs 50,000For Continuing Failure: Rs 500 for each dayMaximum: Rs 5 lakh |

## Procedure for Filing MCA Form MGT-14

Follow these detailed steps to file MCA Form MGT-14:

### Visit the MCA Website:

Access the official website of the Ministry of Corporate Affairs official.

### Log In to MCA Account:

- Click on the "Login" button located at the top right corner of the homepage.
- Enter your User ID and Password, then click on the "Login" button. If you do not have an account, you will need to create one by clicking on "Register" and following the registration process.

### Download Form MGT-14:

Before uploading, ensure you have downloaded and filled out Form MGT-14. You can download the form from the "Company Forms Download" section under the "MCA Services" tab.

### Fill Out Form MGT-14:

Complete the form with all the necessary details, including company information, resolution details, and explanatory statements. Ensure all mandatory fields are filled, and all required documents are attached.

### Upload E-forms:

- Once logged in, navigate to the "E-Forms" section in the user dashboard.
- Select "Upload E-forms" from the options provided.

### Select Normal Forms:

- Click on "Normal Forms," which will allow you to upload standard forms.
- Click on the "Browse" button to locate and select your saved Form MGT-14 from your computer.

### Upload the Form:

After selecting the form, click on the "Upload" button. The system will verify the form and check for any errors. Ensure that your internet connection is stable during this process to avoid interruptions.

### Generate SRN:

Once the form is successfully uploaded, the system will generate a Service Request Number (SRN). This SRN is a unique identifier for your form submission.Note down the SRN or save it for future reference, as it will be required for making the payment and tracking the status of your form.

### Payment of Form Fees:

Navigate to the "Payments" section on the MCA portal.

- Enter the SRN generated during the upload process to proceed with the payment.
- Select the payment method (net banking, credit card, debit card, etc.) and complete the payment process. Ensure you receive a confirmation of payment.

### Confirmation of Submission:

After successful payment, a confirmation message will be displayed on the screen.You will also receive an acknowledgement receipt on your registered email ID confirming the submission and payment of Form MGT-14.

## Processing of Form:

- The RoC will process the submitted form after the payment is confirmed.
- You can track the status of your form submission using the SRN on the MCA portal.

## Download MGT Form 14

You can download Form MGT-14 directly from the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) portal. Please visit the MCA website and navigate to the 'Company Forms Downloads' section to find and download the form.

## Steps to Follow if  MGT-14 is Not Filed Within 300 Days of Passing a Resolution

If a company fails to file the e-form MGT-14 within 300 days of passing a resolution, it faces specific procedural requirements due to the delay. Since MGT-14 necessitates including the SRN (Service Request Number) of form INC-28 and INC-28 can only be submitted after receiving a condonation order from the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA), the company must take the following steps:

- **File Form CG-1 with MCA:** This is to request condonation for the delayed submission of e-form MGT-14.
- **Penalty Imposition:** MCA will issue a condonation order that includes a penalty, which the company must pay.
- **Submission of Proof:** After paying the penalty, the company must submit a copy of the condonation order and the penalty receipt using form INC-28 through the ROC software.
- **Filing of e-form MGT-14:** Once the above steps are completed, the company can submit e-form MGT-14, referencing the SRN of INC-28.

This process ensures that the company rectifies the failure to file on time by following the legal requirements set by the MCA.

## Conclusion

In conclusion, it is mandatory for companies to submit resolutions passed in board meetings to the [Registrar of Companies (RoC)](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/registrar-of-companies-roc) using Form MGT-14. This requirement applies to three types of resolutions, and to avoid penalties, submissions must be made within 30 days of the resolution's approval or the agreement's execution. Form MGT-14 plays a crucial role in documenting important corporate decisions and enhancing transparency and accountability in corporate governance. _For assistance with company compliance and navigating the complexities of Form MGT-14, IndiaFilings offers expert services to help you get started and maintain compliance effectively._[Get Started!](https://www.indiafilings.com/company-annual-filing)

## Frequently Asked Questions

Common questions aboutMGT-14.

What is Form MGT-14, and why is it important?

Form MGT-14 is a crucial document required to be filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC) under the Companies Act 2013. It serves to document and register significant resolutions passed during board meetings, shareholder meetings, or creditor meetings. Filing MGT-14 is essential for ensuring transparency and accountability in corporate governance, as it records important decisions made by the company.

What types of resolutions must be filed using Form MGT-14?

The three main types of resolutions that must be filed using Form MGT-14 are board resolutions (Annexure A), special resolutions (Annexure B), and ordinary resolutions (Annexure C). Board resolutions cover matters like appointment of key managerial personnel, approval of financial statements, and issuance of securities. Special resolutions pertain to significant decisions such as amendments to the Articles of Association or company restructuring. Ordinary resolutions include routine matters like the appointment of auditors or delegation of board powers.

Who is required to file Form MGT-14?

Public companies are required to file Form MGT-14 for all special resolutions and key board resolutions. Private companies must file MGT-14 for special resolutions, but they are exempted from filing certain board resolutions related to matters like borrowing money or issuing securities.

What is the deadline for filing Form MGT-14?

Form MGT-14 must be filed within 30 days from the date the resolution is passed or the agreement is executed. Failure to meet this deadline can result in significant penalties.

What documents are required to be submitted along with Form MGT-14?

When filing Form MGT-14, companies must attach a copy of the resolution or agreement, an explanatory statement providing details of the resolution, and a copy of the altered Articles of Association (if applicable).

What are the penalties for failing to file Form MGT-14 on time?

If a company fails to file Form MGT-14 within 30 days, it will incur a minimum penalty of Rs. 1,00,000. Additionally, there is a daily fine of Rs. 500 for each day the filing is delayed beyond the initial 30-day period, until the document is submitted.

How can companies file Form MGT-14 with the MCA?

Companies can file Form MGT-14 electronically through the MCA portal by following these steps: log in to the MCA account, download and fill out the form, upload the form, generate a Service Request Number (SRN), make the payment, and wait for confirmation of submission.

Is there a fee for filing Form MGT-14?

Yes, there is a fee for filing Form MGT-14, which varies based on the company's share capital. The fee ranges from Rs. 200 per document for companies with share capital less than Rs. 1,00,000 to Rs. 600 per document for companies with share capital of Rs. 1,00,00,000 and above.

What should a company do if it fails to file Form MGT-14 within 300 days of passing a resolution?

If a company fails to file Form MGT-14 within 300 days, it must first file Form CG-1 with the MCA to request condonation for the delayed submission. After paying the penalty imposed by the MCA and submitting proof, the company can then file Form MGT-14, referencing the SRN of Form INC-28.

Why is it essential for companies to comply with the MGT-14 filing requirements?

Complying with the MGT-14 filing requirements is crucial for companies to maintain transparency and accountability in their corporate governance practices. It ensures that significant resolutions and decisions are properly documented and registered with the regulatory authorities, promoting trust and confidence among stakeholders, including shareholders, creditors, and the general public.
