content_sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
content_sections.content:
Common questions aboutWhich ITR Form Should a Company File.

What is an Income Tax Return (ITR)?

An Income Tax Return (ITR) is a form where taxpayers provide information about their income and tax liability to the income tax department. It is mandatory for all taxpayers to file their ITR on or before the due date specified by the government.

What are the different ITR forms available for companies?

The main ITR forms applicable for companies are ITR-4 (for firms other than LLPs), ITR-5 (for LLPs and partnerships), ITR-6 (for companies not claiming exemption under Section 11), and ITR-7 (for companies mandated to file under specific sections).

When should a company file ITR-4?

A company should file ITR-4 if it is a firm other than an LLP, has a total income of up to ₹50 lakhs, and its income is calculated under Sections 44AD, 44ADA, or 44AE of the Income Tax Act.

What type of companies should file ITR-5?

ITR-5 should be filed by Limited Liability Partnerships (LLPs) and other partnership firms. It is specifically designed for partnerships and associations of persons to file their income tax returns.

Can a company claiming exemption under Section 11 file ITR-6?

No, ITR-6 is meant for companies that are not claiming exemption under Section 11 of the Income Tax Act. Companies claiming exemption under Section 11 should file their returns using the appropriate form, such as ITR-7.

When should a company file ITR-7?

ITR-7 should be filed by companies that are mandated to file returns under Sections 139(4A), 139(4B), 139(4C), or 139(4D) of the Income Tax Act. This form is primarily for companies, firms, and trusts that do not fall under any other category of ITR forms.

What personal details are required in an ITR form?

In an ITR form, companies are typically required to provide personal details such as the company's name, Permanent Account Number (PAN), address, and other relevant information about the company's registration and incorporation.

Do companies need to provide details of foreign assets and income in their ITR?

Yes, if a company has foreign assets or income, it is required to provide details of the same in the relevant ITR form. This information is essential for the income tax department to assess the company's total income and tax liability accurately.

Is it mandatory for dormant companies to file ITR?

Yes, according to the article, all companies, irrespective of whether they have made profits or losses, are expected to file ITR returns. Even dormant companies that have not undertaken any business activities in a year are still required to file their income tax returns.

What is the 'Pay Later' option for income tax filing?

The income tax e-filing portal recently introduced a 'Pay Later' option, which allows taxpayers to complete their tax filing process before making any tax payments. This option enables taxpayers to file their returns first and make the tax payment at a later date.

# Which ITR should a company file?

In India, all companies, irrespective of profit or loss, are expected to file ITR returns. Companies that are dormant and have undertaken no business decisions in a year are still expected to file returns. The applicability of ITR forms varies depending on the taxpayer's income sources, the amount of the income earned, and the category of the taxpayer, like individuals, HUF, companies, etc. In this article, we will examine which ITR a company should file.Get in touch with IndiaFilings to file your [Company tax return filing](https://www.indiafilings.com/business-itr-filing).

## Income Tax Return (ITR)

An income Tax Return (ITR) is a form in which the taxpayers file information about their income earned and tax applicable to the [income tax](https://www.indiafilings.com/income-tax-filing) department. To date, the department has notified seven forms, i.e., [ITR-1](https://www.indiafilings.com/itr-1-sahaj-form), [ITR-2](https://www.indiafilings.com/itr-2-form), [ITR-3](https://www.indiafilings.com/itr-3-form), [ITR-4](https://www.indiafilings.com/itr-4-sugam-form), [ITR-5](https://www.indiafilings.com/itr-5-form), [ITR-6](https://www.indiafilings.com/itr-6-form) & ITR-7. Every taxpayer should file his ITR on or before the specified due date.

## Which ITR should a company file?

The type of ITR (Income Tax Return) a company should file depends on the type of company it is.

- **Form ITR-4** – This ITR can be used to File ITR for those firms other than LLPs, which have a total income of up to ₹50 lakhs, and that income is calculated under Sections 44AD, 44ADA, 44AE
- **Form ITR-5** \- This ITR can be used for filing ITR for LLPs and partnerships, not ITR 7.
- **File ITR-6** \- Those companies not claiming exemption under Section 11 can use ITR-6 to file an Income tax return.
- **File ITR-7** – This can be used for those companies that are mandated to file returns from Sections 139(4A), 139(4B), 139(4C), and 139(4D) only.

## Latest Update on the Pay Later Option for Income Tax Filing

The Income Tax e-filing portal has recently rolled out a 'Pay Later' option, allowing you to complete your tax filing process before making any tax payments. You can pay taxes after you are done filing. For additional information, please refer to our guide – [Pay later option for the Income tax return filing](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/pay-later-option-for-the-income-tax-return-filing).

## ITR 4 Form (Sugam) - For firms other than LLPs

[ITR-4 return filing](https://www.indiafilings.com/itr-4-sugam-form) is a form for ITR filing which should be used by assessees having a business income. Only assesses who have opted for a presumptive taxation scheme should use Form ITR 4.

### Applicability

Form ITR 4 (Sugam) should be filed when the following conditions are satisfied:

- The assessee falls under either one of the following categories:
  - Individual,
  - Hindu Undivided Family(HUF), or
  - Partnership firm which is not a [Limited Liability Partnership](https://www.indiafilings.com/llp-registration) (LLP)
- The assessee is considered an ordinary resident per Section 6(6) of the Income Tax Act.
- The assessee obtains income under the heading Profits and Gains of Business or Profession as mentioned in Section 28 of the Income Tax Act.
- The assessee has opted for a presumptive taxation scheme under Sections 44AD, 44ADA or 44AE
- The assessee's taxable income is calculated in the manner provided in Sections 44AD, 44ADA, or 44AE.
- The assessee is covered by the requirement to file Form 3CA or 3CB and also Form 3CD as per Rule 6G

ITR-7 (Income Tax Return 7) is a form used for filing income tax returns by persons, including companies, who are required to furnish returns under section 139(4A) or section 139(4B), or section 139(4C), or section 139(4D) of the Income Tax Act, 1961.ITR-7 applies to the following entities:

## Details required in an ITR form

The details required in an ITR form vary based on the type of ITR form. However, in general, the following information is required:

- **Personal details:** Name, permanent account numbers (PAN), address, date of birth, and other personal details.
- **Details of income:** Information about the taxpayer's income from salary, business or profession, capital gains, and other sources.
- **Details of deductions and exemptions:** Information about deductions claimed under various sections of the Income Tax Act, 1961, and exemptions claimed for investments in specified savings instruments.
- **Details of tax payments:** Information about taxes paid, including advance tax, self-assessment tax, and TDS (tax deducted at source).
- Details of foreign assets and income: If applicable, information about foreign assets and income.
- Signature and verification: The Formtaxpayer or authorized signatory must sign and verify the form.

It is essential to provide accurate information in the ITR form to avoid penalties and legal consequences for filing false tax returns.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Common questions aboutWhich ITR Form Should a Company File.

What is an Income Tax Return (ITR)?

An Income Tax Return (ITR) is a form where taxpayers provide information about their income and tax liability to the income tax department. It is mandatory for all taxpayers to file their ITR on or before the due date specified by the government.

What are the different ITR forms available for companies?

The main ITR forms applicable for companies are ITR-4 (for firms other than LLPs), ITR-5 (for LLPs and partnerships), ITR-6 (for companies not claiming exemption under Section 11), and ITR-7 (for companies mandated to file under specific sections).

When should a company file ITR-4?

A company should file ITR-4 if it is a firm other than an LLP, has a total income of up to ₹50 lakhs, and its income is calculated under Sections 44AD, 44ADA, or 44AE of the Income Tax Act.

What type of companies should file ITR-5?

ITR-5 should be filed by Limited Liability Partnerships (LLPs) and other partnership firms. It is specifically designed for partnerships and associations of persons to file their income tax returns.

Can a company claiming exemption under Section 11 file ITR-6?

No, ITR-6 is meant for companies that are not claiming exemption under Section 11 of the Income Tax Act. Companies claiming exemption under Section 11 should file their returns using the appropriate form, such as ITR-7.

When should a company file ITR-7?

ITR-7 should be filed by companies that are mandated to file returns under Sections 139(4A), 139(4B), 139(4C), or 139(4D) of the Income Tax Act. This form is primarily for companies, firms, and trusts that do not fall under any other category of ITR forms.

What personal details are required in an ITR form?

In an ITR form, companies are typically required to provide personal details such as the company's name, Permanent Account Number (PAN), address, and other relevant information about the company's registration and incorporation.

Do companies need to provide details of foreign assets and income in their ITR?

Yes, if a company has foreign assets or income, it is required to provide details of the same in the relevant ITR form. This information is essential for the income tax department to assess the company's total income and tax liability accurately.

Is it mandatory for dormant companies to file ITR?

Yes, according to the article, all companies, irrespective of whether they have made profits or losses, are expected to file ITR returns. Even dormant companies that have not undertaken any business activities in a year are still required to file their income tax returns.

What is the 'Pay Later' option for income tax filing?

The income tax e-filing portal recently introduced a 'Pay Later' option, which allows taxpayers to complete their tax filing process before making any tax payments. This option enables taxpayers to file their returns first and make the tax payment at a later date.

blogs.title: FCRA Registration for Trusts and NGOs

content_sections.heading: FCRA Registration for Trusts and NGOs
content_sections.content:
Charitable Trusts, Societies,

[Section 8 Company](https://www.indiafilings.com/section-8-company-registration) that receive foreign contribution or donation from foreign sources are required to obtain registration under Section 6(1) of Foreign Contribution Regulation Act, 2010. Such a registration under the Foreign Contribution Regulation Act, 2010 is called a FCRA registration. In this article, we look at the procedure for obtaining FCRA registration in India.

content_sections.heading: Eligibility for obtaining FCRA Registration
content_sections.content:
Organizations seeking foreign contributions for definite cultural, social, economic, educational or religious programmes may obtain FCRA registration or receive foreign contribution through "prior permission" route. It is preferable for an FCRA applicant to be a Trust or Society or a Section 8 Company. The not-for-profit entity must have also been in existence for a minimum of three years while making the FCRA application and should not have received any foreign contribution prior to that without the Government's approval. Additionally, the entity seeking registration should have spent at least Rs.10,00,000/- over the last three years on its aims and objects, excluding administrative expenditure. Statements of Income & Expenditure, duly audited by Chartered Accountant, for last three years are to be submitted to substantiate that it meets the financial parameter.

In case a newly registered entity would like to receive foreign contributions, then approval for a specific activity, specific purpose and from a specific source can be made to the Ministry of Home Affairs through the Prior Permission (PP) method.

content_sections.heading: Criteria for grant of FCRA Registration
Applying for FCRA Registration
Online FCRA Registration process
content_sections.content:
The procedure for online FCRA registration is explained here.

**Step 1:** Go to FCRA online portal.

**Step 2:** Click on ‘FCRA online forms’ to register in FCRA.

![Image 1 FCRA Registration for Trusts and NGOs](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/Image-1-FCRA-Registration-for-Trusts-and-NGOs.jpg) Image 1 FCRA Registration for Trusts and NGOs

**Step 3:** In the next screen select application for FCRA registration link. The link will redirect to next page.

![Image 2 FCRA Registration for Trusts and NGOs](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/Image-2-FCRA-Registration-for-Trusts-and-NGOs.jpg) Image 2 FCRA Registration for Trusts and NGOs

**Step 4:** Click on 'Click to apply online' button to apply for FC3 (Registration).

![Image 3 FCRA Registration for Trusts and NGOs](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/Image-3-FCRA-Registration-for-Trusts-and-NGOs-1.jpg) Image 3 FCRA Registration for Trusts and NGOs

**Sign up for FCRA Account** **Step 5:** You need to sign up into FCRA, select sign-up option. The link will move to next page.

![Image 4 FCRA Registration for Trusts and NGOs](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/Image-4-FCRA-Registration-for-Trusts-and-NGOs.jpg) Image 4 FCRA Registration for Trusts and NGOs

**Step 6:** Enter all mandatory details and click on save.

![Image 5 FCRA Registration for Trusts and NGOs](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/Image-5-FCRA-Registration-for-Trusts-and-NGOs.jpg) Image 5 FCRA Registration for Trusts and NGOs

![Image 6 FCRA Registration for Trusts and NGOs](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/Image-6-FCRA-Registration-for-Trusts-and-NGOs.jpg) Image 6 FCRA Registration for Trusts and NGOs

**Step 7:** On clicking on save a message will be shown in the screen ‘User ID successfully created and Your user ID is:’

**Login to FCRA** **Step 8:** Login into the portal using this User ID and password.

**Step 9:** You can see an option ‘I am applying for’ select FCRA registration from drop-down menu. Click on Apply online.

**Step 10:** To proceed registration ‘click here to Proceed New Registration’

**Step 11:** Click on FC3 Menu in title bar for proceedings step by step registration.

**Association Details** **Step 12:** Select Association Details from the menu. The association detail form will be displayed. Enter all below mentioned mandatory details.

- Darpan ID
- Address of Association
- Registration number
- Place of registration
- Date of registration
- Nature of association
- Main aim of the association

**Step 13:** Click on submit button to save data.

**Executive Committee Form** **Step 14:** Now go to Executive Committee Form by clicking on Executive Committee option from menu bar.

**Step 16:** Enter all details about Executive Committee.

**Step 17:** Select ‘Add details of Key Functionary’, you can now edit/delete/add Details of Information of Executive Committee.

**Step 18:** To add further foreigner details, select checkbox of the record which one you want and click on Add/View button.

**Step 19:** New screen will be displayed, add related foreigner details. You can able to Edit/Delete Record by clicking on the appropriate option.

**EC detail and others** **Step 20:** You need to fill EC details and others. Select this option from the menu list.

**Step 21:** Click on save after entering all mandatory details of EC.

**Bank Details** **Step 22:** In this section provide your bank details such as Bank Name, IFSC code, Account Number, Address of the bank.

**Other details Section** **Step 23:** Click on Other Details option from the menu to provide all other information.

**Upload documents** **Step 24:** You need to upload all relevant documents in PDF format.

**Final Submission** **Step 25:** Click on final submission from the menu bar. You have to declare the application form, enter place and date and click on final submit.

**Step 26:** Once you submitted finally, a pop-up window will appear, click on OK.

Note: After final submission, you can’t modify application details.

**Online payment** **Step 27:** After clicking on Make Online Payment button from menu bar, the payment screen will be displayed.

**Step 28:** Click on Continue for Payment button in this screen, a screen will be pop up on the screen. Select the payment gateway and click on payment.

content_sections.heading: Renewal of FCRA Registration
content_sections.content:
Once FCRA registration is granted, it is valid for a period of five years. An application for renewal of FCRA registration can be made 6 months prior to the date of expiry, to keep the registration valid.

**Step 1:** Select Application for Renewal of FCRA Registration from FCRA Online Forms.

![Image 7 FCRA Registration for Trusts and NGOs](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/Image-7-FCRA-Registration-for-Trusts-and-NGOs.jpg) Image 7 FCRA Registration for Trusts and NGOs

**Step 2:** On clicking on this, the page will be redirected to next page. Select Click to apply online.

**Step 3:** Enter your user ID & password and login to the FCRA portal.

**Step 4:** You can see an option ‘I am applying for’ select FCRA renewal from drop-down menu. For renewing FCRA registration follow above given steps 10 to 28.

**To obtain FCRA Registration in India, get in touch with a [Contact CA](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/fcra-registration-for-trusts-and-ngos) or IndiaFilings Business Advisor.**

content_sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
content_sections.content:
Common questions aboutFCRA Registration for NGOs & Trusts.

What is FCRA registration?

FCRA registration refers to the registration obtained under Section 6(1) of the Foreign Contribution Regulation Act, 2010 by organizations that receive foreign contributions or donations from foreign sources for definite cultural, social, economic, educational or religious programs.

Who is eligible to apply for FCRA registration?

Organizations like Charitable Trusts, Societies, or Section 8 Companies that have been in existence for a minimum of three years and have spent at least Rs. 10,00,000/- over the last three years on their aims and objects, excluding administrative expenditure, are eligible to apply for FCRA registration.

What are the criteria for granting FCRA registration?

The criteria for granting FCRA registration include factors such as ensuring the organization is not fictitious or engaged in activities aimed at forceful religious conversion, creating communal tension, or advocating sedition. The foreign contribution should not affect India's sovereignty, security, public interest, or fair elections.

How can an organization apply for FCRA registration?

Organizations can apply for FCRA registration using Form FC-3, along with required documents like registration certificate, activity report, and audited financial statements for the past three years. The application can be submitted online through the FCRA online portal.

What is the validity period of FCRA registration?

FCRA registration is valid for a period of five years. An application for renewal of FCRA registration can be made six months prior to the date of expiry to keep the registration valid.

Can a newly registered organization receive foreign contributions?

Yes, a newly registered organization can receive foreign contributions through the Prior Permission (PP) method, where approval is sought from the Ministry of Home Affairs for a specific activity, purpose, and source.

What documents are required for FCRA registration?

The documents required for FCRA registration include self-certified copies of registration certificate/Trust deed, Memorandum of Association/Articles of Association, activity report for the last three years, and audited financial statements (Assets and Liabilities, Receipt and Payment, Income and Expenditure) for the past three years.

What is the purpose of the FCRA online portal?

The FCRA online portal is a platform where organizations can apply for FCRA registration, renewal, and make online payments for the application process. It streamlines the application procedure and facilitates the submission of required documents.

Can an organization with a pending prosecution apply for FCRA registration?

No, an organization where any of its directors or office bearers have been prosecuted or convicted under any law for the time being in force, or have a pending prosecution, is not eligible to apply for FCRA registration.

What happens if an organization fails to meet the criteria for FCRA registration?

If an organization fails to meet the criteria for FCRA registration, such as being involved in activities that affect India's sovereignty or security, or likely to misuse foreign contributions, the registration may be denied. The acceptance of foreign contribution should not lead to incitement of an offense or endanger anyone's life or physical safety.

# FCRA Registration for Trusts and NGOs

Charitable Trusts, Societies,

[Section 8 Company](https://www.indiafilings.com/section-8-company-registration) that receive foreign contribution or donation from foreign sources are required to obtain registration under Section 6(1) of Foreign Contribution Regulation Act, 2010. Such a registration under the Foreign Contribution Regulation Act, 2010 is called a FCRA registration. In this article, we look at the procedure for obtaining FCRA registration in India.

## Eligibility for obtaining FCRA Registration

Organizations seeking foreign contributions for definite cultural, social, economic, educational or religious programmes may obtain FCRA registration or receive foreign contribution through "prior permission" route. It is preferable for an FCRA applicant to be a Trust or Society or a Section 8 Company. The not-for-profit entity must have also been in existence for a minimum of three years while making the FCRA application and should not have received any foreign contribution prior to that without the Government's approval. Additionally, the entity seeking registration should have spent at least Rs.10,00,000/- over the last three years on its aims and objects, excluding administrative expenditure. Statements of Income & Expenditure, duly audited by Chartered Accountant, for last three years are to be submitted to substantiate that it meets the financial parameter.

In case a newly registered entity would like to receive foreign contributions, then approval for a specific activity, specific purpose and from a specific source can be made to the Ministry of Home Affairs through the Prior Permission (PP) method.

## Criteria for grant of FCRA Registration

Once, an FCRA application is made in the prescribed format, the following criteria are check before providing registration.

**The 'person' or 'entity' making an application for registration or grant of prior permission-**

- Is not fictitious or benami;
- Has not been prosecuted or convicted for indulging in activities aimed at conversion through inducement or force, either directly or indirectly, from one religious faith to another;
- Has not been prosecuted or convicted for creating communal tension or disharmony in any specified district or any other part of the country;
- Has not been found guilty of diversion or mis-utilisation of its funds;
- Is not engaged or likely to engage in propagation of sedition or advocate violent methods to achieve its ends;
- Is not likely to use the foreign contribution for personal gains or divert it for undesirable purposes;
- Has not contravened any of the provisions of this Act;
- Has not been prohibited from accepting foreign contribution;
- The person being an individual, such individual has neither been convicted under any law for the time being in force nor any prosecution for any offence is pending against him.
- The person being other than an individual, any of its directors or office bearers has neither been convicted under any law for the time being in force nor any prosecution for any offence is pending against him.

**The acceptance of foreign contribution by the entity / person is not likely to affect prejudicially –**

- The sovereignty and integrity of India;
- The security, strategic, scientific or economic interest of the State;
- The public interest;
- Freedom or fairness of election to any Legislature;
- Friendly relation with any foreign State;
- Harmony between religious, racial, social, linguistic, regional groups, castes or communities.

**The acceptance of foreign contribution-**

- Shall not lead to incitement of an offence;
- Shall not endanger the life or physical safety of any person.

## Applying for FCRA Registration

Application for FCRA registration can be made using Form FC-3. Along with the application, the following documents must be submitted:

- Self-certified copy of registration certificate/Trust deed etc., of the association
- Self-certified copy of relevant pages of Memorandum of Association/ Article of Association showing aim and objects of the association.
- Activity Report indicating details of activities during the last three years;
- Copies of relevant audited statement of accounts for the past three years (Assets and Liabilities, Receipt and Payment, Income and Expenditure) clearly reflecting expenditure incurred on aims and objects of the association and on administrative expenditure;

Once FCRA registration is granted, it is valid for a period of five years. An application for renewal of FCRA registration can be made 6 months prior to the date of expiry, to keep the registration valid.

## **Online FCRA Registration process**

The procedure for online FCRA registration is explained here.

**Step 1:** Go to FCRA online portal.

**Step 2:** Click on ‘FCRA online forms’ to register in FCRA.

![Image 1 FCRA Registration for Trusts and NGOs](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/Image-1-FCRA-Registration-for-Trusts-and-NGOs.jpg) Image 1 FCRA Registration for Trusts and NGOs

**Step 3:** In the next screen select application for FCRA registration link. The link will redirect to next page.

![Image 2 FCRA Registration for Trusts and NGOs](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/Image-2-FCRA-Registration-for-Trusts-and-NGOs.jpg) Image 2 FCRA Registration for Trusts and NGOs

**Step 4:** Click on 'Click to apply online' button to apply for FC3 (Registration).

![Image 3 FCRA Registration for Trusts and NGOs](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/Image-3-FCRA-Registration-for-Trusts-and-NGOs-1.jpg) Image 3 FCRA Registration for Trusts and NGOs

**Sign up for FCRA Account** **Step 5:** You need to sign up into FCRA, select sign-up option. The link will move to next page.

![Image 4 FCRA Registration for Trusts and NGOs](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/Image-4-FCRA-Registration-for-Trusts-and-NGOs.jpg) Image 4 FCRA Registration for Trusts and NGOs

**Step 6:** Enter all mandatory details and click on save.

![Image 5 FCRA Registration for Trusts and NGOs](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/Image-5-FCRA-Registration-for-Trusts-and-NGOs.jpg) Image 5 FCRA Registration for Trusts and NGOs

![Image 6 FCRA Registration for Trusts and NGOs](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/Image-6-FCRA-Registration-for-Trusts-and-NGOs.jpg) Image 6 FCRA Registration for Trusts and NGOs

**Step 7:** On clicking on save a message will be shown in the screen ‘User ID successfully created and Your user ID is:’

**Login to FCRA** **Step 8:** Login into the portal using this User ID and password.

**Step 9:** You can see an option ‘I am applying for’ select FCRA registration from drop-down menu. Click on Apply online.

**Step 10:** To proceed registration ‘click here to Proceed New Registration’

**Step 11:** Click on FC3 Menu in title bar for proceedings step by step registration.

**Association Details** **Step 12:** Select Association Details from the menu. The association detail form will be displayed. Enter all below mentioned mandatory details.

- Darpan ID
- Address of Association
- Registration number
- Place of registration
- Date of registration
- Nature of association
- Main aim of the association

**Step 13:** Click on submit button to save data.

**Executive Committee Form** **Step 14:** Now go to Executive Committee Form by clicking on Executive Committee option from menu bar.

**Step 16:** Enter all details about Executive Committee.

**Step 17:** Select ‘Add details of Key Functionary’, you can now edit/delete/add Details of Information of Executive Committee.

**Step 18:** To add further foreigner details, select checkbox of the record which one you want and click on Add/View button.

**Step 19:** New screen will be displayed, add related foreigner details. You can able to Edit/Delete Record by clicking on the appropriate option.

**EC detail and others** **Step 20:** You need to fill EC details and others. Select this option from the menu list.

**Step 21:** Click on save after entering all mandatory details of EC.

**Bank Details** **Step 22:** In this section provide your bank details such as Bank Name, IFSC code, Account Number, Address of the bank.

**Other details Section** **Step 23:** Click on Other Details option from the menu to provide all other information.

**Upload documents** **Step 24:** You need to upload all relevant documents in PDF format.

**Final Submission** **Step 25:** Click on final submission from the menu bar. You have to declare the application form, enter place and date and click on final submit.

**Step 26:** Once you submitted finally, a pop-up window will appear, click on OK.

Note: After final submission, you can’t modify application details.

**Online payment** **Step 27:** After clicking on Make Online Payment button from menu bar, the payment screen will be displayed.

**Step 28:** Click on Continue for Payment button in this screen, a screen will be pop up on the screen. Select the payment gateway and click on payment.

## **Renewal of FCRA Registration**

Once FCRA registration is granted, it is valid for a period of five years. An application for renewal of FCRA registration can be made 6 months prior to the date of expiry, to keep the registration valid.

**Step 1:** Select Application for Renewal of FCRA Registration from FCRA Online Forms.

![Image 7 FCRA Registration for Trusts and NGOs](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/Image-7-FCRA-Registration-for-Trusts-and-NGOs.jpg) Image 7 FCRA Registration for Trusts and NGOs

**Step 2:** On clicking on this, the page will be redirected to next page. Select Click to apply online.

**Step 3:** Enter your user ID & password and login to the FCRA portal.

**Step 4:** You can see an option ‘I am applying for’ select FCRA renewal from drop-down menu. For renewing FCRA registration follow above given steps 10 to 28.

**To obtain FCRA Registration in India, get in touch with a [Contact CA](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/fcra-registration-for-trusts-and-ngos) or IndiaFilings Business Advisor.**

[Back to Learn](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn)

## Frequently Asked Questions

Common questions aboutFCRA Registration for NGOs & Trusts.

What is FCRA registration?

FCRA registration refers to the registration obtained under Section 6(1) of the Foreign Contribution Regulation Act, 2010 by organizations that receive foreign contributions or donations from foreign sources for definite cultural, social, economic, educational or religious programs.

Who is eligible to apply for FCRA registration?

Organizations like Charitable Trusts, Societies, or Section 8 Companies that have been in existence for a minimum of three years and have spent at least Rs. 10,00,000/- over the last three years on their aims and objects, excluding administrative expenditure, are eligible to apply for FCRA registration.

What are the criteria for granting FCRA registration?

The criteria for granting FCRA registration include factors such as ensuring the organization is not fictitious or engaged in activities aimed at forceful religious conversion, creating communal tension, or advocating sedition. The foreign contribution should not affect India's sovereignty, security, public interest, or fair elections.

How can an organization apply for FCRA registration?

Organizations can apply for FCRA registration using Form FC-3, along with required documents like registration certificate, activity report, and audited financial statements for the past three years. The application can be submitted online through the FCRA online portal.

What is the validity period of FCRA registration?

FCRA registration is valid for a period of five years. An application for renewal of FCRA registration can be made six months prior to the date of expiry to keep the registration valid.

Can a newly registered organization receive foreign contributions?

Yes, a newly registered organization can receive foreign contributions through the Prior Permission (PP) method, where approval is sought from the Ministry of Home Affairs for a specific activity, purpose, and source.

What documents are required for FCRA registration?

The documents required for FCRA registration include self-certified copies of registration certificate/Trust deed, Memorandum of Association/Articles of Association, activity report for the last three years, and audited financial statements (Assets and Liabilities, Receipt and Payment, Income and Expenditure) for the past three years.

What is the purpose of the FCRA online portal?

The FCRA online portal is a platform where organizations can apply for FCRA registration, renewal, and make online payments for the application process. It streamlines the application procedure and facilitates the submission of required documents.

Can an organization with a pending prosecution apply for FCRA registration?

No, an organization where any of its directors or office bearers have been prosecuted or convicted under any law for the time being in force, or have a pending prosecution, is not eligible to apply for FCRA registration.

What happens if an organization fails to meet the criteria for FCRA registration?

If an organization fails to meet the criteria for FCRA registration, such as being involved in activities that affect India's sovereignty or security, or likely to misuse foreign contributions, the registration may be denied. The acceptance of foreign contribution should not lead to incitement of an offense or endanger anyone's life or physical safety.

content_sections.content:

content_sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
content_sections.content:
Common questions aboutTrademark Form TM-48.

What is the purpose of Form TM 48?

Form TM 48, also known as the Power of Attorney, is required when a trademark application is filed by a person other than the trademark applicant. It authorizes a trademark attorney or agent to act on behalf of the applicant for the registration, protection, renewal, and maintenance of the trademark.

Who can execute Form TM 48?

Form TM 48 must be executed by the trademark applicant in favor of the trademark attorney or agent who will be representing them in the trademark registration process.

Can Form TM 48 be executed in favor of a firm or company?

No, Form TM 48 must be executed in favor of an individual trademark agent or attorney. A Power of Attorney in favor of a firm without mentioning the name of an individual agent or attorney is not acceptable.

What is the format of Form TM 48?

The format of Form TM 48 includes the applicant's name and address, the authorized agent's name and address, a statement authorizing the agent to act on behalf of the applicant, and a revocation of any previous authorizations.

On what type of paper should Form TM 48 be printed?

Form TM 48 must be printed on a non-judicial stamp paper of Rs. 100 value.

When should Form TM 48 be filed?

Form TM 48 should be filed along with the trademark application if the application is being filed by a trademark attorney or agent on behalf of the applicant.

Can Form TM 48 be revoked?

Yes, Form TM 48 can be revoked by the applicant. The revocation statement is included in the form itself, where the applicant can revoke all previous authorizations, if any.

Is it necessary to mention the respective Trademark Office in Form TM 48?

Yes, the respective Trademark Office where the trademark application is being filed should be mentioned in Form TM 48.

Can a substitute agent be appointed through Form TM 48?

Yes, Form TM 48 includes a provision for authorizing the appointed agent to appoint a substitute or substitutes as they may deem necessary or expedient in connection with the trademark registration process.

What is the significance of the date in Form TM 48?

The date on which Form TM 48 is executed by the trademark applicant is mentioned in the form. This date serves as a reference for the validity and effectiveness of the Power of Attorney.

# Trademark Form TM 48

When a trademark application is filed by someone other than the trademark applicant, a duly stamped TM-48 or Power of Attorney must be filed. This article delves into the trademark Form TM 48 format and the filing procedure.

## Form TM 48 Requirement

If a trademark application has been submitted by a trademark attorney, representative, or authorized agent, the applicant must execute a Power of Attorney (Form TM 48) to empower the filing agent. Remember, the Power of Attorney must be directed to an individual agent or attorney. Form 48 granted to a firm without a specific agent mentioned is unacceptable. What is the purpose of Form TM 48?

Form TM 48, also known as the Power of Attorney, is required when a trademark application is filed by a person other than the trademark applicant. It authorizes a trademark attorney or agent to act on behalf of the applicant for the registration, protection, renewal, and maintenance of the trademark.

Who can execute Form TM 48?

Form TM 48 must be executed by the trademark applicant in favor of the trademark attorney or agent who will be representing them in the trademark registration process.

Can Form TM 48 be executed in favor of a firm or company?

No, Form TM 48 must be executed in favor of an individual trademark agent or attorney. A Power of Attorney in favor of a firm without mentioning the name of an individual agent or attorney is not acceptable.

What is the format of Form TM 48?

The format of Form TM 48 includes the applicant's name and address, the authorized agent's name and address, a statement authorizing the agent to act on behalf of the applicant, and a revocation of any previous authorizations.

On what type of paper should Form TM 48 be printed?

Form TM 48 must be printed on a non-judicial stamp paper of Rs. 100 value.

When should Form TM 48 be filed?

Form TM 48 should be filed along with the trademark application if the application is being filed by a trademark attorney or agent on behalf of the applicant.

Can Form TM 48 be revoked?

Yes, Form TM 48 can be revoked by the applicant. The revocation statement is included in the form itself, where the applicant can revoke all previous authorizations, if any.

Is it necessary to mention the respective Trademark Office in Form TM 48?

Yes, the respective Trademark Office where the trademark application is being filed should be mentioned in Form TM 48.

The date on which Form TM 48 is executed by the trademark applicant is mentioned in the form. This date serves as a reference for the validity and effectiveness of the Power of Attorney.

content_sections.heading: Grounds for Trademark Rectification in India
content_sections.content:
In India, Section 57 of the Trade Marks Act (1999) outlines the grounds for rectification of trademark and proceedings of the relevant authorities,

1. **Contravention or Failure to Observe Conditions:** If any person feels aggrieved due to a violation or failure to observe a condition related to a trademark registered in India, they can apply to the High Court or the Registrar. Depending on the case, the High Court or the Registrar may decide to cancel or vary the registration of the trademark based on the grounds presented.
2. **Absence or Omission from the Register:** Individuals aggrieved by the absence or omission of any entry in the trademark register, any entry made without sufficient cause, or any entry wrongly remaining on the register can apply to the High Court or the Registrar. Upon review, the High Court or the Registrar may order the making, expunging, or varying of the entry as deemed appropriate.
3. **Decision on Necessary Questions:** In any proceeding under this section, the High Court or the Registrar has the authority to decide any question necessary or expedient in connection with the rectification of the register. This ensures that all relevant issues are addressed effectively during the trademark rectification process.
4. **Initiation of Rectification Proceedings:** The High Court or the Registrar, may initiate rectification proceedings. After providing notice to the concerned parties and granting them an opportunity to be heard, the High Court or the Registrar can make any order as specified in subsections (1) or (2) based on the case's merits.
5. **Notice of Rectification Order:** Upon the High Court's order rectifying the register, it directs that notice of the rectification be served upon the Registrar in the prescribed manner. Upon receipt of such notice, the Registrar must rectify the register accordingly, ensuring the necessary changes are made under the court's decision.

content_sections.heading: Precautions to Prevent Mark Rectification
content_sections.content:
Use the following precautions to prevent the rectification or removal of the registered trademark from the registrar.

- Renew the registered trademark within the prescribed timeframe to maintain its legal protection.
- Preserve the trademark's distinctive character and avoid its becoming deceptively similar to other marks.
- Don’t leave your trademark unused for a period exceeding five years.
- Take legal action against or restrain others from infringing your trademark.
- Avoid using generic terms, descriptive terms, or deceptive elements when you are deciding your trademark.

content_sections.content:

Choose the Appropriate Authority:** This is the first crucial step, as it determines the form you need and the overall trademark rectification process.

- **Intellectual Property Appellate Board (IPAB):** To make any substantial changes, like cancellation or rectification of the registered trademark.

**2\. Choose the Correct Form:**

- **Correction or Cancellation Requested by the Trademark Proprietor:** Submit the "TM-16" form along with necessary payments.
- **Rectification or Cancellation requested by the Registrar:** Use the "TM-M" form and pay prescribed fees.
- **Rectification or Cancellation Initiated by Any Aggrieved Party:** Complete the "TM-26" form and submit it with the required fees.

**3\. Submit Documents:** Provide necessary modifications and supporting documentation with the trademark rectification application(s), such as identification or address verification. **4\. Draft the Application:** Fill out the application form with all relevant details. **5\. Submit the Form:** Send the form and the required payments to the Registrar. **6\. Ensure Comprehensive Justification:** Include detailed justifications for filing a rectification application supported by adequate evidence. **7\. Await Government Approval:** The Registrar reviews the application and makes any necessary rectifications to the registered mark. **8\. Respond to Registrar's Notifications (for Aggrieved Party):** If an aggrieved party requests correction,

- Submit the trademark rectification application and required payments to the Registrar.
- Receive notification from the Registrar to submit a counter-statement.
- Both parties submit affidavits with supporting documentation.
- The registrar or Appellate Board may decide on rectification based on the arguments presented.

The rectification filed in trademark process requires thorough documentation and evidence to support the requested changes to the registration.

Common questions aboutTrademark Rectification in India for Brand Protection.

What is trademark rectification, and why is it important?

Trademark rectification is the legal process of correcting errors or inaccuracies in a trademark's registration details. It is crucial for maintaining the accuracy and integrity of a trademark registration, ensuring that it faithfully represents the goods or services it aims to protect, thereby upholding the sanctity of intellectual property rights.

What are some common reasons for requiring trademark rectification?

Some common reasons for requiring trademark rectification include typographical or clerical errors in the registration details, incorrect information about the trademark owner or business structure, misleading details, or the need for updates due to changes in ownership or the nature of the business.

How does trademark rectification help in brand protection?

Trademark rectification plays a vital role in brand protection by correcting errors that could misrepresent the nature or ownership of the trademark. It also helps prevent potential trademark infringement issues and consumer confusion arising from similarities between registered trademarks. By ensuring accurate and up-to-date information, rectification strengthens the legal standing of the brand owner in enforcement and litigation.

What is the process for filing a trademark rectification application in India?

In India, trademark rectification applications must be submitted to the Trade Marks Registry where the initial trademark registration was filed. The process requires detailed documentation justifying the rectification, including evidence of errors and the proposed corrections. It is advisable to seek guidance from IP lawyers specializing in trademark law to ensure compliance with legal nuances.

How does trademark rectification contribute to market clarity and consumer trust?

By ensuring that each trademark uniquely identifies its owner's goods or services, rectification helps prevent confusion among consumers, which can be detrimental to a brand's reputation. It also maintains the integrity of the market by providing a clear and accurate registry for consumers to differentiate between brands, fostering trust in the intellectual property system.

What are the legal implications of not rectifying errors in trademark registrations?

Failing to rectify errors or inaccuracies in trademark registrations can lead to legal complications, such as potential trademark infringement disputes, weakened legal standing in enforcement and litigation, and non-compliance with the stipulations of the Trademarks Act, which may result in legal penalties or even cancellation of the trademark.

Can trademark rectification be carried out for trademarks registered in multiple jurisdictions?

Yes, trademark rectification can be carried out for trademarks registered in multiple jurisdictions. However, the process and specific requirements may vary across different countries or regions. It is essential to consult with IP professionals familiar with the relevant trademark laws and regulations in each jurisdiction where the trademark is registered to ensure proper compliance and effective protection.

# Trademark Application Correction

Trademark application correction may be required for a number of reasons like erroneous data-entry or erroneous filing of trademark application. A correction of any errors in a trademark application can be made and is permitted by the Trade Marks Act 1999 and Rules 2002. In this article, we look at the procedure for filing a trademark application correction or amendment.

## Trademark Form-16

Before the registration of a trademark, an applicant who has filed a trademark registration application can request for correction or amendment of a trademark application by filing trademark Form- 16 along with the prescribed fee and supporting documents.

Once, the application is submitted, the Trademark office will upload the digitized version of TM-16 into the trademark system. Through an [online search for the documents filed for trademark application](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/trademark-search), the TM-16 uploaded can be verified by the applicant.

## Trademark Correction or Amendement

Trademark Form-16 can be used for correction of clerical errors in the application. Request for correction or amendment or errors that seek substantial alteration in the application for registration of trademark would not be allowed. Also, any amendment in the applied Trademark which may substantially alter proprietor details, specification of goods and services (except deletion of some items), statement as to the use of the mark are not be permitted.

Request for amendment in the proprietorship of the trademark on the basis of valid assignment or transmission, change in address of the applicant or in the address for service, deletion or confinement of any item in the specification of goods/services, confinement/limitation in the area of sales of goods/services, division of multiclass application, etc. can be allowed.

## Data Entry Errors

In case of an error(s) in the data entry and request for correction of the same, the trademark officer after verification of relevant document, can make a change in the system along with the remarks to this effect in the system by concerned officer.

## Correction in Trademark Registration Certificate

In case of erroneous registration certificate and request is made for correction, the Trademark Office would examine the contents of the request on the basis of relevant documents and if the request is acceptable, provide a new trademark registration certificate and take back the erroneous registration certificate from the applicant.

content_sections.heading: What is the Trademark Certificate Number?
content_sections.content: In the realm of business, establishing a unique identity is paramount. This is where trademarks come into play, serving as vital tools for differentiating your brand's goods and services from those of others. In India, registering a trademark is a testament to a business's commitment to its brand identity. Once the[trademark registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/trademark-registration-in-india-a-comprehensive-guide) process is completed, a unique identifier, known as the Trademark Certificate Number, will be issued to the applicant. This article delves into the essence of the Trademark Certificate Number, elucidating its significance and the process of obtaining it.IndiaFilings' trademark experts are here to guide you through obtaining your [Trademark Registration Certificate](https://www.indiafilings.com/trademark-registration-certificate). [Get Started!](https://www.indiafilings.com/trademark-registration-certificate)

content_sections.heading: Trademark
content_sections.content: A trademark represents a form of Intellectual Property that assigns a distinct legal identity to a brand, product, or service. This unique identifier can be a symbol, logo, design, word, phrase, or expression. Trademarks can be owned by businesses, individuals, or legal entities. Essentially, a trademark serves as a recognizable sign or expression legally capable of distinguishing one entity's goods or services from those of others.

content_sections.heading: Trademark Certificate
content_sections.content: When a trademark is successfully registered, the Indian Trademark Registry issues a trademark registration certificate. This certificate is a legal document that validates the trademark registration under the Trade Marks Act of 1999. Embedded within this certificate is the trademark certificate number, a unique identifier assigned to each registered trademark.

content_sections.heading: What is a Trademark Certificate Number?
content_sections.content: As mentioned above, A Trademark Certificate Number is more than just a sequence of letters and numbers; it's the official acknowledgement of your trademark's registration. Assigned by the Indian Trade Marks Registry, this unique alphanumeric code becomes the legal identifier of your trademark, encapsulating your brand's exclusivity and authenticity.

content_sections.heading: Purpose and Significance of Trademark Certificate Number
content_sections.content:
The trademark certificate number serves several critical functions:

- **Unique Identification:** It uniquely identifies your trademark registration, distinguishing it from millions of other entries in the registry. This unique number facilitates easier search and reference in the official records.
- **Legal Proof of Registration:** The number on your trademark certificate is a testament to the legal protection afforded to your brand. It is concrete proof that your trademark has been officially registered and recognized by the Indian Trademark Registry.
- **Renewal and Maintenance:** This number is essential for administrative purposes, such as renewals, amendments, or legal disputes related to the trademark. It streamlines the process of maintaining the legal protections associated with your trademark.

[_Know more about How to Keep Your Trademark Alive in India?_](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/how-to-keep-your-trademark-alive-in-india)

content_sections.heading: Advantages of Trademark Certificate Number
content_sections.content:
Obtaining a trademark certificate number offers several advantages crucial for businesses aiming to establish and protect their brand identity in the marketplace. Here are some of the key benefits:

- **Legal Protection:** A trademark certificate number signifies that your trademark is officially registered, granting you exclusive rights to use it with the goods or services listed in the registration. This legal recognition helps protect your brand from infringement and unauthorized use by others.
- **Brand Recognition:** A registered trademark helps build and reinforce brand recognition. Customers are likelier to remember and trust a legally protected brand, increasing customer loyalty and brand value.
- **Market Differentiation:** With a unique trademark, your products or services stand out in a crowded marketplace. This differentiation is crucial for attracting and retaining customers, ultimately driving business success.
- **Asset Value:** A trademark can become a valuable asset to your business. As your brand grows, the value of your trademark increases, which can be beneficial in business transactions such as mergers, acquisitions, or licensing agreements.
- **Access to Legal Remedies:** A trademark certificate number provides a solid foundation for legal action in case of infringement. Registered trademark owners have access to legal remedies, including injunctions, damages, and compensation for infringement.
- **Use of the ® Symbol:** Once you obtain a trademark certificate number, you are entitled to use the ® symbol with your trademark, indicating that it is a registered and protected trademark. This can deter potential infringers and signal your commitment to protecting intellectual property.
- **Geographical Expansion:** A registered trademark is a key asset when expanding your business geographically. It facilitates obtaining trademark registration in other countries, providing a global shield for your brand.
- **Prevention of Counterfeiting:** A registered trademark makes it easier for authorities to take action against counterfeiters and fraudsters who attempt to imitate your brand, ensuring the authenticity of your products or services.

In conclusion, obtaining a trademark certificate number is a strategic move for any business looking to secure its brand identity, enhance its market presence, and effectively protect its intellectual property rights.

content_sections.heading: How to obtain a Trademark Registration Number?
content_sections.content: Obtaining a trademark certificate number involves a structured process, which includes:

content_sections.heading: Step 1: Trademark Search
content_sections.content:
Start by conducting a thorough [Trademark search](https://www.indiafilings.com/trademark/search)to ensure your desired trademark isn't already in use or too similar to existing trademarks. This step is crucial to avoid potential conflicts and rejections.

**Step 2: Filing the Application**

Once you've identified a unique trademark, apply with the Trademark Registry. This can be done online or through a physical submission. The application should include detailed information about the trademark, the goods or services it represents, and the applicant's details.

content_sections.heading: Step 3: Examination
content_sections.content: After submission, the Trademark Office will examine your application to comply with legal requirements and ensure no conflicts with pre-existing trademarks.

content_sections.heading: Step 4: Publication
content_sections.content: If your application passes the examination stage, the trademark is then published in the Trademark Journal. This publication period allows third parties to file any opposition to registering your trademark.

content_sections.heading: Step 5: Registration
content_sections.content:
The trademark is officially registered if no oppositions are filed within the prescribed period or if you successfully overcome any challenges. The Trademark Registry will issue a Trademark Registration Certificate, including your unique Trademark Registration Number.It's important to note that each step in this process must be carefully managed to avoid delays or rejections. Seek expert assistance from IndiaFilings for an easy process and effortlessly obtain your trademark certificate.

content_sections.heading: Where to Find Your Trademark Registration Number in India
content_sections.content: After completing your application to register a trademark, you will be allotted a trademark application number. This application number also serves as your trademark registration number. In other words, the trademark application number and the registration number are the same. However, you might want to check the status of your application to know if your trademark number has been registered successfully.

content_sections.heading: Conclusion
content_sections.content: Obtaining a Trademark Certificate Number is a strategic move for any business looking to secure its brand identity and leverage the myriad benefits of trademark registration. It offers robust legal protection and contributes significantly to brand recognition, market presence, and the overall valuation of your business. With the backing of a registered trademark, your brand is well-positioned to navigate the competitive business landscape with confidence and authority.

# What is the Trademark Certificate Number?

In the realm of business, establishing a unique identity is paramount. This is where trademarks come into play, serving as vital tools for differentiating your brand's goods and services from those of others. In India, registering a trademark is a testament to a business's commitment to its brand identity. Once the[trademark registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/trademark-registration-in-india-a-comprehensive-guide) process is completed, a unique identifier, known as the Trademark Certificate Number, will be issued to the applicant. This article delves into the essence of the Trademark Certificate Number, elucidating its significance and the process of obtaining it.IndiaFilings' trademark experts are here to guide you through obtaining your [Trademark Registration Certificate](https://www.indiafilings.com/trademark-registration-certificate). [Get Started!](https://www.indiafilings.com/trademark-registration-certificate)

## Trademark

A trademark represents a form of Intellectual Property that assigns a distinct legal identity to a brand, product, or service. This unique identifier can be a symbol, logo, design, word, phrase, or expression. Trademarks can be owned by businesses, individuals, or legal entities. Essentially, a trademark serves as a recognizable sign or expression legally capable of distinguishing one entity's goods or services from those of others.

## Trademark Certificate

When a trademark is successfully registered, the Indian Trademark Registry issues a trademark registration certificate. This certificate is a legal document that validates the trademark registration under the Trade Marks Act of 1999. Embedded within this certificate is the trademark certificate number, a unique identifier assigned to each registered trademark.

## What is a Trademark Certificate Number?

As mentioned above, A Trademark Certificate Number is more than just a sequence of letters and numbers; it's the official acknowledgement of your trademark's registration. Assigned by the Indian Trade Marks Registry, this unique alphanumeric code becomes the legal identifier of your trademark, encapsulating your brand's exclusivity and authenticity.

## Purpose and Significance of Trademark Certificate Number

The trademark certificate number serves several critical functions:

- **Unique Identification:** It uniquely identifies your trademark registration, distinguishing it from millions of other entries in the registry. This unique number facilitates easier search and reference in the official records.
- **Legal Proof of Registration:** The number on your trademark certificate is a testament to the legal protection afforded to your brand. It is concrete proof that your trademark has been officially registered and recognized by the Indian Trademark Registry.
- **Renewal and Maintenance:** This number is essential for administrative purposes, such as renewals, amendments, or legal disputes related to the trademark. It streamlines the process of maintaining the legal protections associated with your trademark.

[_Know more about How to Keep Your Trademark Alive in India?_](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/how-to-keep-your-trademark-alive-in-india)

## Advantages of Trademark Certificate Number

Obtaining a trademark certificate number offers several advantages crucial for businesses aiming to establish and protect their brand identity in the marketplace. Here are some of the key benefits:

- **Legal Protection:** A trademark certificate number signifies that your trademark is officially registered, granting you exclusive rights to use it with the goods or services listed in the registration. This legal recognition helps protect your brand from infringement and unauthorized use by others.
- **Brand Recognition:** A registered trademark helps build and reinforce brand recognition. Customers are likelier to remember and trust a legally protected brand, increasing customer loyalty and brand value.
- **Market Differentiation:** With a unique trademark, your products or services stand out in a crowded marketplace. This differentiation is crucial for attracting and retaining customers, ultimately driving business success.
- **Asset Value:** A trademark can become a valuable asset to your business. As your brand grows, the value of your trademark increases, which can be beneficial in business transactions such as mergers, acquisitions, or licensing agreements.
- **Access to Legal Remedies:** A trademark certificate number provides a solid foundation for legal action in case of infringement. Registered trademark owners have access to legal remedies, including injunctions, damages, and compensation for infringement.
- **Use of the ® Symbol:** Once you obtain a trademark certificate number, you are entitled to use the ® symbol with your trademark, indicating that it is a registered and protected trademark. This can deter potential infringers and signal your commitment to protecting intellectual property.
- **Geographical Expansion:** A registered trademark is a key asset when expanding your business geographically. It facilitates obtaining trademark registration in other countries, providing a global shield for your brand.
- **Prevention of Counterfeiting:** A registered trademark makes it easier for authorities to take action against counterfeiters and fraudsters who attempt to imitate your brand, ensuring the authenticity of your products or services.

In conclusion, obtaining a trademark certificate number is a strategic move for any business looking to secure its brand identity, enhance its market presence, and effectively protect its intellectual property rights.

## How to obtain a Trademark Registration Number?

Obtaining a trademark certificate number involves a structured process, which includes:

### **Step 1: Trademark Search**

Start by conducting a thorough [Trademark search](https://www.indiafilings.com/trademark/search)to ensure your desired trademark isn't already in use or too similar to existing trademarks. This step is crucial to avoid potential conflicts and rejections.

**Step 2: Filing the Application**

Once you've identified a unique trademark, apply with the Trademark Registry. This can be done online or through a physical submission. The application should include detailed information about the trademark, the goods or services it represents, and the applicant's details.

### **Step 3: Examination**

After submission, the Trademark Office will examine your application to comply with legal requirements and ensure no conflicts with pre-existing trademarks.

### **Step 4: Publication**

If your application passes the examination stage, the trademark is then published in the Trademark Journal. This publication period allows third parties to file any opposition to registering your trademark.

### **Step 5: Registration**

The trademark is officially registered if no oppositions are filed within the prescribed period or if you successfully overcome any challenges. The Trademark Registry will issue a Trademark Registration Certificate, including your unique Trademark Registration Number.It's important to note that each step in this process must be carefully managed to avoid delays or rejections. Seek expert assistance from IndiaFilings for an easy process and effortlessly obtain your trademark certificate.

[Register Now!](https://www.indiafilings.com/trademark-registration)

## Where to Find Your Trademark Registration Number in India

After completing your application to register a trademark, you will be allotted a trademark application number. This application number also serves as your trademark registration number. In other words, the trademark application number and the registration number are the same. However, you might want to check the status of your application to know if your trademark number has been registered successfully.

## Conclusion

Obtaining a Trademark Certificate Number is a strategic move for any business looking to secure its brand identity and leverage the myriad benefits of trademark registration. It offers robust legal protection and contributes significantly to brand recognition, market presence, and the overall valuation of your business. With the backing of a registered trademark, your brand is well-positioned to navigate the competitive business landscape with confidence and authority.

content_sections.heading: What is a Trademark Certificate?
content_sections.content: A Trademark Certificate is a legal document issued by the Trade Marks Registry that verifies the successful [trademark registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/trademark-registration-in-india-a-comprehensive-guide). It serves as evidence of the ownership rights held by the trademark owner, granting them the exclusive right to utilise the trademark for the specified goods and services. The certificate incorporates details such as the trademark, its registration date and number, the relevant class of goods or services it covers, the proprietor's name and address, and the duration of the trademark's protection. Essentially, the Trademark Certificate is a valuable asset that bolsters the legal protection of a trademark and deters unauthorised use by others.

content_sections.heading: Benefits of Trademark Registration Certificate
content_sections.content:
A Trademark Registration Certificate in India offers a range of significant benefits for businesses and individuals:

- Exclusivity: The certificate grants the owner exclusive rights to use the trademark for the specified goods and services within the registered classes. This allows them to control how their brand is presented and prevent others from using confusingly similar marks.
- Legal Protection Against Infringement: Registration strengthens your legal position in case of [trademark infringement](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/trademark-infringement-in-india). The certificate serves as prima facie evidence of ownership, making it easier to pursue legal action against unauthorised use of your trademark.
- Brand Differentiation: A registered trademark helps distinguish your products or services from competitors. Customers can easily recognise and associate the mark with your brand, fostering brand loyalty and reputation.
- Creation of a Valuable Asset: The trademark itself becomes an intangible asset. The certificate strengthens this by providing documented ownership. This asset can be licensed, franchised, or even sold, creating additional revenue streams.
- Enhanced Brand Value: Registration signifies the legitimacy and professionalism of your brand. This can increase customer confidence and trust, potentially leading to higher brand value and market recognition.
- Facilitates Global Expansion: A registered trademark in India can serve as a base for international trademark registration. This can be crucial if you intend to expand your business overseas.

content_sections.heading: How to Get a Trademark Application Number?
content_sections.content:
Your trademark application number is crucial for downloading your trademark certificate online from the Trade Marks Registry website. Here's how to find the trademark application number using the IP India Website:

1. Visit the IP India website: Go to the official website of Intellectual Property India (IP India).
2. Search for your Trademark: Enter the brand name or company name to find your trademark application number.
3. Refine your Search (Optional): You can also enter the class of goods or services your trademark applies to for a more targeted search. This will help narrow down the results, especially if you have common brand names.
4. Find your Trademark Details: The search results will display any matching trademarks. Look for your specific trademark and check the details provided. This should include the application number and the current status of your application.
5. Note down the Application Number: Once you've located your application number, make sure to note it down for future reference. You'll need this number to download your trademark certificate once it's been issued.

content_sections.heading: Necessary Requirements for Trademark Certificate Download
content_sections.content:
The generation of trademark registration certificates in India is fully automated. This allows applicants to download their certificates online, provided the following conditions are met:

- Trademark Publication: The trademark must be published in the Trade Marks Journal.
- Registration Status: The trademark’s registration status must not be marked as ‘Abandoned’ or ‘Removed’.
- Electronic Database Record: The original trademark registration application must exist in the Trade Marks Registry’s electronic database.
- No Pending Amendment Requests: There should be no pending applications for amendments to the trademark.
- Pending Compliances: All necessary compliances, such as payment of fees or submission of a Power of Attorney, must be completed.

Once these conditions are fulfilled, the trademark registration certificate will be transmitted to the applicant or their authorised agent via the email address recorded with the trademark office.

content_sections.heading: How to Download Trademark Certificate Online?
content_sections.content:
The Government of India allows for easy online access to trademark registration certificates. This section will guide you through the steps for a Trademark certificate download from the official Trade Marks Registry website.
Step 1: Visit the official Trade Marks Registry website.![trademark-certificates step-1](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/step-1-download-trademark-certificates.png)
Step 2: Click on the "Trade Mark Application/Registered Mark" option.![trademark-certificates step-2](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/step-2-download-trademark-certificate.jpg)
Step 3: Select the "National/IRDI Number" option.![trademark-certificates step-1](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/step-3-download-trademark-certificate.jpg)
Step 4: Enter the trademark application number and the provided captcha code. Click "View".![trademark-certificates step-1](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/step-4-download-trademark-certificate.jpg)
Step 5: Click on the displayed trademark number.
Step 6: Select "View Registration Certificate".
Step 7: The certificate will open in a new tab. Click the download icon to save it as a PDF.
Please note: Only published trademarks without pending compliances will have downloadable certificates.

content_sections.heading: Validity of Trademark Certificate
content_sections.content: In India, a registered trademark holds its validity for a period of ten years from the date of registration. This means the legal protection and exclusive right to use the trademark are enforceable for a decade. However, to maintain this protection beyond ten years, renewal is necessary. The process for renewal is generally straightforward and can be initiated within a year before the expiry date to ensure uninterrupted ownership. **Learn more:** [What is the validity of trademark?](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/what-is-the-validity-of-a-trademark)

content_sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
content_sections.content:
Common questions aboutTrademark Certificate Download.

What is a trademark certificate?

A trademark certificate is an official document issued by the Trade Marks Registry that serves as proof of registration for a trademark. It provides details about the trademark, its registration date and number, the proprietor's name and address, and the goods or services it covers, granting the owner exclusive rights to use the trademark.

Why is it important to obtain a trademark certificate?

Obtaining a trademark certificate is crucial because it establishes legal ownership and grants exclusive rights to use the registered trademark for the specified goods or services. It prevents others from using confusingly similar marks and serves as evidence in case of infringement disputes. The certificate also enhances brand value and facilitates global expansion.

How long is a trademark certificate valid in India?

In India, a registered trademark is valid for 10 years from the date of registration. To maintain the protection beyond this period, the trademark owner must renew the registration before it expires.

Can I download the trademark certificate online?

Yes, the Indian government allows trademark owners to download their registration certificates online from the Trade Marks Registry website. However, this option is only available for published trademarks that have no pending compliances or amendment requests.

What information is required to download a trademark certificate?

To download a trademark certificate online, you will need the trademark application number. You can find this number by searching for your trademark on the Intellectual Property India (IP India) website.

Are there any prerequisites for downloading a trademark certificate?

Yes, there are certain prerequisites for downloading a trademark certificate. The trademark must be published in the Trade Marks Journal, its registration status should not be marked as 'Abandoned' or 'Removed', and the original application should exist in the Trade Marks Registry's electronic database.

How can I renew my trademark registration?

To renew your trademark registration in India, you need to submit a renewal application along with the prescribed fees within one year before the expiry date of the registration. This process can be completed online or through a registered trademark agent.

Can I transfer ownership of a registered trademark?

Yes, the ownership of a registered trademark can be transferred to another party. This process is known as an assignment and requires filing a request for assignment with the Trade Marks Registry, along with the necessary documents and fees.

What happens if someone infringes on my registered trademark?

If someone infringes on your registered trademark by using a confusingly similar mark for identical or related goods or services, you can take legal action against them. The trademark certificate serves as prima facie evidence of your ownership rights, strengthening your case in court.

How can I ensure timely renewal of my trademark certificate?

To ensure timely renewal of your trademark certificate, you can set reminders or seek assistance from professional trademark services like IndiaFilings. Their experts can guide you through the renewal process and help maintain the legal protection of your trademark.
